name: Adolf Hitler
organization_en: NSDAP · Reich government · Armed Forces High Command
role_en: Führer and Reich Chancellor, head of state and supreme commander of the armed forces
role_pl: Führer and Reich Chancellor of Germany
role_de: Führer und Reichskanzler, Staatsoberhaupt und Oberbefehlshaber der Wehrmacht
role_ru: фюрер и рейхсканцлер, глава государства и верховный главнокомандующий вооружёнными силами
role_fr: Führer et chancelier du Reich, chef de l’État et commandant suprême des forces armées
crime_tags_pl: Wojna napastnicza;Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa;Praca przymusowa;Akcja „T4”;Propaganda i podżeganie
status_en: not tried; died by suicide in 1945
interpretation_en: Hitler occupied the apex of the decision chain: his ideological programme, authorisations and commands set state and party institutions in motion. This does not erase the separate agency and responsibility of the many officials and perpetrators who implemented them.
postwar_en: Hitler was never tried. He died by suicide in the Berlin bunker on 30 April 1945; the International Military Tribunal later judged surviving leaders of the regime and classified its policies as crimes against peace, war crimes and crimes against humanity.
limitations_en: The profile describes Hitler's supreme political and command responsibility. It does not convert the overlapping crimes of the state, party, SS, police and armed forces into an individual victim total.

name: Heinrich Himmler
organization_en: SS · German Police · Reich Main Security Office system
role_en: Reichsführer-SS, Chief of German Police and Reich Minister of the Interior
role_pl: Reichsführer-SS and Chief of German Police
role_de: Reichsführer-SS, Chef der Deutschen Polizei und Reichsminister des Innern
role_ru: рейхсфюрер СС, шеф германской полиции и рейхсминистр внутренних дел
role_fr: Reichsführer-SS, chef de la police allemande et ministre de l’Intérieur du Reich
region_en: SS and police apparatus across German-occupied Europe
region_pl: SS and Police across German-occupied Europe
crime_tags_pl: Wojna napastnicza;Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa;Praca przymusowa
status_en: not tried; died by suicide in British custody in 1945
interpretation_en: Himmler's responsibility lay in building and commanding the institutional system that translated racial policy into deportation, forced labour and mass murder. Individual offices and commanders retained responsibility for their own decisions and operations.
postwar_en: After attempting separate negotiations and fleeing under a false identity, Himmler was captured by British forces. On 23 May 1945 he bit a concealed cyanide capsule and died before he could be tried; the International Military Tribunal later declared the SS a criminal organisation.
limitations_en: The profile identifies Himmler's command over the SS and police system without attributing every crime committed by every subordinate unit to a personal order from him.

name: Hermann Göring
organization_en: Reich government · Luftwaffe · Four Year Plan administration
role_en: Reichsmarschall, commander-in-chief of the Luftwaffe and plenipotentiary for the Four Year Plan
role_pl: Reichsmarschall and Commander-in-Chief of the Luftwaffe
role_de: Reichsmarschall, Oberbefehlshaber der Luftwaffe und Beauftragter für den Vierjahresplan
role_ru: рейхсмаршал, главнокомандующий люфтваффе и уполномоченный по Четырёхлетнему плану
role_fr: Reichsmarschall, commandant en chef de la Luftwaffe et plénipotentiaire au Plan de quatre ans
region_en: German Reich and the economies of occupied Europe
crime_tags_pl: Wojna napastnicza;Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa;Praca przymusowa
status_en: sentenced to death at Nuremberg; died by suicide in custody in 1946
interpretation_en: Göring connected senior political authority, policing, air power and economic mobilisation. The profile therefore treats his signed measures and institutional powers as distinct forms of agency rather than assigning all Luftwaffe or occupation crimes to him automatically.
postwar_en: The International Military Tribunal found Göring guilty on all four counts and sentenced him to death on 1 October 1946. He died by cyanide poisoning in his cell on 15 October, hours before the scheduled execution.
limitations_en: His high-level responsibility overlapped with that of ministries, SS offices, industrial managers and operational commanders; the profile does not treat that overlap as a measurable personal share of every crime.

name: Reinhard Heydrich
organization_en: Reich Main Security Office (RSHA) · Security Police and SD
role_en: chief of the RSHA and acting Reich Protector of Bohemia and Moravia
role_pl: Chief of the Reich Main Security Office (RSHA)
role_de: Chef des RSHA und stellvertretender Reichsprotektor in Böhmen und Mähren
role_ru: начальник РСХА и исполняющий обязанности рейхспротектора Богемии и Моравии
role_fr: chef du RSHA et protecteur du Reich par intérim en Bohême-Moravie
region_en: German security apparatus in occupied Europe and the Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia
region_pl: Security apparatus in Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia and occupied Europe
crime_tags_pl: Wojna napastnicza;Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa;Praca przymusowa
status_en: not tried; died in 1942 after the Prague assassination attack
interpretation_en: Heydrich occupied the coordinating centre between political authorisation and police execution. His responsibility is grounded in institutions, directives and coordination; it does not make him the sole author of every operation conducted by the RSHA or Einsatzgruppen.
postwar_en: Heydrich did not survive to face trial. Czechoslovak agents attacked him in Prague on 27 May 1942 and he died from his wounds on 4 June; the occupation authorities then carried out mass reprisals, including the destruction of Lidice and Ležáky.
limitations_en: The profile separates Heydrich's documented direction and coordination from crimes later committed in his name or after his death, including subsequent phases of Operation Reinhard.

name: Joseph Goebbels
organization_en: Reich Ministry of Public Enlightenment and Propaganda · NSDAP
role_en: Reich propaganda minister and Gauleiter of Berlin
role_pl: Reich Minister of Public Enlightenment and Propaganda
role_de: Reichsminister für Volksaufklärung und Propaganda und Gauleiter von Berlin
role_ru: рейхсминистр пропаганды и гауляйтер Берлина
role_fr: ministre de la Propagande du Reich et Gauleiter de Berlin
region_en: German Reich, with political authority in Berlin
crime_tags_pl: Wojna napastnicza;Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa;Propaganda i podżeganie
status_en: not tried; died by suicide in 1945
interpretation_en: Goebbels's agency lay in sustained incitement, censorship and mobilisation that helped legitimise persecution and war. Propaganda's contribution is documented without treating it as a substitute for the decisions of deportation, police and killing agencies.
postwar_en: After Hitler's death Goebbels served as Reich Chancellor for one day. On 1 May 1945 Joseph and Magda Goebbels had their six children poisoned and then died by suicide in Berlin, so he never appeared before a court.
limitations_en: The profile documents Goebbels's own ministry, public incitement and recorded approval of mass murder; it does not assign to him every crime committed by audiences or agencies influenced by Nazi propaganda.

name: Martin Bormann
organization_en: NSDAP Party Chancellery · Führer's headquarters
role_en: head of the NSDAP Party Chancellery and secretary to Hitler
role_pl: Head of the Party Chancellery
role_de: Leiter der Parteikanzlei der NSDAP und Sekretär Hitlers
role_ru: глава Партийной канцелярии НСДАП и секретарь Гитлера
role_fr: chef de la chancellerie du Parti nazi et secrétaire d’Hitler
region_en: German Reich and the central party administration
crime_tags_pl: Wojna napastnicza;Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa;Praca przymusowa
status_en: sentenced to death in absentia; died in Berlin in 1945
interpretation_en: Bormann exercised power through gatekeeping, drafting, transmission and party supervision. The profile ties responsibility to his own documents and office rather than assuming that every policy communicated through the Chancellery originated with him.
postwar_en: Because his fate was unknown, the International Military Tribunal tried Bormann in absentia, convicted him of war crimes and crimes against humanity and sentenced him to death in 1946. Remains found in Berlin in 1972 were identified as his, with DNA confirmation in 1998.
limitations_en: Bormann's bureaucratic influence was extensive but often indirect; the profile distinguishes documented directives and institutional control from unsupported claims of personal authorship.

name: Ernst Kaltenbrunner
tier_label_en: Designers of the machinery of destruction
organization_en: Reich Main Security Office (RSHA) · SS and Police
role_en: chief of the RSHA and former Higher SS and Police Leader in Austria
role_pl: Chief of the Reich Main Security Office (RSHA)
role_de: Chef des RSHA und ehemaliger Höherer SS- und Polizeiführer in Österreich
role_ru: начальник РСХА и бывший высший руководитель СС и полиции в Австрии
role_fr: chef du RSHA et ancien chef supérieur de la SS et de la police en Autriche
region_en: German security-police apparatus across occupied Europe
region_pl: RSHA and security apparatus across occupied Europe
crime_tags_pl: Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa;Praca przymusowa
status_en: convicted at Nuremberg and executed in 1946
interpretation_en: Kaltenbrunner inherited an established killing apparatus but chose to lead and sustain it. His responsibility rests on command, signed documentation and continued operations, while the conduct of subordinate offices remains separately attributable.
postwar_en: US forces arrested Kaltenbrunner in Austria in May 1945. The International Military Tribunal convicted him of war crimes and crimes against humanity, sentenced him to death and had him executed by hanging on 16 October 1946.
limitations_en: The profile does not retroactively assign to Kaltenbrunner crimes completed before he became RSHA chief, and it distinguishes his command responsibility from the individual actions of subordinate departments.

name: Odilo Globocnik
tier_label_en: Designers of the machinery of destruction
organization_en: SS and Police · Operation Reinhard apparatus
role_en: SS and Police Leader in the Lublin district and head of Operation Reinhard
role_pl: SS and Police Leader in Lublin district
role_de: SS- und Polizeiführer im Distrikt Lublin und Leiter der Aktion Reinhardt
role_ru: руководитель СС и полиции в Люблинском дистрикте и глава операции «Рейнхард»
role_fr: chef de la SS et de la police dans le district de Lublin et responsable de l’opération Reinhard
region_en: Lublin district of the General Government and later the Adriatic Littoral
crime_tags_pl: Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa;Praca przymusowa
status_en: not tried; died by suicide in British custody in 1945
interpretation_en: Globocnik linked Himmler's authorisation to construction, staffing, transport, forced labour and asset accounting. Responsibility for particular deportations and killings was also borne by the commanders and offices that executed them.
postwar_en: British troops captured Globocnik in Carinthia on 31 May 1945. He bit a concealed cyanide capsule and died before interrogation or trial; later proceedings against camp personnel and historical research documented the operation he had led.
limitations_en: The profile attributes to Globocnik the documented programme he directed, not every act by every police unit, camp employee or civil office operating within the same territory.

name: Adolf Eichmann
tier_label_en: Designers of the machinery of destruction
organization_en: Reich Main Security Office, Gestapo Section IV B4
role_en: head of the RSHA section for Jewish affairs and deportations
role_pl: Head of Jewish Affairs Section IV B4 in RSHA
role_de: Leiter des RSHA-Referats für jüdische Angelegenheiten und Deportationen
role_ru: руководитель отдела РСХА по еврейским делам и депортациям
role_fr: chef de la section du RSHA chargée des affaires juives et des déportations
region_en: deportation networks across German-occupied and allied Europe
region_pl: Deportations of Jews from across occupied Europe
crime_tags_pl: Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Praca przymusowa
status_en: convicted in Israel and executed in 1962
interpretation_en: Eichmann's responsibility demonstrates how railway planning, inter-agency negotiation and administrative enforcement became instruments of mass murder. It is distinct from, but connected to, the responsibility of national authorities, railway offices and killing-centre personnel.
postwar_en: Eichmann escaped to Argentina under the name Ricardo Klement. Israeli agents captured him in 1960; a Jerusalem court convicted him of crimes including crimes against the Jewish people, crimes against humanity and war crimes, and he was hanged on 1 June 1962.
limitations_en: The profile centres on Eichmann's documented deportation role and avoids portraying him as the sole planner of the Holocaust or as the direct perpetrator of every death following a transport.

name: Rudolf Höss
tier_label_en: Designers of the machinery of destruction
organization_en: SS concentration-camp system · Auschwitz camp complex
role_en: commandant of Auschwitz and later deputy inspector of concentration camps
role_pl: Commandant of Auschwitz concentration and extermination camp
role_de: Kommandant von Auschwitz und später stellvertretender Inspekteur der Konzentrationslager
role_ru: комендант Аушвица и позднее заместитель инспектора концентрационных лагерей
role_fr: commandant d’Auschwitz, puis inspecteur adjoint des camps de concentration
region_en: Auschwitz concentration and extermination camp in occupied Poland
crime_tags_pl: Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa;Praca przymusowa
status_en: convicted in Poland and executed in 1947
interpretation_en: Höss exercised direct command and organisational agency over the Auschwitz complex and its killing process. The profile does not equate his office with every individual act by guards, doctors, transport agencies or WVHA superiors.
postwar_en: British military police arrested Höss in March 1946. After testifying at Nuremberg he was extradited to Poland, convicted by the Supreme National Tribunal and hanged at the former Auschwitz I camp on 16 April 1947.
limitations_en: The profile follows the documented periods of Höss's command and return in 1944; it does not treat the entire history of Auschwitz or all crimes of the SS camp system as his personal acts.

name: Hans Frank
organization_en: General Government civil administration · Reich government
role_en: Governor-General of the General Government in occupied Poland
role_pl: Governor-General of the General Government in occupied Poland
role_de: Generalgouverneur des Generalgouvernements im besetzten Polen
role_ru: генерал-губернатор Генерал-губернаторства в оккупированной Польше
role_fr: gouverneur général du Gouvernement général en Pologne occupée
region_en: central and southern occupied Poland administered as the General Government
crime_tags_pl: Wojna napastnicza;Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa;Praca przymusowa
status_en: convicted at Nuremberg and executed in 1946
interpretation_en: Frank's responsibility derived from the policy, resources and administration of the General Government. Conflicts with SS and police leaders divided competences but did not remove his agency or their separate responsibility.
postwar_en: US forces arrested Frank in May 1945. His own official diary became major evidence before the International Military Tribunal, which convicted him of war crimes and crimes against humanity and had him hanged on 16 October 1946.
limitations_en: The profile distinguishes Frank's civil-administrative authority from the operational command of SS and police formations and does not attribute every crime in the General Government to his personal order.

name: Alfred Rosenberg
organization_en: Reich Ministry for the Occupied Eastern Territories · NSDAP · Einsatzstab Reichsleiter Rosenberg
role_en: chief NSDAP ideologue and Reich Minister for the Occupied Eastern Territories
role_pl: Reich Minister for the Occupied Eastern Territories
role_de: führender Ideologe der NSDAP und Reichsminister für die besetzten Ostgebiete
role_ru: главный идеолог НСДАП и рейхсминистр оккупированных восточных территорий
role_fr: principal idéologue du NSDAP et ministre du Reich aux Territoires occupés de l’Est
region_en: occupied eastern Europe, including Reichskommissariat Ostland and Reichskommissariat Ukraine
region_pl: Occupied Eastern Territories (Reich Ministry for the East)
crime_tags_pl: Wojna napastnicza;Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa;Praca przymusowa;Propaganda i podżeganie
status_en: convicted at Nuremberg and executed in 1946
interpretation_en: Rosenberg joined ideological legitimation to ministerial and plunder administration. Jurisdictional disputes with SS and regional commissioners limit claims of direct control over particular killings but do not negate his documented institutional role.
postwar_en: The International Military Tribunal convicted Rosenberg on all four counts, including crimes against peace, war crimes and crimes against humanity. He was sentenced to death on 1 October and hanged in Nuremberg on 16 October 1946.
limitations_en: The profile separates Rosenberg's own ideology, ministry and plunder task force from crimes directed independently by SS, police and regional occupation authorities.

name: Fritz Sauckel
organization_en: Office of the Plenipotentiary General for Labour Allocation · NSDAP
role_en: Plenipotentiary General for Labour Allocation and Gauleiter of Thuringia
role_pl: Plenipotentiary General for Labour Allocation
role_de: Generalbevollmächtigter für den Arbeitseinsatz und Gauleiter von Thüringen
role_ru: генеральный уполномоченный по использованию рабочей силы и гауляйтер Тюрингии
role_fr: plénipotentiaire général pour l’affectation de la main-d’œuvre et Gauleiter de Thuringe
region_en: German Reich and recruitment zones throughout occupied Europe
region_pl: Forced labour system across the German Reich
status_en: convicted at Nuremberg and executed in 1946
interpretation_en: Sauckel controlled the procurement and allocation link in the forced-labour chain. Employers, occupation authorities and police units remained separately responsible for recruitment violence and workplace abuse.
postwar_en: The International Military Tribunal rejected Sauckel's claim that he was merely an employment official. It convicted him of war crimes and crimes against humanity, sentenced him to death and had him hanged on 16 October 1946.
limitations_en: The profile attributes to Sauckel the coercive recruitment system he directed, not every death or abuse committed by a local recruiter, guard, factory manager or camp authority.

name: Albert Speer
organization_en: Reich Ministry of Armaments and War Production · Organisation Todt
role_en: Reich Minister of Armaments and War Production and Hitler's chief architect
role_pl: Reich Minister of Armaments and War Production
role_de: Reichsminister für Rüstung und Kriegsproduktion und Hitlers Chefarchitekt
role_ru: рейхсминистр вооружений и военного производства и главный архитектор Гитлера
role_fr: ministre du Reich à l’Armement et à la Production de guerre et architecte en chef d’Hitler
region_en: German war economy and armaments production
status_en: convicted at Nuremberg; served twenty years and died in 1981
interpretation_en: Speer linked production targets, construction and labour demand to the coercive apparatus. The profile distinguishes his ministerial decisions from Sauckel's recruitment machinery, SS custody and factory-level management.
postwar_en: The International Military Tribunal convicted Speer of war crimes and crimes against humanity and sentenced him to twenty years. After serving the full term at Spandau, he cultivated a self-portrait as an apolitical technocrat that later document-based research contradicted; he died in 1981.
limitations_en: The profile avoids accepting Speer's postwar memoirs at face value and confines responsibility to documented powers, requests and institutional cooperation rather than all abuses in the war economy.

name: Heinrich Müller
tier_label_en: Designers of the machinery of destruction
organization_en: Reich Main Security Office, Amt IV (Gestapo)
role_en: chief of the Gestapo and head of RSHA Amt IV
role_pl: Chief of the Gestapo
role_de: Chef der Gestapo und Leiter des RSHA-Amts IV
role_ru: начальник гестапо и глава ведомства IV РСХА
role_fr: chef de la Gestapo et responsable de l’Amt IV du RSHA
region_en: Gestapo apparatus throughout the Reich and German-occupied Europe
crime_tags_pl: Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa;Praca przymusowa
status_en: never tried; missing since May 1945
interpretation_en: Müller converted political and racial directives into Gestapo procedure, reporting and enforcement. The profile identifies his command role without treating every arrest or killing by a Gestapo office as a personally signed order.
postwar_en: Müller was last seen near the Reich Chancellery in Berlin on 1 May 1945. Allied searches failed to find him, a purported grave proved false, and although later intelligence assessments considered death in Berlin likely, neither his death nor a grave has been conclusively established.
limitations_en: His fate after 1 May 1945 remains uncertain. The profile reports the documented last sighting and does not present unverified escape stories as fact.

name: Karl Brandt
organization_en: Führer's Chancellery · T4 programme · Reich health administration
role_en: Hitler's personal physician, co-director of the T4 programme and Reich health commissioner
role_pl: Hitler's personal physician and head of Aktion T4 euthanasia programme
role_de: Hitlers Begleitarzt, Mitverantwortlicher des T4-Programms und Reichskommissar für das Sanitäts- und Gesundheitswesen
role_ru: личный врач Гитлера, соруководитель программы убийств T4 и рейхский комиссар здравоохранения
role_fr: médecin personnel d’Hitler, codirecteur du programme T4 et commissaire à la santé du Reich
region_en: Germany and Austria, with authority in the concentration-camp medical system
region_pl: Aktion T4 euthanasia program (Germany and Austria)
crime_tags_pl: Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Inne ludobójstwa;Akcja „T4”;Eksperymenty pseudomedyczne
status_en: convicted in the Doctors' Trial and executed in 1948
interpretation_en: Brandt supplied medical authority, access to Hitler and programme-level supervision to organised murder. Responsibility for selections, transport and killings was also borne by T4 administrators, physicians and facility personnel.
postwar_en: An American military tribunal convicted Brandt of war crimes, crimes against humanity and membership in the criminal SS in the Doctors' Trial. Sentenced to death on 20 August 1947, he was hanged at Landsberg prison on 2 June 1948.
limitations_en: The profile distinguishes Brandt's programme and health-system authority from the individual conduct of every doctor and from killings conducted outside his documented remit.

name: Philipp Bouhler
organization_en: Führer's Chancellery · T4 programme
role_en: head of the Führer's Chancellery and co-director of the T4 killing programme
role_pl: Chief of the Führer Chancellery
role_de: Leiter der Kanzlei des Führers und Mitverantwortlicher des T4-Tötungsprogramms
role_ru: глава Канцелярии фюрера и соруководитель программы убийств T4
role_fr: chef de la chancellerie du Führer et codirecteur du programme de mise à mort T4
region_en: Germany and Austria, including T4 institutions and concentration camps
region_pl: Aktion T4 euthanasia program (Germany and Austria)
status_en: not tried; died by suicide in US custody in 1945
interpretation_en: Bouhler's responsibility rests on creating and supervising the administrative structure behind medicalised mass murder. The profile preserves the separate agency of physicians, evaluators, transport staff and killing-centre personnel.
postwar_en: US forces arrested Bouhler near Zell am See on 10 May 1945. He died by cyanide poisoning in an American internment camp on 19 May, before he could be tried; the T4 programme was later documented in the Doctors' Trial.
limitations_en: The profile follows Bouhler's documented chancellery and T4 authority and does not make him personally responsible for every later crime committed by former T4 staff.

name: Wilhelm Keitel
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Armed Forces High Command (OKW) · Wehrmacht
role_en: chief of the Armed Forces High Command
role_pl: Chief of the Oberkommando der Wehrmacht (OKW)
role_de: Chef des Oberkommandos der Wehrmacht
role_ru: начальник Верховного командования вооружённых сил
role_fr: chef du Haut Commandement des forces armées
region_en: German armed-forces command and German-occupied Europe
region_pl: Oberkommando der Wehrmacht (OKW) and German armed forces
crime_tags_pl: Wojna napastnicza;Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa;Praca przymusowa
status_en: convicted at Nuremberg and executed in 1946
interpretation_en: Keitel gave criminal policy formal military effect through command documents. The profile does not attribute to him every battlefield crime, but neither treats signature and transmission as neutral administration.
postwar_en: The International Military Tribunal convicted Keitel on all four counts, rejecting superior orders as a defence for manifestly criminal conduct. It sentenced him to death and he was hanged on 16 October 1946.
limitations_en: The profile ties Keitel to documented command instruments and senior coordination, while maintaining the responsibility of field commanders and personnel who issued or executed further orders.

name: Joachim von Ribbentrop
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Reich Foreign Ministry
role_en: Reich Foreign Minister and diplomatic agent of German expansion
role_pl: Reich Minister of Foreign Affairs
role_de: Reichsaußenminister und diplomatischer Akteur deutscher Expansion
role_ru: рейхсминистр иностранных дел и дипломатический проводник германской экспансии
role_fr: ministre des Affaires étrangères du Reich et agent diplomatique de l’expansion allemande
region_en: German foreign policy and relations with occupied, allied and satellite states
region_pl: Foreign policy of the German Reich

status_en: convicted at Nuremberg and executed in 1946
interpretation_en: Ribbentrop's agency lay in diplomatic preparation, coercion and intergovernmental coordination. The profile distinguishes this role from military invasion and the police execution of deportations while showing how they formed one chain.
postwar_en: The International Military Tribunal convicted Ribbentrop on all four counts and sentenced him to death on 1 October 1946. He was hanged in Nuremberg on 16 October 1946.
limitations_en: The profile attributes only the documented policies and diplomacy of Ribbentrop's ministry, not every decision made independently by foreign governments, military commands or the SS.

name: Arthur Seyss-Inquart
organization_en: Reich government · occupation administration of the Netherlands
role_en: Reich Commissioner for the occupied Netherlands and former Austrian chancellor
role_pl: Reich Commissioner for the Occupied Netherlands
role_de: Reichskommissar für die besetzten Niederlande und ehemaliger österreichischer Bundeskanzler
role_ru: рейхскомиссар оккупированных Нидерландов и бывший канцлер Австрии
role_fr: commissaire du Reich pour les Pays-Bas occupés et ancien chancelier autrichien
region_en: Austria, the General Government and the occupied Netherlands
crime_tags_pl: Wojna napastnicza;Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Praca przymusowa
status_en: convicted at Nuremberg and executed in 1946
interpretation_en: Seyss-Inquart's responsibility changed with each office but consistently joined political annexation and civil administration to persecution. Operational police and SS agencies retained separate responsibility for arrests, transports and killings.
postwar_en: The International Military Tribunal convicted Seyss-Inquart of crimes against peace, war crimes and crimes against humanity, citing deportations, forced labour and hostage shootings. He was sentenced to death and hanged on 16 October 1946.
limitations_en: The profile distinguishes Seyss-Inquart's supreme civil authority from the operational chains of the German police, SS and collaborating offices in each territory.

name: Baldur von Schirach
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: NSDAP · Hitler Youth · Vienna Gau administration
role_en: Reich Youth Leader and later Gauleiter and Reich Governor of Vienna
role_pl: Reich Youth Leader of the NSDAP
role_de: Reichsjugendführer sowie später Gauleiter und Reichsstatthalter von Wien
role_ru: рейхсюгендфюрер, позднее гауляйтер и рейхсштатгальтер Вены
role_fr: chef de la jeunesse du Reich, puis Gauleiter et gouverneur du Reich à Vienne
crime_tags_pl: Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Propaganda i podżeganie
status_en: convicted at Nuremberg; served twenty years and died in 1974
interpretation_en: Von Schirach's responsibility had two forms: long-term ideological formation and later territorial participation in deportation. The profile does not presume that indoctrination mechanically determined every later act of Hitler Youth members.
postwar_en: The International Military Tribunal convicted von Schirach of crimes against humanity in connection with the deportation of Vienna's Jews and sentenced him to twenty years. He completed the sentence at Spandau, was released in 1966 and died in 1974.
limitations_en: The profile separates his documented authority over youth policy and Vienna from the conduct of other party, police and deportation agencies.

name: Otto Georg Thierack
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Reich Ministry of Justice · People's Court
role_en: Reich Minister of Justice and former president of the People's Court
role_pl: Reich Minister of Justice
role_de: Reichsminister der Justiz und ehemaliger Präsident des Volksgerichtshofs
role_ru: рейхсминистр юстиции и бывший председатель Народной судебной палаты
role_fr: ministre de la Justice du Reich et ancien président du Tribunal du peuple
region_en: judicial and penal system of the German Reich
region_pl: Nazi justice system in the German Reich
crime_tags_pl: Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa;Praca przymusowa
status_en: not tried; died by suicide in Allied custody in 1946
interpretation_en: Thierack used legal institutions to remove protection and deliver prisoners to the concentration-camp system. Judges, prosecutors, prison officials and SS personnel retained responsibility for their own decisions within that chain.
postwar_en: After internment by the Allies, Thierack died by poisoning on 26 October 1946 before the Nuremberg Justice Case could try him. His ministry colleagues and subordinates were prosecuted in that later proceeding.
limitations_en: The profile attributes to Thierack the policies and transfers he directed, not every sentence issued by every German court during his tenure.

name: Franz Stangl
organization_en: T4 programme · SS · Operation Reinhard
role_en: commandant of the Sobibór and Treblinka killing centres
role_pl: Commandant of Sobibor and Treblinka extermination camps
role_de: Kommandant der Tötungszentren Sobibór und Treblinka
role_ru: комендант центров убийств Собибор и Треблинка
role_fr: commandant des centres de mise à mort de Sobibór et de Treblinka
region_en: Sobibór and Treblinka in occupied Poland, later the Trieste area
crime_tags_pl: Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa
status_en: sentenced to life imprisonment; died in prison in 1971
interpretation_en: Stangl's command responsibility was operational: he organised staff, routines and throughput at two killing centres. This does not collapse the responsibility of Operation Reinhard superiors, transport authorities or individual camp personnel into his office.
postwar_en: Stangl escaped custody in 1948, travelled through Syria and settled in Brazil. Extradited to West Germany in 1967, he was convicted in Düsseldorf in December 1970 and sentenced to life imprisonment; he died in custody on 28 June 1971.
limitations_en: The profile follows Stangl's own command periods and does not attribute murders before or after them, or all crimes of Operation Reinhard, to him personally.

name: Amon Göth
organization_en: SS · Kraków-Płaszów concentration camp
role_en: commandant of the Kraków-Płaszów camp and SS officer in the Kraków district
role_pl: Commandant of Plaszow concentration camp
role_de: Kommandant des Lagers Kraków-Płaszów und SS-Offizier im Distrikt Krakau
role_ru: комендант лагеря Краков-Плашув и офицер СС в краковском дистрикте
role_fr: commandant du camp de Kraków-Płaszów et officier de la SS dans le district de Cracovie
region_en: Kraków, Płaszów, Tarnów and Szebnie in occupied Poland
region_pl: Kraków-Płaszów concentration camp and Kraków district
crime_tags_pl: Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa;Praca przymusowa
status_en: convicted in Poland and executed in 1946
interpretation_en: Göth combined camp command with field operations and personal violence. The profile confines attribution to documented locations and actions rather than treating him as responsible for every crime in the Kraków district.
postwar_en: US forces captured Göth and extradited him to Poland. The Supreme National Tribunal convicted him of war crimes and crimes against humanity, including participation in genocide, and he was hanged in Kraków on 13 September 1946.
limitations_en: Survivor testimony documents both command responsibility and personal killings; the profile does not extend those findings beyond the operations and camp under examination.

name: Josef Mengele
organization_en: SS medical service · Auschwitz-Birkenau
role_en: SS physician at Auschwitz-Birkenau who conducted selections and criminal experiments
role_pl: Physician at Auschwitz concentration camp
role_de: SS-Arzt in Auschwitz-Birkenau, der Selektionen und verbrecherische Experimente durchführte
role_ru: врач СС в Аушвице-Биркенау, проводивший селекции и преступные эксперименты
role_fr: médecin SS à Auschwitz-Birkenau, auteur de sélections et d’expériences criminelles
crime_tags_pl: Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa;Eksperymenty pseudomedyczne
status_en: never tried; escaped to South America and died in 1979
interpretation_en: Mengele's responsibility rests on his own selections and experiments within the SS camp system. The profile does not attribute to him every medical crime at Auschwitz or every death following selections made by other doctors.
postwar_en: Mengele was briefly held but not identified after the war, then escaped to Argentina, Paraguay and Brazil. He died after a stroke while swimming near São Paulo on 7 February 1979; forensic examination in 1985 and DNA analysis in 1992 confirmed the identity of his remains.
limitations_en: The profile relies on the documented Auschwitz role and survivor evidence and does not repeat unverified stories or assign experiments conducted by other camp physicians to Mengele.

name: Wilhelm Frick
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Reich Ministry of the Interior · Protectorate administration
role_en: Reich Minister of the Interior and later Reich Protector of Bohemia and Moravia
role_pl: Reich Minister of the Interior
role_de: Reichsminister des Innern und später Reichsprotektor in Böhmen und Mähren
role_ru: рейхсминистр внутренних дел, позднее рейхспротектор Богемии и Моравии
role_fr: ministre de l’Intérieur du Reich, puis protecteur du Reich en Bohême-Moravie
region_en: German domestic administration and the Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia
region_pl: Interior ministry and legal framework of the Nazi state
crime_tags_pl: Wojna napastnicza;Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa;Praca przymusowa;Akcja „T4”
status_en: convicted at Nuremberg and executed in 1946
interpretation_en: Frick's responsibility demonstrates that drafting law and organising administration were active parts of persecution. The profile distinguishes his formal authority in the Protectorate from Karl Hermann Frank's stronger operational control.
postwar_en: The International Military Tribunal convicted Frick of crimes against peace, war crimes and crimes against humanity. It sentenced him to death and he was hanged on 16 October 1946.
limitations_en: The profile treats lawmaking and ministerial administration as documented agency without assigning Frick every police action taken under the resulting legal order.

name: Alfred Jodl
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Armed Forces High Command, Operations Staff
role_en: chief of the Operations Staff of the Armed Forces High Command
role_pl: Chief of the Operations Staff of the OKW
role_de: Chef des Wehrmachtführungsstabs des Oberkommandos der Wehrmacht
role_ru: начальник оперативного штаба Верховного командования вооружённых сил
role_fr: chef de l’état-major des opérations du Haut Commandement des forces armées
region_en: German military planning and command across all theatres
crime_tags_pl: Wojna napastnicza;Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa
status_en: convicted at Nuremberg and executed in 1946
interpretation_en: Jodl's responsibility derived from military planning, drafting and transmission rather than direct participation in shootings. Field commands and personnel remained responsible for their own orders and executions.
postwar_en: The International Military Tribunal convicted Jodl on all four counts and sentenced him to death. He was hanged in Nuremberg on 16 October 1946; a later West German denazification ruling favourable to him was subsequently annulled.
limitations_en: The profile ties responsibility to surviving plans and signed directives and does not infer personal control over every operation conducted by the armed forces.

name: Julius Streicher
organization_en: NSDAP · Der Stürmer publishing organisation
role_en: publisher of Der Stürmer and former Gauleiter of Franconia
role_pl: Publisher of the antisemitic newspaper Der Stürmer
role_de: Herausgeber des Stürmer und ehemaliger Gauleiter von Franken
role_ru: издатель Der Stürmer и бывший гауляйтер Франконии
role_fr: éditeur de Der Stürmer et ancien Gauleiter de Franconie
crime_tags_pl: Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Propaganda i podżeganie
status_en: convicted at Nuremberg and executed in 1946
interpretation_en: Streicher did not command a killing unit, but sustained public incitement was his documented contribution to persecution and genocide. The profile does not claim a direct operational role he did not hold.
postwar_en: The International Military Tribunal acquitted Streicher of crimes against peace but convicted him of crimes against humanity for incitement to the murder of Jews. He was sentenced to death and hanged on 16 October 1946.
limitations_en: The profile distinguishes criminal incitement from command responsibility and avoids attributing individual deportation or killing operations to Streicher.

name: Karl Dönitz
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Kriegsmarine · Flensburg government
role_en: commander-in-chief of the Kriegsmarine and Hitler's successor as head of state
role_pl: Commander-in-Chief of the Kriegsmarine
role_de: Oberbefehlshaber der Kriegsmarine und Hitlers Nachfolger als Staatsoberhaupt
role_ru: главнокомандующий кригсмарине и преемник Гитлера в качестве главы государства
role_fr: commandant en chef de la Kriegsmarine et successeur d’Hitler comme chef de l’État
region_en: German naval warfare and the final Reich government
status_en: convicted at Nuremberg; served ten years and died in 1980
interpretation_en: Dönitz's profile concerns naval command, participation in aggressive war and leadership of the final government. It does not attribute crimes of other Wehrmacht branches or all acts at sea to him automatically.
postwar_en: The International Military Tribunal convicted Dönitz of crimes against peace and war crimes, acquitted him of conspiracy and sentenced him to ten years. He served the full term at Spandau, was released in 1956 and died in 1980.
limitations_en: The profile follows the offences and offices considered in the surviving record and does not expand his responsibility to unrelated land-war or SS crimes.

name: Walther Funk
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Reich Ministry of Economics · Reichsbank
role_en: Reich Economics Minister and president of the Reichsbank
role_pl: Reich Minister of Economics
role_de: Reichswirtschaftsminister und Präsident der Reichsbank
role_ru: рейхсминистр экономики и президент Рейхсбанка
role_fr: ministre de l’Économie du Reich et président de la Reichsbank
region_en: German central economic and banking administration
crime_tags_pl: Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Praca przymusowa
status_en: sentenced to life imprisonment; released in 1957 and died in 1960
interpretation_en: Funk's responsibility was financial and institutional rather than operational: the bank processed plunder and helped finance the regime. The profile distinguishes this from the SS seizure and killing operations that produced the assets.
postwar_en: The International Military Tribunal convicted Funk of crimes against peace, war crimes and crimes against humanity and sentenced him to life imprisonment. He was released from Spandau for health reasons in May 1957 and died in 1960.
limitations_en: The profile does not portray Funk as the principal architect of economic policy and limits attribution to the offices, knowledge and transactions documented in the record.

name: Oswald Pohl
tier_label_en: Designers of the machinery of destruction
organization_en: SS Economic and Administrative Main Office (WVHA)
role_en: chief of the WVHA and central administrator of SS enterprises and concentration camps
role_pl: Chief of the SS Economic and Administrative Main Office (WVHA)
role_de: Chef des WVHA und zentraler Verwalter der SS-Betriebe und Konzentrationslager
role_ru: начальник WVHA и центральный администратор предприятий СС и концентрационных лагерей
role_fr: chef du WVHA et administrateur central des entreprises de la SS et des camps de concentration
region_en: SS economic administration and concentration-camp system across occupied Europe
region_pl: SS Economic and Administrative Main Office (WVHA) and camp system
crime_tags_pl: Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa;Praca przymusowa
status_en: convicted in the Pohl Trial and executed in 1951
interpretation_en: Pohl joined camp custody, construction, labour allocation and accounting in one administrative centre. The profile preserves the distinct responsibility of Amtsgruppe D, camp commandants, industrial employers and killing personnel.
postwar_en: British forces arrested Pohl in May 1946. An American military tribunal convicted him of war crimes, crimes against humanity and SS membership and sentenced him to death; after review and rejected clemency petitions, he was hanged at Landsberg on 7 June 1951.
limitations_en: The profile attributes to Pohl the WVHA structures and directives he controlled, not every killing in every camp or every abuse by an industrial enterprise.

name: Richard Glücks
tier_label_en: Designers of the machinery of destruction
organization_en: Concentration Camps Inspectorate · WVHA Amtsgruppe D
role_en: Inspector of Concentration Camps and head of WVHA Amtsgruppe D
role_pl: Inspector of Concentration Camps in SS Main Office and WVHA
role_de: Inspekteur der Konzentrationslager und Leiter der Amtsgruppe D des WVHA
role_ru: инспектор концентрационных лагерей и начальник группы D WVHA
role_fr: inspecteur des camps de concentration et chef de l’Amtsgruppe D du WVHA
region_en: central administration of the SS concentration-camp system
region_pl: Inspection of concentration camps within WVHA
crime_tags_pl: Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa;Praca przymusowa
status_en: not tried; reportedly died by suicide in 1945
interpretation_en: Glücks was the central supervisory link between WVHA policy and individual camp commandants. His office did not replace the agency of Pohl, camp commanders, medical staff or employers.
postwar_en: Glücks never faced trial. Most accounts state that he died by cyanide poisoning at Flensburg-Mürwik on 10 May 1945; his superior Oswald Pohl and camp commandants including Rudolf Höss were later prosecuted.
limitations_en: The reported circumstances of Glücks's death are less firmly documented than his wartime office. The profile does not attribute all crimes of all concentration camps to a personal directive from him.

name: Christian Wirth
tier_label_en: Designers of the machinery of destruction
organization_en: T4 programme · Operation Reinhard
role_en: commandant of Bełżec and inspector of the Operation Reinhard killing centres
role_pl: Commandant of Belzec extermination camp and inspector of Aktion Reinhardt camps
role_de: Kommandant von Bełżec und Inspekteur der Tötungszentren der Aktion Reinhardt
role_ru: комендант Белжеца и инспектор центров убийств операции «Рейнхард»
role_fr: commandant de Bełżec et inspecteur des centres de mise à mort de l’opération Reinhard
region_en: T4 facilities, Bełżec, Sobibór and Treblinka, later the Trieste area
region_pl: Aktion Reinhardt extermination camps in General Government
crime_tags_pl: Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa;Akcja „T4”
status_en: not tried; killed in 1944
interpretation_en: Wirth transferred personnel, techniques and routines from T4 into Operation Reinhard and exercised direct operational supervision. The profile does not erase Globocnik's programme command or the agency of individual camp staffs.
postwar_en: Wirth never faced a court. Yugoslav partisans shot and killed him near Hrpelje–Kozina, close to Trieste, on 26 May 1944; postwar trials of Bełżec, Sobibór and Treblinka personnel documented his central role.
limitations_en: The profile distinguishes Wirth's T4 and Operation Reinhard posts from later crimes in the Trieste region and from acts of subordinates not shown to have been directed by him.

name: Friedrich Jeckeln
organization_en: Higher SS and Police Leadership · SS · Order Police
role_en: Higher SS and Police Leader in occupied Ukraine and Ostland
role_pl: Higher SS and Police Leader in the Baltic States and Ukraine
role_de: Höherer SS- und Polizeiführer in der besetzten Ukraine und im Ostland
role_ru: высший руководитель СС и полиции в оккупированной Украине и Остланде
role_fr: chef supérieur de la SS et de la police en Ukraine occupée et dans l’Ostland
region_en: occupied Ukraine, the Baltic states and Belarus
crime_tags_pl: Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa
status_en: convicted by a Soviet military tribunal and executed in 1946
interpretation_en: Jeckeln held territorial command and designed operational procedure rather than merely transmitting orders. Units and personnel that assembled, guarded and shot victims remained responsible for their own conduct.
postwar_en: Captured by Soviet forces in May 1945, Jeckeln was tried with other German commanders in Riga. The military tribunal sentenced him to death, and he was publicly hanged in Riga on 3 February 1946.
limitations_en: The profile follows Jeckeln's documented command regions and operations and does not attribute every Einsatzgruppe or police crime across the occupied Soviet territories to him.

name: Arthur Greiser
organization_en: Warthegau civil administration · NSDAP
role_en: Gauleiter and Reich Governor of the Warthegau
role_pl: Gauleiter and Reichsstatthalter of the Warthegau
role_de: Gauleiter und Reichsstatthalter des Warthegaus

role_fr: Gauleiter et gouverneur du Reich dans le Warthegau
region_en: Reichsgau Wartheland in annexed occupied Poland
crime_tags_pl: Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa;Praca przymusowa
status_en: convicted in Poland and executed in 1946
interpretation_en: Greiser's office supplied regional policy and civil-administrative power for Germanisation, exploitation and genocide. Police, SS, ghetto administrators and Kulmhof personnel carried distinct operational responsibility.
postwar_en: US forces captured Greiser and extradited him to Poland. The Supreme National Tribunal in Poznań convicted him of war crimes, crimes against humanity and participation in aggressive war; he was publicly hanged at Poznań Citadel on 21 July 1946.
limitations_en: The profile distinguishes Greiser's regional authority from Heinrich Himmler's, Wilhelm Koppe's and Herbert Lange's roles and does not make him the direct perpetrator of every Warthegau crime.

name: Erich Koch
organization_en: Reichskommissariat Ukraine · East Prussia Gau administration
role_en: Gauleiter of East Prussia and Reich Commissioner for Ukraine
role_pl: Gauleiter of East Prussia and Reich Commissioner for Ukraine
role_de: Gauleiter von Ostpreußen und Reichskommissar für die Ukraine
role_ru: гауляйтер Восточной Пруссии и рейхскомиссар Украины
role_fr: Gauleiter de Prusse-Orientale et commissaire du Reich pour l’Ukraine
region_en: East Prussia, the Białystok district and Reichskommissariat Ukraine
crime_tags_pl: Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa;Praca przymusowa
status_en: sentenced to death in Poland; sentence not carried out, died in prison in 1986
interpretation_en: Koch's responsibility was that of a territorial ruler whose civil apparatus enabled exploitation and police terror. Operational SS, police and military formations retained their own command chains.
postwar_en: British authorities arrested Koch in Hamburg in 1949 and extradited him to Poland. A Warsaw court sentenced him to death in 1959 for crimes against Polish civilians in East Prussia and the Białystok district; the sentence was not carried out and he died in Barczewo prison in 1986.
limitations_en: The Polish trial did not adjudicate Koch's crimes in Ukraine. The profile notes that gap and does not present allegations about hidden cultural property as established reasons for non-execution of the sentence.

name: Kurt Daluege
organization_en: Order Police · SS · Protectorate administration
role_en: chief of the Order Police and acting Reich Protector of Bohemia and Moravia
role_pl: Chief of the Order Police (Ordnungspolizei)
role_de: Chef der Ordnungspolizei und stellvertretender Reichsprotektor in Böhmen und Mähren

role_fr: chef de la police d’ordre et protecteur du Reich par intérim en Bohême-Moravie
region_en: German Order Police across occupied Europe and the Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia
region_pl: Order Police and Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia
crime_tags_pl: Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa
status_en: convicted in Czechoslovakia and executed in 1946
interpretation_en: Daluege linked central Order Police command to deployed battalions and, later, territorial reprisal policy. Local commanders and individual policemen remained accountable for their operational decisions.
postwar_en: British forces arrested Daluege and extradited him to Czechoslovakia in 1946. A Prague court convicted him of war crimes and crimes against humanity, including responsibility for Lidice, and he was hanged on 24 October 1946.
limitations_en: The profile distinguishes Daluege's central and Protectorate offices from the separate orders and conduct of specific police battalions outside his direct presence.

name: Theodor Eicke
tier_label_en: Designers of the machinery of destruction
organization_en: Concentration Camps Inspectorate · SS-Totenkopf formations
role_en: Inspector of Concentration Camps and commander of the SS Totenkopf Division
role_pl: Inspector of Concentration Camps and commander of the SS Totenkopf Division
role_de: Inspekteur der Konzentrationslager und Kommandeur der SS-Totenkopf-Division

region_en: Dachau, the SS camp system and later the European fronts
region_pl: Dachau concentration camp and SS-Totenkopf Division
crime_tags_pl: Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa;Praca przymusowa
status_en: not tried; killed in 1943
interpretation_en: Eicke designed institutions, discipline and personnel culture that enabled camp terror and carried it into a Waffen-SS formation. The profile does not attribute all later camp or divisional crimes to his personal order.
postwar_en: Eicke died on 26 February 1943 when his reconnaissance aircraft was shot down near Lozova in Ukraine. He therefore never faced trial; later proceedings against camp personnel and SS administrators documented the system he had shaped.
limitations_en: The profile separates Eicke's foundational role and command periods from crimes committed by later camp leadership or division personnel after his death.

name: Otto Ohlendorf
organization_en: Reich Main Security Office, Amt III · Einsatzgruppe D
role_en: commander of Einsatzgruppe D and head of the RSHA domestic SD office
role_pl: Commander of Einsatzgruppe D
role_de: Kommandeur der Einsatzgruppe D und Leiter des Inlands-SD-Amts im RSHA
role_ru: командир айнзацгруппы D и начальник внутреннего отдела СД РСХА
role_fr: commandant de l’Einsatzgruppe D et chef du service intérieur du SD au RSHA
region_en: Bessarabia, southern Ukraine, Crimea and the Caucasus
region_pl: Einsatzgruppe D in southern Ukraine and Crimea
crime_tags_pl: Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa
status_en: convicted in the Einsatzgruppen Trial and executed in 1951
interpretation_en: Ohlendorf exercised command over a mobile killing formation and standardised its procedures and reporting. Subordinate commanders, shooters and cooperating military or police units retained individual responsibility.
postwar_en: Arrested in May 1945, Ohlendorf first described the killing operations as a witness at the main Nuremberg trial. An American military tribunal then convicted him of war crimes, crimes against humanity and criminal-organisation membership; he was hanged at Landsberg on 7 June 1951.
limitations_en: The profile confines responsibility to Einsatzgruppe D during Ohlendorf's command and his own RSHA office, not all Einsatzgruppen or every crime in their operational area.

name: Paul Blobel
organization_en: Sonderkommando 4a, Einsatzgruppe C · Aktion 1005
role_en: commander of Sonderkommando 4a and organiser of Aktion 1005
role_pl: Commander of Sonderkommando 4a of Einsatzgruppe C

status_en: convicted in the Einsatzgruppen Trial and executed in 1951
interpretation_en: Blobel's responsibility covered both an operational killing unit and a later programme to destroy evidence. The profile retains the responsibility of superior RSHA authorities and participating local units.
postwar_en: An American military tribunal convicted Blobel in the Einsatzgruppen Trial of war crimes, crimes against humanity and criminal-organisation membership and sentenced him to death. He was hanged at Landsberg during the night of 7–8 June 1951.
limitations_en: Because Aktion 1005 destroyed evidence, exact totals remain difficult to establish. The profile avoids assigning Blobel every mass grave processed by units beyond the documented programme chain.

name: Oskar Dirlewanger
organization_en: SS special penal unit, later the Dirlewanger Brigade
role_en: commander of the SS penal formation known as the Dirlewanger unit
role_pl: Commander of the SS penal unit known as the Dirlewanger Brigade

crime_tags_pl: Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa
status_en: never tried; died in detention in June 1945 under uncertain circumstances
interpretation_en: Dirlewanger commanded a unit deliberately assembled and tolerated as an instrument of extreme terror. The profile distinguishes his command and personal participation from the individual crimes of identifiable subordinates.
postwar_en: French occupation authorities arrested Dirlewanger at Altshausen in early June 1945. He died in detention around 7 June; a 1960 exhumation confirmed his identity, but the precise date and circumstances of death remain disputed and he was never tried.
limitations_en: Accounts differ on whether guards fatally beat Dirlewanger and on the exact date of death. The profile reports this uncertainty rather than presenting one version as settled fact.

name: Hans Lammers
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Reich Chancellery
role_en: head of the Reich Chancellery and Hitler's senior legal-administrative intermediary
role_pl: Head of the Reich Chancellery
role_de: Leiter der Reichskanzlei und Hitlers ranghöchster juristisch-administrativer Vermittler
role_ru: глава Рейхсканцелярии и старший правовой и административный посредник Гитлера
role_fr: chef de la chancellerie du Reich et principal intermédiaire juridique et administratif d’Hitler
region_en: central government administration of the German Reich
crime_tags_pl: Wojna napastnicza;Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa;Praca przymusowa
status_en: convicted in the Ministries Trial; released early and died in 1962
interpretation_en: Lammers exercised power through selection, legal formulation and transmission at the centre of government. The profile does not treat every decree passing through the Chancellery as his original policy.
postwar_en: An American military tribunal convicted Lammers in the Ministries Trial and sentenced him to twenty years in 1949. The sentence was reduced to ten years and he was released in December 1951 after time credited from his 1945 arrest; he died in 1962.
limitations_en: The profile identifies documented chancellery functions and legal acts while preserving the separate responsibility of Hitler, initiating ministries and executing police or occupation bodies.

name: Hans Biebow
organization_en: German Łódź Ghetto Administration (Gettoverwaltung)
role_en: head of the German administration of the Łódź ghetto
role_pl: German administrator of the Łódź ghetto
role_de: Leiter der deutschen Verwaltung des Ghettos Łódź
role_ru: глава немецкой администрации Лодзинского гетто
role_fr: chef de l’administration allemande du ghetto de Łódź
crime_tags_pl: Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Praca przymusowa
status_en: convicted in Poland and executed in 1947
interpretation_en: Biebow linked municipal administration, economic exploitation and deportation. The Jewish Council and Chaim Rumkowski acted under German coercion and did not possess the sovereign authority held by Biebow's office.
postwar_en: Recognised by a survivor in Bremen, Biebow was arrested and extradited to Poland. The Łódź District Court convicted him of exploitation, starvation, plunder and participation in deportations; he was hanged in Łódź on 23 June 1947.
limitations_en: The profile distinguishes Biebow's German administrative power from the constrained acts of ghetto institutions and from the separate killing-centre command at Kulmhof.

name: Karl Gebhardt
organization_en: SS medical service · Hohenlychen clinic · Ravensbrück concentration camp
role_en: chief SS and police surgeon and organiser of experiments at Ravensbrück
role_pl: Chief surgeon in the SS and police and physician at Hohenlychen and Ravensbrück
role_de: oberster SS- und Polizeichirurg und Organisator der Experimente in Ravensbrück
role_ru: главный хирург СС и полиции и организатор экспериментов в Равенсбрюке
role_fr: chirurgien en chef de la SS et de la police et organisateur d’expériences à Ravensbrück
status_en: convicted in the Doctors' Trial and executed in 1948
interpretation_en: Gebhardt joined senior medical status, SS power and programme supervision in non-consensual human experimentation. Subordinate physicians and camp personnel remained responsible for their own participation.
postwar_en: The American military tribunal in the Doctors' Trial convicted Gebhardt of war crimes, crimes against humanity and SS membership. Sentenced to death on 20 August 1947, he was hanged at Landsberg on 2 June 1948.
limitations_en: The profile confines Gebhardt's responsibility to the programmes he organised or supervised and does not attribute every medical experiment in the concentration-camp system to him.

name: Carl Clauberg
organization_en: SS medical service · Auschwitz and Ravensbrück
role_en: gynaecologist who conducted mass-sterilisation experiments on prisoners
role_pl: SS physician conducting sterilization experiments at Auschwitz and Ravensbrück
role_de: Gynäkologe, der an Gefangenen Massensterilisierungsexperimente durchführte
role_ru: гинеколог, проводивший эксперименты по массовой стерилизации над заключёнными
role_fr: gynécologue ayant mené sur des détenues des expériences de stérilisation de masse
crime_tags_pl: Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa;Eksperymenty pseudomedyczne
status_en: convicted in the Soviet Union; released in 1955 and died in West German custody in 1957
interpretation_en: Clauberg used specialist authority and direct access to SS leadership to turn involuntary experimentation into a proposed population policy. The profile separates his programme from experiments by Mengele, Schumann and other doctors.
postwar_en: A Soviet court sentenced Clauberg to twenty-five years, but he returned to West Germany under the 1955 repatriation arrangements. Public protests led to a new arrest and preparation of a West German prosecution; he died in Kiel prison on 9 August 1957 before that trial began.
limitations_en: The profile distinguishes the completed Soviet proceeding from the West German case that never reached trial and avoids merging Clauberg's experiments with those of other Auschwitz physicians.

name: Ilse Koch
organization_en: Buchenwald concentration camp
role_en: wife of the Buchenwald commandant, convicted for abuses against prisoners
role_pl: Wife of the Buchenwald commandant implicated in abuses of prisoners
role_de: Ehefrau des Kommandanten von Buchenwald, wegen Misshandlungen von Gefangenen verurteilt
role_ru: жена коменданта Бухенвальда, осуждённая за злоупотребления в отношении заключённых
role_fr: épouse du commandant de Buchenwald, condamnée pour des sévices contre des détenus
status_en: sentenced to life imprisonment in West Germany; died by suicide in prison in 1967
interpretation_en: Koch's documented responsibility is individual abuse enabled by proximity to camp command, not formal control of Buchenwald. Her case also requires separating trial evidence from sensational postwar legend.
postwar_en: A US military court initially sentenced Koch to life imprisonment, but the sentence was reduced and she was released in 1949. West German authorities rearrested her and a court imposed a new life sentence in 1951; she died by suicide at Aichach prison in 1967.
limitations_en: Some highly publicised allegations about Koch were never proved. The profile retains only documented abuse and the findings of the two proceedings, without repeating sensational claims as fact.

name: Wilhelm Koppe
organization_en: Higher SS and Police Leadership in the Warthegau and General Government
role_en: Higher SS and Police Leader in the Warthegau and later the General Government
role_pl: Higher SS and Police Leader in the Warthegau and later the General Government
role_de: Höherer SS- und Polizeiführer im Warthegau und später im Generalgouvernement
role_ru: высший руководитель СС и полиции в Вартегау, позднее в Генерал-губернаторстве
role_fr: chef supérieur de la SS et de la police dans le Warthegau, puis dans le Gouvernement général
region_en: annexed western Poland and the General Government
crime_tags_pl: Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa;Praca przymusowa
status_en: prosecuted but not convicted; proceedings ended on medical grounds, died in 1975
interpretation_en: Koppe occupied the territorial SS and police command level linking Himmler's policy to regional units. Lange, Kulmhof personnel and district commanders retained direct responsibility for their operations.
postwar_en: Koppe lived in West Germany as Wilhelm Lohmann until his arrest in 1960. A Bonn trial opened in 1964 but was suspended and ultimately discontinued in 1966 on medical grounds; he was never convicted and died free in 1975.
limitations_en: Because the West German case ended without a verdict, the profile does not present allegations in that indictment as judicial findings and relies on documented office and command relationships.

name: Friedrich-Wilhelm Krüger
organization_en: Higher SS and Police Leadership in the General Government
role_en: Higher SS and Police Leader in the General Government
role_pl: Higher SS and Police Leader in the General Government
role_de: Höherer SS- und Polizeiführer im Generalgouvernement
role_ru: высший руководитель СС и полиции в Генерал-губернаторстве
role_fr: chef supérieur de la SS et de la police dans le Gouvernement général
crime_tags_pl: Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa;Praca przymusowa
status_en: not tried; died by suicide in 1945
interpretation_en: Krüger connected Himmler to district commanders including Globocnik and Stroop and coordinated the region-wide police system. Those commanders and their units retained responsibility for the particular deportations and killing operations they executed.
postwar_en: After leaving the General Government Krüger held Waffen-SS commands. He died by suicide in May 1945 and was never tried; occupation documents and later proceedings against other officials preserve evidence of his role.
limitations_en: The absence of a trial means there is no judgment delimiting his personal criminal liability. The profile therefore centres on surviving orders, offices and command relationships.

name: Albert Forster
organization_en: Danzig–West Prussia Gau administration · NSDAP
role_en: Gauleiter and Reich Governor of Danzig–West Prussia
role_pl: Gauleiter and Reichsstatthalter of Danzig-West Prussia
role_de: Gauleiter und Reichsstatthalter von Danzig–Westpreußen
role_ru: гауляйтер и рейхсштатгальтер Данцига—Западной Пруссии
role_fr: Gauleiter et gouverneur du Reich de Dantzig–Prusse-Occidentale
region_en: Free City of Danzig and occupied Polish Pomerania
crime_tags_pl: Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa;Praca przymusowa
status_en: convicted in Poland and executed in 1952
interpretation_en: Forster's responsibility was territorial and political: incitement, policy and control of the Gau administration. SS, police and Selbstschutz leaders remained directly responsible for organising and carrying out specific massacres.
postwar_en: British forces captured Forster and extradited him to Poland. The Supreme National Tribunal in Gdańsk convicted him on 29 April 1948 of war crimes and crimes against humanity; after delayed execution and refusal of clemency, he was hanged in Warsaw on 28 February 1952.
limitations_en: The profile distinguishes Forster's regional authority and incitement from the operational responsibility of Richard Hildebrandt, Selbstschutz leaders and individual killing units.

name: Franz Ziereis
organization_en: Mauthausen concentration-camp complex · SS
role_en: commandant of the Mauthausen concentration-camp complex
role_pl: Commandant of Mauthausen concentration camp
role_de: Kommandant des Konzentrationslagerkomplexes Mauthausen
role_ru: комендант комплекса концентрационных лагерей Маутхаузен
role_fr: commandant du complexe concentrationnaire de Mauthausen
region_en: Mauthausen, Gusen and the subcamp network in the Danube region
crime_tags_pl: Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości;Zagłada Żydów;Inne ludobójstwa;Praca przymusowa
status_en: not tried; fatally shot during capture in May 1945
interpretation_en: Ziereis implemented central SS and WVHA policy through daily camp command. The profile preserves the separate authority of WVHA superiors, subcamp commanders, guards and industrial beneficiaries.
postwar_en: US soldiers found Ziereis in Upper Austria on 23 May 1945 and shot him when he attempted to escape. He was questioned while mortally wounded and died shortly afterwards, on 24 or 25 May according to differing sources, before any trial.
limitations_en: Sources differ by one day on the date of death. His last statement is important evidence but must be read alongside survivor testimony and records rather than treated as a complete account.

name: Robert Ley
organization_en: NSDAP · German Labour Front (DAF)
role_en: NSDAP Reichsleiter and head of the German Labour Front
role_pl: Reichsleiter NSDAP, szef Niemieckiego Frontu Pracy (DAF) kierujący eksploatacją milionów robotników przymusowych
role_de: Reichsleiter der NSDAP und Leiter der Deutschen Arbeitsfront
role_ru: рейхсляйтер НСДАП и руководитель Германского трудового фронта
role_fr: Reichsleiter du NSDAP et chef du Front allemand du travail
region_en: German Reich and the forced-labour system drawing workers from occupied Europe
status_en: died by suicide in Allied custody in 1945 before trial
interpretation_en: Ley's responsibility arose from his leadership of an organisation that linked party control of labour with wartime exploitation and from his antisemitic propaganda. This does not make him personally responsible for every abuse committed across the entire forced-labour system.
postwar_en: US forces captured Ley in May 1945. He was indicted at Nuremberg but killed himself in his cell during the night of 24–25 October 1945, before the trial began, and therefore received no judgment.
limitations_en: The Polish profile notes a one-day variation in accounts of his death because it occurred overnight. His institutional responsibility for forced labour must be distinguished from the acts of employers, ministries, police units and camp administrations elsewhere in the system.

name: Gottlob Berger
organization_en: SS Main Office · Waffen-SS · prisoner-of-war administration
role_en: chief of the SS Main Office and organiser of Waffen-SS recruitment
role_pl: Szef Głównego Urzędu SS (SS-Hauptamt), odpowiedzialny za rekrutację do Waffen-SS i nadzór nad jeńcami wojennymi
role_de: Chef des SS-Hauptamts und Organisator der Rekrutierung für die Waffen-SS
role_ru: руководитель Главного управления СС и организатор набора в войска СС
role_fr: chef de l’Office central SS et organisateur du recrutement de la Waffen-SS
status_en: convicted in 1949; sentence reduced and released in 1951
interpretation_en: Berger connected central SS administration, personnel policy and protection of violent formations with operational crimes. His position supports responsibility for decisions and institutional support, but not automatic attribution of every crime committed by every Waffen-SS formation to him.
postwar_en: An American tribunal sentenced Berger to twenty-five years in April 1949. The sentence was reduced to ten years and he was released in 1951; he died a free man in 1975.
limitations_en: The Polish profile records uncertainty over whether he assumed full leadership of the SS Main Office in late 1939 or in 1940. His responsibility spans several institutions, so the crimes of subordinate formations must be tied to documented orders, protection or supervision rather than treated as a personal total.

name: Richard Walther Darré
organization_en: Reich Ministry of Food and Agriculture · SS Race and Settlement Main Office (RuSHA) · NSDAP
role_en: Reich agriculture minister, former head of RuSHA and ideologue of 'Blood and Soil'
role_pl: Minister Żywności i Rolnictwa Rzeszy, szef Głównego Urzędu Rasowo-Osadniczego SS (RuSHA), ideolog „Krwi i Gleby”
role_de: Reichsminister für Ernährung und Landwirtschaft, ehemaliger Leiter des RuSHA und Ideologe von „Blut und Boden“
role_ru: рейхсминистр сельского хозяйства, бывший руководитель RuSHA и идеолог доктрины «Кровь и почва»
role_fr: ministre de l’Agriculture du Reich, ancien chef du RuSHA et idéologue du « Sang et Sol »
region_en: German Reich and plans for occupied Eastern Europe
status_en: convicted in 1949; released in 1950
interpretation_en: Darré's responsibility lies primarily in supplying racial-settlement policy with ideological doctrine and administrative tools later used for dispossession, selection and Germanisation. He did not command the field units that carried out every expulsion or killing associated with those policies.
postwar_en: Darré was tried in the Ministries Trial, acquitted of crimes against peace but convicted on three other counts in April 1949. He received seven years, was released in 1950 and died in 1953.
limitations_en: Darré formally remained agriculture minister beyond the point at which he lost effective influence in 1942, and he had ceased leading RuSHA in 1938. The profile therefore separates the influence of institutions and doctrines he created from later operations directed by other officials.

name: Alois Brunner
tier_label_en: Designers of the machinery of destruction
organization_en: RSHA Section IV B4 · SS · Vienna Central Office for Jewish Emigration · Drancy transit camp
role_en: Eichmann associate who organised deportations and commanded the Drancy transit camp
role_pl: „Judenreferent” / komendant Drancy; organizator deportacji z Wiednia, Salonik, Francji i Słowacji
role_de: Eichmann-Mitarbeiter, der Deportationen organisierte und das Durchgangslager Drancy befehligte
role_ru: соратник Эйхмана, организовывавший депортации и командовавший транзитным лагерем Дранси
role_fr: collaborateur d’Eichmann qui organisa des déportations et commanda le camp de transit de Drancy
status_en: convicted in absentia but never extradited or imprisoned
interpretation_en: Brunner's documented responsibility is operational as well as administrative: he was sent to accelerate deportations and controlled transit sites and transport arrangements. The profile does not collapse the work of all local police, railway and camp personnel involved in those deportations into his personal actions.
postwar_en: Brunner escaped through Egypt to Syria in 1954 under the name Georg Fischer. Repeated extradition efforts failed, and he died in Damascus without serving either French sentence.
limitations_en: The year of Brunner's death remains disputed: later investigations point to December 2001, while other reports placed it as late as 2010. The figures for deportations in the four countries overlap with the responsibility of Eichmann's office and local implementing authorities.

name: Dieter Wisliceny
tier_label_en: Designers of the machinery of destruction
organization_en: RSHA Section IV B4 · SS · German diplomatic missions
role_en: Eichmann’s deputy and adviser who organised anti-Jewish policy and deportations
role_pl: Zastępca Eichmanna; organizator deportacji m.in. na Słowacji i Węgrzech
role_de: Eichmanns Stellvertreter und Berater, der antijüdische Politik und Deportationen organisierte
role_ru: заместитель Эйхмана и советник, организовывавший антиеврейскую политику и депортации
role_fr: adjoint d’Eichmann et conseiller ayant organisé la politique antijuive et les déportations
status_en: convicted in Czechoslovakia and executed in 1948
interpretation_en: Wisliceny translated RSHA policy into legislation, isolation and transport operations in several states. His responsibility concerns the deportation mechanisms he helped organise; it should not be stated as sole responsibility for every arrest or killing within those national operations.
postwar_en: Wisliceny became an important prosecution witness at the International Military Tribunal, describing Eichmann's office and the deportation system. A Czechoslovak court sentenced him to death on 27 February 1948, and he was hanged on 4 May 1948.
limitations_en: Published totals for the Slovak deportations vary, and the Polish profile distinguishes the date of sentence from the later execution date. His work formed part of wider operations involving German diplomats, RSHA personnel, local governments and police.

name: Theodor Dannecker
tier_label_en: Designers of the machinery of destruction
organization_en: RSHA Section IV B4 · SS · Security Service (SD)
role_en: Eichmann specialist who coordinated deportations in France, Bulgaria, Italy and Hungary
role_pl: Specjalista Eichmanna ds. deportacji; Judenreferent we Francji, potem w Bułgarii, Italii i na Węgrzech
role_de: Eichmann-Spezialist, der Deportationen in Frankreich, Bulgarien, Italien und Ungarn koordinierte
role_ru: специалист Эйхмана, координировавший депортации во Франции, Болгарии, Италии и Венгрии
role_fr: spécialiste d’Eichmann qui coordonna les déportations en France, en Bulgarie, en Italie et en Hongrie
status_en: died by suicide in American custody in 1945 before trial
interpretation_en: Dannecker was a travelling RSHA specialist who converted central instructions into arrest lists, cooperation agreements and transport plans. His role was substantial, but deportations in each country also depended on other German offices and local authorities.
postwar_en: Dannecker was held by the United States Army at Bad Tölz in Bavaria. He hanged himself in his cell on 10 December 1945 and was never judicially tried.
limitations_en: The Polish profile treats victim figures as orders of magnitude because Dannecker was one participant in broader national deportation systems, particularly in Hungary. His responsibility must be tied to the operations and periods documented for his postings.

name: Franz Novak
tier_label_en: Designers of the machinery of destruction
organization_en: RSHA Section IV B4 · SS · Deutsche Reichsbahn liaison
role_en: transport specialist in Eichmann's department who scheduled deportation trains
role_pl: „Fahrdienstleiter des Todes” — ekspert od kolejowych rozkładów deportacji do obozów
role_de: Transportspezialist in Eichmanns Referat, der Deportationszüge disponierte
role_ru: транспортный специалист отдела Эйхмана, составлявший расписания депортационных поездов
role_fr: spécialiste des transports au sein du service d’Eichmann, chargé de programmer les trains de déportation
region_en: German Reich, Austria, Hungary and occupied Europe
region_pl: Austria; Europa okupowana; deportacje do Auschwitz i innych obozów
status_en: received a final seven-year sentence in Austria and was released
