interpretation_en: Novak supplied the railway logistics that connected arrest and concentration with ghettos, camps and killing centres. His administrative function was indispensable, but transport totals generated by the whole department cannot be treated as an individually separable victim count.
postwar_en: Novak was arrested in Vienna in 1961. Austrian courts tried him repeatedly in 1964, 1966, 1969 and 1972; the final seven-year sentence was largely treated as already served and he later received clemency. He died free in 1983.
limitations_en: The sequence and legal basis of Novak's several Austrian judgments is complex because earlier verdicts were repeatedly set aside. Estimates associated with all transports handled by Eichmann's department are broader than the conduct that can be attributed specifically to Novak.

name: Gerhard Klopfer
tier_label_en: Designers of the machinery of destruction
organization_en: NSDAP Party Chancellery · SS
role_en: senior Party Chancellery official and participant in the Wannsee Conference
role_pl: Dyrektor w Kancelarii Partii NSDAP (podwładny Bormanna), uczestnik konferencji w Wannsee
role_de: hoher Beamter der Parteikanzlei und Teilnehmer der Wannsee-Konferenz
role_ru: высокопоставленный чиновник Партийной канцелярии и участник Ванзейской конференции
role_fr: haut responsable de la Chancellerie du parti et participant à la conférence de Wannsee
status_en: investigation discontinued; only minor denazification sanctions
interpretation_en: Klopfer represented the party bureaucracy in inter-agency coordination of persecution and expropriation. Attendance at Wannsee and his office establish participation in the administrative chain, but do not justify attributing every subsequent deportation or murder to him personally.
postwar_en: Klopfer gave evidence in the Ministries Trial, while proceedings against him were discontinued for lack of evidence. A denazification court imposed a 2,000-mark fine and three years of supervision in 1949; he later resumed legal practice and died in 1987.
limitations_en: The evidence establishes his office, attendance and coordinating function more clearly than any single operational order. The scale of the Holocaust must not be converted into a personal victim total for a coordinating official.

name: Wilhelm Stuckart
tier_label_en: Designers of the machinery of destruction
organization_en: Reich Ministry of the Interior · SS
organization_pl: Reich Ministry of the Interior / SS
role_en: state secretary, co-author of the Nuremberg Laws and participant in the Wannsee Conference
role_pl: Staatssekretär w Reichsministerium des Innern; współautor ustaw norymberskich, uczestnik Wannsee
role_de: Staatssekretär, Mitverfasser der Nürnberger Gesetze und Teilnehmer der Wannsee-Konferenz
role_ru: статс-секретарь, соавтор Нюрнбергских законов и участник Ванзейской конференции
role_fr: secrétaire d’État, coauteur des lois de Nuremberg et participant à la conférence de Wannsee
region_en: German Reich and the racial-law apparatus in annexed and occupied territories
status_en: convicted in the Ministries Trial and released after time served
interpretation_en: Stuckart's principal agency lay in creating and administering the legal infrastructure of exclusion, dispossession and deportation. That role made persecution enforceable across many offices, but it is distinct from direct command of field arrests and killings.
crime_profile_pl: wymiar „sprawiedliwości” / legalna infrastruktura prześladowań i wywłaszczeń
postwar_en: An American tribunal sentenced Stuckart in April 1949, but the term was almost entirely credited as pretrial detention and he was soon released. He died in a road accident near Hanover in 1953.
limitations_en: Sources differ in how they describe the exact sentence because it was effectively treated as time served. The profile distinguishes legal and institutional responsibility from proof of direct participation in individual deportations or murders.

name: Albert Ganzenmüller
tier_label_en: Designers of the machinery of destruction
organization_en: Reich Ministry of Transport · Deutsche Reichsbahn
role_en: state secretary and deputy director-general of the German state railway
role_pl: Podsekretarz stanu w Ministerstwie Transportu i zastępca dyrektora kolei Deutsche Reichsbahn
role_de: Staatssekretär und stellvertretender Generaldirektor der Deutschen Reichsbahn
role_ru: статс-секретарь и заместитель генерального директора германских государственных железных дорог
role_fr: secrétaire d’État et directeur général adjoint des chemins de fer allemands
region_en: German Reich and railway routes across occupied Europe
status_en: charged in West Germany, but proceedings were discontinued without judgment
interpretation_en: Ganzenmüller linked SS deportation demands with the technical capacity of the state railway. His responsibility concerns executive control and documented coordination of transports, while arrests, loading, guarding and killing were performed by other parts of the apparatus.
postwar_en: Ganzenmüller escaped from Allied detention to Argentina in 1945 and returned to West Germany in 1955. His trial opened in April 1973 but was halted after a heart attack; he was declared unfit and the case ended in 1977. He died free in 1996.
limitations_en: Estimates for people carried by the railway system during his tenure vary widely and overlap with the responsibility of transport planners, railway divisions, police and camp authorities. The surviving letter is strong evidence of knowledge and coordination, not a basis for assigning every deportation train to him personally.

name: Bruno Streckenbach
tier_label_en: Designers of the machinery of destruction
organization_en: RSHA Office I · Security Police and SD · Einsatzgruppe I
role_en: head of RSHA personnel administration and organiser of Einsatzgruppen staffing and training
role_pl: Szef Amt I RSHA (kadry); organizował i szkolił personel Einsatzgruppen przed Barbarossą
role_de: Leiter der RSHA-Personalverwaltung und Organisator der Besetzung und Schulung der Einsatzgruppen
role_ru: руководитель кадрового управления РСХА и организатор комплектования и подготовки айнзацгрупп
role_fr: chef de l’administration du personnel du RSHA et organisateur de l’affectation et de la formation des Einsatzgruppen
region_en: Berlin, occupied Poland and the occupied Soviet territories
status_en: convicted by a Soviet court; later prosecution in West Germany was suspended
interpretation_en: Streckenbach combined field command in occupied Poland with central authority over the personnel who staffed the Security Police and the Einsatzgruppen. His organisational agency is documented, but crimes committed by every officer trained or appointed through RSHA cannot simply be treated as his individual acts.
postwar_en: The Soviet Union held Streckenbach after his capture in May 1945 and sentenced him to twenty-five years in 1952. He was repatriated in 1955. The later West German case was indefinitely suspended in 1974, and he died at home in Hamburg in 1977 without trial for the Holocaust and AB Action allegations.
limitations_en: The profile notes minor uncertainty over the dates of his early party and SS membership and treats estimates connected with the mass crimes of Einsatzgruppen as orders of magnitude. His individual responsibility must be established through staffing, instruction, command and specific operations rather than the entire record of all subordinate units.

name: Gerhard Maurer
tier_label_en: Designers of the machinery of destruction
organization_en: SS Economic and Administrative Main Office (WVHA) · Concentration Camp Inspectorate
role_en: head of WVHA Office D II responsible for allocating concentration-camp prisoner labour
role_pl: Zastępca szefa WVHA Amtsgruppe D (Inspektorat Obozów); szef Amt D II — alokacja pracy niewolniczej więźniów
role_de: Leiter des WVHA-Amts D II für die Zuweisung von Konzentrationslagerhäftlingen zur Zwangsarbeit
role_ru: руководитель отдела D II WVHA, отвечавший за распределение труда заключённых концентрационных лагерей
role_fr: chef du bureau D II du WVHA, responsable de l’affectation au travail des détenus des camps de concentration
region_en: Oranienburg and the concentration-camp system across occupied Europe
status_en: convicted in Poland and executed in 1953
interpretation_en: Maurer connected the concentration-camp inspectorate with industrial demand for slave labour and the lethal distinction between prisoners considered usable and unusable. His responsibility overlaps with WVHA leaders, camp commandants and employers and should not absorb all crimes committed throughout the camp system.
postwar_en: Maurer was questioned as a witness in connection with the Pohl Trial and extradited to Poland in 1948. Tried in Warsaw in 1951, he was sentenced to death and executed in Kraków on 2 April 1953.
limitations_en: The scale of deaths associated with slave labour is systemic and cannot be assigned to one administrator as a discrete total. The profile therefore limits its claim to Maurer's documented authority over labour allocation, directives, transfers and selections.

name: Gustav Richter
tier_label_en: Designers of the machinery of destruction
organization_en: RSHA Section IV B4 · SS · German legation in Bucharest
role_en: German adviser on Jewish affairs in Romania
role_pl: „Judenberater” w Bukareszcie; wysłannik Eichmanna ds. deportacji i „aryzacji”
role_de: deutscher Berater für Judenfragen in Rumänien
role_ru: германский советник по еврейским делам в Румынии
role_fr: conseiller allemand aux affaires juives en Roumanie
status_en: convicted in West Germany in 1982 and given a four-year sentence
interpretation_en: Richter acted as the administrative and diplomatic link between the RSHA and the Antonescu government. The deportation plan he pressed was not implemented, so intent, preparation and other persecution measures must be distinguished from killings that actually occurred under separate Romanian and German commands.
postwar_en: Soviet forces captured Richter after Romania changed sides in August 1944, and a Soviet court convicted him in 1951. Released to West Germany in 1955, he was not convicted there until 1982; he died free in 1997.
limitations_en: Sources place the number covered by the proposed deportation plan at roughly 272,000 to 300,000. Because the plan was stopped in 1942, that number describes intended deportation rather than a personal victim count; Richter's role in wider Romanian persecution also overlapped with Romanian authorities.

name: Hermann Höfle
tier_label_en: Designers of the machinery of destruction
organization_en: SS · staff of the SS and Police Leader in Lublin · Operation Reinhard
role_en: chief of staff for Operation Reinhard and coordinator of deportation logistics
role_pl: Szef sztabu Akcji Reinhardt (Aktion Reinhard), koordynator logistyki transportów do obozów śmierci w Polsce
role_de: Stabschef der Aktion Reinhardt und Koordinator der Deportationslogistik
role_ru: начальник штаба операции «Райнхард» и координатор логистики депортаций
role_fr: chef d’état-major de l’opération Reinhard et coordinateur de la logistique des déportations
region_en: General Government, especially the Lublin and Warsaw districts
status_en: died by suicide in Austrian custody in 1962 before trial
interpretation_en: Höfle converted extermination policy into schedules, personnel assignments and coordinated transports. His telegram documents his central knowledge and role, but it records the output of the whole Operation Reinhard apparatus rather than killings personally carried out by him.
postwar_en: Höfle was detained with Globocnik in 1945 but released and later lived in Salzburg. Austrian authorities arrested him in January 1961; he hanged himself in a Vienna prison cell on 21 August 1962 before trial.
limitations_en: Deportation estimates from the Warsaw ghetto vary, and the total in Höfle's telegram is a report for the whole operation. His responsibility is clearest for documented coordination, orders and logistics and should not replace the separate responsibility of camp, police, railway and local commanders.

name: Rolf Günther
tier_label_en: Designers of the machinery of destruction
organization_en: RSHA Section IV B4 · SS · Vienna Central Office for Jewish Emigration
role_en: Eichmann's permanent deputy in RSHA Section IV B4
role_pl: Stały zastępca Eichmanna w IV B4; nadzorował i podpisywał decyzje deportacyjne
role_de: ständiger Stellvertreter Eichmanns im RSHA-Referat IV B4
role_ru: постоянный заместитель Эйхмана в отделе IV B4 РСХА
role_fr: adjoint permanent d’Eichmann au sein de la section IV B4 du RSHA
region_en: Berlin, Theresienstadt, Greece and occupied Europe
status_en: reported to have died by suicide in American custody in 1945
interpretation_en: Günther occupied a central position in the office that coordinated deportations from across occupied Europe and also took part in specific operations. The total activity of IV B4 cannot, however, be converted into an individual count or attributed solely to Eichmann's deputy.
postwar_en: Günther was interned by United States forces at Ebensee and was reported to have killed himself with poison in August 1945. He was never tried or convicted.
limitations_en: His death was attested by another RSHA official, but later rumours claimed he had escaped; the Polish profile treats suicide at Ebensee as the best-supported account while retaining the uncertainty. His departmental position establishes shared responsibility, not sole authorship of all IV B4 deportations.

name: Wolfram Sievers
tier_label_en: Designers of the machinery of destruction
organization_en: SS Ahnenerbe · Institute for Military Scientific Research
role_en: managing director of the Ahnenerbe and administrator of criminal human experiments
role_pl: Dyrektor administracyjny Ahnenerbe SS, szef Instytutu Wojskowo-Naukowych Badań Celowych
role_de: Geschäftsführer des Ahnenerbe und Verwalter verbrecherischer Menschenversuche
role_ru: управляющий директор «Аненербе» и администратор преступных опытов над людьми
role_fr: directeur administratif de l’Ahnenerbe et administrateur d’expériences criminelles sur des êtres humains
status_en: convicted in the Doctors' Trial and executed in 1948
interpretation_en: Sievers was an administrator rather than a physician, but his logistical decisions made lethal research projects possible. His responsibility concerns the programmes he supplied and coordinated, not every experiment performed under every Ahnenerbe-associated researcher.
postwar_en: An American military tribunal sentenced Sievers to death on 20 August 1947. He was hanged at Landsberg prison on 2 June 1948.
limitations_en: Sources give either 86 or 112 for the anatomical-collection victims depending on which selections and transports are counted. Broader estimates for experimental programmes remain orders of magnitude and should not be treated as a personal tally.

name: Erich von dem Bach-Zelewski
organization_en: SS and Police · anti-partisan command formations
role_en: senior SS commander for anti-partisan warfare and commander of forces suppressing the Warsaw Uprising
role_pl: Szef formacji do walki z partyzantką (Bandenkampf) na Wschodzie, dowódca sił tłumiących Powstanie Warszawskie
role_de: hoher SS-Führer für die Partisanenbekämpfung und Befehlshaber der bei der Niederschlagung des Warschauer Aufstands eingesetzten Kräfte
role_ru: старший командир СС по борьбе с партизанами и командующий силами, подавлявшими Варшавское восстание
role_fr: haut commandant de la SS chargé de la lutte contre les partisans et commandant des forces réprimant l’insurrection de Varsovie
status_en: imprisoned for prewar murders but never tried for his principal wartime crimes
interpretation_en: Bach-Zelewski held command authority over a system in which anti-partisan language served as a framework for mass violence against civilians. Responsibility for command and operational policy must still be distinguished from the individual acts of subordinate formations and commanders.
postwar_en: Bach-Zelewski testified for the prosecution at Nuremberg and was not extradited for crimes in the East or Warsaw. West German courts later convicted him for prewar political murders, including a 1962 life sentence; he died in custody in 1972.
limitations_en: Estimates differ greatly according to whether they cover individual massacres or all operations under his command. His later convictions did not judicially determine responsibility for the wartime crimes described here.

name: Herbert Backe
organization_en: Reich Ministry of Food and Agriculture · SS
role_en: agricultural minister and principal planner of the Hunger Plan
role_pl: Minister Żywności i Rolnictwa Rzeszy, twórca i realizator ludobójczego Hungerplan (Planu Głodu)
role_de: Landwirtschaftsminister und wichtigster Planer des Hungerplans
role_ru: министр сельского хозяйства и главный разработчик плана голода
role_fr: ministre de l’Agriculture et principal concepteur du plan de la Faim
region_en: Occupied Soviet territories and Eastern Europe
status_en: died by suicide in Nuremberg custody in 1947 before trial
interpretation_en: Backe used food allocation as an instrument of occupation and planned mass death rather than merely failing to prevent wartime shortages. The actual deaths resulted through a wider military and civilian occupation apparatus, so each famine death cannot be assigned to him alone.
postwar_en: Allied authorities detained Backe for a planned Ministries Trial. On 6 April 1947, before he could be tried, he hanged himself in his Nuremberg cell.
limitations_en: The Hunger Plan projected deaths on a vastly greater scale than can be isolated as its realised result, and historians' estimates for starvation deaths vary. No judgment was issued against Backe because he died before trial.

name: Viktor Brack
organization_en: Chancellery of the Führer · SS · Aktion T4
role_en: head of Office II in the Führer Chancellery and organiser of Aktion T4
role_pl: Szef urzędu w Kanzlei des Führers; współorganizator Aktion T4 i sterylizacji przymusowej
role_de: Leiter des Amtes II in der Kanzlei des Führers und Organisator der Aktion T4
role_ru: руководитель отдела II Канцелярии фюрера и организатор акции T4
role_fr: chef du bureau II de la Chancellerie du Führer et organisateur de l’Aktion T4
region_en: German Reich and the Aktion T4 killing-centre network
status_en: convicted in the Doctors' Trial and executed in 1948
interpretation_en: Brack's administrative authority connected the Führer Chancellery to the implementation of mass killing and to the later transfer of personnel and techniques. That connection does not make him the sole author of all crimes later committed by former T4 personnel.
crime_profile_pl: „T4”, eksperymenty, współudział w logistycznym transferze metod zabijania
postwar_en: The Doctors' Trial convicted Brack of war crimes, crimes against humanity and membership in the criminal SS and sentenced him to death on 20 August 1947. He was hanged at Landsberg on 2 June 1948.
limitations_en: Victim estimates differ between the centralised T4 phase and all later phases of the so-called euthanasia killings. The profile therefore identifies Brack's documented organisational remit without assigning all subsequent programme deaths to him individually.

name: Hanns Albin Rauter
organization_en: Higher SS and Police Leader in the Netherlands · Security Police · Order Police
role_en: Higher SS and Police Leader and General Commissioner for Security in the occupied Netherlands
role_pl: HSSPF / General Commissioner for Security w okupowanej Holandii
role_de: Höherer SS- und Polizeiführer und Generalkommissar für das Sicherheitswesen in den besetzten Niederlanden
role_ru: высший руководитель СС и полиции и генеральный комиссар по безопасности в оккупированных Нидерландах
role_fr: chef supérieur de la SS et de la police et commissaire général à la Sécurité dans les Pays-Bas occupés
status_en: convicted in the Netherlands and executed in 1949
interpretation_en: Rauter's offices united the police institutions that arrested, detained and deported people and carried out reprisals. His command responsibility is well documented, while individual crimes also involved German subordinate services, the occupation administration and Dutch collaborators.
postwar_en: Dutch courts convicted Rauter and upheld his death sentence on appeal in January 1949. He was executed by firing squad near Scheveningen on 24 March 1949.
limitations_en: Sources give slightly different totals for Jews deported from the Netherlands, generally around 102,000 to 110,000. Those deportations were a coordinated process, so Rauter's high command role must be described alongside the distinct actions of transit-camp, railway, police and civil authorities.

name: Karl Oberg
organization_en: Higher SS and Police Leader in France · Gestapo · Security Police and SD
role_en: Higher SS and Police Leader in occupied France
role_pl: Wyższy Dowódca SS i Policji (HSSPF) we Francji (znany jako „Rzeźnik Paryża”)
role_de: Höherer SS- und Polizeiführer im besetzten Frankreich
role_ru: высший руководитель СС и полиции в оккупированной Франции
role_fr: chef supérieur de la SS et de la police dans la France occupée
status_en: sentenced to death in France, later pardoned and released in 1962
interpretation_en: Oberg directed the German police system that combined deportation policy, hostage executions and repression of resistance with collaboration by French agencies. His command role does not erase the separate agency of his deputy, local offices or Vichy police personnel.
postwar_en: American forces arrested Oberg in 1945 and transferred him to France. Sentenced to death in October 1954, he later received successive commutations and was pardoned by President Charles de Gaulle; he was released on 28 November 1962 and died in 1965.
limitations_en: Sources distinguish deportations during Oberg's tenure from the larger total deported from France over the whole occupation. The profile therefore describes command and negotiated cooperation rather than assigning to Oberg every act committed by German and French police.

name: Edmund Veesenmayer
organization_en: Reich Foreign Office · SS · plenipotentiary in Hungary
role_en: Reich plenipotentiary and minister in occupied Hungary
role_pl: Minister i poseł nadzwyczajny Rzeszy na Węgrzech, koordynator deportacji węgierskich Żydów
role_de: Reichsbevollmächtigter und Gesandter im besetzten Ungarn
role_ru: рейхсуполномоченный и министр в оккупированной Венгрии
role_fr: plénipotentiaire et ministre du Reich dans la Hongrie occupée
status_en: convicted in 1949; sentence reduced and released in 1951
interpretation_en: Veesenmayer used occupation authority and diplomacy to secure Hungarian governmental cooperation with deportation policy. He was not the technical railway organiser or camp commander, so his responsibility must be located in political coercion, oversight and reporting.
postwar_en: The Ministries Trial convicted Veesenmayer of crimes against humanity, enslavement and membership in the criminal SS and sentenced him to twenty years in April 1949. The term was reduced to ten years and he was released in December 1951; he died free in 1977.
limitations_en: The deportations were jointly executed by Eichmann's unit, German diplomatic and police offices, Hungarian authorities and the railway system. The figures reported by Veesenmayer document the operation's scale but are not an individual victim count.

name: Hans-Adolf Prützmann
organization_en: Higher SS and Police Leader · SS · Security Police · Order Police
rank: SS-Obergruppenführer und General der Waffen-SS und Polizei
role_en: Higher SS and Police Leader in Ostland and later in southern occupied Soviet territories
role_pl: HSSPF „Ostland und Russland-Nord”, potem „Russland-Süd”; nadzór nad SS, SD i Orpo
role_de: Höherer SS- und Polizeiführer im Ostland und später in den südlichen besetzten sowjetischen Gebieten
role_ru: высший руководитель СС и полиции в Остланде, а затем на юге оккупированных советских территорий
role_fr: chef supérieur de la SS et de la police dans l’Ostland, puis dans le sud des territoires soviétiques occupés
status_en: died by suicide in British custody in 1945 before trial
interpretation_en: Prützmann occupied the regional command layer between Himmler and the police and killing units. The report demonstrates the scale of crimes within his command system, but individual shootings were planned and performed by subordinate units with their own commanders.
postwar_en: British forces captured Prützmann near Lüneburg in May 1945. He killed himself with a concealed cyanide capsule while in custody and was never tried.
limitations_en: Sources differ between 16 and 21 May 1945 for his death. The December 1942 figure is a command report covering a broad apparatus and cannot be presented as a personal tally of killings committed by Prützmann.

name: Hans-Joachim Riecke
organization_en: Economic Staff East · Reich Ministry of Food and Agriculture · Reich Ministry for the Occupied Eastern Territories
role_en: head of the agricultural section of Economic Staff East and senior food-policy official
role_pl: Szef sekcji rolnej Sztabu Gospodarczego Wschód; główny wykonawca Planu Głodowego Backego
role_de: Leiter der Landwirtschaftsabteilung des Wirtschaftsstabs Ost und hoher Funktionär der Ernährungspolitik
role_ru: руководитель сельскохозяйственного отдела Экономического штаба «Восток» и высокопоставленный чиновник продовольственной политики
role_fr: chef de la section agricole de l’État-major économique Est et haut responsable de la politique alimentaire
status_en: received a minor denazification sentence and was released
interpretation_en: Riecke helped turn Backe's food policy into administrative instructions for extraction and allocation in the East. The resulting starvation involved military commands, occupation authorities and supply agencies, so the full effects of the policy cannot be assigned to him alone.
postwar_en: Riecke was interned from May 1945 until 1949. A denazification proceeding sentenced him to two years in 1950 but credited his internment, and he later returned to work in the agricultural trade; he died in 1986.
limitations_en: The planned and realised death tolls associated with the Hunger Plan differ greatly, and the Polish profile warns against confusing Riecke's functional responsibility with all starvation deaths. Some rank details in the earlier record required correction during the Polish research.

name: Hinrich Lohse
organization_en: Reichskommissariat Ostland · Reich Ministry for the Occupied Eastern Territories · NSDAP
organization_pl: Reich Ministry for the Occupied Eastern Territories / NSDAP
role_en: Reich Commissioner for Ostland and head of its civilian occupation administration
role_pl: Reichskommissar Ostland; najwyższy cywilny administrator na terenach bałtyckich i białoruskich
role_de: Reichskommissar für das Ostland und Leiter seiner zivilen Besatzungsverwaltung
role_ru: рейхскомиссар Остланда и глава его гражданской оккупационной администрации
role_fr: commissaire du Reich pour l’Ostland et chef de son administration civile d’occupation
region_en: Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia and occupied Belarus
status_en: convicted in Germany, sentenced to ten years and released in 1951
interpretation_en: Lohse's civilian apparatus supplied legal, economic and administrative infrastructure for persecution and mass murder alongside SS, police and Wehrmacht structures. Jurisdictional overlap means that the crimes of all security units in Ostland cannot automatically be assigned to the civilian commissioner.
postwar_en: Lohse was tried at Bielefeld and sentenced to ten years and confiscation of property. Released in 1951, he was later classified as a lesser offender in denazification and died at liberty in 1964.
limitations_en: Lohse sometimes disputed the immediate killing of Jewish forced labourers for economic reasons, not on humanitarian grounds. The profile distinguishes such disputes over timing and exploitation from opposition to extermination and separates civilian-administration responsibility from SS and police operations.

name: Jakob Sporrenberg
organization_en: SS and Police Leader in the Lublin district · SS · Order Police
role_en: SS and Police Leader in the Lublin district and organiser of Operation Erntefest
role_pl: Dowódca SS i Policji (SSPF) w dystrykcie lubelskim, następca Globocnika, organizator masakry Erntefest
role_de: SS- und Polizeiführer im Distrikt Lublin und Organisator der Aktion Erntefest
role_ru: руководитель СС и полиции в Люблинском дистрикте и организатор операции «Эрнтефест»
role_fr: chef de la SS et de la police dans le district de Lublin et organisateur de l’opération Erntefest
region_en: Lublin district of the General Government
status_en: convicted in Poland and executed in 1952
interpretation_en: Sporrenberg held the regional command responsible for planning and coordinating Erntefest, while the shootings were carried out by multiple SS, police and auxiliary formations. The profile attributes command and organisation without erasing the agency of the direct perpetrators.
postwar_en: British forces captured Sporrenberg in Norway and extradited him to Poland in October 1946. A Warsaw court sentenced him to death in 1950, and he was hanged at Mokotów Prison on 6 December 1952.
limitations_en: The number murdered in Erntefest is well documented at roughly 42,000–43,000, while broader estimates for his district command are less precise. Polish materials contain limited detail about some stages and dates of the trial.

name: Josef Bühler
organization_en: Government of the General Government · civilian occupation administration
role_en: state secretary and head of government in the General Government
role_pl: Szef rządu Generalnego Gubernatorstwa, zastępca i doradca gubernatora Hansa Franka
role_de: Staatssekretär und Leiter der Regierung im Generalgouvernement
role_ru: статс-секретарь и руководитель правительства Генерал-губернаторства
role_fr: secrétaire d’État et chef du gouvernement du Gouvernement général
status_en: convicted in Poland and executed in 1948
interpretation_en: Bühler's administration connected civil governance with ghettoisation, exploitation, forced labour, seizure of property and the administrative preparation of extermination. SS and police commands carried out many killings, so the distinct role of the civil government must be stated rather than treating it as the sole perpetrator.
postwar_en: After giving evidence at Nuremberg, Bühler was extradited to Poland in May 1946. The Supreme National Tribunal sentenced him to death on 10 July 1948; clemency was refused and he was hanged at Montelupich Prison in Kraków in August 1948.
limitations_en: Sources differ by one day on the date of execution. The evidence establishes leadership of the civilian administration and his Wannsee intervention, while the criminal acts of police, SS and camp authorities require their own attribution.

name: Karl Hermann Frank
organization_en: Higher SS and Police Leader in the Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia · State Ministry
role_en: Higher SS and Police Leader and State Minister in the Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia
role_pl: Wyższy Dowódca SS i Policji (HSSPF) w Protektoracie Czech i Moraw, od 1943 Minister Państwowy
role_de: Höherer SS- und Polizeiführer und Staatsminister im Protektorat Böhmen und Mähren
role_ru: высший руководитель СС и полиции и государственный министр в протекторате Богемии и Моравии
role_fr: chef supérieur de la SS et de la police et ministre d’État dans le protectorat de Bohême-Moravie
status_en: convicted in Czechoslovakia and executed in 1946
interpretation_en: Frank's senior police and governmental authority connected policy, emergency measures and the forces that executed reprisals. Responsibility for Lidice, Ležáky and wider terror is documented at command level, while the individual acts of subordinate police and units remain separately attributable.
postwar_en: US forces captured Frank and transferred him to Czechoslovakia. An Extraordinary People's Court in Prague convicted him of war crimes and crimes against humanity and he was hanged at Pankrác Prison on 22 May 1946.
limitations_en: Victim estimates combine different forms of repression and cannot be reduced to one exact personal total. Sources use slightly different English names for the Prague court, while the conviction and execution are not in dispute.

name: Konrad Meyer
organization_en: Reich Commissioner for the Strengthening of Germandom (RKFDV) · SS Planning Office
role_en: head of the RKFDV Planning Office and principal author of Generalplan Ost
role_pl: Szef biura planowania RKFDV; główny autor Generalplan Ost
role_de: Leiter des Planungsamts des RKFDV und Hauptautor des Generalplans Ost
role_ru: руководитель планового управления RKFDV и главный автор Генерального плана «Ост»
role_fr: chef de l’Office de planification du RKFDV et principal auteur du Generalplan Ost
region_en: Berlin and plans for occupied Eastern Europe
status_en: convicted only of SS membership and released after time served
interpretation_en: Meyer supplied demographic and spatial-planning expertise to a programme of expulsion, Germanisation and colonial rule. Planned populations and later crimes influenced by the plan must be distinguished from direct implementation personally ordered by Meyer.
postwar_en: Meyer was tried in the RuSHA Trial in 1947–1948. Released after conviction only for SS membership, he later returned to an academic career and died in 1973.
limitations_en: The enormous figures in Generalplan Ost describe intended demographic transformation, not a number of people personally killed on Meyer's orders. His acquittal on the principal charges must be reported accurately alongside the content and institutional use of his planning work.

name: Ludolf-Hermann von Alvensleben
organization_en: SS · Selbstschutz West Prussia · SS and Police commands in the occupied Soviet territories
role_en: commander of Selbstschutz West Prussia and later regional SS and police commander
role_pl: Dowódca Selbstschutzu w Prusach Zachodnich, dowódca SSPF na Krymie i HSSPF w Czarnogórze
role_de: Befehlshaber des Selbstschutzes Westpreußen und später regionaler SS- und Polizeiführer
role_ru: командир «Зельбстшутца» Западной Пруссии, позднее региональный командир СС и полиции
role_fr: commandant du Selbstschutz de Prusse-Occidentale, puis commandant régional de la SS et de la police
region_en: Pomerania in occupied Poland, Crimea and the northern Black Sea region
status_en: escaped to Argentina and was never tried in person
interpretation_en: Alvensleben commanded and encouraged a regional formation engaged in systematic killing of Polish elites and other civilians. Site-wide totals for Pomeranian crimes involve several units and chains of command, so the documented judicial minimum and his command role should be kept distinct.
postwar_en: Alvensleben escaped from British internment and reached Argentina in 1946, where he lived as Carlos Lücke and obtained citizenship. A Polish court sentenced him to death in absentia and a Munich court issued an arrest warrant in 1964, but he was never extradited and died in Argentina in 1970.
limitations_en: The Polish research corrected a confusion with another member of the Alvensleben family who served in Montenegro. A Munich warrant documented responsibility for at least 4,247 murders, while higher regional estimates cover a wider set of perpetrators and sites.

name: Ludwig Fischer
organization_en: Warsaw district administration · General Government · NSDAP · SA
role_en: governor of the Warsaw district and head of its civilian occupation administration
role_pl: Gouverneur des Distrikts Warschau; administrator getta warszawskiego i terroru w dystrykcie
role_de: Gouverneur des Distrikts Warschau und Leiter seiner zivilen Besatzungsverwaltung
role_ru: губернатор Варшавского дистрикта и глава его гражданской оккупационной администрации
role_fr: gouverneur du district de Varsovie et chef de son administration civile d’occupation
status_en: convicted in Poland and executed in 1947
interpretation_en: Fischer supplied the civil regulations, resources and administration that enabled ghettoisation, exploitation and occupation terror. Deportations and mass shootings were often executed by SS and police forces, whose operational responsibility remains distinct from Fischer's civilian authority.
postwar_en: US forces captured Fischer in May 1945 and extradited him to Poland in March 1946. The Supreme National Tribunal sentenced him to death on 3 March 1947, and he was hanged at Mokotów Prison on 8 March 1947.
limitations_en: Figures for victims in the Warsaw district combine deaths caused by ghetto conditions, deportations and police terror involving several institutions. The profile limits Fischer's attribution to his regulations, executive authority and the documented conduct of his administration.

name: Ulrich Greifelt
organization_en: Reich Commissioner for the Strengthening of Germandom (RKFDV) · SS
role_en: chief of staff of the RKFDV and administrator of expulsions and Germanisation
role_pl: Szef sztabu RKFDV (Komisariat ds. Umacniania Niemczyzny); germanizacja i wysiedlenia w ramach Generalplan Ost
role_de: Stabschef des RKFDV und Verwalter von Vertreibungen und Germanisierung
role_ru: начальник штаба RKFDV и администратор выселений и германизации
role_fr: chef d’état-major du RKFDV et administrateur des expulsions et de la germanisation
region_en: Occupied Poland and other parts of Central and Eastern Europe
status_en: convicted in the RuSHA Trial and died in prison in 1949
interpretation_en: Greifelt converted Himmler's population policy into directives and administrative programmes of displacement, selection and Germanisation. His central responsibility overlaps with regional expulsion offices, police, Lebensborn and camp authorities that implemented individual actions.
postwar_en: Greifelt was the principal defendant in the RuSHA Trial. Sentenced to life imprisonment on 10 March 1948, he died at Landsberg Prison on 6 February 1949.
limitations_en: The well-documented Zamość figures form only one part of the RKFDV programme, while broader totals are estimates. Responsibility for individual abductions, expulsions and deaths must also be assigned to the regional bodies that carried them out.

name: Wilhelm Kube
organization_en: General Commissariat for White Ruthenia · civilian occupation administration · NSDAP
role_en: General Commissioner for occupied Belarus
role_pl: Generalkommissar für Weißruthenien; cywilny zwierzchnik okupowanej Białorusi
role_de: Generalkommissar für das besetzte Belarus
role_ru: генеральный комиссар оккупированной Белоруссии
role_fr: commissaire général pour la Biélorussie occupée
status_en: killed by the Soviet resistance in 1943 and never tried
interpretation_en: Kube's civil government was part of the machinery that organised property, labour, ghettos and support for killing operations. His occasional disputes with SS officials concerned timing and labour exploitation and did not constitute opposition to the policy of extermination.
postwar_en: Soviet resistance operative Yelena Mazanik placed a bomb in Kube's Minsk residence, killing him on 22 September 1943. He therefore never faced criminal proceedings; German forces answered the attack with reprisals against civilians.
limitations_en: Estimates vary according to whether they cover crimes during Kube's tenure in his district or all wartime losses in Belarus. The profile separates his civilian authority from the operational commands of the SS, police and auxiliary formations.

name: Josef Kramer
organization_en: SS concentration-camp system · Natzweiler-Struthof · Auschwitz-Birkenau · Bergen-Belsen
role_en: commandant of Natzweiler-Struthof, Birkenau and Bergen-Belsen
role_pl: Komendant Birkenau i Bergen-Belsen; wcześniej Natzweiler
role_de: Kommandant von Natzweiler-Struthof, Birkenau und Bergen-Belsen
role_ru: комендант Нацвейлер-Штрутгофа, Биркенау и Берген-Бельзена
role_fr: commandant de Natzweiler-Struthof, de Birkenau et de Bergen-Belsen
status_en: convicted by a British military court and executed in 1945
interpretation_en: Kramer's responsibility includes both personal killing and command over camp systems in which selection, starvation and disease caused mass death. Deaths at each camp also involved wider SS policy and subordinate camp personnel and should not be reduced to a single personal total.
postwar_en: British forces arrested Kramer at Bergen-Belsen. The Belsen Trial convicted him of crimes at Auschwitz and Bergen-Belsen and sentenced him to death on 17 November 1945; he was hanged at Hameln on 13 December 1945.
limitations_en: Some secondary accounts differ by one day on the execution date; the Polish profile follows the trial and execution records. Death totals for Bergen-Belsen and the Hungarian action at Birkenau describe institutional crimes under his command, not killings all performed personally by Kramer.

name: Karl Jäger
organization_en: Einsatzkommando 3 · Einsatzgruppe A · RSHA · SS
role_en: commander of Einsatzkommando 3 and author of the Jäger Report
role_pl: Dowódca Einsatzkommando 3, autor słynnego Raportu Jägera szczegółowo opisującego Zagładę na Litwie
role_de: Kommandeur des Einsatzkommandos 3 und Verfasser des Jäger-Berichts
role_ru: командир айнзацкоманды 3 и автор отчёта Ягера
role_fr: commandant de l’Einsatzkommando 3 et auteur du rapport Jäger
status_en: died by suicide in West German custody in 1959 before trial
interpretation_en: The Jäger Report is direct perpetrator documentation of command, knowledge and the organised character of the killings. Its figures record crimes by the entire unit and auxiliaries under his authority, not acts carried out by Jäger alone.
postwar_en: Jäger lived under his own name until the report was identified in 1959. Arrested on 10 April, he hanged himself at Hohenasperg prison on 22 June 1959 before trial.
limitations_en: The report gives 137,346 victims for the earlier reporting period and 138,272 in a later supplement; the difference reflects coverage, not two competing counts of the same period. The numbers remain those reported by the perpetrators themselves.

name: Maria Mandl
organization_en: SS camp auxiliary staff · Ravensbrück · Auschwitz-Birkenau
role_en: senior overseer and head of the women's camp at Auschwitz-Birkenau
role_pl: Oberaufseherin / Schutzhaftlagerführerin kobiecego odcinka Auschwitz-Birkenau
role_de: leitende Aufseherin und Leiterin des Frauenlagers in Auschwitz-Birkenau
role_ru: старшая надзирательница и руководительница женского лагеря в Аушвице-Биркенау
role_fr: surveillante principale et cheffe du camp des femmes d’Auschwitz-Birkenau
status_en: convicted in Poland and executed in 1948
interpretation_en: Mandl held genuine command authority within the women's camp and also personally participated in selections and abuse. Claims covering all women and children who passed through Birkenau must nevertheless be distinguished from decisions and actions documented specifically under her authority.
postwar_en: US forces arrested Mandl in August 1945 and extradited her to Poland in November 1946. Convicted on 22 December 1947, she was hanged at Montelupich Prison in Kraków on 24 January 1948.
limitations_en: Mandl belonged to the female SS auxiliary staff rather than formally to the SS or NSDAP. Claims that her signatures covered approximately half a million prisoners indicate institutional reach but do not isolate an exact personal victim count.

name: Martin Sandberger
organization_en: Sonderkommando 1a · Security Police and SD in Estonia · Gestapo in Verona
role_en: commander of Sonderkommando 1a and Security Police and SD commander in Estonia
role_pl: Dowódca Sonderkommando 1a / KdS w Estonii; później odpowiedzialny także za deportacje we Włoszech
role_de: Kommandeur des Sonderkommandos 1a und Befehlshaber der Sicherheitspolizei und des SD in Estland
role_ru: командир зондеркоманды 1a и командующий полицией безопасности и СД в Эстонии
role_fr: commandant du Sonderkommando 1a et chef de la Police de sûreté et du SD en Estonie
region_en: Estonia, the Baltic region and later northern Italy
status_en: sentenced to death in the Einsatzgruppen Trial; sentence commuted and released in 1958
interpretation_en: Sandberger combined field command with territorial control over the Security Police and SD, making him responsible for orders and operations under those structures. The wider death toll in occupied Estonia includes crimes by other German and local formations and cannot be attributed wholly to him.
postwar_en: The Einsatzgruppen Trial convicted Sandberger of war crimes, crimes against humanity and membership in criminal organisations and sentenced him to death. The term was commuted to life imprisonment and then reduced; he was released in May 1958 and died in 2010.
limitations_en: Estimates vary from crimes directly reported by Sonderkommando 1a to the broader record of the KdS apparatus in Estonia. Sandberger minimised his responsibility at trial, so the profile relies on operational reports while avoiding a single undifferentiated total.

name: Arthur Nebe
organization_en: RSHA Criminal Police Office (Kripo) · Einsatzgruppe B · SS
role_en: chief of the Criminal Police and commander of Einsatzgruppe B in 1941
role_pl: Szef Kripo i dowódca Einsatzgruppe B w 1941
role_de: Chef der Kriminalpolizei und 1941 Kommandeur der Einsatzgruppe B
role_ru: начальник уголовной полиции и командир айнзацгруппы B в 1941 году
role_fr: chef de la Police criminelle et commandant de l’Einsatzgruppe B en 1941
region_en: Occupied Belarus and the rear area of Army Group Centre
status_en: executed by the Nazi regime in 1945 for involvement in the 20 July plot
interpretation_en: Nebe's later participation in the plot against Hitler does not negate his earlier command of mass murder. The reported killings were carried out by units under his command, so command responsibility is documented without implying that he personally fired every shot.
postwar_en: After the failed 20 July 1944 plot, Nebe went into hiding but was arrested by the Gestapo. The People's Court sentenced him to death for treason, and the Nazi regime hanged him at Plötzensee Prison on 21 March 1945; he was never tried for Einsatzgruppe crimes.
limitations_en: The documented figure of more than 45,000 derives from the group's own reports and is a minimum rather than a full total. His execution concerned resistance to Hitler, not a judicial accounting for the mass murders described in the profile.

name: Erich Naumann
organization_en: Einsatzgruppe VI in Poland · Einsatzgruppe B · RSHA · SS and SD
role_en: commander of Einsatzgruppe B and earlier commander of Einsatzgruppe VI
role_pl: Dowódca Einsatzgruppe B
role_de: Kommandeur der Einsatzgruppe B und zuvor Kommandeur der Einsatzgruppe VI
role_ru: командир айнзацгруппы B и ранее командир айнзацгруппы VI
role_fr: commandant de l’Einsatzgruppe B et, auparavant, de l’Einsatzgruppe VI
region_en: Poznań region, occupied Belarus and western Russia
status_en: convicted in the Einsatzgruppen Trial and executed in 1951
interpretation_en: Naumann held operational command over mobile killing units in two major phases of German occupation violence. The whole operational record of Einsatzgruppe B extended beyond his term, so group totals and killings he specifically admitted must remain differentiated.
postwar_en: An American military tribunal sentenced Naumann to death in April 1948. After clemency requests failed, he was hanged at Landsberg Prison on 7 June 1951.
limitations_en: Einsatzgruppe B killed more than 130,000 people over its entire activity, while Naumann admitted responsibility for more than 17,000 killings around Smolensk. These measures overlap but are not interchangeable as an individual total.

name: Franz Reichleitner
organization_en: Aktion T4 · Operation Reinhard · Sobibór killing centre · SS
role_en: commandant of the Sobibór killing centre after Franz Stangl
role_pl: Komendant Sobiboru po Stanglu
role_de: Kommandant des Vernichtungslagers Sobibór nach Franz Stangl
role_ru: комендант центра убийства Собибор после Франца Штангля
role_fr: commandant du centre de mise à mort de Sobibór après Franz Stangl
region_en: Hartheim, Sobibór and later the Adriatic operational zone
status_en: killed by partisans in 1944 and never tried
interpretation_en: Reichleitner commanded Sobibór during its principal period of operation and was responsible for the camp's organisation and personnel. The total number murdered at Sobibór describes the work of the entire killing-centre apparatus, not acts performed by him alone.
postwar_en: After Sobibór was dismantled, Reichleitner was transferred with other Operation Reinhard personnel to the Adriatic region. Partisans shot him near Fiume, now Rijeka, on 3 January 1944, so he never faced trial.
limitations_en: Estimates for the number murdered at Sobibór range from at least 167,000 to higher totals in other studies. The profile uses the camp total to describe the scale of his command while retaining the separate responsibility of staff, guards and deportation organisers.

name: Gustav Wagner
organization_en: Aktion T4 · Hartheim killing centre · Operation Reinhard · Sobibór killing centre
role_en: deputy commandant and quartermaster of the Sobibór killing centre
role_pl: Zastępca komendanta obozu Sobibór (znany jako „Kat z Sobiboru”), słynący z sadystycznego okrucieństwa
role_de: stellvertretender Kommandant und Quartiermeister des Vernichtungslagers Sobibór
role_ru: заместитель коменданта и интендант центра убийства Собибор
role_fr: commandant adjoint et quartier-maître du centre de mise à mort de Sobibór
status_en: never tried; died in Brazil in 1980 in a death officially classified as suicide
interpretation_en: Wagner helped organise the daily functioning of Sobibór and exercised direct violence there. The overall number murdered in the camp reflects a system involving commandants, staff, guards and deportation authorities and is not an individual victim count for Wagner.
postwar_en: Wagner escaped through Italy and reached Brazil in 1950 under the name Günther Mendel. Exposed in 1978, he was sought by West Germany, Israel, Austria and Poland, but Brazil denied extradition. The grounds differed by request: limitation for Austria; jurisdiction and non-retroactivity for Israel; non-retroactivity and limitation for Poland; a divided limitation ruling for West Germany. He died from knife wounds in Atibaia on 3 October 1980 in a death officially treated as suicide.
limitations_en: USHMM gives a lower bound of at least 167,000 people murdered at Sobibór. This covers the entire camp, not a count of killings committed personally by Wagner. No separate total for his individual acts is established here.

name: Irmfried Eberl
organization_en: Aktion T4 · Brandenburg and Bernburg killing centres · Operation Reinhard · Treblinka II
role_en: Aktion T4 physician and first commandant of the Treblinka II killing centre
role_pl: Lekarz T4; pierwszy komendant Treblinki II
role_de: Arzt der Aktion T4 und erster Kommandant des Vernichtungszentrums Treblinka II
role_ru: врач акции T4 и первый комендант центра убийства Треблинка II
role_fr: médecin de l’Aktion T4 et premier commandant du centre de mise à mort de Treblinka II
status_en: died by suicide in custody in 1948 before trial
interpretation_en: Eberl linked the medical killing programme to the early operation of Treblinka and held command responsibility for the centre during its most chaotic first weeks. The number killed during that short command cannot be isolated precisely from the broader Treblinka record.
postwar_en: After the war Eberl worked as a physician in Blaubeuren. He was arrested on 8 January 1948 and died by suicide in his cell at Ulm on 16 February 1948, before a trial could take place.
limitations_en: The documented totals for Brandenburg and Bernburg concern the killing centres he directed, while estimates for his brief Treblinka command vary widely and are often expressed as daily rates or broad ranges. They should not be combined into a single personal victim count.

name: Jürgen Stroop
organization_en: SS and Police Leader · Security Police · Order Police · Waffen-SS
rank: SS-Gruppenführer / Generalleutnant der Waffen-SS und Polizei
role_en: commander of the German forces that liquidated the Warsaw ghetto
role_pl: Dowódca SS i Policji w Warszawie, kierujący brutalną pacyfikacją getta warszawskiego, autor „Raportu Stroopa”
role_de: Befehlshaber der deutschen Kräfte, die das Warschauer Ghetto liquidierten
role_ru: командующий германскими силами, ликвидировавшими Варшавское гетто
role_fr: commandant des forces allemandes qui liquidèrent le ghetto de Varsovie
status_en: convicted in Poland and executed in 1952
interpretation_en: Stroop was the field commander who planned, directed and reported the suppression of the uprising and liquidation of the ghetto. His report's aggregate figure combines several outcomes and does not mean that every death or deportation was his personal act.
postwar_en: An American military court at Dachau sentenced Stroop to death in March 1947 for the execution of captured US airmen. Extradited to Poland, he was tried in Warsaw with Franz Konrad, sentenced to death in July 1951 and hanged at Mokotów Prison on 6 March 1952.
limitations_en: Estimates of those killed or deported during the liquidation range from roughly 50,000 to 70,000. The figure of 56,065 in Stroop's own report combines people killed, captured and deported and must not be presented as a direct personal death toll.

name: Rudolf Lange
organization_en: Einsatzkommando 2 · Einsatzgruppe A · Security Police and SD in Latvia
role_en: commander of Einsatzkommando 2 and commander of the Security Police and SD in Latvia
role_pl: Dowódca Einsatzkommando 2 i KdS na Łotwie; uczestnik konferencji w Wannsee
role_de: Kommandeur des Einsatzkommandos 2 und Befehlshaber der Sicherheitspolizei und des SD in Lettland
role_ru: командир айнзацкоманды 2 и командующий полицией безопасности и СД в Латвии
role_fr: commandant de l’Einsatzkommando 2 et chef de la Police de sûreté et du SD en Lettonie
region_en: Latvia, especially Riga, and the Baltic region
status_en: never tried; died in Poznań in 1945, probably by suicide, although a combat death cannot be excluded
interpretation_en: Lange combined mobile killing-unit command with territorial police authority, connecting policy coordination to implementation in Latvia. Regional totals include actions by German subordinates and Latvian auxiliaries and cannot be treated as a count of killings he personally carried out.
postwar_en: Lange remained in senior Security Police posts until the final months of the war. He died at Poznań on 23 February 1945 during the Soviet siege, probably by suicide to avoid capture, although a combat death cannot be excluded; he never faced trial.
limitations_en: The approximately 25,000 victims at Rumbula form part of a broader total associated with Einsatzkommando 2 and the Latvian KdS. Sources are also not conclusive about whether Lange died by suicide or in combat.

name: Werner Heyde
organization_en: Aktion T4 · Aktion 14f13 · SS medical apparatus
role_en: medical director and first chief medical assessor of Aktion T4
role_pl: Kierownik medyczny T4 / Obergutachter; czołowy psychiatra aparatu mordów „eutanazyjnych”
role_de: medizinischer Leiter und erster medizinischer Hauptgutachter der Aktion T4
role_ru: медицинский директор и первый главный медицинский эксперт акции T4
role_fr: directeur médical et premier expert médical en chef de l’Aktion T4
region_en: German Reich and concentration camps incorporated into Aktion 14f13
status_en: died by suicide in custody in 1964 before trial
interpretation_en: Heyde's responsibility lay in medical authorisation, institutional design and professional supervision rather than control of every local killing. The wider total for Nazi medical murder encompasses phases and institutions beyond the central programme he directed.
postwar_en: Heyde escaped British custody in 1947 and lived for years as Dr Fritz Sawade while working as a medical expert. He surrendered in November 1959, but died by suicide at Butzbach Prison on 13 February 1964, five days before his trial was due to begin.
limitations_en: The total of more than 70,000 concerns the central Aktion T4 phase, while estimates of 250,000–300,000 cover the wider Nazi 'euthanasia' programme. Secondary sources differ over the exact place associated with his death, and no judgment was delivered.

name: Eduard Strauch
organization_en: Einsatzkommando 2 · Security Police and SD in Belarus · Security Police in Brussels
role_en: commander of Einsatzkommando 2 and commander of the Security Police and SD in occupied Belarus
role_pl: Dowódca Einsatzkommando 2 (EG A); zaangażowany w mordy na Białorusi
role_de: Kommandeur des Einsatzkommandos 2 und Befehlshaber der Sicherheitspolizei und des SD im besetzten Belarus
role_ru: командир айнзацкоманды 2 и командующий полицией безопасности и СД в оккупированной Белоруссии
role_fr: commandant de l’Einsatzkommando 2 et chef de la Police de sûreté et du SD en Biélorussie occupée
status_en: twice sentenced to death; died in custody in 1955
interpretation_en: Strauch held successive operational and territorial commands that made him responsible for policies and actions carried out by the forces under him. Figures reported for Latvia and Belarus overlap with the work of subordinate units and the broader occupation apparatus.
postwar_en: The Einsatzgruppen Trial sentenced Strauch to death on 9 April 1948. Extradited to Belgium, he received another death sentence from a Liège court for the killing of prisoners of war. Neither sentence was carried out after Belgian authorities found him mentally unfit; he died in a custody hospital at Uccle on 15 September 1955.
limitations_en: The regional figures cited in contemporary evidence describe operations by large organisations, not a discrete personal total for Strauch. His two death sentences were not executed, and disputes over his mental condition affected proceedings without erasing the documented command record.

name: Ernst Biberstein
organization_en: Einsatzkommando 6 · Einsatzgruppe C · SS, SD and Gestapo
role_en: commander of Einsatzkommando 6 in occupied Ukraine
role_pl: Dowódca Einsatzkommando 6 (EG C); były pastor protestancki
role_de: Kommandeur des Einsatzkommandos 6 in der besetzten Ukraine
role_ru: командир айнзацкоманды 6 на оккупированной Украине
role_fr: commandant de l’Einsatzkommando 6 en Ukraine occupée
region_en: Eastern Ukraine and the Rostov region
status_en: death sentence commuted; released in 1958
interpretation_en: Biberstein's command and presence at executions establish both organisational and direct dimensions of responsibility. Proven figures for his unit must remain separate from the much larger total for Einsatzgruppe C across all commanders and periods.
postwar_en: The Einsatzgruppen Trial sentenced Biberstein to death in April 1948. His sentence was commuted in 1951 to life imprisonment and later reduced; he was released from Landsberg Prison in 1958 and died in Neumünster in 1986.
limitations_en: Sources place the beginning of his command in either June or September 1942. Trial evidence attributed roughly 2,000–3,000 killings to Einsatzkommando 6 during the relevant period, while higher figures concern the unit's full history or all of Einsatzgruppe C.

name: Eugen Steimle
organization_en: Sonderkommando 7a · Sonderkommando 4a · Einsatzgruppen B and C · RSHA foreign intelligence
role_en: commander of Sonderkommando 7a and later Sonderkommando 4a
role_pl: Dowódca Sonderkommando 7a, później Sk 4a (EG B/C)
role_de: Kommandeur des Sonderkommandos 7a und später des Sonderkommandos 4a
role_ru: командир зондеркоманды 7a, позднее зондеркоманды 4a
role_fr: commandant du Sonderkommando 7a, puis du Sonderkommando 4a
status_en: death sentence commuted; released in 1954
interpretation_en: Steimle's successive commands placed him in charge of units carrying out mass shootings of Jews, civilians and Soviet prisoners. Crimes committed by Sonderkommando 4a before August 1942, including Babi Yar, fall outside his command and must not be assigned to him.
postwar_en: An American military tribunal sentenced Steimle to death in April 1948. The sentence was commuted to twenty years on 31 January 1951, and he was released from Landsberg Prison on 28 June 1954. He later worked as a teacher and died in Ravensburg on 6 October 1987.
limitations_en: The approximately 500 documented victims relate to Sonderkommando 7a during his command, while other unit and Einsatzgruppe totals cover different periods and commanders. Older biographical records also contain conflicting death details.

name: Franz Kutschera
organization_en: SS and Police Leader in the Warsaw District · Security Police · Order Police
role_en: SS and Police Leader for the Warsaw District
role_pl: Dowódca SS i Policji (SSPF) w dystrykcie warszawskim, koordynator ulicznego terroru i egzekucji
role_de: SS- und Polizeiführer für den Distrikt Warschau
role_ru: руководитель СС и полиции Варшавского дистрикта
role_fr: chef de la SS et de la police dans le district de Varsovie
status_en: killed by the Polish underground in 1944 and never tried
interpretation_en: Kutschera's responsibility derived from regional command and the system of repression he directed, while individual roundups and executions were carried out by subordinate police and security formations. His killing was an underground operation during the occupation, not a postwar judicial settlement.
postwar_en: Kutschera was killed in the wartime Home Army operation before the SS headquarters in Warsaw. He therefore did not survive to face a postwar court; the action followed a sentence issued by the clandestine Polish Underground State.
limitations_en: The precise number of victims under his command is uncertain: sources describe several thousand deaths and an estimated rate of about 300 people per week. These figures concern the regional apparatus and should not be converted into a personal execution count.

name: Franz Walter Stahlecker
organization_en: Einsatzgruppe A · Security Police and SD in Ostland · Gestapo
role_en: commander of Einsatzgruppe A and later commander of the Security Police and SD in Ostland
role_pl: Dowódca Einsatzgruppe A i BdS w Ostlandzie
role_de: Kommandeur der Einsatzgruppe A und später Befehlshaber der Sicherheitspolizei und des SD im Ostland
role_ru: командир айнзацгруппы A, позднее командующий полицией безопасности и СД в Остланде
role_fr: commandant de l’Einsatzgruppe A, puis chef de la Police de sûreté et du SD dans l’Ostland
region_en: Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia and the occupied western Soviet territories
status_en: died from wounds in March 1942 and was never tried
interpretation_en: Stahlecker connected central Security Police policy with mobile killing operations and territorial command in Ostland. His reports document the scale of crimes by a multi-unit apparatus, not a number of victims killed by him personally.
postwar_en: Stahlecker was mortally wounded near Krasnogvardeysk, now Gatchina, on 22 March 1942 and died the following day. He was succeeded by Heinz Jost and never faced trial; his operational report later became evidence at Nuremberg.
limitations_en: Krasnogvardeysk and Gatchina are names for the same location, and sources distinguish the date of wounding from the date of death. The Einsatzgruppe's perpetrator-produced figures require critical treatment and describe collective unit operations rather than personal acts.

name: Heinz Jost
organization_en: SS, SD and RSHA
role_en: head of RSHA Office VI and, from March to September 1942, commander of Einsatzgruppe A
role_pl: Dowódca Einsatzgruppe A (następca Stahleckera)
role_de: Leiter des RSHA-Amts VI und von März bis September 1942 Befehlshaber der Einsatzgruppe A
role_ru: начальник VI управления РСХА и, с марта по сентябрь 1942 года, командир айнзацгруппы A
role_fr: chef de l’Office VI du RSHA et, de mars à septembre 1942, commandant de l’Einsatzgruppe A
region_en: the Baltic states and the Leningrad area, with headquarters in Riga
status_en: convicted in the Einsatzgruppen Trial and sentenced to life imprisonment; released in 1951 after commutation
interpretation_en: Jost connected senior RSHA work with operational command in the East. Responsibility is based on his office, knowledge and command during 1942, not on assigning to him the entire earlier record of Einsatzgruppe A.
postwar_en: His life sentence was reduced during the review of the Nuremberg sentences. He left Landsberg prison in December 1951 and was not prosecuted again before his death in 1964.
limitations_en: The frequently cited total of more than 135,000 people murdered by Einsatzgruppe A relates chiefly to the period before Jost assumed command. It must not be presented as the total for his own tenure, although the tribunal found him responsible for crimes committed while he commanded the formation.

name: Karl-Otto Koch
organization_en: SS concentration-camp system
role_en: first commandant of Buchenwald and Majdanek, after earlier service as commandant of Sachsenhausen
role_pl: Pierwszy komendant Buchenwaldu (1937–41) i pierwszy komendant Majdanka (1941–42); wcześniej Sachsenhausen
role_de: erster Kommandant von Buchenwald und Majdanek, zuvor Kommandant von Sachsenhausen
role_ru: первый комендант Бухенвальда и Майданека; ранее служил комендантом Заксенхаузена
role_fr: premier commandant de Buchenwald et de Majdanek, après avoir auparavant commandé Sachsenhausen
region_en: Buchenwald in Germany and Majdanek in occupied Poland
status_en: convicted by an SS court and executed by an SS firing squad in Buchenwald in April 1945
interpretation_en: As commandant, Koch helped establish and enforce the camp regimes through which imprisonment, exploitation and lethal violence were organised. The profile does not attribute every death over the full histories of Buchenwald and Majdanek to his command periods.
postwar_en: Koch never faced an Allied court. The SS tried and executed him before the end of the war, principally in connection with corruption, embezzlement and unauthorised murders rather than for the camp system's crimes against its prisoners as such.
limitations_en: Some biographical details differ between secondary accounts. Figures for all victims of Buchenwald and Majdanek cover periods beyond Koch's command and cannot be used as a personal victim total.

name: Kurt Franz
organization_en: SS, Operation Reinhard and Treblinka II extermination camp
role_en: deputy commandant and final commandant of the Treblinka II extermination camp
role_pl: Ostatni komendant obozu zagłady Treblinka II (zastępca, następnie komendant)
role_de: stellvertretender und letzter Kommandant des Vernichtungslagers Treblinka II
role_ru: заместитель коменданта и последний комендант лагеря смерти Треблинка II
role_fr: commandant adjoint puis dernier commandant du centre d’extermination de Treblinka II
status_en: sentenced to life imprisonment in the first Treblinka trial; released on health grounds in 1993
interpretation_en: Franz's responsibility combines operational command with personally documented brutality. The camp-wide number of people murdered describes the institution in which he served and later commanded; it is not a separate personal total.
postwar_en: Franz lived in West Germany until his arrest in December 1959. He received a life sentence in 1965, was released for health reasons in 1993 and died in 1998.
limitations_en: The court finding of participation in the murder of at least 300,000 people is not identical to the full estimated number murdered at Treblinka. Camp-wide estimates and the different periods in which Franz served as deputy and commandant must remain distinct.

name: Otto Rasch
organization_en: SS, SD and Einsatzgruppe C
role_en: commander of Einsatzgruppe C during the 1941 invasion of the Soviet Union
role_pl: Dowódca Einsatzgruppe C (odpowiedzialnej m.in. za Babi Jar)
role_de: Befehlshaber der Einsatzgruppe C während des Überfalls auf die Sowjetunion 1941
role_ru: командир айнзацгруппы C во время вторжения в Советский Союз в 1941 году
role_fr: commandant de l’Einsatzgruppe C pendant l’invasion de l’Union soviétique en 1941
status_en: indicted in the Einsatzgruppen Trial, but proceedings were discontinued for illness; died in 1948 without judgment
interpretation_en: Rasch's responsibility rests on command of the formation and its reporting and on the documented chain surrounding mass shootings during his tenure. It does not erase the separate roles of Paul Blobel, subordinate units, police auxiliaries or Wehrmacht authorities.
postwar_en: Rasch was arrested and brought before the United States military tribunal in the Einsatzgruppen Trial. Advanced illness prevented a judgment, and he died in November 1948.
limitations_en: The 33,771 victims recorded for Babi Yar are the best-defined figure for one operation. Wider totals for Einsatzgruppe C are formation-level estimates involving many commanders and units and must not be converted into Rasch's individual victim count.

name: Walter Blume
organization_en: SS, SD, Gestapo and Sonderkommando 7a
role_en: commander of Sonderkommando 7a in 1941 and commander of the Security Police and SD in occupied Greece in 1943–1944
role_pl: Dowódca Sonderkommando 7a (EG B)
role_de: 1941 Befehlshaber des Sonderkommandos 7a und 1943–1944 Befehlshaber der Sicherheitspolizei und des SD im besetzten Griechenland
role_ru: командир зондеркоманды 7a в 1941 году и командующий полицией безопасности и СД в оккупированной Греции в 1943–1944 годах
role_fr: commandant du Sonderkommando 7a en 1941 puis commandant de la police de sûreté et du SD en Grèce occupée en 1943–1944
region_en: Belarus and western Russia; later occupied Greece
status_en: sentenced to death in the Einsatzgruppen Trial; sentence commuted and released in 1955
interpretation_en: The profile links two distinct operational roles: command of a mobile killing unit and later leadership of a regional deportation apparatus. Responsibility is based on those posts and proven operations, not on every crime committed by Einsatzgruppe B or all German authorities in Greece.
postwar_en: Blume's death sentence was changed to twenty-five years' imprisonment during the postwar sentence reviews. He was released in 1955 and later proceedings in West Germany did not produce a further conviction.
limitations_en: The surviving reports give specific minimum figures for killings by Sonderkommando 7a, while much larger numbers concern the Einsatzgruppen as a whole. The deportation total from Greece likewise involved several offices and cannot be treated as a personal victim count.

name: Werner Braune
organization_en: SS, SD, Gestapo and Sonderkommando 11b
role_en: commander of Sonderkommando 11b of Einsatzgruppe D
role_pl: Dowódca Sonderkommando 11b (EG D)
role_de: Befehlshaber des Sonderkommandos 11b der Einsatzgruppe D
role_ru: командир зондеркоманды 11b айнзацгруппы D
role_fr: commandant du Sonderkommando 11b de l’Einsatzgruppe D
status_en: sentenced to death in the Einsatzgruppen Trial and executed at Landsberg in 1951
interpretation_en: Braune exercised direct operational command over a unit whose killing actions and reports were documented. His responsibility is tied to that command and to specified operations, while the wider record of Einsatzgruppe D involved other commands and participants.
postwar_en: A United States military tribunal convicted Braune of crimes against humanity, war crimes and membership in criminal organisations and sentenced him to death in April 1948. Appeals and clemency requests failed, and the sentence was carried out in 1951.
limitations_en: The Simferopol figure is a documented operation-level total. Broader estimates for killings across southern Ukraine and Crimea concern the work of several Einsatzgruppe D units and should not be assigned to Braune without narrower evidence.

name: Carl Krauch
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: IG Farben and the Four Year Plan administration
role_en: chairman of IG Farben's supervisory board and plenipotentiary for chemical production under the Four Year Plan
role_pl: Przewodniczący rady nadzorczej IG Farben; pełnomocnik ds. produkcji chemicznej
role_de: Vorsitzender des Aufsichtsrats der IG Farben und Generalbevollmächtigter für Sonderfragen der chemischen Erzeugung im Vierjahresplan
role_ru: председатель наблюдательного совета IG Farben и генеральный уполномоченный по вопросам химического производства в рамках Четырёхлетнего плана
role_fr: président du conseil de surveillance d’IG Farben et plénipotentiaire pour la production chimique dans le cadre du Plan de quatre ans
region_en: Germany and the Monowitz industrial complex at Auschwitz
status_en: convicted in the IG Farben Trial and sentenced to six years; released early in 1950
interpretation_en: Krauch's responsibility arose from high-level industrial and state planning that made the Monowitz labour system possible. It should not be confused with direct camp command or used to assign every death connected with Auschwitz or IG Farben personally to him.
postwar_en: Krauch was convicted of war crimes and crimes against humanity in the IG Farben case. He was released from Landsberg prison in 1950 and faced no further criminal punishment before his death in 1968.
limitations_en: Figures for people exploited at Monowitz and throughout IG Farben's labour system vary in scope. They describe an institutional system with numerous managers and SS authorities, not a count attributable to Krauch alone. He was a civilian industrial leader and Wehrwirtschaftsführer, not an SS officer.

name: Roland Freisler
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Reich Ministry of Justice and the People's Court (Volksgerichtshof)
role_en: president of the People's Court and a leading architect of Nazi judicial terror
role_pl: Prezes Volksgerichtshof; symbol sądowego terroru politycznego
role_de: Präsident des Volksgerichtshofs und führender Gestalter des nationalsozialistischen Justizterrors
role_ru: председатель Народной судебной палаты и один из ведущих архитекторов нацистского судебного террора
role_fr: président du Tribunal du peuple et l’un des principaux architectes de la terreur judiciaire nazie
status_en: killed in an air raid in February 1945 and never tried
interpretation_en: Freisler turned judicial office and courtroom procedure into instruments of political persecution and execution. The profile distinguishes the judgments he personally presided over from the wider record of the People's Court as an institution.
postwar_en: Freisler died in the People's Court building during an American air raid on Berlin on 3 February 1945. He therefore never faced postwar proceedings; the court was later formally condemned in Germany as an instrument of unlawful state terror.
limitations_en: Different figures refer respectively to sentences imposed by Freisler's own senate, sentences he signed and all death sentences issued during his presidency. Those categories must not be merged into a single personal total.

name: Walter von Reichenau
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Wehrmacht, Sixth Army and Army Group South
role_en: commander of the Sixth Army and author of the criminal Severity Order
role_pl: Dowódca 6. Armii na froncie wschodnim, autor zbrodniczego Severity Order (rozkazu o surowości)
role_de: Oberbefehlshaber der 6. Armee und Urheber des verbrecherischen Schärfebefehls
role_ru: командующий 6-й армией и автор преступного «приказа о суровости»
role_fr: commandant de la sixième armée et auteur de l’ordre criminel dit « ordre sur la conduite des troupes à l’Est »
region_en: occupied Ukraine and the eastern front
status_en: died on active service in January 1942 and was never tried
interpretation_en: Reichenau's responsibility rests on command decisions, logistical cooperation and an explicit order encouraging the army's participation in persecution. It does not mean that he personally carried out, or can be assigned without distinction, every crime within the Sixth Army's area.
postwar_en: Reichenau died more than three years before the end of the war and was never tried. His order and the army's cooperation with killing units were later used as evidence of Wehrmacht participation in Nazi crimes.
limitations_en: Accounts differ on whether his death resulted from the stroke or injuries sustained during the evacuation flight. Victim estimates for crimes in the Sixth Army's area describe overlapping responsibility among military, SS, police and auxiliary formations.

name: Alfried Krupp
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Krupp industrial group
role_en: sole owner and head of the Krupp industrial group from 1943
role_pl: Właściciel i szef koncernu Krupp od 1943; jedna z głównych figur przemysłu zbrojeniowego
role_de: ab 1943 Alleineigentümer und Leiter des Krupp-Konzerns
role_ru: единоличный владелец и руководитель промышленной группы Krupp с 1943 года
role_fr: propriétaire unique et dirigeant du groupe industriel Krupp à partir de 1943
status_en: sentenced to twelve years in the Krupp Trial; released and his property restored in 1951
interpretation_en: Krupp's responsibility followed from ownership and executive control over an industrial system that sought, deployed and profited from coerced labour and property seizure. It is distinct from SS camp command and does not make every death in associated camps an individual act by Krupp.
postwar_en: United States High Commissioner John J. McCloy released Krupp in January 1951 and reversed the forfeiture order. Krupp regained control of his industrial property and returned to corporate leadership before his death in 1967.
limitations_en: Sources vary in how they define the total workforce subjected to forced or slave labour across the group. Krupp's status as a supporting member of the SS did not constitute service as a uniformed SS officer.

name: Erich von Manstein
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Wehrmacht, Eleventh Army and eastern-front army groups
role_en: field marshal; commander of the Eleventh Army and later army groups on the eastern front
role_pl: Feldmarschall; dowódca 11. Armii, później grup armii na Wschodzie
role_de: Generalfeldmarschall; Befehlshaber der 11. Armee und späterer Befehlshaber von Heeresgruppen an der Ostfront
role_ru: фельдмаршал; командующий 11-й армией, позднее — группами армий на Восточном фронте
role_fr: maréchal ; commandant de la onzième armée puis de groupes d’armées sur le front de l’Est
region_en: Crimea and the southern sector of the eastern front
status_en: convicted by a British military court in 1949; released early in 1953
interpretation_en: Manstein's responsibility derives from his orders, the conduct of troops within his command and cooperation with Einsatzgruppe D. This is command responsibility, not a claim that he personally performed or exclusively controlled every killing in the army's operational area.
crime_profile_pl: wojna na Wschodzie / zbrodnie przeciw ludności cywilnej i Żydom
