interpretation_en: The profile explains cultural plunder as a bureaucratic chain: confiscation, expert selection, transport and absorption into the occupier’s institutions. It does not attribute every burning of Warsaw libraries to Abb.
postwar_en: Abb was killed in Berlin in April 1945 and was never tried.
limitations_en: Assessing individual decisions requires distinguishing systematic plunder from attempts to preserve selected holdings in the final phase of the war. The profile states this ambiguity explicitly.

name: Walter Braemer
organization_en: Wehrmacht · military occupation administration
role_en: military commander of Bydgoszcz and a rear-area district in September 1939
role_pl: dowódca wojskowy Bydgoszczy i okręgu tyłowego we wrześniu 1939 roku
role_de: Militärbefehlshaber von Bydgoszcz und eines rückwärtigen Militärbezirks im September 1939
role_ru: военный комендант Быдгоща и одного из тыловых военных округов в сентябре 1939 года
role_fr: commandant militaire de Bydgoszcz et d’un district de l’arrière en septembre 1939
status_en: interned; never tried for Bydgoszcz
interpretation_en: The profile documents a commander’s responsibility for the repressive regime he established. It does not automatically attribute to him every later crime committed by police formations in the region.
postwar_en: Braemer was interned by the Allies but never stood trial for crimes in Bydgoszcz. He died in Hamburg in 1955.
limitations_en: Research distinguishes successive phases of military rule, Einsatzgruppen operations, Selbstschutz violence and civilian administration. This profile remains within the period and orders connected with Braemer’s command.

name: Franz Schlegelberger
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Reich Ministry of Justice
role_en: state secretary (1931–1942) and acting Reich minister of justice (1941–1942)
role_pl: sekretarz stanu (1931–1942) i p.o. ministra sprawiedliwości Rzeszy (1941–1942)
role_de: Staatssekretär (1931–1942) und kommissarischer Reichsjustizminister (1941–1942)
role_ru: статс-секретарь (1931–1942) и исполняющий обязанности министра юстиции рейха (1941–1942)
role_fr: secrétaire d’État (1931–1942) et ministre de la Justice du Reich par intérim (1941–1942)
region_en: the German Reich and occupied Polish territories
status_en: life sentence; medical parole granted in 1951
interpretation_en: Schlegelberger’s responsibility lay in using legislation, ministerial instructions and judicial procedures for persecution. He argued that remaining in office had protected the justice system from worse interference by the police. The tribunal rejected that justification: it found that the ministry itself had served criminal ends. His departure in August 1942 did not undo the decisions he had already made.
postwar_en: On 4 December 1947, the American military tribunal in the Judges’ Trial sentenced Schlegelberger to life imprisonment after finding him guilty on counts II and III, concerning war crimes and crimes against humanity. John J. McCloy’s order of 31 January 1951 left that sentence unmodified; the accompanying announcement provided for release on medical parole. This distinction matters: health-related release was not an acquittal or a cancellation of the life sentence in that decision.
limitations_en: The wartime findings here are attributed to the tribunal’s judgment, rather than inferred from Schlegelberger’s title alone. They do not establish that he personally issued every sentence under Nazi rule. Later measures taken under Thierack require their own evidence and must be distinguished from Schlegelberger’s documented acts.

name: Hans Bothmann
organization_en: Sonderkommando Kulmhof · Security Police and SD
role_en: second commandant of the Chełmno killing centre
role_pl: drugi komendant ośrodka zagłady Kulmhof
role_de: zweiter Kommandant der Vernichtungsstätte Chełmno
role_ru: второй комендант центра уничтожения Хелмно (Кульмхоф)
role_fr: deuxième commandant du centre de mise à mort de Chełmno
status_en: died by suicide in captivity in 1946
interpretation_en: The profile shows command succession, continuity of personnel and the logistical reactivation of the killing centre in 1944. Bothmann’s responsibility is documented through command and orders without combining victim totals from both periods.
postwar_en: Bothmann entered British captivity after the war and died by suicide in April 1946. He never stood trial.
limitations_en: Sources date the change of command to either March or April 1942. The profile retains the range rather than claiming greater precision than the evidence allows.

name: Günter Fuchs
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Gestapo in Łódź · Section II B
role_en: head of Section II B of the Łódź Gestapo, responsible for Jewish affairs
role_pl: kierownik referatu II B Gestapo w Łodzi odpowiedzialnego za sprawy żydowskie
role_de: Leiter des für Judenangelegenheiten zuständigen Referats II B der Gestapo in Łódź
role_ru: начальник отдела II B лодзинского гестапо, отвечавшего за «еврейские дела»
role_fr: chef de la section II B de la Gestapo de Łódź, chargée des affaires juives
region_en: Łódź, the Łódź ghetto and Chełmno
region_pl: Łódź · getto łódzkie · Chełmno nad Nerem
status_en: life sentence in 1963
interpretation_en: The profile distinguishes the head of the entire Gestapo office from the head of a specialist section performing defined tasks. Read together, the Bradfisch and Fuchs profiles reveal how an instruction moved from office leadership to field operation.
postwar_en: In 1963 the Hanover Regional Court sentenced Fuchs to life imprisonment for murder, attempted murder and assistance in the mass murder of residents of the Łódź ghetto.
limitations_en: The later execution of the sentence and Fuchs’s date of death are not securely established in the sources used here. Those fields remain open.

name: Georg Michalsen
organization_en: Odilo Globocnik’s staff · Operation Reinhard · SS
role_en: Operation Reinhard staff officer involved in deportations from Warsaw and Białystok
role_pl: funkcjonariusz sztabu akcji „Reinhardt” uczestniczący w deportacjach z Warszawy i Białegostoku
role_de: Stabsoffizier der Aktion Reinhardt, beteiligt an Deportationen aus Warschau und Białystok
role_ru: офицер штаба операции «Рейнхард», участвовавший в депортациях из Варшавы и Белостока
role_fr: officier d’état-major de l’Aktion Reinhard impliqué dans les déportations depuis Varsovie et Białystok
region_en: Warsaw, Białystok and the Lublin district
status_en: twelve years’ imprisonment; released in 1979
interpretation_en: The profile documents a mobile staff-and-operations level: an officer who appeared in successive cities and linked Globocnik’s command with local railways, police forces and assembly points.
postwar_en: Michalsen was arrested in 1961. The Hamburg Regional Court sentenced him to twelve years’ imprisonment for assistance in murder in 1974; he was released in 1979.
limitations_en: The records distinguish allegations, findings in the judgment and the wider activity of Globocnik’s staff. The profile does not present every allegation in the indictment as finally proven.

name: Wilhelm Altenloh
organization_en: Security Police and SD in the Białystok District · Gestapo
organization_pl: Sipo i SD · Gestapo · KdS Białystok
role_en: commander of the Security Police and SD (KdS) in the Białystok District
role_pl: komendant Policji Bezpieczeństwa i SD (KdS) w okręgu białostockim
role_de: Befehlshaber der Sicherheitspolizei und des SD (KdS) im Bezirk Białystok
role_ru: командир Полиции безопасности и СД (KdS) в Белостокском округе
role_fr: commandant de la police de sûreté et du SD (KdS) dans le district de Białystok
region_en: Białystok, the Białystok District and Grodno
status_en: convicted in West Germany; died in 1985
interpretation_en: This profile identifies the regional level at which the leadership of the Security Police and SD combined police administration, the Gestapo and policy toward the Jewish population. It does not automatically assign Altenloh every crime committed in the district or every decision of the RSHA centre.
postwar_en: The Bielefeld Regional Court sentenced Altenloh in 1967 to eight years' imprisonment for aiding and abetting murder; the ruling was reviewed by the Federal Court of Justice in 1970.
limitations_en: The trial files and scholarship distinguish the responsibility of individuals and separate deportations and executions. The profile does not treat holding the KdS office as proof that Altenloh personally carried out every crime of subordinate formations.

name: Fritz Gustav Friedel
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Gestapo in Białystok · Security Police and SD
organization_pl: Gestapo · Sipo i SD · referat żydowski Gestapo
role_en: head of the Jewish affairs section of the Gestapo in Białystok
role_pl: kierownik referatu żydowskiego Gestapo w Białymstoku
role_de: Leiter des Judenreferats der Gestapo in Białystok
role_ru: руководитель реферата по еврейским делам белостокского гестапо
role_fr: chef de la section des affaires juives de la Gestapo de Białystok
status_en: sentenced to death; executed in 1952
interpretation_en: This profile explains the Jewish affairs section as an intermediary between police leadership and ghetto administration. Friedel's office does not mean that he was the sole decision-maker in deportations or that he personally carried out every crime attributed to the Security Police and SS in Białystok.
postwar_en: After extradition to Poland, he was sentenced to death by a court in Białystok in 1949; the sentence was carried out in 1952.
limitations_en: The records contain variants of the surname, Friedel and Friedl. Accounts of the final liquidation of the ghetto require a distinction between his section's role, the KdS chain of command and the actions of other SS and police formations.

name: Franz Bürkl
organization_en: Security Police at Pawiak prison
role_en: Security Police officer at Pawiak prison; sources describe him either as deputy commandant or as a shift leader
role_pl: funkcjonariusz Sipo w więzieniu Pawiak; w źródłach określany jako zastępca komendanta albo szef zmiany załogi
role_de: Sipo-Funktionär im Gefängnis Pawiak; in den Quellen als stellvertretender Kommandant oder als Schichtführer bezeichnet
role_ru: сотрудник Сипо в тюрьме Павяк; источники называют его заместителем коменданта либо начальником смены
role_fr: officier de la police de sûreté à la prison de Pawiak ; les sources le décrivent soit comme commandant adjoint, soit comme chef de quart
status_en: killed by the Polish Home Army in 1943; not tried after the war
interpretation_en: The profile concerns a prison link in the machinery of terror: daily violence, preparation of transports and the connection between Pawiak and execution sites. It does not equate Bürkl with the entire staff or assign him every crime committed at Pawiak.
postwar_en: Bürkl was killed in 1943, before the end of the war and before postwar criminal proceedings.
limitations_en: Sources describe Bürkl's precise position at Pawiak differently: as deputy commandant or as a Zugführer/shift leader. The profile retains that uncertainty and assigns individual responsibility only for documented acts.

name: Werner Kampe
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: NSDAP · occupation municipal administration in Bydgoszcz
organization_pl: NSDAP · administracja miejska Bydgoszczy · Reichsgau Gdańsk–Prusy Zachodnie
role_en: NSDAP Kreisleiter and municipal commissioner, later occupation mayor of Bydgoszcz
role_pl: Kreisleiter NSDAP oraz komisarz miejski, następnie nadburmistrz okupacyjnej Bydgoszczy
role_de: Kreisleiter der NSDAP und Stadtkommissar, später Oberbürgermeister des besetzten Bydgoszcz
role_ru: крайсляйтер НСДАП и городской комиссар, позднее обер-бургомистр оккупационной Быдгощи
role_fr: Kreisleiter du NSDAP et commissaire municipal, puis maire d’occupation de Bydgoszcz
region_en: Bydgoszcz, Gdańsk Pomerania and Reichsgau Danzig–West Prussia
region_pl: Bydgoszcz · Pomorze Gdańskie · Reichsgau Gdańsk–Prusy Zachodnie
status_en: subject of a postwar investigation; no final conviction established
interpretation_en: Kampe shows that local administration and the party structure were not a passive backdrop to terror: they initiated measures, gave them an official framework and communicated repression. The profile does not present him as the personal perpetrator of every crime of the Selbstschutz, Wehrmacht, SD or Einsatzgruppen in Bydgoszcz.
postwar_en: The Pilecki Institute Archive holds files of an investigation by the German Central Office for the Investigation of National Socialist Crimes from 1969 to 1971. The available archival description does not document a final conviction.
limitations_en: The complete investigation files require separate reading. Sources establish initiative, official functions and a public proclamation, but do not justify assigning Kampe the personal execution of all murders committed by different formations in Bydgoszcz.

name: Robert Schefe
organization_en: Security Police and SD · Einsatzgruppe V · Gestapo in Łódź
organization_pl: Einsatzkommando 2/V · Einsatzgruppe V · Gestapo Łódź · Sipo i SD
role_en: commander of Einsatzkommando 2/V in 1939, later head of the Gestapo in Łódź
role_pl: dowódca Einsatzkommando 2/V w 1939 roku, następnie szef Gestapo w Łodzi
role_de: Kommandeur des Einsatzkommandos 2/V 1939, anschließend Leiter der Gestapo in Łódź
role_ru: командир айнзацкоманды 2/V в 1939 году, затем начальник гестапо в Лодзи
role_fr: commandant de l’Einsatzkommando 2/V en 1939, puis chef de la Gestapo de Łódź
region_en: northern Mazovia, Łódź and the Wartheland
status_en: missing at the end of the war; later declared dead with 1945 recorded as the date of death; not tried
interpretation_en: The profile links the phase of a mobile task-force unit with a permanent Gestapo office. It shows the transition from operations in September 1939 to command of a regional terror office, without automatically assigning Schefe every later crime of the Łódź Gestapo.
postwar_en: Schefe disappeared late in the war and was later declared dead with 1945 recorded as his date of death; he never stood trial for his activities in Poland.
limitations_en: The operations of individual Einsatzgruppe V detachments and the competencies of successive departments of the Łódź Gestapo must be distinguished. Holding the office does not prove personal participation in every act committed by its staff.

name: Heinrich Hamann
organization_en: Security Police and SD · Grenzpolizeikommissariat Nowy Sącz
organization_pl: Sipo i SD · Grenzpolizeikommissariat Nowy Sącz
role_en: head of the Grenzpolizeikommissariat, a Security Police and SD branch office, in Nowy Sącz
role_pl: kierownik Grenzpolizeikommissariat (placówki Sipo i SD) w Nowym Sączu
role_de: Leiter des Grenzpolizeikommissariats, einer Außenstelle von Sipo und SD, in Nowy Sącz
role_ru: руководитель Grenzpolizeikommissariat, отделения Сипо и СД, в Новом Сонче
role_fr: chef du Grenzpolizeikommissariat, antenne de la police de sûreté et du SD à Nowy Sącz
region_en: Nowy Sącz, the Sącz region and the Kraków District
status_en: sentenced to life imprisonment; released on health grounds
interpretation_en: The profile explains the mechanism of a local Security Police and SD branch office: arrests, the police prison, suppression of resistance and policy toward Jews. It does not replace an analysis of individual operations or assign Hamann every crime committed by the commissariat's staff and cooperating formations.
postwar_en: In 1966 Hamann was sentenced to life imprisonment in Bochum. According to local documentation, he was released on health grounds in 1985 and died in 1993.
limitations_en: An IPN source on Operation 'Dora' considers Hamann's precise role not fully clarified: it confirms that he signed a later proclamation but does not establish that he personally commanded the whole operation. Nor does the profile transfer every action of his office to him.

name: Wilhelm Rosenbaum
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Security Police and SD school in Rabka
organization_pl: Sipo i SD · Sicherheitspolizeischule Rabka · SS
role_en: commandant of the Security Police and SD school in Rabka
role_pl: komendant szkoły Policji Bezpieczeństwa i SD w Rabce
role_de: Kommandant der Schule der Sicherheitspolizei und des SD in Rabka
role_ru: комендант школы Полиции безопасности и СД в Рабке
role_fr: commandant de l’école de la police de sûreté et du SD à Rabka
region_en: Rabka, Podhale and the Kraków District
status_en: sentenced to life imprisonment; later conditionally released
interpretation_en: The profile shows that a police school was not only a site for training personnel but also an element of the local system of violence. Rosenbaum's responsibility follows both from a leadership role and from judicial findings on specific orders and acts; it does not make him responsible for all actions of persons trained in Rabka.
postwar_en: Arrested in West Germany in 1961, Rosenbaum was sentenced by a Hamburg court to life imprisonment in 1968. He was later conditionally released on health grounds and died in 1984.
limitations_en: Materials on the school, forced labour and executions cover different periods and many perpetrators. The profile distinguishes acts covered by Rosenbaum's conviction from the activities of the entire school and its trainees.

name: Karl Streibel
organization_en: SS training camp in Trawniki · Operation Reinhard
organization_pl: SS · obóz szkoleniowy SS Trawniki · SS i policja dystryktu lubelskiego
role_en: commandant of the SS training camp in Trawniki
role_pl: komendant obozu szkoleniowego SS w Trawnikach
role_de: Kommandant des SS-Ausbildungslagers Trawniki
role_ru: комендант учебного лагеря СС в Травниках
role_fr: commandant du camp d’entraînement SS de Trawniki
region_en: Trawniki, the Lublin District and the General Government
status_en: acquitted in Hamburg in 1976; died in 1986
interpretation_en: Streibel represents the level at which recruitment, training, discipline and the allocation of auxiliary units became a resource for deportations, camp guarding and police operations. This does not mean that every later crime of every dispatched formation can be assigned to him as personal execution or an independent decision.
postwar_en: In 1970 Streibel was charged with other Trawniki officers before a Hamburg court. In 1976 all defendants in that case were acquitted; he died in 1986.
limitations_en: Sources clearly document Streibel's command and training function, but do not prove his personal involvement in every deployment, execution or deportation carried out later by graduates and subordinate formations. A procedural acquittal is not treated as a finding of historical innocence.

name: Gottlieb Hering
organization_en: SS-Sonderkommando Bełżec · Operation Reinhard
role_en: commandant of the German Bełżec killing centre
role_pl: komendant niemieckiego obozu zagłady w Bełżcu
role_de: Kommandant des deutschen Vernichtungslagers Bełżec
role_ru: комендант германского центра уничтожения в Белжеце
role_fr: commandant du centre de mise à mort allemand de Bełżec
region_en: Bełżec, the Lublin District and the General Government
status_en: died in 1945 before criminal proceedings
interpretation_en: The profile concerns command of a killing centre as a link connecting transports, staffing, camp procedures and the concealment of traces. It does not replace profiles of Wirth, Globocnik, guards or those directing deportations, and it does not assign Hering the personal execution of every crime committed by the staff.
postwar_en: Hering died in 1945 before criminal proceedings could be brought against him.
limitations_en: Studies differ on the date he assumed office, giving June or August 1942; this profile follows the 1 August date given by the Bełżec Museum. The scale of crime at the camp is not treated as Hering's personal total.

name: Johann Niemann
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: SS · Operation T4 · Operation Reinhard · SS-Sonderkommando Sobibór
role_en: deputy commandant of the German Sobibór killing centre
role_pl: zastępca komendanta niemieckiego obozu zagłady w Sobiborze
role_de: stellvertretender Kommandant des deutschen Vernichtungslagers Sobibór
role_ru: заместитель коменданта германского центра уничтожения в Собиборе
role_fr: commandant adjoint du centre de mise à mort allemand de Sobibór
region_en: Bełżec, Sobibór and the General Government
status_en: killed during the Sobibór prisoners' uprising in 1943
interpretation_en: Niemann shows the transfer of personnel and expertise from Operation T4 to Operation Reinhard and the day-to-day leadership level of a killing centre. The profile does not equate deputy command with one-person direction of all Sobibór or with every action of the staff and guards.
postwar_en: Niemann was killed on 14 October 1943 during the Sobibór prisoners' uprising and never stood trial after the war.
limitations_en: The Niemann collection is important but is a perpetrator-produced source. The profile therefore reads it alongside institutional research and does not treat photographs as proof of his personal participation in every situation shown.

name: Erich Fuchs
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: SS · Operation T4 · Operation Reinhard
role_en: technician of Operation T4 and Operation Reinhard, associated with the installation of gassing equipment
role_pl: technik akcji „T4” i akcji „Reinhardt”, związany z instalowaniem urządzeń gazowania
role_de: Techniker der „Aktion T4“ und der „Aktion Reinhardt“, verbunden mit dem Einbau von Vergasungsanlagen
role_ru: техник акции «T4» и операции «Рейнхард», связанный с установкой оборудования для отравления газом
role_fr: technicien des opérations T4 et Reinhard, associé à l’installation des dispositifs de gazage
region_en: Bełżec, Sobibór, Treblinka and the General Government
status_en: sentenced in Hagen to four years' imprisonment; died in 1980
interpretation_en: The profile describes a technical link in mass killing: supplying, installing and starting equipment within a system created by SS superiors, camp administrations and guard personnel. It does not assign Fuchs the independent design of the whole system or every crime of the centres where he worked.
postwar_en: In the Sobibór trial before the Hagen Regional Court, Fuchs was sentenced in 1966 to four years' imprisonment. He died in 1980.
limitations_en: Some findings about successive technical tasks derive from postwar examinations and trial records, whose detail is uneven. The profile is limited to the documented technical role and does not assign him every death at Bełżec, Sobibór or Treblinka.

name: Georg Wippern
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: SS Standortverwaltung Lublin · SS Economic and Administrative Main Office · Operation Reinhard
organization_pl: SS-Standortverwaltung Lublin · SS-Wirtschafts- und Verwaltungshauptamt · Akcja „Reinhardt”
role_en: head of SS Standortverwaltung Lublin, responsible for the inventory and transfer of stolen property
role_pl: kierownik SS-Standortverwaltung Lublin, odpowiedzialny za ewidencję i transfer zrabowanego mienia
role_de: Leiter der SS-Standortverwaltung Lublin, zuständig für Erfassung und Transfer geraubten Eigentums
role_ru: руководитель SS-Standortverwaltung в Люблине, отвечавший за учёт и передачу похищенного имущества
role_fr: chef de la SS Standortverwaltung Lublin, responsable de l’inventaire et du transfert des biens volés
region_en: Lublin, the Lublin District and Berlin
status_en: no conviction established in the sources used; died in 1993
interpretation_en: Wippern represents the economic-administrative stage of the crime: taking property, turning it into inventory entries and transporting valuables to the Reich's financial centre. The profile distinguishes this stage from decisions on deportation and killing, even though both belonged to one system of exploitation.
postwar_en: After the war, Wippern escaped American internment. The sources used did not identify a criminal judgment for his activities in Lublin; he later worked in lower-level administration.
limitations_en: The flow of valuables involved many offices, carriers, firms and banks. Surviving documents support assigning Wippern an inventory-and-transfer function, but do not support assigning him every individual shipment, confiscation or decision about its owner's fate.

name: Walter Caspar Többens
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Többenswerke · German armaments firms in the Warsaw ghetto · SS forced-labour system in Poniatowa
organization_pl: Többenswerke · przedsiębiorstwa zbrojeniowe w getcie warszawskim · system pracy przymusowej SS w Poniatowej
role_en: German entrepreneur exploiting forced labour in the Warsaw ghetto and Poniatowa
role_pl: niemiecki przedsiębiorca wykorzystujący pracę przymusową w getcie warszawskim i Poniatowej
role_de: deutscher Unternehmer, der Zwangsarbeit im Warschauer Ghetto und in Poniatowa ausbeutete
role_ru: германский предприниматель, использовавший принудительный труд в Варшавском гетто и Понятове
role_fr: entrepreneur allemand exploitant le travail forcé dans le ghetto de Varsovie et à Poniatowa
region_en: Warsaw, the Warsaw ghetto, Poniatowa and the Lublin District
region_pl: Warszawa · getto warszawskie · Poniatowa · dystrykt lubelski
status_en: convicted after the war, later classified as a 'Mitläufer'; died in 1954
interpretation_en: Többens shows how a private enterprise could be incorporated into the occupation system of forced labour and subordinated to the SS. The profile does not equate his economic and selection role with operational command of every deportation, execution or subsequent liquidation of a camp.
postwar_en: After the war Többens was convicted, but later classified only as a 'Mitläufer'. He returned to business in Bremen and died in 1954.
limitations_en: Testimony from the ghetto is varied and concerns many stages of the operation of his enterprises. It is read alongside museum and encyclopaedic documentation; the profile does not adopt every assertion in an individual testimony without an additional basis.

name: Ernst Zörner
organization_en: General Government · Lublin District administration · NSDAP
organization_pl: rząd Generalnego Gubernatorstwa · administracja dystryktu lubelskiego · NSDAP
role_en: governor of the Lublin District of the General Government
role_pl: gubernator dystryktu lubelskiego Generalnego Gubernatorstwa
role_de: Gouverneur des Distrikts Lublin im Generalgouvernement
role_ru: губернатор Люблинского дистрикта Генерал-губернаторства
role_fr: gouverneur du district de Lublin dans le Gouvernement général
region_en: Lublin, the Lublin District and the General Government
status_en: missing after 1945; legally declared dead in 1960
interpretation_en: Zörner represents regional civil authority that converted occupation policy into proclamations, ghetto boundaries, official circulation and logistics. The profile does not present him as the independent commander of Operation Reinhard or assign him every deportation or crime of SS and police formations active in the same district.
postwar_en: From 1945 Zörner was considered missing; in 1960 a court legally declared him dead. The sources used did not identify criminal proceedings against him.
limitations_en: Sources differ on the exact end date of his tenure and his fate after 1945, so the year of death remains undetermined. The evidence documents orders and the administrative involvement of his office, not his personal issuance of every deportation decision.

name: Emil Puhl
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Reichsbank · Reich Ministry of Economics · the Reich financial system
organization_pl: Reichsbank · Ministerstwo Gospodarki Rzeszy · system finansowy Rzeszy
role_en: Reichsbank vice-president responsible for implementing arrangements with the SS concerning stolen valuables
role_pl: wiceprezes Reichsbanku odpowiedzialny za wykonanie ustaleń z SS dotyczących zrabowanych wartości
role_de: Vizepräsident der Reichsbank, zuständig für die Umsetzung von Absprachen mit der SS über geraubte Werte
role_ru: вице-президент Рейхсбанка, отвечавший за выполнение договорённостей с СС о похищенных ценностях
role_fr: vice-président de la Reichsbank chargé d’appliquer les arrangements avec la SS concernant les valeurs volées
region_en: Berlin, Nazi Germany and occupied Poland
status_en: sentenced at Nuremberg to five years' imprisonment; died in 1962
interpretation_en: Puhl shows the final financial stage in a chain of crime: accepting, securing, accounting for and using valuables taken from people deported and murdered. The profile separates this documented agency from decisions on deportation, camp management and direct killing.
postwar_en: In the Nuremberg Ministries Trial, Puhl was sentenced to five years' imprisonment for war crimes. He died in 1962.
limitations_en: Surviving sources document the arrangements and flow of valuables very well, but do not allow Puhl to be assigned every specific delivery or its value without a risk of duplication. The profile does not construct a ranking of stolen property or victims.

name: Ernst Lautz
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: People's Court · Reich Ministry of Justice
role_en: chief public prosecutor at the People's Court in Berlin
role_pl: naczelny prokurator Trybunału Ludowego w Berlinie
role_de: Oberreichsanwalt beim Volksgerichtshof in Berlin
role_ru: главный прокурор Народной судебной палаты в Берлине
role_fr: procureur général auprès du Tribunal du peuple à Berlin
region_en: Berlin, Nazi Germany and Polish territories annexed to the Reich
region_pl: Berlin · Rzesza Niemiecka · ziemie wcielone do Rzeszy
status_en: sentenced to ten years' imprisonment; released in 1951
interpretation_en: The profile shows the prosecutorial stage of the chain of repression: choosing court jurisdiction, preparing indictments and expecting a death sentence. It does not equate Lautz's office with personally issuing every judgment or carrying out every execution.
postwar_en: At the Nuremberg Justice Trial, Lautz was sentenced in 1947 to ten years' imprisonment. He was released in 1951.
limitations_en: The surviving records reveal a pattern of prosecutorial activity and some cases, but not the full path of every indictment. The profile does not assume that every case retained by the People's Court ended in the same outcome.

name: Günther Joël
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Reich Ministry of Justice · General Prosecutor's Office in Hamm
organization_pl: Ministerstwo Sprawiedliwości Rzeszy · prokuratura w Hamm · SS i SD
role_en: Reich Ministry of Justice criminal-law official, later general prosecutor in Hamm
role_pl: referent Ministerstwa Sprawiedliwości Rzeszy do spraw karnych, później prokurator generalny w Hamm
role_de: Referent des Reichsjustizministeriums für Strafsachen, später Generalstaatsanwalt in Hamm
role_ru: референт Министерства юстиции рейха по уголовным делам, позднее генеральный прокурор в Хамме
role_fr: fonctionnaire chargé du droit pénal au ministère de la Justice du Reich, puis procureur général à Hamm
region_en: Berlin, Polish territories annexed to the Reich and Hamm
region_pl: Berlin · ziemie wcielone do Rzeszy · Hamm
status_en: sentenced to ten years' imprisonment; released in 1951
interpretation_en: The profile places Joël at the junction of ministerial control over criminal cases, prosecution and racial occupation law. It does not assign him every proceeding conducted by the ministry, regional prosecution services, the SS or the SD.
postwar_en: At the Nuremberg Justice Trial, Joël was sentenced in 1947 to ten years' imprisonment. He was released in 1951.
limitations_en: Trial material establishes his function, knowledge and the scope of cases examined in the ministry, but does not settle Joël's personal involvement in every judgment or execution. It also preserves the distinction between his earlier activity and the later period of wartime repression.

name: Johannes Thümmler
organization_en: Security Police and SD · Gestapo · KdS Katowice
organization_pl: Sipo i SD · Gestapo · KdS Katowice
role_en: commander of the Security Police in Katowice and presiding judge of the police summary court operating at Auschwitz concentration camp
role_pl: komendant Policji Bezpieczeństwa w Katowicach i przewodniczący policyjnego sądu doraźnego działającego w KL Auschwitz
role_de: Kommandeur der Sicherheitspolizei in Kattowitz und Vorsitzender des im Konzentrationslager Auschwitz tagenden Polizeistandgerichts
role_ru: командир Полиции безопасности в Катовице и председатель полицейского чрезвычайного суда (Polizeistandgericht), действовавшего в концлагере Аушвиц
role_fr: commandant de la Police de sûreté à Katowice et président du tribunal sommaire de police siégeant au camp de concentration d’Auschwitz
region_en: Katowice, the Katowice administrative district and Auschwitz concentration camp
status_en: subject to multiple investigations but never finally convicted; died in 2002
interpretation_en: This profile shows how regional Security Police leadership was connected to an extrajudicial mechanism for sentencing prisoners, whose judgments were carried out at Auschwitz. Thümmler's testimony is an important source for his powers and the procedure, but his claims justifying his own decisions must be tested against museum documentation and investigation files.
postwar_en: In 1964 he appeared as a witness at the first Frankfurt Auschwitz trial. Surviving finding aids document long-running investigations in East and West Germany, but no final conviction followed. The Stuttgart public prosecutor discontinued the last proceeding in March 2002 because the evidence did not sufficiently individualise the acts; Thümmler died on 28 April 2002.
limitations_en: Thümmler's own testimony contains defensive claims and cannot be treated as an impartial account. Finding aids establish the scope of proceedings but do not substitute for the complete files. The profile does not automatically attribute to him every crime of the Katowice Gestapo or Auschwitz; it records his powers, confirmed court sessions and the documented execution of his judgments. The new basis relative to the Wave 4 deferral is the combined record of the 1964 testimony, the Federal Archives research guide and a separate Baden-Württemberg State Archives file group.

name: Fritz Liphardt
organization_en: Einsatzkommando 2/III · Security Police and SD · KdS Radom
organization_pl: Einsatzkommando 2/III · Sipo i SD · KdS Radom
role_en: commander of Einsatzkommando 2/III in 1939, then commander of the Security Police and SD (KdS) in the Radom District
role_pl: dowódca Einsatzkommando 2/III w 1939 roku, następnie komendant Policji Bezpieczeństwa i SD (KdS) w dystrykcie radomskim
role_de: Kommandeur des Einsatzkommandos 2/III im Jahr 1939, anschließend Kommandeur der Sicherheitspolizei und des SD (KdS) im Distrikt Radom
role_ru: командир айнзацкоманды 2/III в 1939 году, затем командир Полиции безопасности и СД (KdS) в Радомском дистрикте
role_fr: commandant de l’Einsatzkommando 2/III en 1939, puis commandant de la Police de sûreté et du SD (KdS) dans le district de Radom
region_en: Łódź, Radom and the Radom District
status_en: died in a Polish prison before trial in 1947; suicide was the officially reported cause
interpretation_en: Liphardt connects two stages in the construction of the machinery of terror: a mobile Einsatzkommando operating during the 1939 war and a permanent regional Security Police and SD command in the General Government. The profile describes his organisational authority and documented operations of subordinate structures, but does not attribute to him without evidence every act of the KdS Radom field offices.
postwar_en: The British arrested him in Flensburg in June 1945, after which he was extradited to Poland. He died in prison in Szczecin on 18 May 1947 before a trial could take place; IPN documentation states that the death was officially ruled a suicide.
limitations_en: The scope of responsibility held by the commander of EK 2/III and a KdS does not amount to personal commission of every arrest, execution and deportation in the district. The circumstances of his death are known from postwar documentation, without a judicial determination. The new basis relative to the Wave 4 deferral consists of independent sources: a study of the KdS Radom structure, university research on EK 2/III and a publication held by the Library of Congress describing the transition of Einsatzgruppe personnel into the permanent Security Police apparatus.

name: Waldemar Macholl
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Suwałki Border Police Commissariat · Gestapo · KdS Białystok
role_en: border police commissioner in Suwałki, then head of the Białystok Gestapo's Section IV A-3 for combating resistance
role_pl: komisarz policji granicznej w Suwałkach, następnie kierownik referatu IV A-3 Gestapo w Białymstoku do zwalczania ruchu oporu
role_de: Grenzpolizeikommissar in Suwałki, anschließend Leiter des Referats IV A-3 der Gestapo in Białystok zur Bekämpfung des Widerstands
role_ru: комиссар пограничной полиции в Сувалках, затем начальник отдела IV A-3 белостокского гестапо по борьбе с движением сопротивления
role_fr: commissaire de la police des frontières à Suwałki, puis chef, au sein de la Gestapo de Białystok, de la section IV A-3 chargée de combattre la résistance
status_en: sentenced to death in Poland; executed on 15 July 1949
interpretation_en: This profile shows the progression from a border police office to a section of the Białystok Gestapo and then to the final stage of the machinery of crime: erasing the traces of mass executions. Responsibility rests on his function, the investigation's specific finding concerning Szczebra and the trial record, rather than on wholesale attribution to him of every Gestapo operation in the Białystok District.
postwar_en: He was tried by the Regional Court in Białystok in March 1949, sentenced to death and executed on 15 July 1949 after clemency was denied.
limitations_en: The IPN inventory description summarises the charges in the indictment, not all of the court's final findings. In particular, the allegation that he personally killed 31 prisoners is not presented here as an independently confirmed fact; the Grabówka study shows conflicting accounts of the number killed and the number who survived. The new basis relative to the Wave 5 deferral consists of the sources considered together: IPN court files, the later investigative finding in the Szczebra case, a critical study of Grabówka and independent documentation of the course of the trial.

name: Heinz Errelis
organization_en: Gestapo · Security Police and SD · KdS Białystok
organization_pl: Gestapo · Sipo i SD · KdS Białystok
role_en: head of the Gestapo field office in Grodno, subordinate to KdS Białystok
role_pl: kierownik placówki Gestapo w Grodnie podporządkowanej KdS Białystok
role_de: Leiter der dem KdS Białystok unterstellten Gestapo-Außenstelle in Grodno
role_ru: начальник территориального отделения гестапо в Гродно, подчинённого KdS Белосток
role_fr: chef de l’antenne de la Gestapo à Grodno, subordonnée au KdS Białystok
region_en: Grodno, Kiełbasin and the Białystok District
status_en: sentenced in West Germany to 6 years and 6 months for aiding deportations; acquitted in a separate case
interpretation_en: Errelis represents the field-office level: between the regional KdS and the officers managing ghettos, the assembly point and transports. The judgments make it possible to separate proven aiding of deportations from specific killings that the Cologne court did not find proven.
postwar_en: After British captivity, he escaped from the camp at Rimini in 1947 and lived under a false name until 1950. The Bielefeld Regional Court sentenced him in 1967 to six years and six months' imprisonment; after appellate review, he began serving the sentence in 1970 and was conditionally released in 1974. He died in Bochum in 1994.
limitations_en: The Cologne judgment did not confirm the allegations of personal killing, and the profile does not repeat them as facts. Leadership of the field office must not be equated with personally carrying out every act of his subordinates. Some secondary English-language indexes use the form ‘Heinz Erreles’; the canonical spelling ‘Heinz Errelis’ appears in the German judgment, the IPN inventory and current scholarship. His date of death is confirmed by later academic literature.

name: Wilhelm Haase
organization_en: SS · SS and Police Leader in Kraków · Security Police and Order Police
organization_pl: SS · SSPF Kraków · Policja Bezpieczeństwa i Policja Porządkowa
role_en: chief of staff to the SS and Police Leader in the Kraków District, involved in planning and commanding deportation operations
role_pl: szef sztabu dowódcy SS i Policji w dystrykcie krakowskim, uczestnik planowania i dowodzenia akcjami deportacyjnymi
role_de: Stabschef des SS- und Polizeiführers im Distrikt Krakau, beteiligt an Planung und Führung von Deportationsaktionen
role_ru: начальник штаба руководителя СС и полиции в Краковском дистрикте, участвовавший в планировании депортационных операций и командовании ими
role_fr: chef d’état-major du chef de la SS et de la police dans le district de Cracovie, impliqué dans la planification et le commandement d’opérations de déportation
region_en: Kraków, Bochnia, Szebnie and the Kraków District
status_en: sentenced to death in Poland; executed on 23 May 1952
interpretation_en: Haase illustrates the role of an SSPF staff as a link that translated decisions by the SS and Police Leader into coordinated action by the Gestapo, Order Police and other formations during deportations and ghetto liquidations. His responsibility rests on documented planning, command and presence during specific operations, not merely on his official title.
postwar_en: After the war, a British court sentenced him to two years' imprisonment for membership in the SS and NSDAP, after which he was extradited to Poland. The Regional Court in Kraków sentenced him to death on 29 June 1951; after the Supreme Court upheld the judgment, he was executed on 23 May 1952.
limitations_en: His birth certificate gives the forename ‘Willi’, whereas the Polish court files and much of the historiography use ‘Wilhelm’; the profile retains the form familiar from the literature while explicitly noting the discrepancy. The role of chief of staff does not prove personal involvement in every killing committed by SSPF units, so the account is limited to specific operations confirmed by judicial material.

name: Walther Bierkamp
organization_en: Einsatzgruppe D · Security Police and SD · BdS General Government
organization_pl: Einsatzgruppe D · Sipo i SD · BdS Generalne Gubernatorstwo
role_en: commander of Einsatzgruppe D, then commander of the Security Police and SD (BdS) in the General Government
role_pl: dowódca Einsatzgruppe D, następnie dowódca Policji Bezpieczeństwa i SD (BdS) w Generalnym Gubernatorstwie
role_de: Kommandeur der Einsatzgruppe D, anschließend Befehlshaber der Sicherheitspolizei und des SD (BdS) im Generalgouvernement
role_ru: командир айнзацгруппы D, затем командующий Полицией безопасности и СД (BdS) в Генерал-губернаторстве
role_fr: commandant de l’Einsatzgruppe D, puis commandant de la Police de sûreté et du SD (BdS) dans le Gouvernement général
region_en: the General Government, Kraków, Radom and Warsaw
crime_tags_pl: Einsatzgruppen;Sipo i SD;Ewakuacje i mordowanie więźniów
status_en: died by suicide on 15 May 1945; never tried
interpretation_en: Bierkamp is a profile of a regional order-giver: he not only managed the BdS–KdS hierarchy but left a document referring directly to the killing of prisoners if evacuation was impossible. This does not mean attributing to him, without separate evidence, every crime of Einsatzgruppe D or of all Security Police field offices in the General Government.
postwar_en: After the collapse of the Third Reich, he did not stand trial. He died by suicide in Scharbeutz on 15 May 1945, before proceedings concerning his command activities could be initiated.
limitations_en: The order of 20 July 1944 confirms a central directive for the territory under his authority, but its implementation in individual prisons and camps requires separate local documentation. The profile neither aggregates nor automatically attributes to Bierkamp every killing by Einsatzgruppe D and the entire BdS network. Differences of several weeks in dates for his formal assumption of the BdS post arise from distinctions between appointment, arrival and handover of the office.

name: Helmut Tanzmann
organization_en: Gestapo · Security Police and SD · KdS Lwów
organization_pl: Gestapo · Sipo i SD · KdS Lwów
role_en: head of the Gestapo in Gdańsk, then commander of the Security Police and SD (KdS) in Lwów
role_pl: szef Gestapo w Gdańsku, następnie komendant Policji Bezpieczeństwa i SD (KdS) we Lwowie
role_de: Leiter der Gestapo in Danzig, anschließend Kommandeur der Sicherheitspolizei und des SD (KdS) in Lemberg
role_ru: начальник гестапо в Гданьске, затем командир Полиции безопасности и СД (KdS) во Львове
role_fr: chef de la Gestapo à Dantzig, puis commandant de la Police de sûreté et du SD (KdS) à Lwów
region_en: Danzig–West Prussia, Lwów and the Galicia District
status_en: died by suicide in British internment on 6 March 1946; never tried
interpretation_en: Tanzmann connects two important areas of the regional Security Police apparatus: the initial organisation of the Gestapo in annexed Danzig and Pomerania, and leadership of the KdS in the Galicia District. The profile explains the command structure and police mechanisms; it does not automatically attribute to him every killing by subordinate field offices or every action of the SSPF Galicia.
postwar_en: He escaped from Norway in a sailor's uniform and under a false identity, but the British established who he was. He was transferred to the London Cage interrogation centre and on 6 March 1946 died by hanging himself before trial.
limitations_en: Older literature incorrectly stated that Tanzmann had been executed and even gave differing dates of death. The IfZ edition and research in declassified files point to suicide on 6 March 1946; the death was registered under a false identity, which explains some of the discrepancies. Sources also differ on the end of his term in Lwów, placing it either in autumn 1942 or in early 1943.

name: Peter Leideritz
organization_en: Security Police and SD · Gestapo · KdS Lwów
organization_pl: Sipo i SD · Gestapo · KdS Lwów
role_en: head of the Security Police and SD field office in Kołomyja
role_pl: kierownik placówki terenowej Policji Bezpieczeństwa i SD w Kołomyi
role_de: Leiter der Außenstelle der Sicherheitspolizei und des SD in Kołomyja
role_ru: начальник территориального отделения Полиции безопасности и СД в Коломые
role_fr: chef de l’antenne de la Police de sûreté et du SD à Kołomyja
region_en: Kołomyja, Horodenka, Szeparowce and the Galicia District
crime_tags_pl: Sipo i SD;Masowe egzekucje;Deportacje do Bełżca
status_en: sentenced to death in Poland; executed on 22 February 1949
interpretation_en: Leideritz shows how a small KdS field office could combine police intelligence, mobile execution groups, administration of a ghetto and deportations to an extermination camp. The profile grounds responsibility in his leadership of the office, specific operations and the judgment, while keeping accounts of personal shootings within the limits of what the files actually established.
postwar_en: The Americans detained him on 7 August 1946 under the name Peter Lewald and extradited him to Poland in December. The Regional Court in Warsaw sentenced him to death on 17 November 1947; after appeals were rejected and clemency denied, the judgment was carried out on 22 February 1949.
limitations_en: The Polish judgment encompassed broadly phrased participation in mass murders and membership in the Gestapo; it did not determine separately every episode described by witnesses. Older compilations incorrectly give 1947 as the year of his death—the execution records used by the IPN confirm 22 February 1949. Estimates of the number of victims of individual operations are not used to determine the circle of responsibility.

name: Josef Bürger
organization_en: Gestapo · Security Police and SD · KdS field office in Radzyń
organization_pl: Gestapo · Sipo i SD · placówka KdS Radzyń
role_en: officer of the Radzyń Gestapo field office responsible for matters concerning the Łuków ghetto
role_pl: funkcjonariusz radzyńskiej placówki Gestapo odpowiedzialny za sprawy getta w Łukowie
role_de: Beamter der Gestapo-Außenstelle in Radzyń, zuständig für Angelegenheiten des Ghettos Łuków
role_ru: сотрудник территориального отделения гестапо в Радзыне, отвечавший за вопросы Лукувского гетто
role_fr: agent de l’antenne de la Gestapo à Radzyń chargé des affaires concernant le ghetto de Łuków
region_en: Łuków, Radzyń Podlaski and the Lublin District
status_en: sentenced in West Germany to life imprisonment for ten murders; died in 1986
interpretation_en: Bürger represents a local Gestapo case officer who combined day-to-day management of a ghetto, the extraction of goods and labour, securing looted property and participation in deportations with individual violence. The profile deliberately distinguishes the ten murders confirmed by the judgment from the broader indictment and from collective operations by other units.
postwar_en: After internment, a denazification tribunal classified him in 1948 merely as a ‘follower’ (Mitläufer), and in 1953 he returned to police service. He was arrested in 1963. The Düsseldorf Regional Court sentenced him to life imprisonment in 1970; he served the sentence in Straubing. Conditional release was granted in 1985, but he died on 2 April 1986 before the prosecution's challenge to that decision was resolved.
limitations_en: Press reports in 1970 summarised the indictment as alleging 44 killings, whereas the final judgment concerned ten murders; the remaining acts must not be presented as proven in court. Bürger did not command Police Battalion 101 or units arriving from Lublin, so the profile does not attribute the entire deportation and liquidation of the ghetto to him. Biographical data and the trial's outcome come from a study based on the complete files in the North Rhine-Westphalia State Archives and are confirmed by independent publications.

name: Anton Brunner
organization_en: Central Office for Jewish Emigration in Vienna · Eichmann section in the RSHA · Eichmann Special Detachment
organization_pl: Zentralstelle für jüdische Auswanderung Wien · referat Eichmanna w RSHA · Sonderkommando Eichmann
role_en: head of ‘commissioning’ in Vienna's assembly camps and employee of the Central Office for Jewish Emigration, known as ‘Brunner II’
role_pl: kierownik „komisjonowania” w wiedeńskich obozach zbiorczych i pracownik Centrali do spraw Emigracji Żydowskiej, określany jako „Brunner II”
role_de: Leiter der „Kommissionierungen“ in Wiener Sammellagern und Mitarbeiter der Zentralstelle für jüdische Auswanderung, bezeichnet als „Brunner II“
role_ru: руководитель отборочных процедур в венских сборных лагерях и сотрудник Центрального управления по еврейской эмиграции, известный как «Бруннер II»
role_fr: responsable des « sélections pour les convois » dans les camps de rassemblement viennois et employé de l’Office central pour l’émigration juive, connu sous le nom de « Brunner II »
status_en: sentenced to death by the Vienna People's Court; executed on 24 May 1946
interpretation_en: Anton Brunner illustrates the administrative and coercive link in deportation that preceded transport to ghettos and extermination centres, including to occupied Poland. His role was not merely clerical: it encompassed selecting people, confiscating documents and property, and violence in assembly camps. At the same time, he must not be confused with Alois Brunner or assigned all of his superior's operations.
postwar_en: After the war, he was arrested and tried by the Vienna People's Court on the basis of extensive evidence, including survivor testimony and documentation of the ‘commissionings’. He was sentenced to death on 10 May 1946 and executed by hanging on 24 May 1946.
limitations_en: Anton Brunner (‘Brunner II’, 1898–1946) was not Alois Brunner (‘Brunner I’, 1912–probably 2001/2010). Two University of Vienna studies give different days of birth—8 March and 8 August 1898—so the canonical record retains only the secure year. The trial formula referring to responsibility for approximately 48 thousand deportees describes his role in the deportation apparatus and does not mean that he personally killed all the victims. The role family ‘ss_police’ describes the office's institutional subordination to Eichmann's section; sources indicate that Brunner himself was not a member of the SS.

name: Julius Wohlauf
organization_en: Order Police · Reserve Police Battalion 101 · Police Regiment 25
organization_pl: Ordnungspolizei · 101. Rezerwowy Batalion Policji · 25. Pułk Policji
role_en: commander of the 1st Company and deputy commander of Reserve Police Battalion 101
role_pl: dowódca 1. kompanii i zastępca dowódcy 101. Rezerwowego Batalionu Policji
role_de: Kompaniechef der 1. Kompanie und stellvertretender Kommandeur des Reserve-Polizei-Bataillons 101
role_ru: командир 1-й роты и заместитель командира 101-го резервного полицейского батальона
role_fr: commandant de la 1re compagnie et commandant adjoint du 101e bataillon de réserve de police
region_en: the Lublin District, Józefów Biłgorajski, Końskowola and Międzyrzec Podlaski
region_pl: dystrykt lubelski · Józefów Biłgorajski · Końskowola · Międzyrzec Podlaski
status_en: sentenced in West Germany to 8 years' imprisonment; died in 2002
interpretation_en: Wohlauf represents the company-command level that translated a battalion order into the organisation of execution sites, assignment of policemen and discipline of subordinates. The profile bases his responsibility on documented decisions and the final judicial outcome, rather than simply transferring to a commander the full record of crimes committed by Battalion 101.
postwar_en: After the war, he returned to the Hamburg police. He was suspended in January 1963 and arrested in 1964. The Hamburg Regional Court imposed an eight-year prison sentence in 1968; the Federal Court of Justice reviewed the case in 1970, and the final sentence was eight years.
limitations_en: The figure of 9,200 describes the scope of legal attribution in the trial, not a victim ranking or the sum of every crime committed by the battalion. Police witnesses' reconstructions differ on details of the briefing and particular scenes at Józefów; the profile retains only elements supported by the judicial material and comparative scholarship.

name: Hartwig Gnade
organization_en: Order Police · Reserve Police Battalion 101 · Police Regiment 25
organization_pl: Ordnungspolizei · 101. Rezerwowy Batalion Policji · 25. Pułk Policji
role_en: commander of the 2nd Company of Reserve Police Battalion 101
role_pl: dowódca 2. kompanii 101. Rezerwowego Batalionu Policji
role_de: Kompaniechef der 2. Kompanie des Reserve-Polizei-Bataillons 101
role_ru: командир 2-й роты 101-го резервного полицейского батальона
role_fr: commandant de la 2e compagnie du 101e bataillon de réserve de police
region_en: the Lublin District, Józefów Biłgorajski, Łomazy and Międzyrzec Podlaski
region_pl: dystrykt lubelski · Józefów Biłgorajski · Łomazy · Międzyrzec Podlaski
status_en: subsequent fate unresolved; never tried
interpretation_en: The profile shows how a company commander allocated tasks among cordons, transport and shooting groups, and made operational decisions during an action. Not every killing committed by the 2nd Company or by auxiliaries from Trawniki can be attributed to Gnade as a personal shooting; his command role and specific orders are documented.
postwar_en: He did not stand trial. The sources used for this profile do not establish the date or circumstances of his death reliably; his individual responsibility was later reconstructed from the trials of other battalion members, unit records and historical research.
limitations_en: Sources differ on the precise date of the Łomazy operation and the number of people murdered; the profile therefore gives the month and explains the mechanism without constructing a victim tally. The assigned sources do not confirm the date or circumstances of Gnade's death, so the profile does not repeat as fact a secondary claim that he died during the war. Later testimony by policemen requires critical reading because of the witnesses' interests in the criminal proceedings.

name: Wolfgang Hoffmann
organization_en: Order Police · Reserve Police Battalion 101 · Police Regiment 25
organization_pl: Ordnungspolizei · 101. Rezerwowy Batalion Policji · 25. Pułk Policji
role_en: commander of the 3rd Company of Reserve Police Battalion 101
role_pl: dowódca 3. kompanii 101. Rezerwowego Batalionu Policji
role_de: Kompaniechef der 3. Kompanie des Reserve-Polizei-Bataillons 101
role_ru: командир 3-й роты 101-го резервного полицейского батальона
role_fr: commandant de la 3e compagnie du 101e bataillon de réserve de police
region_en: the Lublin District, Józefów Biłgorajski, Łomazy and Końskowola
region_pl: dystrykt lubelski · Józefów Biłgorajski · Łomazy · Końskowola
status_en: finally sentenced in West Germany to 4 years' imprisonment after a retrial; died in 1989
interpretation_en: Hoffmann illustrates a company commander's responsibility for sealing off the site of an operation, setting rules for the use of weapons and exerting pressure on subordinates. The profile presents the final outcome after appellate review and retrial rather than stopping at the harsher first-instance sentence.
postwar_en: After the war, he served in the Hamburg police; he was suspended in January 1963 and arrested in 1964. In 1968, he received eight years' imprisonment for aiding the murder of 1,810 people, but the part of the judgment concerning him was overturned. After a retrial, he was finally sentenced to four years for aiding the murder of 800 people; he was released on 16 May 1975.
limitations_en: The figures of 1,810 and 800 describe, respectively, the scope of attribution in the first judgment and in the final judgment, not the total number of victims of the 3rd Company. Witness accounts differ on details of the briefing and the opportunity to refuse; Hoffmann must also not be assigned personal commission of every act carried out by his subordinates.

name: Ernst Weis
organization_en: Order Police · Police Battalion 309 · 221st Security Division
role_en: commander of Police Battalion 309 during the attack on the Soviet Union and the Białystok massacre
role_pl: dowódca 309. Batalionu Policji podczas ataku na ZSRR i masakry w Białymstoku
role_de: Kommandeur des Polizei-Bataillons 309 beim Angriff auf die Sowjetunion und während des Massakers in Białystok
role_ru: командир 309-го полицейского батальона во время нападения на СССР и массового убийства в Белостоке
role_fr: commandant du bataillon de police 309 lors de l’attaque contre l’Union soviétique et du massacre de Białystok
region_en: Białystok, the Białystok District and occupied Soviet territories
region_pl: Białystok · okręg białostocki · tereny okupowanego ZSRR
status_en: investigated in West Germany; died in 1964 before an indictment was filed
interpretation_en: Weis is an example of a battalion commander who, before an operation, gave subordinates his own expansive interpretation of orders and issued operational assignments at Białystok. He must not, however, automatically be assigned every killing: a later court identified other officers as the direct initiators and perpetrators of the synagogue burning.
postwar_en: After the war, he did not return to active service but received a police pension. From 1960, he was a suspect in the investigation of the Białystok massacre. A court in Mönchengladbach refused to issue an arrest warrant, taking the view at that stage that he had no connection with the murders; the public prosecutor continued the investigation, which ended after his death in 1964. Weis was not a defendant in the later Wuppertal trial.
limitations_en: The refusal to issue an arrest warrant was not an acquittal, and Weis's death prevented judicial assessment of the allegations against him. The sources distinguish his orders and command presence from the direct initiative for burning the synagogue attributed to other officers. The reported number of victims concerns crimes committed by the battalion, not Weis's personal actions.

name: Max Montua
organization_en: Order Police · Warsaw Police Regiment · Police Regiment Centre
organization_pl: Ordnungspolizei · Pułk Policji Warszawa · Pułk Policji Środek
role_en: Commander of the Order Police in Warsaw, later commander of Police Regiment Centre
role_pl: dowódca Policji Porządkowej w Warszawie, następnie dowódca Pułku Policji Środek
role_de: Kommandeur der Ordnungspolizei in Warschau, anschließend Kommandeur des Polizei-Regiments Mitte
role_ru: командующий Полицией порядка в Варшаве, затем командир полицейского полка «Центр»
role_fr: commandant de la Police d’ordre à Varsovie, puis commandant du régiment de police Centre
region_en: Warsaw, Białystok, Mogilev and the rear area of Army Group Centre
region_pl: Warszawa · Białystok · Mogilew · tyły Grupy Armii Środek
status_en: died by suicide in April 1945; never tried
interpretation_en: Montua represents the regimental-command level at which an order from a Higher SS and Police Leader was converted into instructions for execution, reporting, concealing graves and managing the reactions of the perpetrators. The order of 11 July transmitted Bach-Zelewski's directive, which arose from Himmler's hierarchy; this does not remove Montua's agency in specifying and implementing the procedure.
postwar_en: He did not stand trial after the war. He died by suicide at Dahme on 20 April 1945, before the end of the war in Europe.
limitations_en: The order of 11 July 1941 transmitted an instruction from a superior commander, so the profile distinguishes the directive's source from the operational instructions signed by Montua. His participation in the Mogilev conference does not prove that he personally ordered or carried out every killing during its demonstrations or the later operations of Police Regiment Centre.

name: Gerhard Riebel
organization_en: Order Police · Police Battalion 322 · Police Regiment Centre
organization_pl: Ordnungspolizei · 322. Batalion Policji · Pułk Policji Środek
role_en: commander of the 3rd Company of Police Battalion 322, later the 9th Company of Police Regiment Centre
role_pl: dowódca 3. kompanii 322. Batalionu Policji, następnie 9. kompanii Pułku Policji Środek
role_de: Kompaniechef der 3. Kompanie des Polizei-Bataillons 322, anschließend der 9. Kompanie des Polizei-Regiments Mitte
role_ru: командир 3-й роты 322-го полицейского батальона, затем 9-й роты полицейского полка «Центр»
role_fr: commandant de la 3e compagnie du bataillon de police 322, puis de la 9e compagnie du régiment de police Centre
region_en: Białystok, Dulag 185, Mogilev and occupied Belarus
status_en: finally acquitted in West Germany in 1963–1964; date of death unknown
interpretation_en: Riebel's case makes it possible to compare a company commander's own reports with the outcome of a later trial. The reports document command responsibility and the recording of killings committed by the company, but they do not substitute for proof that he personally shot anyone; the final acquittal must be presented alongside the documents, neither suppressed nor interpreted as meaning that the events described in them did not occur.
postwar_en: He stood trial before the Freiburg Regional Court with other members of Police Battalion 322 on charges of participation in mass executions. The court acquitted him on 12 July 1963. The Federal Court of Justice rejected the prosecution's appeal on 14 January 1964, so the proceeding did not end in a conviction.
limitations_en: The company reports describe the results of collective operations and do not permit the automatic conclusion that Riebel personally killed the people listed. It is equally important to distinguish his documented signature and command function from the scope of evidence deemed sufficient in the trial, which ended in a final acquittal. His date of death has not been confirmed.

name: Paul Werner Hoppe
organization_en: SS · Concentration Camps Inspectorate · Stutthof concentration camp
organization_pl: SS · Inspekcja Obozów Koncentracyjnych · KL Stutthof
role_en: commandant of Stutthof concentration camp from September 1942 to spring 1945
role_pl: komendant KL Stutthof od września 1942 do wiosny 1945 roku
role_de: Kommandant des Konzentrationslagers Stutthof von September 1942 bis Frühjahr 1945
role_ru: комендант концлагеря Штуттгоф с сентября 1942 до весны 1945 года
role_fr: commandant du camp de concentration de Stutthof de septembre 1942 au printemps 1945
region_en: Stutthof, Gdańsk Pomerania and the Stutthof subcamp network
region_pl: Stutthof · Pomorze Gdańskie · sieć podobozów KL Stutthof
status_en: finally sentenced in West Germany to 9 years' imprisonment; died in 1974
interpretation_en: The new evidentiary core supports reconsidering a candidacy previously deferred: it comprises a specific gassing order, the organisation of forced labour and a signed evacuation order. The profile does not equate the office of commandant with personally carrying out every crime at Stutthof, and it distinguishes historically documented mechanisms from the much narrower scope of the final conviction.
postwar_en: After the war, he went into hiding and was detained in 1953. The Bochum Regional Court sentenced him in 1955 to five years and three months, but the Federal Court of Justice overturned the judgment in November 1956. At the retrial in 1957, Hoppe received nine years' imprisonment for aiding the murder of several hundred Jewish prisoners in the gas chamber. He was released before serving the full nine years and died in 1974.
limitations_en: The final 1957 judgment covered the gassing complex involving several hundred prisoners, not the camp's entire operation, its forced-labour system or the death march. The court acquitted Hoppe of allegations including forty killings by injection, ten killings with dogs and individual cases of shooting and hanging; some other execution allegations were discontinued before trial. The time at which the gassing order was given and the extent of Hoppe's subsequent supervision could not be established with complete precision.

name: Arthur Liebehenschel
organization_en: SS-WVHA · Concentration Camps Inspectorate · Auschwitz concentration camp · Lublin-Majdanek concentration camp
organization_pl: SS-WVHA · Inspekcja Obozów Koncentracyjnych · KL Auschwitz · KL Lublin-Majdanek
role_en: commandant of Auschwitz I and commander of the Auschwitz garrison, later commandant of Lublin-Majdanek concentration camp
role_pl: komendant KL Auschwitz I i komendant garnizonu Auschwitz, następnie komendant KL Lublin-Majdanek
role_de: Kommandant des Konzentrationslagers Auschwitz I und Standortältester in Auschwitz, anschließend Kommandant des Konzentrationslagers Lublin-Majdanek
role_ru: комендант концлагеря Аушвиц I и комендант гарнизона Аушвиц, затем комендант концлагеря Люблин-Майданек
role_fr: commandant d’Auschwitz I et commandant de la garnison d’Auschwitz, puis commandant du camp de concentration de Lublin-Majdanek
status_en: sentenced to death by the Supreme National Tribunal; executed in 1948
interpretation_en: Liebehenschel connects the central administration of the concentration-camp system with two commandant's offices in occupied Poland. His own order dividing work according to a racist hierarchy is especially clear evidence. The profile preserves the division of authority within the Auschwitz complex and does not automatically transfer to him all crimes committed at Birkenau or Majdanek.
postwar_en: After extradition to Poland, he was indicted with 39 other members of the Auschwitz staff before the Supreme National Tribunal in Kraków. The trial began on 24 November 1947. He was sentenced to death on 22 December and hanged at a prison in Kraków on 24 January 1948.
limitations_en: The office of commandant is not in itself proof of personally carrying out every killing. From November 1943, the Auschwitz complex was divided and Auschwitz II-Birkenau had its own commandant; the profile identifies the scope of Liebehenschel's authority without erasing that division. Nor does it state an individual victim count, which the sources used and the structure of the group trial do not allow to be established reliably.

name: Erich Mußfeldt
organization_en: SS · Lublin-Majdanek concentration camp · Sonderaktion 1005 · Auschwitz-Birkenau concentration camp
organization_pl: SS · KL Lublin-Majdanek · Sonderaktion 1005 · KL Auschwitz-Birkenau
role_en: head of the crematorium and corpse-disposal detail at Lublin-Majdanek concentration camp, later a crematoria supervisor at Auschwitz-Birkenau
role_pl: kierownik krematorium i komanda usuwającego zwłoki w KL Lublin-Majdanek, następnie nadzorca krematoriów w Auschwitz-Birkenau
role_de: Leiter des Krematoriums und des Leichenkommandos im Konzentrationslager Lublin-Majdanek, anschließend Aufseher der Krematorien in Auschwitz-Birkenau
role_ru: начальник крематория и команды по удалению тел в концлагере Люблин-Майданек, затем надзиратель крематориев в Аушвице-Биркенау
role_fr: chef du crématoire et du kommando chargé de l’élimination des corps au camp de concentration de Lublin-Majdanek, puis responsable de la surveillance des crématoires à Auschwitz-Birkenau
status_en: sentenced to death by the Supreme National Tribunal; executed in 1948
interpretation_en: Mußfeldt represents a technical and operational link in mass murder: managing prisoner details, operating crematoria, exhuming and destroying bodies. This agency must be distinguished from issuing the order to shoot during Aktion Erntefest, which came from a higher level.
postwar_en: After the war, he was tried in Kraków with other members of the Auschwitz staff. The Supreme National Tribunal found him guilty in the first Auschwitz trial and sentenced him to death on 22 December 1947. He was hanged at a prison in Kraków on 24 January 1948.
limitations_en: Sources use the spellings Mußfeld, Muhsfeldt and Mussfeldt; these are orthographic variants referring to the same person, not pseudonyms. Some technical details derive from postwar statements by Mußfeldt and his subordinates, given in their own interests during criminal proceedings, and therefore require comparison with camp documentation. The profile does not attribute to him the order to begin Aktion Erntefest and does not construct a personal victim tally.

name: Hellmuth Holland
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: German Public Prosecutor's Office in Piotrków · Sondergericht Petrikau · German judiciary in the General Government
organization_pl: Niemiecka Prokuratura w Piotrkowie · Sondergericht Petrikau · niemiecki wymiar sprawiedliwości w Generalnym Gubernatorstwie
role_en: head of the German Public Prosecutor's Office in Piotrków and prosecutor before the Special Court in Piotrków
role_pl: kierownik Niemieckiej Prokuratury w Piotrkowie i oskarżyciel przed Sądem Specjalnym w Piotrkowie
role_de: Leiter der Deutschen Staatsanwaltschaft in Petrikau und Ankläger vor dem Sondergericht Petrikau
role_ru: руководитель германской прокуратуры в Пётркуве и прокурор при специальном суде в Пётркуве
role_fr: chef du parquet allemand de Piotrków et procureur devant le tribunal spécial de Piotrków
region_en: Piotrków Trybunalski, Tomaszów Mazowiecki and the Radom District
region_pl: Piotrków Trybunalski · Tomaszów Mazowiecki · dystrykt radomski
status_en: convicted twice in Poland; aggregate sentence of 8 years; worked in the West German judiciary after release
interpretation_en: This profile shows how the head of a local public prosecutor's office transformed discriminatory occupation legislation into indictments, demands for death sentences and a prosecutor's participation in executions. It does not attribute to Holland every ruling by the Sondergericht Petrikau or every act of the district's prison, police and administration.
postwar_en: In 1949 he was sentenced to six years' imprisonment. In a separate case in 1954, he received eight years, and the aggregate sentence was eight years; according to the surviving files, he most probably left prison on 21 March 1956. He returned to the West German judiciary. A proceeding initiated in Freiburg in connection with the case of Jan Stępniewski was discontinued in 1979 because Holland was unfit to stand trial.
limitations_en: His date of death has not been confirmed in the sources used. The first court did not find proven, among other allegations, that he starved prisoners, sent Poles to concentration camps without grounds or committed some of the alleged arrest-related acts; these must not be included in the biography as facts. The findings concern specific acts adjudicated in two trials, not the entire work of the Piotrków special court.

name: Gerhard Pchalek
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Special Court in Bielitz · Special Court in Kattowitz · Office of the General Prosecutor in Kattowitz
organization_pl: Sondergericht Bielitz · Sondergericht Kattowitz · Generalstaatsanwaltschaft Kattowitz
role_en: prosecutor before the special courts in Bielitz and Kattowitz and at the Office of the General Prosecutor attached to the Higher Regional Court in Kattowitz
role_pl: prokurator przed sądami specjalnymi w Bielsku i Katowicach oraz w prokuraturze przy Wyższym Sądzie Krajowym w Katowicach
role_de: Staatsanwalt bei den Sondergerichten Bielitz und Kattowitz sowie bei der Generalstaatsanwaltschaft am Oberlandesgericht Kattowitz
role_ru: прокурор при специальных судах в Билице и Каттовице и в Генеральной прокуратуре при Высшем земельном суде в Каттовице
role_fr: procureur devant les tribunaux spéciaux de Bielitz et de Kattowitz ainsi qu’au parquet général près le tribunal régional supérieur de Kattowitz
status_en: sentenced in East Germany to 4 years; conditionally released in 1962
interpretation_en: The profile presents the prosecutor as an active link between racial criminal law, the selection of charges, demands for a particular sanction and extraordinary increases in sentences. It does not make Pchalek responsible for every ruling by the courts in Bielitz and Kattowitz or for acts committed by other prosecutors.
postwar_en: After the war, he continued his career in Thuringia: he headed the public prosecutor's office in Gera, served as acting state general prosecutor and became professor of criminal law at Jena. He was arrested in 1959 and sentenced to four years' imprisonment in 1960. He was conditionally released in June 1962 and died in 1980.
limitations_en: Individual attribution rests on the twenty cases identified in the Gera judgment, not the aggregate activity of the special courts. Pchalek was not a member of the NSDAP, so his responsibility must not be inferred from party membership. The proceeding took place in the political context of East Germany; the profile should present both the documentary evidence and legal classification as aiding murder, as well as the context of the trial and his early release.

name: Kurt Bode
organization_en: Group Eberhardt field court · Higher Regional Court in Danzig · Office of the General Prosecutor for Danzig–West Prussia
organization_pl: sąd polowy Grupy Eberhardta · Oberlandesgericht Danzig · Generalstaatsanwaltschaft Danzig-Westpreußen
role_en: presiding judge of the field court in the trials of the Polish Post Office defenders, later general prosecutor of the Reich District of Danzig–West Prussia
role_pl: przewodniczący sądu polowego w procesach obrońców Poczty Polskiej, następnie prokurator generalny Okręgu Rzeszy Gdańsk–Prusy Zachodnie
role_de: Vorsitzender des Feldgerichts in den Prozessen gegen die Verteidiger der Polnischen Post, später Generalstaatsanwalt des Reichsgaus Danzig–Westpreußen
role_ru: председатель полевого суда на процессах защитников Польской почты, позднее генеральный прокурор рейхсгау Данциг—Западная Пруссия
role_fr: président du tribunal de campagne lors des procès des défenseurs de la Poste polonaise, puis procureur général du Reichsgau Dantzig–Prusse-Occidentale
region_en: Gdańsk, Gdańsk Pomerania and the Reich District of Danzig–West Prussia
region_pl: Gdańsk · Pomorze Gdańskie · Reichsgau Gdańsk–Prusy Zachodnie
status_en: never convicted; pursued a postwar judicial career in West Germany; died in 1979
interpretation_en: Bode combines two levels of judicial crime in one profile: his personal role as presiding judge in the unlawful trials of September 1939 and his later leadership of the regional public prosecution service. The profile does not turn the number of cases passing through the office into an automatic list of judgments personally drafted or approved by Bode.
postwar_en: After Soviet captivity, he underwent denazification and returned to the West German judiciary, eventually becoming vice president of the Higher Regional Court in Bremen. Public prosecutors repeatedly examined his involvement in sentencing the defenders of the Polish Post Office, but he was neither indicted nor convicted during his lifetime. He died in 1979; the unlawful judgments were not overturned until after his death.
limitations_en: Bode's personal role in the two trials of September 1939 is well documented. The approximate figure of 350 judgments concerns the apparatus's activity during his tenure and does not prove the same degree of involvement in every case. The destruction of some files limits a full reconstruction of decisions by the regional prosecution service, so the profile should not produce a closed tally of cases or victims.

name: Rudolf Creutz
organization_en: RKFDV Main Staff Office · SS · germanisation and resettlement apparatus
organization_pl: Stabshauptamt RKFDV · SS · aparat germanizacji i przesiedleń
role_en: Ulrich Greifelt's deputy and head of Main Office Group A in the Main Staff Office of the Reich Commissioner for the Consolidation of German Nationhood
role_pl: zastępca Ulricha Greifelta i szef Amtsgruppe A w Głównym Urzędzie Sztabowym Komisarza Rzeszy do spraw Umacniania Niemczyzny
role_de: Stellvertreter Ulrich Greifelts und Leiter der Amtsgruppe A im Stabshauptamt des Reichskommissars für die Festigung deutschen Volkstums
role_ru: заместитель Ульриха Грайфельта и начальник группы главных управлений A в Главном штабном управлении рейхскомиссара по укреплению германства
role_fr: adjoint d’Ulrich Greifelt et chef de l’Amtsgruppe A au sein de l’Office central d’état-major du Commissaire du Reich pour la consolidation de la germanité
region_en: Berlin, Polish territories annexed to the Reich and occupied territories of Europe
region_pl: Berlin · ziemie polskie wcielone do Rzeszy · okupowane terytoria Europy
