status_en: sentenced to 15 years; sentence reduced; released in 1951
interpretation_en: Creutz illustrates the central level at which personnel decisions, instructions and RKFDV coordination linked expulsions, racial selection, the germanisation of children and the exploitation of labour. His responsibility follows from the judgment's findings concerning specific mechanisms, not solely from his SS rank or position as Greifelt's deputy.
postwar_en: In the RuSHA trial, he was sentenced in 1948 to fifteen years' imprisonment. The sentence was later reduced to ten years, and he was released in 1951. He died in Vienna in 1980.
limitations_en: The tribunal considered the evidence insufficient to attribute to Creutz forced abortions on Eastern workers, the removal of infants from women workers, punishment of foreigners for sexual relations with Germans, or measures to suppress reproduction. These allegations must not be presented as findings of the judgment. Nor does the profile automatically attribute to him every action of the RKFDV, RuSHA or field resettlement offices.

name: Fritz Schwalm
organization_en: SS Race and Settlement Main Office · Central Immigration Office in Litzmannstadt · SS
organization_pl: Rasse- und Siedlungshauptamt SS · Einwandererzentralstelle Litzmannstadt · SS
role_en: chief RuSHA representative at the Central Immigration Office in Łódź, later chief of staff of RuSHA
role_pl: główny przedstawiciel RuSHA przy Centrali Imigracyjnej w Łodzi, później szef sztabu RuSHA
role_de: Hauptbeauftragter des RuSHA bei der Einwandererzentralstelle in Łódź, später Stabschef des RuSHA
role_ru: главный представитель RuSHA при Центральном иммиграционном управлении в Лодзи, позднее начальник штаба RuSHA
role_fr: principal représentant du RuSHA auprès de l’Office central d’immigration à Łódź, puis chef d’état-major du RuSHA
region_en: Łódź, the Wartheland and Polish territories annexed to the Reich
region_pl: Łódź · Kraj Warty · ziemie polskie wcielone do Rzeszy
status_en: sentenced to 10 years; released early in 1951
interpretation_en: The profile explains the Łódź link in racial selection: translating decisions on expulsion and germanisation into examinations, classifications and assignments of specific people and children. It does not reduce Schwalm's responsibility to his post alone, but grounds it in four mechanisms expressly attributed to him by the tribunal.
postwar_en: A U.S. military tribunal sentenced him in 1948 to ten years' imprisonment. He was released early from Landsberg prison on 1 February 1951. He died in Marburg in 1985.
limitations_en: The judgment found the evidence concerning the indictment's remaining allegations insufficient; Schwalm's responsibility therefore must not be extended beyond the four specified mechanisms. Service on Friedrich Jeckeln's staff alone is not, in these materials, a sufficient basis for attributing to him personal participation in mass executions in the Ostland and has not been included among the confirmed findings.

name: Friedrich Flick
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Friedrich Flick KG · Flick concern · Friends of the Reich Leader SS
organization_pl: Friedrich Flick KG · koncern Flicka · Freundeskreis Reichsführer-SS
role_en: owner and dominant head of the Flick concern, one of the Reich's principal heavy-industry and armaments complexes
role_pl: właściciel i dominujący kierownik koncernu Flicka, jednego z głównych kompleksów przemysłu ciężkiego i zbrojeniowego Rzeszy
role_de: Eigentümer und maßgeblicher Leiter des Flick-Konzerns, eines der wichtigsten Schwerindustrie- und Rüstungskomplexe des Reiches
role_ru: владелец и фактический глава концерна Флика, одного из главных комплексов тяжёлой и военной промышленности рейха
role_fr: propriétaire et principal dirigeant du groupe Flick, l’un des principaux complexes d’industrie lourde et d’armement du Reich
region_en: the German Reich, occupied territories of Europe and Upper Silesia
region_pl: Rzesza Niemiecka · okupowane terytoria Europy · Górny Śląsk
status_en: sentenced to 7 years; released early in 1950
interpretation_en: The profile presents an economic chain of agency: ownership and management decisions enabled the procurement of forced labour, exploitation of plants in occupied territories and financing of the SS. It does not automatically transfer to Flick every abuse committed at every plant or the responsibility of state offices that allocated workers.
postwar_en: In the Flick trial, he was found guilty on Counts One, Two and Four and sentenced to seven years' imprisonment. He was released early in 1950. He subsequently rebuilt the concern in West Germany and died in 1972.
limitations_en: The judgment did not cover the full catalogue of allegations: the count concerning acquisitions of Jewish enterprises before the war was dismissed on jurisdictional and evidentiary grounds, while the property-exploitation conviction concerned the Rombach works specifically. The indictment must not be presented as equivalent to the judgment, nor should Flick be assigned every act of plant managers. The attempted acquisition of Bismarckhütte in occupied Katowice did not result in the Flick concern taking over the plant.

name: Georg-Hans Reinhardt
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Wehrmacht · 3rd Panzer Army · Army Group Centre
role_en: commander of the 3rd Panzer Group, subsequently the 3rd Panzer Army, and acting commander of Army Group Centre
role_pl: dowódca 3. Grupy Pancernej, następnie 3. Armii Pancernej i pełniący obowiązki dowódcy Grupy Armii „Środek”
role_de: Befehlshaber der 3. Panzergruppe, anschließend der 3. Panzerarmee, und mit der Führung der Heeresgruppe Mitte beauftragt
role_ru: командующий 3-й танковой группой, затем 3-й танковой армией и исполняющий обязанности командующего группой армий «Центр»
role_fr: commandant du 3e groupe blindé, puis de la 3e armée blindée, et commandant par intérim du groupe d’armées Centre
region_en: Belarus, western Russia and the rear area of the Eastern Front
region_pl: Białoruś · zachodnia Rosja · zaplecze frontu wschodniego
status_en: sentenced to 15 years' imprisonment; released in 1952
interpretation_en: Reinhardt's profile shows the passage from a central order into army circulation, the practice of subordinate corps and reports available to the commander. It does not automatically attribute to him every crime of the 3rd Panzer Army or the whole of Army Group Centre.
postwar_en: An American military tribunal found Reinhardt guilty of war crimes and crimes against humanity and sentenced him to fifteen years' imprisonment. A Bundesarchiv register states that he was released in 1952; he died in 1963.
limitations_en: The tribunal acquitted him of crimes against peace. The material does not establish that he personally read every report on the selection of prisoners of war, and the judgment noted that he did not transmit the Reichenau Order and later ordered that parachutists be treated as lawful combatants. These boundaries must not be blurred or command responsibility turned into a claim that he personally carried out every crime.

name: Karl von Roques
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Wehrmacht · Army Group South Rear Area · Army Group A Rear Area
organization_pl: Wehrmacht · Tyłowy Obszar Grupy Armii „Południe” · Tyłowy Obszar Grupy Armii A
role_en: commander of the Army Group South Rear Area, subsequently the Army Group A Rear Area
role_pl: dowódca tyłowego obszaru Grupy Armii „Południe”, następnie tyłowego obszaru Grupy Armii A
role_de: Befehlshaber des rückwärtigen Heeresgebiets der Heeresgruppe Süd, anschließend des rückwärtigen Heeresgebiets der Heeresgruppe A
role_ru: командующий тыловым районом группы армий «Юг», затем тыловым районом группы армий «А»
role_fr: commandant de la zone arrière du groupe d’armées Sud, puis de celle du groupe d’armées A
region_en: Ukraine, the Caucasus and the rear area of Army Group South
status_en: sentenced to 20 years; died while serving his sentence in 1949
interpretation_en: Roques represents the military administrator of a vast rear area who held executive authority over occupied territory and connected command offices, security units, and the SS and SD. The profile bases responsibility on orders transmitted, reports received and cooperation, rather than on his title of commander alone.
postwar_en: In the High Command Trial he was found guilty of war crimes and crimes against humanity and sentenced to twenty years' imprisonment. He died of natural causes on 24 December 1949 while serving his sentence, in the municipal hospital at Landsberg.
limitations_en: Although Roques transmitted the order of 1 October 1941, the trial material did not establish that hostages were shot in his area under that order. Nor was he charged under every category concerning forced labour and civilians. The profile cannot transfer to him every crime of the SS, SD or all units operating in the rear area.

name: Max von Schenckendorff
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Wehrmacht · Army Group Centre Rear Area · rear-area security forces
organization_pl: Wehrmacht · Tyłowy Obszar Grupy Armii „Środek” · wojska zabezpieczające zaplecze
role_en: commander of the Army Group Centre Rear Area and organiser of the anti-partisan conference in Mogilev
role_pl: dowódca tyłowego obszaru Grupy Armii „Środek” i organizator konferencji antypartyzanckiej w Mohylewie
role_de: Befehlshaber des rückwärtigen Heeresgebiets der Heeresgruppe Mitte und Organisator der Antipartisanenkonferenz in Mogilew
role_ru: командующий тыловым районом группы армий «Центр» и организатор антипартизанской конференции в Могилёве
role_fr: commandant de la zone arrière du groupe d’armées Centre et organisateur de la conférence sur la lutte contre les partisans à Moguilev
region_en: Belarus, Mogilev and the rear area of Army Group Centre
status_en: died in 1943; never tried
interpretation_en: The Mogilev conference shows how rear-area command translated the racist identification of Jews with partisans into joint Wehrmacht, SS and SD training, a field demonstration and material circulated to lower echelons. The profile does not turn this documented transmission of doctrine into automatic attribution to Schenckendorff of every later execution.
postwar_en: He was never tried. He died in 1943, before the end of the war and before the establishment of the postwar tribunals.
limitations_en: The sources permit precise attribution to him of convening the conference, its tone, circulation of its report and authority over the area. They do not prove that he personally fired shots during the demonstration or justify assigning him an aggregate number for all victims of rear-area units. The cause-of-death field remains empty because the institutional sources used in the record confirm the year but do not consistently document a medical cause.

name: Franz Magill
organization_en: 2nd SS Cavalry Regiment · SS Cavalry Brigade · Kommandostab Reichsführer-SS
organization_pl: 2. Pułk Kawalerii SS · Brygada Kawalerii SS · Kommandostab Reichsführer-SS
role_en: commander of a mounted detachment of the 2nd SS Cavalry Regiment during mass executions in Polesia
role_pl: dowódca konnego oddziału 2. Pułku Kawalerii SS podczas masowych egzekucji na Polesiu
role_de: Befehlshaber einer berittenen Abteilung des 2. SS-Kavallerie-Regiments während der Massenerschießungen in Polesien
role_ru: командир конного отряда 2-го кавалерийского полка СС во время массовых расстрелов на Полесье
role_fr: commandant d’un détachement monté du 2e régiment de cavalerie SS lors d’exécutions de masse en Polésie
region_en: Pinsk, Ivanava and the Pripyat Marshes
status_en: sentenced in 1964 to five years' penal servitude
interpretation_en: Magill shows the middle echelon at which Himmler's order was transmitted to squadrons, coordinated with the SD and accounted for in a report. The numbers in the profile are findings of a specific judgment and document, not a victim ranking or a closed total of the unit's crimes.
postwar_en: Following postwar proceedings in West Germany, Braunschweig Regional Court sentenced Magill on 20 April 1964 to five years' penal servitude for aiding and abetting murder and attempted murder. Pretrial detention was credited toward the sentence; in Magill's case no appeal was filed or it was withdrawn. He died in 1972.
limitations_en: The West German judgment applied the category of aiding and abetting, so the profile preserves that legal classification rather than calling Magill the personal perpetrator of every murder. The judicial minimum findings do not cover the full activity of the SS cavalry, and a document signed by the commander does not establish at which executions he was physically present. The number of years actually served is left blank in the absence of separate sentence-enforcement documentation.

name: Hermann Reinecke
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Oberkommando der Wehrmacht · Allgemeines Wehrmachtamt · Chief of Prisoner-of-War Affairs
organization_pl: Oberkommando der Wehrmacht · Allgemeines Wehrmachtamt · Chef des Kriegsgefangenenwesens
role_en: head of the Allgemeines Wehrmachtamt in the OKW, responsible for central directives concerning prisoners of war
role_pl: szef Allgemeines Wehrmachtamt w OKW, odpowiedzialny za centralne dyrektywy dotyczące jeńców wojennych
role_de: Chef des Allgemeinen Wehrmachtamts im OKW, verantwortlich für zentrale Richtlinien zu Kriegsgefangenen
role_ru: начальник Общего управления вермахта в OKW, отвечавший за центральные директивы в отношении военнопленных
role_fr: chef de l’Allgemeines Wehrmachtamt au sein de l’OKW, chargé des directives centrales relatives aux prisonniers de guerre
region_en: the German Reich, the General Government and occupied Europe
region_pl: Rzesza Niemiecka · Generalne Gubernatorstwo · okupowana Europa
status_en: sentenced to life imprisonment in 1948; released early in October 1954
interpretation_en: Reinecke explains the central mechanism in which administrative forms, inspections, camp regulations and selection connected the OKW to the Gestapo and SD. The profile does not reduce responsibility to subordination to Keitel, but grounds it in Reinecke's own role in drafting, signing and supervising directives.
postwar_en: In the High Command Trial he was found guilty of war crimes and crimes against humanity and sentenced to life imprisonment. He was released early from Landsberg Prison in October 1954 and died in 1973.
limitations_en: The tribunal did not establish his connection to the implementation of the Commando Order or responsibility for the forced use of civilians as labour. Nor did it attribute to him participation in the Einsatzgruppen's overall programme of persecution and execution of Jews. The profile is limited to the findings concerning the prisoner-of-war system, selection, directives and the Commissar Order.

name: Walter Warlimont
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Oberkommando der Wehrmacht · Wehrmacht Operations Staff · National Defence Department
organization_pl: Oberkommando der Wehrmacht · Wehrmachtführungsstab · Wydział Obrony Krajowej
role_en: head of the National Defence Department and deputy chief of the Wehrmacht Operations Staff in the OKW
role_pl: szef Wydziału Obrony Krajowej i zastępca szefa Sztabu Operacyjnego Wehrmachtu w OKW
role_de: Chef der Abteilung Landesverteidigung und stellvertretender Chef des Wehrmachtführungsstabs im OKW
role_ru: начальник Отдела обороны страны и заместитель начальника Штаба оперативного руководства вермахта в OKW
role_fr: chef du service de la Défense nationale et chef adjoint de l’état-major des opérations de la Wehrmacht au sein de l’OKW
region_en: Berlin, Führer Headquarters and the European theatres under the OKW
region_pl: Berlin · Kwatera Główna Führera · europejskie teatry działań OKW
status_en: sentenced to life imprisonment; commuted to 18 years; released in 1954
interpretation_en: Warlimont shows the staff as an operative stage between ideological intent, drafting, signature, circulation and implementation of an order. The profile does not present him as the author of every idea advanced by Hitler or Keitel, but precisely describes the contribution that the tribunal found substantial.
postwar_en: In the High Command Trial he was sentenced to life imprisonment. The sentence was later commuted to eighteen years, and the Northern Ireland Screen archive records his release in 1954. He died in 1976.
limitations_en: The tribunal did not establish a criminal connection between him and the Night and Fog programme or the Einsatzgruppen's general programme of persecuting and executing Jews. Nor was he found responsible for every category of prohibited labour. The profile must preserve the distinction between the initiator of an idea, a staff officer who helped draft the text, and a field-level executor.

name: Rudolf Lehmann
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Oberkommando der Wehrmacht · OKW Legal Department · military legal apparatus
organization_pl: Oberkommando der Wehrmacht · Wehrmachtrechtsabteilung · wojskowy aparat prawny
role_en: head of the OKW Legal Department and Generaloberstabsrichter, a co-architect of the legal framework for wartime terror
role_pl: szef Wydziału Prawnego OKW i Generaloberstabsrichter, współtwórca prawnych ram terroru wojennego
role_de: Chef der Rechtsabteilung des OKW und Generaloberstabsrichter, Mitgestalter der rechtlichen Rahmenbedingungen des Kriegsterrors
role_ru: начальник Правового отдела OKW и генерал-обер-штабс-судья, соавтор правовых рамок военного террора
role_fr: chef du service juridique de l’OKW et Generaloberstabsrichter, l’un des architectes du cadre juridique de la terreur en temps de guerre
region_en: Berlin, the Eastern Front and occupied Western Europe
region_pl: Berlin · front wschodni · okupowana Europa Zachodnia
status_en: sentenced to seven years; released early in 1950
interpretation_en: Lehmann shows that legal drafting was not a neutral technique: it removed judicial review, created procedures for the secret disappearance of prisoners and put orders into a form ready for transmission. The profile does not equate this responsibility before the act with personally carrying out executions.
postwar_en: An American military tribunal sentenced him to seven years' imprisonment in the High Command Trial. An archived JTA dispatch from August 1950 recorded his early release for good conduct. He died in 1955.
limitations_en: The tribunal did not claim that Lehmann personally issued orders to shoot civilians or himself transported Night and Fog prisoners. His alteration to the text of the Commissar Order was immaterial and did not constitute a material contribution. The profile should present responsibility for specific legal work, not for the entire military justice system.

name: Wilhelm List
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Wehrmacht · 12th Army · Wehrmacht Commander Southeast
role_en: commander of the 12th Army and Wehrmacht Commander Southeast during the occupation of Yugoslavia and Greece
role_pl: dowódca 12. Armii i Wehrmachtbefehlshaber Südost podczas okupacji Jugosławii i Grecji
role_de: Oberbefehlshaber der 12. Armee und Wehrmachtbefehlshaber Südost während der Besetzung Jugoslawiens und Griechenlands
role_ru: командующий 12-й армией и вермахтом на Юго-Востоке во время оккупации Югославии и Греции
role_fr: commandant de la 12e armée et commandant de la Wehrmacht pour le Sud-Est pendant l’occupation de la Yougoslavie et de la Grèce
main_region_country: Serbia i Grecja (okupowana Jugosławia i Grecja)
status_en: sentenced to life imprisonment in 1948; released early in December 1952
interpretation_en: List shows the chain from a theatre commander, through the delegation of full executive authority to the commander in Serbia, to reports of executions and failure to intervene. The profile does not attribute to him the personal signing of every reprisal order or the physical execution of the shootings.
postwar_en: In the Hostages Trial before an American military tribunal, List was found guilty on two counts concerning war crimes and sentenced to life imprisonment. He was released early in December 1952 on health grounds and died in 1971.
limitations_en: The tribunal found no proof that List personally signed a specific order to kill hostages or fixed reprisal ratios. It did not convict him of implementing the Commissar Order or for the execution of captured partisans, whose legal status it assessed under a contemporary doctrine that is disputed today. The profile must clearly present these historical limits of the judgment.

name: Harald Turner
organization_en: Military Administration in Serbia · SS · German occupation administration in Serbia
organization_pl: Militärverwaltung in Serbien · SS · niemiecka administracja okupacyjna w Serbii
role_en: chief of the administrative staff of the German military commander in occupied Serbia
role_pl: szef sztabu administracyjnego niemieckiego dowódcy wojskowego w okupowanej Serbii
role_de: Chef des Verwaltungsstabes beim deutschen Militärbefehlshaber im besetzten Serbien
role_ru: начальник административного штаба германского военного командующего в оккупированной Сербии
role_fr: chef de l’état-major administratif du commandant militaire allemand en Serbie occupée
status_en: sentenced to death in Belgrade; executed on 9 March 1947
interpretation_en: Turner reveals a civil-military node of occupation: administration, field command offices, collaborationist police, the SD, camps and the logistics of killing. His own reports and letter go beyond responsibility based on office alone, but do not make him the sole executor of every shooting and gassing in Serbia.
postwar_en: After extradition to Yugoslavia he was tried before a military court in Belgrade from 27 February to 3 March 1947. He was sentenced to death by hanging, and the judgment was carried out on 9 March 1947.
limitations_en: In Serbia the powers of the Wehrmacht commander, administrative staff, Einsatzgruppe, HSSPF, SD, police and collaborationist authorities overlapped; profiles cannot transfer the acts of one institution to Turner without documentary support. The April 1942 letter is his own account and evidence of knowledge and active coordination, but it must be read alongside the records and chronology of the camp's transfer to Meyszner.

name: Lothar Heimbach
organization_en: Gestapo · KdS Białystok · Security Police and SD
organization_pl: Gestapo · KdS Białystok · Sipo i SD
role_en: head of Department IV (Gestapo) at KdS Białystok
role_pl: kierownik Oddziału IV (Gestapo) przy KdS Białystok
role_de: Leiter der Abteilung IV (Gestapo) beim KdS Białystok
role_ru: начальник отдела IV (гестапо) при KdS Белосток
role_fr: chef du département IV (Gestapo) du KdS Białystok
main_region_country: Okręg Białystok — okupowana Polska; część obszaru leży dziś w Białorusi
status_en: sentenced to nine years; released after credit for approximately four years in pretrial detention; died in 1968
interpretation_en: Heimbach shows how the head of a Gestapo department linked KdS instructions with the sections responsible for Jewish affairs, prisons and executions. The profile rests on acts individualised by the court, not on his office alone.
postwar_en: Bielefeld Regional Court sentenced Heimbach on 14 April 1967 to nine years' penal servitude for aiding collective murder and participating in a reprisal execution; after receiving credit for pretrial detention, he was released in January 1968. He died on 8 December 1968.
limitations_en: The judgment did not confirm every allegation in the indictment. The profile does not automatically attribute to Heimbach every deportation, pacification or execution by KdS Białystok; it separates the court's findings from the wider organisational context. Press accounts in 1967 reported conflicting sentence lengths, so the record adopts nine years from the judgment and the later account of his release.

name: Karl Pütz
organization_en: KdS Rivne · KdS Lublin · Security Police and SD
organization_pl: KdS Równe · KdS Lublin · Sipo i SD
role_en: commander of the Security Police and SD in Rivne, subsequently in Lublin
role_pl: komendant Policji Bezpieczeństwa i SD w Równem, następnie w Lublinie
role_de: Kommandeur der Sicherheitspolizei und des SD in Rowno, anschließend in Lublin
role_ru: командир Полиции безопасности и СД в Ровно, затем в Люблине
role_fr: commandant de la Police de sûreté et du SD à Rivne, puis à Lublin
region_en: Rivne, Volhynia–Podolia, Lublin and the Lublin District
main_region_country: Wołyń–Podole i dystrykt lubelski — okupowana Ukraina i Polska
status_en: never tried; died by suicide on 6 May 1945
interpretation_en: The profile shows a regional commander connecting a Security Police office to mass-murder operations and hostage terror. The strongest personal trace is the signed notice; for Erntefest and Mizoch the wording must refer to his documented place in the chain of command, not to killing with his own hands.
postwar_en: Pütz never stood trial. On 6 May 1945, near St. Märgen, he died by suicide by shooting himself with his service pistol; this finding rests on a surviving police report and a photograph of his body.
limitations_en: The signature on the notice proves official responsibility for announcing the execution, not that Pütz alone made the entire decision. Subordination of units does not justify attributing every one of their acts to him. The circumstances of the suicide are established by a later police report and photographic documentation, not by criminal proceedings against Pütz.

name: Gerhard Flesch
organization_en: Einsatzgruppe VI · Łódź Gestapo · KdS Bergen · KdS Trondheim
organization_pl: Einsatzgruppe VI · Gestapo Łódź · KdS Bergen · KdS Trondheim
role_en: commander of Einsatzkommando 2/VI and first head of the Gestapo in Łódź, later KdS in Bergen and Trondheim
role_pl: dowódca Einsatzkommando 2/VI i pierwszy szef Gestapo w Łodzi, następnie KdS w Bergen i Trondheim
role_de: Führer des Einsatzkommandos 2/VI und erster Leiter der Gestapo in Łódź, anschließend KdS in Bergen und Trondheim
role_ru: командир айнзацкоманды 2/VI и первый начальник гестапо в Лодзи, затем KdS в Бергене и Тронхейме
role_fr: commandant de l’Einsatzkommando 2/VI et premier chef de la Gestapo à Łódź, puis KdS à Bergen et à Trondheim
region_en: Poznań, Łódź, Bergen, Trondheim and Falstad
main_region_country: Łódź — okupowana Polska; Bergen i Trondheim — okupowana Norwegia
status_en: sentenced to death in Norway and shot on 28 February 1948
interpretation_en: Flesch shows the transfer of regional Gestapo personnel from occupied Poland to an extensive apparatus of prisons, a camp and interrogations in Norway. The crimes individualised by the judgment concern Norway; the Łódź phase reconstructs his career and institutional continuity, rather than automatically attributing every act of the Łódź Gestapo to him.
postwar_en: Frostating Court of Appeal found Flesch guilty on 2 December 1946 of most of the murder and torture charges and sentenced him to death by firing squad. The Supreme Court of Norway unanimously dismissed the appeal on 12 February 1948. The sentence was carried out on 28 February 1948.
limitations_en: The Norwegian judgment expressly distinguished proven acts from two counts ending in acquittal; the profile must preserve that distinction. No equivalent judgment individualising his actions in Łódź was found, so the full terror of that office cannot be attributed to him.

name: Rudolf Batz
organization_en: Einsatzkommando 2 · Einsatzgruppe A · KdS Kraków · Dortmund Security Police
organization_pl: Einsatzkommando 2 · Einsatzgruppe A · KdS Kraków · Sipo Dortmund
role_en: commander of Einsatzkommando 2, subsequently KdS in Kraków and commander of the Security Police in Dortmund
role_pl: dowódca Einsatzkommando 2, następnie KdS w Krakowie i dowódca Sipo w Dortmundzie
role_de: Führer des Einsatzkommandos 2, anschließend KdS in Krakau und Befehlshaber der Sicherheitspolizei in Dortmund
role_ru: командир айнзацкоманды 2, затем KdS в Кракове и командир Полиции безопасности в Дортмунде
role_fr: commandant de l’Einsatzkommando 2, puis KdS à Cracovie et commandant de la Police de sûreté à Dortmund
main_region_country: Łotwa; Kraków — okupowana Polska; Dortmund — Niemcy
status_en: arrested and investigated; died by suicide in custody before trial
interpretation_en: The dossier connects two individualised links: the order to send a unit to Jelgava and the initiation of the prisoner-review procedure in Dortmund. Command alone must not be used to infer responsibility for every execution by Einsatzkommando 2, KdS Kraków or the Dortmund Gestapo.
postwar_en: After the war he lived under an assumed name. He was arrested on 11 November 1960 in connection with Einsatzkommando 2 and mass executions. On 8 February 1961 he died by suicide in custody; there was no trial or judgment.
limitations_en: The Yad Vashem material links an executor's testimony to the contents of the indictment, but Batz died before the evidence could be assessed at his own trial. For Dortmund, his order to review prisoners and his place on the decision-making committee are documented; the profile does not automatically attribute every killing committed by personnel of the office to him.

name: Martin Fellenz
organization_en: SS and Police Leader Kraków · SS and police in the Kraków District
organization_pl: SSPF Kraków · SS i policja dystryktu krakowskiego
role_en: chief of staff to the SS and Police Leader in the Kraków District, directing the field organisation of deportations
role_pl: szef sztabu dowódcy SS i Policji w dystrykcie krakowskim, kierujący terenową organizacją deportacji
role_de: Stabschef des SS- und Polizeiführers im Distrikt Krakau, der die operative Durchführung von Deportationen vor Ort leitete
role_ru: начальник штаба руководителя СС и полиции в Краковском дистрикте, руководивший организацией депортаций на местах
role_fr: chef d’état-major du chef de la SS et de la police dans le district de Cracovie, chargé de diriger sur le terrain l’organisation des déportations
region_en: Kraków, Miechow, Przemyśl, Rzeszow and Tarnów
status_en: sentenced to seven years; released after credit for approximately five years in pretrial detention
interpretation_en: Fellenz is a profile of logistical command over deportation: it connects the SS and Police Leader's staff, field delegates, on-site selection and transport to an extermination centre. The judgment makes it possible to separate responsibility for organisation from unproven allegations that he killed people with his own hands.
postwar_en: The first four-year sentence imposed in 1963 was set aside by the Federal Court of Justice. In the retrial, Kiel Regional Court sentenced Fellenz on 27 January 1966 to seven years' penal servitude for aiding murder in four deportation complexes. Credit for approximately five years of pretrial detention and his release after the judgment meant that he did not serve the full sentence.
limitations_en: The profile is based on the scope of the final second judgment. It does not retain allegations of individual shootings that the court did not find proven and does not attribute to Fellenz sole responsibility for planning the entire Holocaust in the district. The sources differ on his exact date of death, so only the year 2007 is given.

name: Max Pauly
organization_en: Stutthof concentration camp · Neuengamme concentration camp · SS-WVHA
role_en: commandant of Stutthof concentration camp, subsequently Neuengamme concentration camp and its satellite-camp network
role_pl: komendant KL Stutthof, następnie KL Neuengamme i jego sieci podobozów
role_de: Kommandant des KL Stutthof, anschließend des KL Neuengamme und seines Außenlagernetzes
role_ru: комендант концлагеря Штуттгоф, затем концлагеря Нойенгамме и сети его филиалов
role_fr: commandant du camp de concentration de Stutthof, puis du camp de concentration de Neuengamme et de son réseau de camps annexes
region_en: Stutthof, Danzig–West Prussia, Hamburg and Neuengamme
status_en: sentenced to death by a British military court and executed on 8 October 1946
interpretation_en: Pauly makes it possible to describe the commandant's office as a node transmitting orders between the WVHA/RSHA, doctors, labour administration and executors. The profile does not reduce responsibility to the title of commandant, but identifies a specific flow of orders and the matters adjudicated at Neuengamme.
postwar_en: A British military court in the Neuengamme main trial found Pauly guilty of war crimes and sentenced him to death on 3 May 1946. He was hanged at Hameln on 8 October 1946.
limitations_en: The British trial concerned crimes at Neuengamme and its satellite camps, not the full record of his earlier command at Stutthof. Pauly's own testimony is defensive. The profile does not automatically attribute every act of staff to him; it identifies the scope of command and the documented transmission of the Bullenhuser Damm order.

name: Otto Hantke
organization_en: SS and Police Leader Lublin · Budzyn labour camp · Poniatowa camp
organization_pl: SSPF Lublin · obóz pracy Budzyń · obóz Poniatowa
role_en: first commandant of the Budzyn Jewish labour camp, subsequently commandant of Poniatowa
role_pl: pierwszy komendant żydowskiego obozu pracy Budzyń, następnie komendant Poniatowej
role_de: erster Kommandant des jüdischen Zwangsarbeitslagers Budzyń, anschließend Kommandant von Poniatowa
role_ru: первый комендант еврейского трудового лагеря Будзынь, затем комендант Понятовы
role_fr: premier commandant du camp de travail juif de Budzyń, puis commandant de Poniatowa
status_en: sentenced to life imprisonment in 1974; died during a suspension of sentence in 1986
interpretation_en: Hantke illustrates a local commandant who connected selection of the ghetto population, the organisation of industrial labour and direct murder. This is a distinct level of agency from the regional command of the SS and Police Leader and the commandant's office at Majdanek.
postwar_en: After lengthy proceedings, Hamburg Regional Court sentenced Hantke on 25 July 1974 to life imprisonment for four murders. He served the sentence in Bochum and Münster; he died on 18 November 1986 during a suspension of its enforcement.
limitations_en: The sources differ on the number of direct murders: the judgment individualised four, while a museum study gives 21. The profile does not add these figures together or attribute to Hantke all deportations from Warsaw, Białystok or Krasnik covered by the wider subject of the trial.

name: Hermann Hackmann
organization_en: Buchenwald concentration camp · Lublin-Majdanek concentration camp · SS-Totenkopfverbände
role_en: first Schutzhaftlagerführer at Lublin-Majdanek concentration camp, previously a member of the Buchenwald concentration camp command staff
role_pl: pierwszy Schutzhaftlagerführer KL Lublin-Majdanek, wcześniej członek komendantury KL Buchenwald
role_de: erster Schutzhaftlagerführer des KL Lublin-Majdanek, zuvor Angehöriger der Kommandantur des KL Buchenwald
role_ru: первый руководитель лагеря заключённых (Schutzhaftlagerführer) в концлагере Люблин-Майданек, ранее сотрудник комендатуры концлагеря Бухенвальд
role_fr: premier Schutzhaftlagerführer au camp de concentration de Lublin-Majdanek, auparavant membre de l’état-major de commandement du camp de concentration de Buchenwald
status_en: convicted twice; death sentence commuted to life imprisonment and released in 1955; sentenced to ten years in 1981
interpretation_en: Hackmann makes it possible to describe the Schutzhaftlagerführer as the operational head of prisoner-camp order between the commandant and block leaders and guards. The two postwar trials also show how Allied and West German jurisdictions framed the responsibility of camp personnel differently.
postwar_en: In the Buchenwald main trial an American military court sentenced Hackmann to death in 1947; the sentence was commuted to life imprisonment in 1948, and he was released from Landsberg in 1955. In the third Majdanek trial, Düsseldorf Regional Court sentenced him on 30 June 1981 to ten years for aiding murder in two cases involving at least 141 people. Public sources do not permit a reliable determination of how much of the second sentence he served.
limitations_en: The profile does not attribute to Hackmann every crime at Buchenwald or Majdanek. For the second judgment it gives only two murder complexes and the minimum established by the court; the full reasoning is not available in the online sources used. The time served after the 1981 judgment has not been established publicly.

name: Hans-Joachim Böhme
organization_en: Tilsit Gestapo office · Einsatzkommando Tilsit · Einsatzgruppe A
organization_pl: Stapo Tilsit · Einsatzkommando Tilsit · Einsatzgruppe A
role_en: head of the Gestapo in Tilsit and commander of Einsatzkommando Tilsit
role_pl: szef Gestapo w Tylży i dowódca Einsatzkommando Tilsit
role_de: Leiter der Gestapo in Tilsit und Führer des Einsatzkommandos Tilsit
role_ru: начальник гестапо в Тильзите и командир айнзацкоманды Тильзит
role_fr: chef de la Gestapo de Tilsit et commandant de l’Einsatzkommando Tilsit
region_en: Tilsit, Lithuania, the Suwałki region and Augustów
main_region_country: Tylża i pogranicze litewsko-niemieckie; Suwalszczyzna — okupowana Polska
status_en: sentenced to 15 years; released on health grounds shortly before his death in 1968
interpretation_en: Böhme shows how an ordinary regional Gestapo office was transformed into a mobile execution unit and used a network of border police posts. The profile bases responsibility on specific instructions reconstructed by the court, not on the unit's victim count alone.
postwar_en: After concealing part of his past during denazification, Böhme was arrested in August 1956. Ulm Regional Court sentenced him on 29 August 1958 to 15 years' penal servitude and ten years' loss of civil rights. He was released for health reasons in May 1968 and died on 31 May 1968.
limitations_en: The judgment used the legal construction of aiding and abetting and did not cover every murder committed by Einsatzkommando Tilsit; some charges ended in acquittal. The profile distinguishes Böhme's proven instructions, including the Augustów case, from operations carried out independently by other offices and formations.

name: Paul Salitter
organization_en: Düsseldorf Schutzpolizei · Transport Da 38 · Schutzmannschaft Battalion 101
role_en: Schutzpolizei captain and commander of the escort for the Düsseldorf–Riga deportation transport in December 1941
role_pl: kapitan policji ochronnej i dowódca eskorty transportu deportacyjnego Düsseldorf–Ryga w grudniu 1941 roku
role_de: Hauptmann der Schutzpolizei und Führer des Begleitkommandos für den Deportationstransport Düsseldorf–Riga im Dezember 1941
role_ru: капитан охранной полиции и командир эскорта депортационного транспорта Дюссельдорф — Рига в декабре 1941 года
role_fr: capitaine de la Schutzpolizei et commandant de l’escorte du convoi de déportation Düsseldorf–Riga en décembre 1941
status_en: never tried; dismissed from the police; died in 1972
interpretation_en: The profile follows a rail deportation from the assembly of people, through the assignment of the escort and travel conditions, to the commander's report. Salitter's responsibility rests on his own command and document, not on automatically attributing to him the later murder of all those deported.
postwar_en: Following internment and denazification proceedings, he was not readmitted to the police. Investigative authorities examined his activity, but no indictment or judgment followed; he died in 1972.
limitations_en: Salitter's report is a perpetrator source and must be tested against testimony from deportees. Without further evidence, neither the murder of everyone on the transport nor all crimes of Battalion 101 may be attributed to him; the sources support only a cautious finding that he helped secure at least one execution.

name: Robert Scholz
organization_en: Einsatzstab Reichsleiter Rosenberg · Fine Arts Special Staff · Louvre Working Group
organization_pl: Einsatzstab Reichsleiter Rosenberg · Sonderstab Bildende Kunst · Arbeitsgruppe Louvre
role_en: head of the Fine Arts Special Staff in the Einsatzstab Reichsleiter Rosenberg and organiser of the selection and exchange of looted artworks
role_pl: kierownik Sonderstab Bildende Kunst w Einsatzstab Reichsleiter Rosenberg i organizator selekcji oraz wymiany zagrabionych dzieł
role_de: Leiter des Sonderstabs Bildende Kunst im Einsatzstab Reichsleiter Rosenberg und Organisator der Auswahl und des Tauschs geraubter Kunstwerke
role_ru: руководитель Специального штаба изобразительного искусства в Оперативном штабе рейхсляйтера Розенберга и организатор отбора и обмена награбленных произведений
role_fr: chef de l’état-major spécial des Beaux-Arts au sein de l’Einsatzstab Reichsleiter Rosenberg et organisateur de la sélection et de l’échange d’œuvres d’art spoliées
status_en: sentenced in absentia in France to ten years; never served the sentence
interpretation_en: Scholz explains the middle link in the looting chain: expert selection, cataloguing, the decision on an object's destination and exchange on the art market. The profile attributes documented decisions and supervision to him, not the entire record of the ERR.
postwar_en: He was investigated by the American Art Looting Investigation Unit. In August 1950 a French military tribunal sentenced him in absentia to ten years' imprisonment and a residence ban; the judgment was not enforced. He died in 1981.
limitations_en: The INHA database contains a discrepancy in his birth date: its narrative and the Deutsche Digitale Bibliothek give 1902, while one INHA metadata field gives 1909. There is insufficient evidence to attribute to Scholz the burning of some objects in July 1943; the source itself presents this only as a supposition.

name: Karl Rasche
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Dresdner Bank · SS · Deutsche Erd- und Steinwerke
organization_pl: Dresdner Bank · SS · Deutsche Erd- und Steinwerke
role_en: member of the Dresdner Bank management board responsible for the bank's expansion, financing SS enterprises and acquiring assets in occupied Europe
role_pl: członek zarządu Dresdner Bank odpowiedzialny za ekspansję banku, finansowanie przedsiębiorstw SS i przejmowanie aktywów w okupowanej Europie
role_de: Vorstandsmitglied der Dresdner Bank, verantwortlich für die Expansion der Bank, die Finanzierung von SS-Unternehmen und die Übernahme von Vermögenswerten im besetzten Europa
role_ru: член правления Dresdner Bank, отвечавший за экспансию банка, финансирование предприятий СС и захват активов в оккупированной Европе
role_fr: membre du directoire de la Dresdner Bank chargé de l’expansion de la banque, du financement d’entreprises SS et de l’acquisition d’actifs dans l’Europe occupée
status_en: sentenced to seven years; released in 1950
interpretation_en: Rasche shows the bank as a link enabling expansion, takeovers and credit for the SS economy. The documented fact of financing enterprises that used forced labour must be separated from the scope of the final conviction.
postwar_en: In the Ministries Trial he was sentenced to seven years' imprisonment for plunder and spoliation and SS membership. He left prison in August 1950 and died in September 1951.
limitations_en: The tribunal found that the loans to SS enterprises and Rasche's knowledge of their practices had been documented, but acquitted him on count 5, holding that the provision of loans alone was insufficient under the legal test it applied. The profile cannot claim that he was convicted of financing slave labour; the conviction covered plunder and spoliation and the SS.

name: Kurt von Behr
organization_en: Einsatzstab Reichsleiter Rosenberg · Dienststelle Westen · Möbel-Aktion
organization_pl: Einsatzstab Reichsleiter Rosenberg · Dienststelle Westen · Möbel-Aktion
role_en: head of the ERR structures in Western Europe, subsequently of Dienststelle Westen and the Möbel-Aktion
role_pl: kierownik zachodnioeuropejskich struktur ERR, następnie Dienststelle Westen i Möbel-Aktion
role_de: Leiter der westeuropäischen Strukturen des ERR, anschließend der Dienststelle Westen und der Möbel-Aktion
role_ru: руководитель западноевропейских структур ERR, затем Западного управления и «Мебельной акции»
role_fr: chef des structures de l’ERR en Europe occidentale, puis de la Dienststelle Westen et de la Möbel-Aktion
status_en: never tried; died by suicide in April 1945
interpretation_en: Behr makes it possible to show the full economic chain of confiscating household property: identification, seizure, removal firms, forced labour, storage and transport. The office's quantitative data describe the scale of the mechanism, not a ranking of culpability.
postwar_en: He never stood trial. On 19 April 1945, after American troops arrived at his estate, he died by suicide together with his wife.
limitations_en: The figures of 71,619 homes and 29,436 railway wagons come from Dienststelle Westen's final report and must be described as a claim by a perpetrator institution. The suicide followed the arrival of US troops, but the sources do not permit its motive to be established with confidence. Not every ERR action in Western Europe was Behr's personal decision.

name: Paul Pleiger
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Reichswerke Hermann Göring · Reich Coal Association · Deutsche Erd- und Steinwerke
organization_pl: Reichswerke Hermann Göring · Reichsvereinigung Kohle · Deutsche Erd- und Steinwerke
role_en: chairman of Reichswerke Hermann Göring and head of the coal economy, using forced-labour allocations and ventures with the SS
role_pl: prezes Reichswerke Hermann Göring i kierownik gospodarki węglowej wykorzystujący przydziały pracy przymusowej oraz przedsięwzięcia z SS
role_de: Vorstandsvorsitzender der Reichswerke Hermann Göring und Leiter der Kohlenwirtschaft, der Zuteilungen von Zwangsarbeitskräften und Gemeinschaftsprojekte mit der SS nutzte
role_ru: председатель правления Reichswerke Hermann Göring и руководитель угольной промышленности, использовавший распределение принудительных работников и совместные проекты с СС
role_fr: président du groupe Reichswerke Hermann Göring et responsable de l’économie charbonnière, recourant aux affectations de travailleurs forcés et à des entreprises communes avec la SS
status_en: sentenced to 15 years; reduced to ten years; released in 1951
interpretation_en: Pleiger connects central labour planning, the management of a major industrial group and formal ventures with the SS economy. The profile grounds responsibility in his managerial decisions and a specific agreement, not in his office alone.
postwar_en: In the Ministries Trial he was sentenced to fifteen years' imprisonment for plunder and slave labour. In January 1951 the sentence was reduced to ten years, and he was released in March that year, before Easter. He died in 1985.
limitations_en: The indictment and opening statement are not identical to the findings of the judgment; the profile should identify which acts were covered by the conviction. Pleiger cannot automatically be assigned the fate of every worker at every Reichswerke plant or the conduct of every joint venture with the SS.

name: Herbert Hübner
organization_en: RKFDV Staff Main Office · Poznań RKFDV office · SS
organization_pl: Stabshauptamt RKFDV · poznańska placówka RKFDV · SS
role_en: head of the labour and resettlement staffs at the Poznań RKFDV office, involved in expelling Poles and forcibly retaining them as labour
role_pl: kierownik sztabów pracy i przesiedleń w poznańskiej placówce RKFDV, uczestniczący w wysiedleniach Polaków i ich przymusowym zatrzymaniu jako siły roboczej
role_de: Leiter der Arbeits- und Umsiedlungsstäbe in der Posener Dienststelle des RKFDV, beteiligt an der Vertreibung von Polen und ihrer zwangsweisen Festhaltung als Arbeitskräfte
role_ru: руководитель штабов труда и переселения в познанском отделении RKFDV, участвовавший в выселении поляков и их принудительном удержании как рабочей силы
role_fr: chef des services du travail et de la réinstallation au bureau du RKFDV de Poznań, impliqué dans l’expulsion de Polonais et leur maintien forcé comme main-d’œuvre
region_en: Poznań, the Warthegau and occupied Poland
status_en: sentenced to 15 years; reduced to ten years; released in 1951
interpretation_en: Hübner shows a regional administrative document that connected expulsion with control over mobility and exploitation of labour. Responsibility rests on the signed instruction and the judgment's findings, not merely on his function in the RKFDV.
postwar_en: In the RuSHA Trial he was sentenced to fifteen years' imprisonment. The sentence was later reduced to ten years, and he was released in 1951. He died in 1982.
limitations_en: The judgment expressly distinguished proven acts from the remaining specifications for which the evidence against Hübner was insufficient. The profile should be limited to expulsions, retaining Poles as labour and the other findings actually attributed to him in the judgment.

name: Helmut Ortwin Pohl
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: staff of the SS and Police Leader in Lublin · SS · Aktion Reinhardt apparatus
organization_pl: sztab dowódcy SS i policji w Lublinie · SS · aparat Aktion Reinhardt
role_en: officer on Odilo Globocnik's staff who participated in deportations and resettlement in the Lublin District during the first half of 1942
role_pl: oficer sztabu Odila Globocnika uczestniczący w deportacjach i przesiedleniach w dystrykcie lubelskim w pierwszej połowie 1942 roku
role_de: Offizier im Stab Odilo Globocniks, der in der ersten Hälfte des Jahres 1942 an Deportationen und Umsiedlungen im Distrikt Lublin beteiligt war
role_ru: офицер штаба Одило Глобочника, участвовавший в депортациях и переселениях в Люблинском дистрикте в первой половине 1942 года
role_fr: officier de l’état-major d’Odilo Globocnik ayant participé aux déportations et aux réinstallations dans le district de Lublin pendant le premier semestre de 1942
region_en: Lublin, the Lublin District and occupied Poland
status_en: indicted; trial interrupted and proceedings discontinued without a judgment
interpretation_en: Pohl documents the local link between the arrival of a rail transport, selection of those retained for labour and dispatch of the others onward. A short, well-defined chronology does not justify attributing the whole of Aktion Reinhardt to him.
postwar_en: He was indicted in Austria with Ernst Lerch. The trial opened on 17 May 1972 but was adjourned after two days and never resumed; the proceedings were discontinued on 11 May 1976. Pohl died in 1997 without a judgment.
limitations_en: His documented period of service in Lublin runs from January to June 1942. The material supports attribution of specific actions in April and May, not planning or implementing the whole of Aktion Reinhardt. Discontinuance of the trial means there was no judicial determination of guilt.

name: Georg Lörner
tier_label_en: Designers of the machinery of destruction
organization_en: SS-WVHA · Office Group B · SS economic enterprises
organization_pl: SS-Wirtschafts- und Verwaltungshauptamt · Amtsgruppe B · przedsiębiorstwa gospodarcze SS
role_en: deputy head of the WVHA and chief of Office Group B, responsible for supplying the camp apparatus and supervising enterprises that used prisoners
role_pl: zastępca szefa WVHA i kierownik Amtsgruppe B odpowiedzialnej za zaopatrzenie aparatu obozowego oraz nadzór nad przedsiębiorstwami wykorzystującymi więźniów
role_de: stellvertretender Chef des WVHA und Leiter der Amtsgruppe B, verantwortlich für die Versorgung des Lagerapparats und die Aufsicht über Unternehmen, die Häftlinge einsetzten
role_ru: заместитель начальника WVHA и руководитель группы управлений B, отвечавшей за снабжение лагерного аппарата и надзор над предприятиями, использовавшими заключённых
role_fr: chef adjoint du WVHA et chef du groupe d’offices B, chargé d’approvisionner l’appareil concentrationnaire et de superviser des entreprises qui employaient des détenus
region_en: Germany, the concentration-camp system and occupied Europe
region_pl: Niemcy · system obozów koncentracyjnych · okupowana Europa
main_region_country: Niemcy / system obozów koncentracyjnych w okupowanej Europie
status_en: death sentence ultimately commuted to 15 years; released in 1954
interpretation_en: Lörner shows the central material support system for the camps and corporate supervision of prisoner labour. At the same time, the profile must preserve the judgment's evidentiary boundary concerning property from Aktion Reinhardt.
postwar_en: In the WVHA Trial he was sentenced to death in November 1947. In August 1948 the sentence was commuted to life imprisonment and in 1951 to fifteen years. He was released on 31 March 1954 and died in 1959.
limitations_en: The tribunal found the evidence insufficient to convict Lörner of appropriating property from Aktion Reinhardt. The profile cannot present that allegation as fact or attribute to him every instance of prisoner labour in SS enterprises.

name: Wilhelm Keppler
organization_en: Deutsche Umsiedlungs-Treuhand · Foreign Office · SS
role_en: state secretary and economic official who participated in establishing the Deutsche Umsiedlungs-Treuhand and organising the seizure of expellees' property
role_pl: sekretarz stanu i funkcjonariusz gospodarczy uczestniczący w utworzeniu Deutsche Umsiedlungs-Treuhand oraz organizacji przejmowania mienia wysiedlonych
role_de: Staatssekretär und Wirtschaftsfunktionär, beteiligt an der Gründung der Deutschen Umsiedlungs-Treuhand und an der Organisation der Übernahme des Vermögens Vertriebener
role_ru: статс-секретарь и хозяйственный функционер, участвовавший в создании Deutsche Umsiedlungs-Treuhand и организации захвата имущества выселенных
role_fr: secrétaire d’État et responsable économique ayant participé à la création de la Deutsche Umsiedlungs-Treuhand et à l’organisation de la saisie des biens des personnes expulsées
region_en: Germany, annexed territories and occupied Eastern Europe
region_pl: Niemcy · ziemie anektowane · okupowana Europa Wschodnia
main_region_country: Niemcy / anektowana Polska / okupowana Europa Wschodnia
status_en: sentenced to ten years; released in 1951
interpretation_en: Keppler shows how the plunder of those expelled took the form of a trust company, accounting and legalistic circulation of assets. The profile rests on a specific organisational document and the judgment's findings, not simply on proximity to those in power.
postwar_en: In the Ministries Trial he was found guilty under counts 1, 5, 6 and 8 and sentenced to ten years' imprisonment. He was released in February 1951 and died in 1960.
limitations_en: The DUT worked with the extensive HTO, RKFDV and SS apparatus. The profile cannot attribute every confiscation by these institutions to Keppler; his individual responsibility should be tied to the organisational document, his function and the findings of the judgment.

name: Walter Andreas Hofer
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Hermann Göring collection · art market in occupied Paris · Swiss artwork-exchange network
organization_pl: kolekcja Hermanna Göringa · rynek sztuki w okupowanym Paryżu · sieć wymiany dzieł w Szwajcarii
role_en: Hermann Göring's chief art adviser and agent, organising the purchase, confiscation and exchange of looted artworks
role_pl: główny doradca i agent artystyczny Hermanna Göringa, organizujący zakup, konfiskatę i wymianę zagrabionych dzieł
role_de: wichtigster Kunstberater und Kunstagent Hermann Görings, der Erwerb, Beschlagnahme und Tausch geraubter Kunstwerke organisierte
role_ru: главный художественный советник и агент Германа Геринга, организовывавший покупку, конфискацию и обмен награбленных произведений
role_fr: principal conseiller artistique et agent d’Hermann Göring, organisant l’achat, la confiscation et l’échange d’œuvres d’art spoliées
status_en: sentenced in absentia in France to ten years; never served the sentence
interpretation_en: Hofer shows the market link in the looting chain: the expert, intermediary, documentation, pressure on the owner and cross-border exchange. Each object nevertheless requires a separate provenance reconstruction.
postwar_en: After the war he was investigated by the Art Looting Investigation Unit and classified as a Mitläufer in denazification proceedings. A French military tribunal sentenced him in absentia in 1950 to ten years' imprisonment, but he did not serve the sentence. He continued to trade in art and died in 1975.
limitations_en: The existence of an invoice or payment does not prove that a sale under occupation was voluntary, but neither does it alone suffice to describe every object as confiscated. The profile should not attribute Göring's entire collection to Hofer; individual works require provenance research and identification of the specific transaction.

name: Ferdinand von Sammern-Frankenegg
organization_en: SS and Police Leader Warsaw · SS · German police apparatus in the Warsaw District
organization_pl: SSPF Warschau · SS · niemiecki aparat policyjny dystryktu warszawskiego
rank: SS-Oberführer w Warszawie; od lipca 1944 SS-Brigadeführer i Generalmajor der Polizei
role_en: SS and Police Leader in the Warsaw District; directed the deportations during the Grossaktion and the first assault on the ghetto on 19 April 1943
role_pl: dowódca SS i Policji w dystrykcie warszawskim; kierujący deportacjami podczas Grossaktion i pierwszym atakiem na getto 19 kwietnia 1943 r.
role_de: SS- und Polizeiführer im Distrikt Warschau; Leiter der Deportationen während der Großaktion und des ersten Angriffs auf das Ghetto am 19. April 1943
role_ru: командующий СС и полицией в Варшавском дистрикте; руководитель депортаций во время Большой акции и первого штурма гетто 19 апреля 1943 года
role_fr: chef de la SS et de la police dans le district de Varsovie ; dirigea les déportations pendant la Grossaktion et le premier assaut contre le ghetto le 19 avril 1943
status_en: never tried; killed in fighting with Yugoslav partisans on 20 September 1944
interpretation_en: The profile shows a regional commander who connected administrative rules of terror, subordinate police formations and field command of deportations. The strongest evidence of his personal role is his direction of the Grossaktion and the proclamation and police order bearing his signature; his role must not, however, be equated with independently designing Aktion Reinhardt.
postwar_en: He never stood trial. After being transferred to occupied Yugoslavia, he was mortally wounded on 20 September 1944 when Yugoslav partisans shelled his position in the Banja Luka area.
limitations_en: Sources differ on when he began to exercise the Warsaw SSPF post in practice or nominally; the safe range is summer 1942 to 19 April 1943. The profile does not assign him the entire victim toll of the Grossaktion as a personal total or the sole decision on Aktion Reinhardt. His command on 19 April lasted only until the first unsuccessful assault. His later promotion to SS-Brigadeführer was not the rank he held during his Warsaw service.

name: Josef Blösche
organization_en: Warsaw Sipo · SD · SS
role_en: field officer of the Sipo in Warsaw who participated in deportations and executions in the Warsaw ghetto
role_pl: terenowy funkcjonariusz Sipo w Warszawie, uczestnik deportacji i egzekucji w getcie warszawskim
role_de: operativ eingesetzter Sipo-Angehöriger in Warschau, beteiligt an Deportationen und Hinrichtungen im Warschauer Ghetto
role_ru: оперативный сотрудник Полиции безопасности в Варшаве, участник депортаций и казней в Варшавском гетто
role_fr: agent opérationnel de la Police de sûreté à Varsovie qui participa aux déportations et aux exécutions dans le ghetto de Varsovie
status_en: sentenced to death in East Germany and executed on 29 July 1969
interpretation_en: Blösche is a rare case of a rank-and-file perpetrator whose trial brought together his own killings, violence on patrol, participation in deportations and mass executions. The testimony of Ludwik Gutmacher, preserved by the Pilecki Institute, independently identifies the perpetrator known in the ghetto as “Frankenstein.”
postwar_en: He was detained in East Germany on 11 January 1967. The Erfurt District Court sentenced him to death on 30 April 1969 for a complex of crimes in Poland and Belarus; East Germany's highest court upheld the judgment on 13 June. He was executed by a shot in Leipzig on 29 July 1969.
limitations_en: The profile rests on the scope of the court's findings, not journalistic estimates of his victim count. The iconic photograph from the Stroop Report identifies him at the scene of the operation, but does not by itself prove every act attributed to him. The trial took place within the East German justice system; the judgment has therefore been considered alongside independent testimony from 1947 and records held by the Bundesarchiv.

name: Rolf-Heinz Höppner
organization_en: Umwandererzentralstelle Posen · SD-Leitabschnitt Posen · Gau Office for Nationality Affairs
organization_pl: Umwandererzentralstelle Posen · SD-Leitabschnitt Posen · Gauamt für Volkstumsfragen
role_en: de facto head of the Central Resettlement Office in Poznań and chief of the SD section in the Wartheland
role_pl: faktyczny kierownik Centrali Przesiedleńczej w Poznaniu i szef odcinka SD w Kraju Warty
role_de: faktischer Leiter der Umwandererzentralstelle in Posen und Leiter des SD-Abschnitts im Wartheland
role_ru: фактический руководитель Центрального переселенческого управления в Познани и начальник регионального отдела СД в Вартеланде
role_fr: chef de fait de l’Office central de réinstallation de Poznań et chef de la section du SD dans le Wartheland
region_en: Wartheland — Polish territories annexed to the Reich
main_region_country: Kraj Warty — ziemie polskie wcielone do Rzeszy
status_en: sentenced to life imprisonment in 1949; released under an amnesty in early 1957
interpretation_en: Höppner connects forced displacement, ethnic selection, confiscation and early planning for mass murder within a single regional apparatus. The memorandum of July 1941 is strong evidence of his own thinking and its transmission to the centre, but cannot be used to attribute to him the sole decision on the method or site of extermination.
postwar_en: Arrested by the British in July 1945 and interrogated in Nuremberg, he was extradited to Poland on 25 February 1947. The Regional Court in Poznań sentenced him to life imprisonment on 15 March 1949. In early 1957 he was released as a result of an amnesty and returned to West Germany, where he died in 1998.
limitations_en: The memorandum of 16 July 1941 summarises discussions among several officials and contains Höppner's proposal; it does not prove that he personally decided to establish Kulmhof. Secondary accounts sometimes confuse his fate with Herbert Strickner's and incorrectly report a death sentence or execution. The profile adopts life imprisonment and release on the basis of a study that draws on the Polish trial records.

name: Erich Engels
organization_en: KdS Lemberg · Gestapo · Jewish Affairs Section
role_en: head of the Jewish Affairs Section of the Gestapo under the KdS Lemberg
role_pl: kierownik referatu do spraw żydowskich Gestapo przy KdS Lwów
role_de: Leiter des Judenreferats der Gestapo beim KdS Lemberg
role_ru: начальник реферата по еврейским делам гестапо при управлении KdS во Львове
role_fr: chef de la section des affaires juives de la Gestapo auprès du KdS Lemberg
region_en: District of Galicia — occupied Poland; now western Ukraine
main_region_country: dystrykt Galicja — okupowana Polska; dziś zachodnia Ukraina
status_en: sentenced to death in Poland on 13 March 1950; executed in 1951
interpretation_en: Engels shows how a municipal Gestapo Jewish Affairs Section became the mobile command element for operations in several localities within the district. The profile rests on named operations and the order for a public hanging, rather than automatically assigning to him the full toll of deportations from Galicia.
postwar_en: Detained by the United States Army, he was handed over to Poland in late February 1947. A Polish court in Warsaw sentenced him to death on 13 March 1950 for crimes committed in the General Government. The sentence was carried out at Mokotów Prison in 1951.
limitations_en: The publicly available source package does not include the full reasons for the Polish judgment, so the court is recorded in general terms. Sources differ on the exact day of his execution in May 1951; the record retains only the certain year. Actions by the subordinate unit in Bóbrka and other localities document command, not his personally killing every victim or responsibility for the district's entire toll.

name: Karl Heinrich Klaustermeyer
organization_en: Jewish Affairs Section of the KdS Warsaw · Gestapo · Sipo and SD
organization_pl: Judenreferat KdS Warszawa · Gestapo · Sipo i SD
role_en: officer of the Jewish Affairs Section of the KdS Warsaw who conducted inspections and killings in the ghetto
role_pl: funkcjonariusz referatu do spraw żydowskich KdS Warszawa, dokonujący kontroli i zabójstw w getcie
role_de: Angehöriger des Judenreferats beim KdS Warschau, der im Ghetto Kontrollen durchführte und Menschen tötete
role_ru: сотрудник реферата по еврейским делам управления KdS в Варшаве, проводивший проверки и совершавший убийства в гетто
role_fr: officier de la section des affaires juives du KdS Varsovie qui mena des inspections et commit des meurtres dans le ghetto
status_en: sentenced to life imprisonment for nine murders; released in April 1976 when terminally ill
interpretation_en: Klaustermeyer makes it possible to show the murderous arbitrariness of a field officer in the Jewish Affairs Section, while also demonstrating the rigour required when using a trial: nine acts proved, eleven ending in acquittal. The context of the Grossaktion and the uprising does not replace findings about specific killings.
postwar_en: Arrested on 26 January 1961, he was sentenced by Bielefeld Regional Court on 4 February 1965 to nine life terms at hard labour for nine murders. The judgment became final after the Federal Court of Justice's decision of 30 July 1965. He was released on 8 April 1976 because of advanced cancer and died on 21 April.
limitations_en: The twenty alleged killings must not be converted into the number of acts proved: the final conviction covers nine, while the remaining charges ended in acquittal. Photographic material and his presence during operations do not independently prove additional crimes. The exact date of his release on health grounds comes from later scholarship, not from the 1965 judgment itself.

name: Josef Schwammberger
organization_en: Rozwadów forced-labour camp · Przemyśl forced-labour camp · Mielec forced-labour camp · SS
organization_pl: ZAL Rozwadów · ZAL Przemyśl · ZAL Mielec · SS
role_en: commandant of the Jewish forced-labour camps in Rozwadów and Przemyśl, also associated with the camp in Mielec
role_pl: komendant żydowskich obozów pracy w Rozwadowie i Przemyślu, związany także z obozem w Mielcu
role_de: Kommandant der Zwangsarbeitslager für Juden in Rozwadów und Przemyśl, auch mit dem Lager in Mielec verbunden
role_ru: комендант еврейских трудовых лагерей в Розвадове и Пшемысле, связанный также с лагерем в Мельце
role_fr: commandant des camps de travail forcé pour Juifs de Rozwadów et de Przemyśl, également associé au camp de Mielec
status_en: sentenced to life imprisonment in 1992; died in prison in December 2004
interpretation_en: Schwammberger provides an exceptionally well-defined judicial profile of a local commandant and direct killer. At the same time, the reasons given in the trial show the limits imposed by extradition: the court considered the actual scope to have been broader, but did not extend the judgment to acts outside the extradition request.
postwar_en: After escaping from a denazification camp in 1948, he hid in Argentina. He was extradited to West Germany in 1990. Stuttgart Regional Court sentenced him on 18 May 1992 to life imprisonment for murdering 25 people and aiding and abetting the murder of 641. He died in prison in December 2004.
limitations_en: The indictment covered substantially more acts than the final judgment; the profile retains only the 25 victims of murder and 641 victims of aiding and abetting murder found by the court. Mielec remains part of the biography and source context, but not part of the conviction because of the rule of speciality in extradition. Sources give different days for his death, so only December 2004 is recorded.

name: Franz Josef Müller
organization_en: Julag I Płaszów · Julag II Prokocim · Julag III Bieżanów · SSPF Krakau
organization_pl: Julag I Płaszów · Julag II Prokocim · Julag III Bieżanów · SSPF Krakau
role_en: head of the Kraków Julag camps and commandant of Julag I Płaszów
role_pl: szef krakowskich Julagów i komendant Julagu I Płaszów
role_de: Leiter der Krakauer Julags und Kommandant des Julag I Płaszów
role_ru: руководитель краковских юлагов и комендант Юлага I в Плашове
role_fr: chef des camps Julag de Cracovie et commandant du Julag I de Płaszów
status_en: sentenced to life imprisonment in 1961; released on parole in 1970
interpretation_en: Müller explains the system of small urban forced-labour camps that preceded or supplemented KL Płaszów: forced labour on infrastructure, commandant terror and liquidation. The profile preserves the four distinct legal classifications in the judgment and does not add them together as a single victim count.
postwar_en: Mosbach Regional Court sentenced Müller on 24 April 1961 to life at hard labour for 22 murders, 58 cases of incitement to murder, five cases of aiding and abetting murder and four cases of manslaughter. The Federal Court of Justice upheld the judgment on 3 August 1961. He was released on parole in 1970.
limitations_en: He must be distinguished from other people named Franz Josef Müller, including the member of the White Rose. No certain year of death has been established, so it remains `null`. The judgment contains four different legal classifications and four acquittals; they must not be replaced with one aggregated figure or used to attribute to Müller every death in all the Julag camps.

name: Hermann Blache
organization_en: Tarnów forced-labour camp · SSPF Krakau · SS
role_en: commandant of the Jewish forced-labour camp in the Tarnów ghetto
role_pl: komendant żydowskiego obozu pracy w getcie tarnowskim
role_de: Kommandant des Zwangsarbeitslagers für Juden im Ghetto Tarnów
role_ru: комендант еврейского трудового лагеря в Тарнувском гетто
role_fr: commandant du camp de travail forcé pour Juifs dans le ghetto de Tarnów
status_en: finally sentenced to life imprisonment for 22 murders and an additional six years for aiding and abetting the murder of 4,000 people
interpretation_en: Blache is a strongly individualised example of how command of forced labour, everyday terror and participation in a ghetto liquidation converged in one local office. The profile rests on the 22 murders and aiding and abetting concerning 4,000 people established by the court, not on the perpetrator's general reputation.
postwar_en: After the war he underwent brief denazification proceedings and worked in Bochum. He was arrested on 28 September 1961. Bochum Regional Court sentenced him on 30 April 1964 to life at hard labour for each of 22 murders and six years for aiding and abetting the murder of 4,000 people. The Federal Court of Justice upheld the judgment on 20 January 1965. He died in 1985.
limitations_en: The profile adopts the figures from the final judgment, not the higher numbers reported in the press during the trial. The 4,000 people relate to aiding and abetting their murder through deportation to Auschwitz, not 4,000 killings committed by Blache personally. The public source package does not document the later course of his imprisonment equally well, so `years_served` remains `null`.

name: Paul Nitsche
organization_en: T4 Central Office · Chancellery of the Führer · Leipzig-Dösen Psychiatric Institution
organization_pl: Zentraldienststelle T4 · Kanzlei des Führers · Heil- und Pflegeanstalt Leipzig-Dösen
role_en: psychiatrist, senior medical assessor and, from late 1941, head of the medical section of Aktion T4
role_pl: psychiatra, naczelny rzeczoznawca i od końca 1941 roku kierownik medycznego pionu Aktion T4
role_de: Psychiater, Obergutachter und ab Ende 1941 Leiter der medizinischen Abteilung der Aktion T4
role_ru: психиатр, главный эксперт и с конца 1941 года руководитель медицинского направления программы T4
role_fr: psychiatre, expert médical principal et, à partir de la fin de 1941, chef de la section médicale de l’Aktion T4
status_en: sentenced to death for crimes against humanity; executed in 1948
interpretation_en: Nitsche shows the transition from his own practice of pharmaceutical killing at an institution to the central management of T4 medical selection. His responsibility rests on his experiment, assessments and leadership decisions, not solely on his official title.
postwar_en: After the war he was detained and tried with other members of the medical staff in the Dresden trial concerning the so-called euthanasia killings. He was sentenced to death on 7 July 1947; the sentence was carried out on 25 March 1948.
limitations_en: Nitsche must not be assigned every death covered by the broad historiography of Aktion T4 or every killing in its later decentralised phase. The best-documented elements are his own Luminal trial, his role as an assessor, his medical leadership and his support for continued killing; totals for the programme as a whole are a record of the system, not the personal toll of one perpetrator.

name: Friedrich Mennecke
organization_en: Eichberg Psychiatric Institution · T4 Central Office · Aktion 14f13
organization_pl: Heil- und Pflegeanstalt Eichberg · Zentraldienststelle T4 · Aktion 14f13
role_en: director of the Eichberg institution, T4 medical assessor and travelling physician who selected prisoners under Aktion 14f13
role_pl: dyrektor zakładu Eichberg, rzeczoznawca T4 i wędrowny lekarz-selekcjoner więźniów w Aktion 14f13
role_de: Direktor der Anstalt Eichberg, T4-Gutachter und reisender Selektionsarzt für KZ-Häftlinge bei der Aktion 14f13
role_ru: директор учреждения Айхберг, эксперт T4 и разъездной врач, отбиравший заключённых в рамках операции 14f13
role_fr: directeur de l’établissement d’Eichberg, expert médical de T4 et médecin itinérant qui sélectionnait des prisonniers dans le cadre de l’Aktion 14f13
region_pl: Hesja · obozy koncentracyjne w Rzeszy · ośrodki zagłady T4
status_en: sentenced to death in a judgment that did not become final; died in prison before his appeal was heard
interpretation_en: Mennecke connects the local direction of a psychiatric institution with the supraregional, itinerant selection mechanism of T4 and 14f13. His surviving letters make it possible to describe not merely his position but his own working methods.
postwar_en: In the first Eichberg Trial before Frankfurt am Main Regional Court, he was sentenced to death in 1946. He appealed, but died in Butzbach Prison on 28 January 1947 before it was heard; the judgment never became final.
limitations_en: Institutional sources refer to thousands of people selected by Mennecke, but do not provide one uncontested personal total. Figures for Aktion 14f13 as a whole must not be transferred to his account. Accounts of the cause of his death in prison diverge, so the profile should not decide the point without medical records.

name: Richard von Hegener
organization_en: Chancellery of the Führer · Reich Committee for the Scientific Registration of Serious Hereditary and Congenital Illnesses · Aktion T4
organization_pl: Kanzlei des Führers · Reichsausschuss zur wissenschaftlichen Erfassung von erb- und anlagebedingten schweren Leiden · Aktion T4
role_en: official of the Chancellery of the Führer and deputy head of the Reich Committee responsible for the administrative organisation of the murder of children and patients
role_pl: urzędnik Kanzlei des Führers i zastępca kierownika Reichsausschuss odpowiedzialny za administracyjną organizację mordowania dzieci i pacjentów
role_de: Mitarbeiter der Kanzlei des Führers und stellvertretender Leiter des Reichsausschusses, verantwortlich für die administrative Organisation der Tötung von Kindern und Patienten
role_ru: чиновник Канцелярии фюрера и заместитель руководителя Имперского комитета, отвечавший за административную организацию убийства детей и пациентов
role_fr: fonctionnaire de la chancellerie du Führer et chef adjoint du Comité du Reich, responsable de l’organisation administrative du meurtre d’enfants et de patients
region_pl: Berlin · Rzesza Niemiecka · sieć zakładów psychiatrycznych i oddziałów dziecięcych
status_en: sentenced to life imprisonment; released under an amnesty in 1956
interpretation_en: Hegener explains the administrative middle of the chain: receiving a report, preparing the circulation of records, maintaining contact with assessors and wards, and organising the programme. His conviction allows this responsibility to be distinguished from the medical assessments performed by physicians.
postwar_en: After the war he used the name Richard Wegener and obtained employment in Mecklenburg. He was tried before a court in Magdeburg and sentenced to life imprisonment on 20 February 1952. He was released under an amnesty in 1956 and died in 1981.
limitations_en: Hegener organised the programme's administrative flow and implementation, but the medical forms were also assessed by appointed physician-assessors; without his signature on a specific form, he should not be credited personally with issuing every medical decision. Parts of the Magdeburg trial record have not survived in full, limiting reconstruction of the basis for each detailed finding in the judgment.

name: Heinrich Bütefisch
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: IG Farben · IG Auschwitz · Fürstengrube GmbH · SS
organization_pl: IG Farben · IG Auschwitz · Fürstengrube GmbH · SS
role_en: member of the IG Farben managing board responsible for the Auschwitz-Monowitz works and mining ventures that used prisoners
role_pl: członek zarządu IG Farben odpowiedzialny za zakłady Auschwitz-Monowitz i przedsięwzięcia górnicze wykorzystujące więźniów
role_de: Vorstandsmitglied der IG Farben, zuständig für die Werke Auschwitz-Monowitz und Bergbauvorhaben, bei denen Häftlinge eingesetzt wurden
role_ru: член правления IG Farben, отвечавший за предприятия Аушвиц-Моновиц и горнодобывающие проекты, использовавшие труд заключённых
role_fr: membre du directoire d’IG Farben responsable des installations d’Auschwitz-Monowitz et des entreprises minières qui employaient des prisonniers
status_en: sentenced to six years for slave labour; released in 1951
interpretation_en: Bütefisch shows how corporate board decisions, an industrial investment and negotiations with the SS translated into the systematic use of prisoners at Auschwitz and in the mines. The judgment individualises his responsibility while also defining its legal boundaries.
