postwar_en: In the IG Farben Trial before United States Military Tribunal VI, he was found guilty under count 3 and sentenced to six years' imprisonment. He was released in 1951 and died in 1969.
limitations_en: The conviction covered count 3 concerning slave labour. The tribunal acquitted Bütefisch under count 2 on plunder and spoliation and count 4 on SS membership; the profile must not be written as if those charges had also ended in conviction. Nor should he be assigned every abuse at the IG Auschwitz construction site or the corporation's entire policy.

name: Eberhard von Künsberg
organization_en: Foreign Office · Sonderkommando Künsberg · Waffen-SS
role_en: diplomat and commander of Sonderkommando Künsberg who organised the supraregional seizure of archives, libraries, works of art and economic records
role_pl: dyplomata i dowódca Sonderkommando Künsberg organizujący ponadregionalne zajmowanie archiwów, bibliotek, dzieł sztuki i dokumentacji gospodarczej
role_de: Diplomat und Befehlshaber des Sonderkommandos Künsberg, das die überregionale Beschlagnahme von Archiven, Bibliotheken, Kunstwerken und Wirtschaftsdokumentation organisierte
role_ru: дипломат и командир зондеркоманды Кюнсберга, организовывавший межрегиональное изъятие архивов, библиотек, произведений искусства и хозяйственной документации
role_fr: diplomate et commandant du Sonderkommando Künsberg qui organisa la saisie suprarégionale d’archives, de bibliothèques, d’œuvres d’art et de documents économiques
region_pl: okupowana Polska · Francja · Bałkany · okupowany Związek Sowiecki
crime_tags_pl: Grabież dóbr kultury;Grabież archiwów;Mienie żydowskie;Okupowana Europa
status_en: never tried; missing since April 1945; date of death undetermined
interpretation_en: Künsberg connects diplomacy, intelligence, a military formation and plunder. Surviving orders make it possible to move from the general history of the Sonderkommando to his personal decisions to expand its mandate and select specific targets.
postwar_en: He never stood trial. According to an Institute of Contemporary History study based on the family archive, he was last seen in April 1945 during the retreat in Pomerania; his exact fate and date of death remain undetermined.
limitations_en: The term “securing” in the unit's documents is a perpetrator euphemism and does not determine a uniform legal status for every object. The figure of about 300,000 concerns the entire Sonderkommando in the Soviet Union, not Künsberg's personal acts. The absence of a trial means there was no judicial determination of the allegations, while the exact date and circumstances of his death are unknown.

name: Heinz Brückner
organization_en: Main Office of the Ethnic German Liaison Office · VoMi Office VI · SS · Reich Commissioner for the Consolidation of German Nationhood
organization_pl: Hauptamt Volksdeutsche Mittelstelle · Amt VI VoMi · SS · Reichskommissar für die Festigung deutschen Volkstums
role_en: head of Office VI in the Main Office of the Ethnic German Liaison Office, jointly responsible for child abductions, Germanisation, displacement and forced labour
role_pl: kierownik Amt VI w Hauptamt Volksdeutsche Mittelstelle współodpowiedzialny za uprowadzenia dzieci, germanizację, wysiedlenia i pracę przymusową
role_de: Leiter des Amtes VI im Hauptamt Volksdeutsche Mittelstelle, mitverantwortlich für Kinderverschleppung, Germanisierung, Vertreibungen und Zwangsarbeit
role_ru: начальник управления VI Главного управления VoMi, нёсший совместную ответственность за похищение детей, германизацию, выселения и принудительный труд
role_fr: chef du bureau VI de l’Office principal du Bureau de liaison des Allemands de souche, coresponsable des enlèvements d’enfants, de la germanisation, des déplacements et du travail forcé
region_pl: Niemcy · okupowana Polska · okupowany Związek Sowiecki · okupowana Europa Wschodnia
status_en: sentenced to 15 years; sentence reduced to time served on 31 January 1951, then released
interpretation_en: Brückner shows how the Germanisation of children was connected with record-keeping, inter-agency correspondence, the resettlement of families and settlement plans. His own signatures and the letter concerning Halbstadt distinguish individual responsibility from mere membership in the VoMi.
postwar_en: In the RuSHA Trial before United States Military Tribunal I, he was found guilty on all three counts on 10 March 1948 and sentenced to fifteen years' imprisonment. On 31 January 1951 an American review decision reduced the sentence to time served; he was then released in 1951. He died in 1968.
limitations_en: The judgment lists in detail the mechanisms proved against Brückner, but finds insufficient evidence for other parts of the indictment; the profile should not add them. The initial fifteen-year sentence and findings of guilt are documented directly in the judgment; any account of his later release must preserve the distinction between clemency decisions and the tribunal's findings.

name: Hans-Joachim Rehse
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: People's Court · First Senate of the People's Court · NSDAP
role_en: judge of the First Senate of the People's Court who participated in repressive death sentences under the presidency of Roland Freisler
role_pl: sędzia pierwszego senatu Volksgerichtshof współdecydujący o represyjnych wyrokach śmierci pod przewodnictwem Rolanda Freislera
role_de: Richter im Ersten Senat des Volksgerichtshofs, der unter dem Vorsitz Roland Freislers an repressiven Todesurteilen mitwirkte
role_ru: судья первого сената Народной судебной палаты, участвовавший в вынесении репрессивных смертных приговоров под председательством Роланда Фрейслера
role_fr: juge de la première chambre du Tribunal du peuple qui participa à des condamnations à mort répressives sous la présidence de Roland Freisler
region_pl: Berlin · Rzesza Niemiecka · centralny system represyjnego sądownictwa
status_en: five-year sentence overturned; acquitted on retrial; appeal proceedings ended after his death
interpretation_en: Rehse explains the repressive justice system as the work of a collegial bench: his signature and vote contributed to the judgment, although he was not its presiding judge. The postwar course of the case also shows the legal barriers to holding Nazi judges accountable.
postwar_en: From 1956 he again worked as a judge in West Germany. In 1967 he was sentenced to five years at hard labour, but the Federal Court of Justice overturned the judgment. He was acquitted on retrial on 6 December 1968; the prosecution's appeal was not heard because he died in September 1969.
limitations_en: The figure 231 refers to collegial judgments signed by Rehse, not 231 decisions he made alone. The profile should attribute to him his vote, signature and participation in the decision, not sole authorship of every judgment. The postwar acquittal is the legal outcome of a particular trial and does not constitute historical validation of the People's Court's judgments.

name: Ernst Woermann
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Foreign Office · Political Department · Reich Government
role_en: head of the Political Department and undersecretary of state in the Foreign Office who participated in the administrative approval of deportations of Jews from France
role_pl: szef Wydziału Politycznego i podsekretarz stanu w Auswärtiges Amt uczestniczący w administracyjnym zatwierdzaniu deportacji Żydów z Francji
role_de: Leiter der Politischen Abteilung und Unterstaatssekretär im Auswärtigen Amt, beteiligt an der administrativen Genehmigung der Deportation von Juden aus Frankreich
role_ru: начальник Политического отдела и заместитель статс-секретаря Министерства иностранных дел, участвовавший в административном согласовании депортации евреев из Франции
role_fr: chef du département politique et sous-secrétaire d’État au ministère des Affaires étrangères qui participa à l’approbation administrative des déportations de Juifs depuis la France
region_pl: Berlin · okupowana Francja · europejska sieć dyplomatyczna Rzeszy
status_en: ultimately convicted under count 5 and sentenced to five years; released in 1950
interpretation_en: Woermann shows central administration as a mechanism of assent: a short note stating that there was no objection gave an SS action the official support of the foreign ministry. The profile rests on a specific document flow and the final scope of the judgment.
postwar_en: In the Ministries Trial before United States Military Tribunal IV, he was initially sentenced to seven years in 1949. A decision of 12 December 1949 set aside his conviction under count 1, affirmed the conviction under count 5 and reduced the sentence to five years. He was released in 1950 and died in 1979.
limitations_en: The original judgment must be distinguished from the decision of 12 December 1949: the conviction under count 1 was set aside, while that under count 5 was affirmed. The profile cannot assign Woermann the full body of Einsatzgruppen crimes or the Foreign Office's entire policy. The most secure individual basis is his part in approving the specific deportation of 6,000 people from France; the court did not base the conviction on a finding that at the time of the note he knew every detail of the later Auschwitz mechanism.

name: Klaus Barbie
organization_en: Sipo and SD · Gestapo in Lyon · KdS Lyon
organization_pl: Sipo i SD · Gestapo w Lyonie · KdS Lyon
role_en: head of a Gestapo section in Lyon, responsible for repression, interrogations and deportations
role_pl: szef sekcji Gestapo w Lyonie, odpowiedzialny za represje, przesłuchania i deportacje
role_de: Leiter einer Gestapo-Abteilung in Lyon, verantwortlich für Repression, Vernehmungen und Deportationen
role_ru: начальник секции гестапо в Лионе, отвечавший за репрессии, допросы и депортации
role_fr: chef d’une section de la Gestapo à Lyon, responsable de la répression, des interrogatoires et des déportations
status_en: sentenced to life imprisonment in 1987; died in prison in 1991
interpretation_en: Barbie's profile shows local Sipo and SD command as a link between interrogation and torture, a police operation against children and deportation. His own telegram concerning Izieu and the French trial make it possible to move from a familiar epithet to specific acts and their late legal classification.
postwar_en: After the war Barbie used the name Klaus Altmann, among others, and lived in Bolivia. Following years of disputes, he was extradited to France in 1983. The trial ended in 1987 with a life sentence for crimes against humanity; he died in prison in 1991.
limitations_en: The 1987 judgment concerned crimes against humanity within the French proceedings, not automatically every offence committed by the security apparatus in Lyon. The surviving telegram individualises the Izieu operation, but does not justify assigning Barbie the personal execution of every act during the arrest and transport. The profile does not uncritically repeat every postwar claim about his activities.

name: Friedrich Christiansen
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Wehrmacht · Wehrmacht Commander in the Netherlands · 25th Army
organization_pl: Wehrmacht · Wehrmachtsbefehlshaber in den Niederlanden · 25. Armia
role_en: Wehrmacht commander in the occupied Netherlands
role_pl: dowódca Wehrmachtu w okupowanej Holandii
role_de: Wehrmachtbefehlshaber in den besetzten Niederlanden
role_ru: командующий вермахтом в оккупированных Нидерландах
role_fr: commandant de la Wehrmacht dans les Pays-Bas occupés
status_en: sentenced to twelve years' imprisonment in 1948; released after the remainder of his sentence was remitted
interpretation_en: Christiansen contributes a distinct mechanism of collective military reprisal: a decision by the highest occupation commander was translated by subordinate units into a round-up, the burning of buildings and the deportation of civilians. The profile shows that occupation repression was not solely the province of the Sipo and SD.
postwar_en: He was arrested on 6 July 1945 and handed over to the Netherlands. In 1948 a special court in Arnhem sentenced him to twelve years' imprisonment for participating in occupation crimes, including the reprisal at Putten. The remainder of the sentence was remitted, and he was released on 19 December 1951; he died in 1972.
limitations_en: Christiansen's order individualises the decision on the reprisal, but arrests, executions, burnings and selections on the ground were carried out by subordinate units. Figures for those detained, deported and surviving differ with the scope and date of the tally; the profile does not turn these estimates into one seemingly exact number or attribute to the commander personal participation in every act.

name: Alexander von Falkenhausen
organization_en: Wehrmacht · Military Administration in Belgium and Northern France
organization_pl: Wehrmacht · Militärverwaltung in Belgien und Nordfrankreich
role_en: military governor of occupied Belgium and northern France
role_pl: wojskowy gubernator okupowanej Belgii i północnej Francji
role_de: Militärbefehlshaber im besetzten Belgien und in Nordfrankreich
role_ru: военный губернатор оккупированных Бельгии и Северной Франции
role_fr: gouverneur militaire de la Belgique et du nord de la France occupés
status_en: sentenced in Belgium in 1951 to twelve years' hard labour; released after prior detention was credited
interpretation_en: Von Falkenhausen shows military administration as an apparatus that both made rules and applied repression: decrees on hostages and forced labour supplied the framework for executions, arrests and deportations. His contacts with the German opposition do not remove the responsibility established by the Belgian court.
postwar_en: After being removed from office and imprisoned by the Nazi regime, he was handed over to Belgium after the war. In 1951 he was sentenced to twelve years at hard labour. Credit for his lengthy detention meant that he left prison soon after the judgment and returned to Germany; he died in 1966.
limitations_en: The powers of von Falkenhausen, administrative chief Eggert Reeder and the Sipo and SD structures overlapped. The profile attributes to the governor his decrees, knowledge, supervision and the scope established by the judgment, not the personal selection of every hostage, labourer or deported Jew. Sources also document his conflicts with the Nazi leadership and contacts with the opposition; these are not grounds for diminishing the documented repression.

name: Günther Pancke
organization_en: SS · Higher SS and Police Leader Denmark · German police in Denmark
organization_pl: SS · Höherer SS- und Polizeiführer Dänemark · niemiecka policja w Danii
role_en: Higher SS and Police Leader in occupied Denmark
role_pl: wyższy dowódca SS i policji w okupowanej Danii
role_de: Höherer SS- und Polizeiführer im besetzten Dänemark
role_ru: высший руководитель СС и полиции в оккупированной Дании
role_fr: chef supérieur de la SS et de la police dans le Danemark occupé
status_en: sentenced in Denmark in 1948 to twenty years' imprisonment; pardoned and expelled in 1953
interpretation_en: Pancke represents a distinct occupation mechanism: the removal of a national police force as an institutional obstacle to German terror. His role comprised preparing the plan, obtaining approval within the SS hierarchy and co-directing the operation, rather than merely holding office.
postwar_en: Pancke was tried in Denmark together with other senior occupation officials. In 1948 he received a sentence of twenty years' imprisonment. In 1953 he was pardoned and expelled to the Federal Republic of Germany; he died in 1973.
limitations_en: Planning, approval and execution of the operation were divided among Pancke, von Hanneken, Bovensiepen, Himmler, Hitler and the units on the ground. The profile does not attribute to Pancke the personal arrest of every police officer or every later crime of auxiliary formations. The approximate number of deportees is retained as such instead of creating false precision.

name: Herbert Kappler
organization_en: Sipo and SD · Gestapo · Rome Außenkommando
organization_pl: Sipo i SD · Gestapo · Außenkommando Rom
role_en: commander of the Sipo and SD in occupied Rome
role_pl: dowódca Sipo i SD w okupowanym Rzymie
role_de: Befehlshaber der Sicherheitspolizei und des SD im besetzten Rom
role_ru: командующий Полицией безопасности и СД в оккупированном Риме
role_fr: commandant de la Police de sûreté et du SD dans la Rome occupée
status_en: sentenced to life imprisonment; escaped to West Germany in 1977 and died in 1978
interpretation_en: Kappler connects two dimensions of Sipo and SD occupation activity: extortion, arrest and deportation directed against Jews, and a police-military reprisal execution. The trial makes it possible to distinguish his own role in the Fosse Ardeatine in detail from decisions made higher in the chain of command.
postwar_en: In 1948 an Italian military court sentenced Kappler to life imprisonment for his role in the Fosse Ardeatine massacre. He served his sentence in Italy and was later moved to a military hospital because of his health. In 1977 he escaped to West Germany, which did not extradite him back to Italy; he died the following year.
limitations_en: The Italian judgment of 1948 primarily individualises the Fosse Ardeatine massacre; historical findings on the extortion and deportation of Jews have a separate basis and should not be presented as the subject of the same conviction. The chain of decision-making on the reprisal also included Albert Kesselring, Eberhard von Mackensen, Kurt Mälzer and others, so the profile does not assign Kappler sole authorship of the reprisal policy.

name: Walter Reder
organization_en: Waffen-SS · 16th SS Panzergrenadier Division Reichsführer-SS · SS Panzer Reconnaissance Battalion 16
role_en: commander of the reconnaissance battalion of the 16th SS Panzergrenadier Division Reichsführer-SS
role_pl: dowódca batalionu rozpoznawczego 16. Dywizji Grenadierów Pancernych SS „Reichsführer-SS”
role_de: Kommandeur der Aufklärungsabteilung der 16. SS-Panzergrenadier-Division ‚Reichsführer-SS‘
role_ru: командир разведывательного батальона 16-й моторизованной дивизии СС «Рейхсфюрер СС»
role_fr: commandant du bataillon de reconnaissance de la 16e division de Panzergrenadiers SS Reichsführer-SS
status_en: sentenced to life imprisonment in 1951; released on parole in 1985
interpretation_en: Reder contributes the mechanism of a mobile Waffen-SS unit that, under the doctrine of anti-partisan warfare, carried out synchronised operations against entire concentrations of civilians. His profile is deliberately based both on the command structure and on the precise boundary of the Italian judgment.
postwar_en: After extradition to Italy, Reder was tried by the Military Tribunal of Bologna. In 1951 he received a life sentence and was imprisoned for decades in Gaeta. In 1985 he was released on parole and transferred to Austria; he died in 1991.
limitations_en: The Italian court held Reder responsible for only four of the nine episodes it considered; acquittals and unproved charges must not be concealed. Commanding the battalion does not mean that he personally fired every shot. Victim figures for individual localities and for the operation as a whole depend on the geographic scope and set of episodes adopted, so the profile does not aggregate them into one unverified total.

name: Friedrich-Wilhelm Müller
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Wehrmacht · 22nd Infantry Division · Fortress Crete
role_en: commander of the 22nd Infantry Division and commandant of Fortress Crete
role_pl: dowódca 22. Dywizji Piechoty i komendant Twierdzy Kreta
role_de: Kommandeur der 22. Infanterie-Division und Kommandant der Festung Kreta
role_ru: командир 22-й пехотной дивизии и комендант крепости Крит
role_fr: commandant de la 22e division d’infanterie et commandant de la forteresse de Crète
status_en: sentenced to death in Greece; executed by firing squad on 20 May 1947
interpretation_en: Müller is an example of the direct connection between Wehrmacht command, a written order to destroy a locality and the field execution of civilians. Placing Viannos and Anogia together shows a repeated mechanism of reprisal, but the profile remains confined to episodes individualised by documents.
postwar_en: After the war Müller was handed over to Greece and stood trial with Bruno Bräuer before a special military court in Athens. He was sentenced to death in December 1946. The sentence was carried out by firing squad on 20 May 1947.
limitations_en: The Greek trial covered a broad set of occupation crimes on Crete, while later research warns against automatically assigning every crime to a single commander. The profile bases its core on documented orders and operations in Viannos and Anogia; it does not attribute to Müller every German massacre on the island or every act of subordinate soldiers. Estimates for the victims of Viannos vary with the geographic scope used.

name: Herbert Andorfer
organization_en: SS · BdS Belgrade · Semlin Jewish Camp · Sonderkommando Andorfer
organization_pl: SS · BdS Belgrad · Judenlager Semlin · Sonderkommando Andorfer
role_en: commandant of the Sajmište camp and commander of Sonderkommando Andorfer in Italy
role_pl: komendant obozu Sajmište i dowódca Sonderkommando Andorfer we Włoszech
role_de: Kommandant des Lagers Sajmište und Befehlshaber des Sonderkommandos Andorfer in Italien
role_ru: комендант лагеря Саймиште и командир зондеркоманды Андорфера в Италии
role_fr: commandant du camp de Sajmište et chef du Sonderkommando Andorfer en Italie
region_pl: Sajmište · Jajinci · Belgrad · Bassano del Grappa
status_en: sentenced in 1969 to two years and six months; released after pretrial detention was credited
interpretation_en: Andorfer shows how the function of camp commandant connected a daily transport routine with the gas-van killing technique and concealment of the victims' bodies. His later command of a special unit in Italy broadens the profile to show continuity in a career of repression, but the two theatres are kept separate in the sources.
postwar_en: After the war Andorfer hid under the name Hans Mayer. He was arrested in 1967. Dortmund Regional Court sentenced him in January 1969 to two years and six months' imprisonment for aiding and abetting the murder of more than 5,500 Sajmište prisoners; the entire sentence was covered by time already spent in custody. He died in 2003.
limitations_en: The Dortmund judgment concerned participation in the murder of Sajmište prisoners, not the Italian crimes of Sonderkommando Andorfer. Surviving correspondence, the court's findings and survivor accounts allow the commandant's regular participation to be described, but not each route or death individually. Sources give both 16 and 30 January 1969; the profile records the month without deciding, in the absence of the files, whether these are the dates of judgment and pronouncement.

name: Willi Seibert
organization_en: Einsatzgruppe D · Security Service · RSHA Office III
organization_pl: Einsatzgruppe D · Sicherheitsdienst · RSHA Amt III
role_en: de facto deputy commander of Einsatzgruppe D and officer linking command with the reporting of executions
role_pl: faktyczny zastępca dowódcy Einsatzgruppe D i oficer łączący dowództwo z raportowaniem egzekucji
role_de: faktischer Stellvertreter des Befehlshabers der Einsatzgruppe D und Verbindungsoffizier zwischen Führung und Berichterstattung über Hinrichtungen
role_ru: фактический заместитель командира айнзацгруппы D и офицер, связывавший командование с отчётностью о казнях
role_fr: commandant adjoint de fait de l’Einsatzgruppe D et officier assurant la liaison entre le commandement et les rapports sur les exécutions
region_en: occupied Soviet Union — southern Ukraine and Crimea
main_region_country: okupowany ZSRR — południowa Ukraina i Krym
status_en: sentenced to death in 1948; sentence commuted to fifteen years, released in 1954
interpretation_en: Seibert shows that reporting was not a passive clerical function: aggregating exact data on executions, transmitting orders and maintaining liaison with the army were elements in commanding a mobile mass-murder formation. The profile separates that proved participation from a claim that he was physically present at every shooting.
postwar_en: Seibert was a defendant in the ninth subsequent Nuremberg trial. In 1948 he was sentenced to death on all three categories of charges. In 1951 an American review of the sentences commuted the penalty to fifteen years' imprisonment; Seibert left prison in 1954 and died in 1976.
limitations_en: The defence disputed Seibert's formal title as deputy and his direct supervision of individual executions; after analysing the documents, the tribunal found him to have been the de facto deputy and a perpetrator or accomplice. Reports, signatures and liaison prove knowing participation, but not his presence at every mass shooting or his personal killing of all victims of Einsatzgruppe D.

name: Robert Ritter
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Reich Health Office · Race Hygiene and Population Biology Research Unit · Criminal Biology Institute of the Security Police
organization_pl: Reichsgesundheitsamt · Rassenhygienische und bevölkerungspolitische Forschungsstelle · Kriminalbiologisches Institut der Sicherheitspolizei
rank: dr med.; kierownik Rassenhygienische und bevölkerungspolitische Forschungsstelle
role_en: physician and child psychiatrist; head of the unit that registered and pseudoscientifically classified Roma and Sinti for the Nazi apparatus of persecution
role_pl: lekarz i psychiatra dziecięcy; kierownik placówki, która rejestrowała i pseudonaukowo klasyfikowała Romów i Sinti na potrzeby nazistowskiego aparatu prześladowań
role_de: Arzt und Kinderpsychiater; Leiter der Stelle, die Sinti und Roma für den nationalsozialistischen Verfolgungsapparat erfasste und pseudowissenschaftlich klassifizierte
role_ru: врач и детский психиатр; руководитель учреждения, которое регистрировало и псевдонаучно классифицировало рома и синти для нацистского аппарата преследования
role_fr: médecin et pédopsychiatre ; chef du service qui recensait et classait pseudo-scientifiquement les Roms et les Sinti pour l’appareil nazi de persécution
region_en: Germany — Berlin and the nationwide public-health and criminal-police apparatus
main_region_country: Niemcy — Berlin i ogólnokrajowy aparat zdrowia oraz policji kryminalnej
status_en: never tried; a preliminary investigation opened in Frankfurt in 1950 was dismissed
interpretation_en: The profile shows how a physician’s authority, questionnaires and files became instruments of police persecution. Ritter’s documented connection lies in producing classifications, a register and assessments used by the state apparatus; it does not establish that he personally issued every later deportation order or participated in every crime against Roma and Sinti.
postwar_en: Denazification authorities allowed Ritter to resume work, and in 1947 he became head of youth psychiatry in Frankfurt am Main. Complaints by survivors led to a preliminary investigation in 1950, but the prosecutor dismissed it. Ritter died in 1951 without having stood trial.
limitations_en: The profile does not assign Ritter the aggregate death toll of the genocide of Roma and Sinti or authorship of every deportation order. The sources establish his leadership, classification methods, cooperation with the police and the use of the register; a separate document is required to connect him to a specific deportation or killing. His non-membership in the Nazi Party does not diminish the professional and institutional responsibility established here.

name: Konstantin von Neurath
organization_en: German Foreign Office · Reich Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia · Secret Cabinet Council · Reich Defence Council
organization_pl: Auswärtiges Amt · Reichsprotektorat Böhmen und Mähren · Geheimer Kabinettsrat · Reichsverteidigungsrat
role_en: German Foreign Minister from 1932 to 1938 and Reich Protector of Bohemia and Moravia from 1939 to 1941
role_pl: minister spraw zagranicznych Rzeszy w latach 1932–1938 i Protektor Rzeszy Czech i Moraw w latach 1939–1941
role_de: deutscher Außenminister von 1932 bis 1938 und Reichsprotektor für Böhmen und Mähren von 1939 bis 1941
role_ru: министр иностранных дел Германии в 1932–1938 годах и рейхспротектор Богемии и Моравии в 1939–1941 годах
role_fr: ministre allemand des Affaires étrangères de 1932 à 1938 et protecteur du Reich en Bohême-Moravie de 1939 à 1941
region_en: Germany and the occupied Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia
main_region_country: Niemcy i okupowany Protektorat Czech i Moraw
status_en: sentenced by the IMT to 15 years’ imprisonment; released for reasons of health in 1954 after serving eight years
interpretation_en: Neurath’s profile connects two distinct phases: diplomatic support for the state’s aggressive policy and leadership of the administration of the occupied Protectorate. Attribution rests on the IMT judgment’s findings about his offices, knowledge and authority; it does not automatically transfer to him every police act or Heydrich’s later terror.
postwar_en: The IMT found Neurath guilty of conspiracy, crimes against peace, war crimes and crimes against humanity. He received a sentence of 15 years’ imprisonment. He was released for reasons of health in 1954 after serving eight years and died in 1956.
limitations_en: The profile separates his term as Foreign Minister (1932–1938) from the period in which he actually exercised the office of Reich Protector (18 March 1939–27 September 1941). He formally retained the title until August 1943, but went on leave and refused to continue acting after Heydrich was sent to Prague. The judgment also noted his interventions for some detainees; these mitigating circumstances did not alter the finding of guilt on all four counts.

name: Fritz ter Meer
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: IG Farben executive board · IG Farben Technical Committee · Chemical Industry Economic Group
organization_pl: IG Farben Vorstand · Technischer Ausschuss IG Farben · Wirtschaftsgruppe Chemische Industrie
rank: członek Vorstand; przewodniczący Technischer Ausschuss; Wehrwirtschaftsführer
role_en: IG Farben executive-board member and chair of its Technical Committee; convicted of spoliation in occupied countries and participation in forced labour
role_pl: członek zarządu i przewodniczący komitetu technicznego IG Farben; skazany za grabież mienia w krajach okupowanych i udział w pracy przymusowej
role_de: Vorstandsmitglied der IG Farben und Vorsitzender ihres Technischen Ausschusses; wegen Plünderung in besetzten Ländern und Beteiligung an Zwangsarbeit verurteilt
role_ru: член правления IG Farben и председатель Технического комитета; осуждён за разграбление в оккупированных странах и участие в принудительном труде
role_fr: membre du directoire d’IG Farben et président de son comité technique ; condamné pour spoliation dans les pays occupés et participation au travail forcé
region_en: occupied Poland and France — IG Farben, Auschwitz-Monowitz and seized enterprises
main_region_country: okupowana Polska i Francja — IG Farben, Auschwitz-Monowitz i przejmowane przedsiębiorstwa
status_en: convicted on Counts II and III in the IG Farben Trial and sentenced to seven years; released in 1950
interpretation_en: The profile individualises a senior corporate officer’s responsibility through specific judicial findings: participation in property seizures and active procurement of forced labour. It does not rely on board membership alone and does not attribute to ter Meer every IG Farben operation, every plant or medical experiments conducted by others.
postwar_en: The United States Military Tribunal in the IG Farben Trial convicted ter Meer on Counts II and III and sentenced him to seven years in prison. He was released for good behaviour in 1950. Bayer AG elected him to its supervisory board in 1956; he remained a member until 1964. He died in 1967.
limitations_en: The judgment links ter Meer personally to specified acts of spoliation and to forced-labour procurement for Auschwitz and Fürstengrube. The profile does not attribute to him all IG Farben activities, conditions at every construction site, Zyklon B production or medical experiments. His convictions were on Counts II and III; all defendants were acquitted on the crimes-against-peace and related conspiracy counts.

name: Heinz Schubert
organization_en: Einsatzgruppe D · SD · SS
role_en: Otto Ohlendorf’s adjutant in Einsatzgruppe D; supervised a mass shooting near Simferopol
role_pl: adiutant Otto Ohlendorfa w Einsatzgruppe D; nadzorował masową egzekucję pod Symferopolem
role_de: Adjutant Otto Ohlendorfs in der Einsatzgruppe D; beaufsichtigte eine Massenerschießung bei Simferopol
role_ru: адъютант Отто Олендорфа в айнзацгруппе D; осуществлял надзор за массовым расстрелом под Симферополем
role_fr: aide de camp d’Otto Ohlendorf dans l’Einsatzgruppe D ; supervisa une fusillade de masse près de Simferopol
status_en: death sentence in 1948; commuted to 10 years in 1951; free by January 1952
interpretation_en: Schubert’s case demonstrates responsibility for supervising the execution of a criminal order. The judgment links him to a specific killing operation, not merely to staff membership. His position must not be confused with the de facto deputy command held by Willi Seibert.
postwar_en: US Military Tribunal II at Nuremberg sentenced him to death in the Einsatzgruppen trial. After commutation to 10 years in 1951, he was released early; he was already free in January 1952. The biographical metadata of Harvard’s Nuremberg Trials Project gives his death year as 1987.
limitations_en: The approximate figure of 700–800 concerns the execution examined in the judgment, not a personal total of all Einsatzgruppe D victims. The perpetrator’s postwar testimony is considered alongside the court’s findings. We do not establish an exact release date or time served; Harvard’s metadata is not a substitute for reading the death certificate.

name: Harry Schulz
organization_en: Selbstschutz Westpreussen · Łobżenica Selbstschutz
role_en: deputy head of the Selbstschutz in Łobżenica and commandant of the camp at Górka Klasztorna
role_pl: zastępca kierownika Selbstschutzu w Łobżenicy i komendant obozu w Górce Klasztornej
role_de: stellvertretender Leiter des Selbstschutzes in Łobżenica und Leiter des Lagers Górka Klasztorna
role_ru: заместитель руководителя зельбстшутца в Лобженице и комендант лагеря в Гурке-Кляшторной
role_fr: chef adjoint du Selbstschutz de Łobżenica et commandant du camp de Górka Klasztorna
status_en: sentenced to death in Poland in 1953; sentence carried out in February 1954
interpretation_en: The profile connects local command with personal violence described by witnesses. Institution, place and individual perpetrator are distinguished: membership in the Selbstschutz does not suffice to attribute every local crime to every member.
postwar_en: According to the Institute for Western Affairs, the summary court in Bydgoszcz found him guilty of murdering 186 residents of Wyrzysk county. The IPN catalogue identifies Nakło as the place of trial. Following the 1953 judgment, the death sentence was carried out in February 1954. The judicial figure is not the total of all local Selbstschutz victims.
limitations_en: Witness accounts were collected after the war; details from Jan Topór’s testimony are not presented as findings from our own examination of the original files. The German rape conviction and the Polish murder conviction were separate proceedings. No execution day or method is given without examined documentation. The birth date comes from a reproduced photograph caption, not a civil register.

name: Karl Fritzsch
organization_en: SS · Auschwitz concentration camp · Flossenbürg concentration camp
role_en: Schutzhaftlagerführer at Auschwitz and Flossenbürg; head of the prisoners’ section
role_pl: Schutzhaftlagerführer w Auschwitz i Flossenbürgu; kierownik obozowej części więźniarskiej
role_de: Schutzhaftlagerführer in Auschwitz und Flossenbürg; Leiter des Häftlingslagers
role_ru: шуцхафтлагерфюрер в Аушвице и Флоссенбюрге; руководитель лагерной части для заключённых
role_fr: Schutzhaftlagerführer à Auschwitz et Flossenbürg ; chef de la partie du camp réservée aux détenus
status_en: died in 1945 according to the Flossenbürg Memorial; no postwar judgment
interpretation_en: Fritzsch’s office gave him authority over everyday camp operations and repression. Attribution of the gassing order rests on specific sources, not simply his position. We do not assign him the later Birkenau crematoria infrastructure or all Auschwitz victims.
postwar_en: No postwar trial or judgment is documented here. The Flossenbürg Memorial states that, after being sent to the front in autumn 1944, Fritzsch died during the battle of Berlin in 1945. We do not establish an exact death date.
limitations_en: The museum dates the start of gassing as probable; earlier experiments and the full sequence require separate reconstruction. An order, an office and personally carrying out an act are different claims. His position is not treated as proof that he personally poured in the substance. The circumstances of his death are attributed to the memorial, without an unverified exact date.

name: Adolf Ott
organization_en: Sonderkommando 7b · Einsatzgruppe B · SS
role_en: commander of Sonderkommando 7b within Einsatzgruppe B
role_pl: dowódca Sonderkommando 7b w Einsatzgruppe B
role_de: Kommandeur des Sonderkommandos 7b der Einsatzgruppe B
role_ru: командир зондеркоманды 7b в составе айнзацгруппы B
role_fr: commandant du Sonderkommando 7b au sein de l’Einsatzgruppe B
region_en: occupied Soviet Union · southern Russia and Ukraine
region_pl: południowa Rosja i Ukraina · okupowany ZSRR
status_en: death sentence in 1948; commuted to life imprisonment; later released
interpretation_en: Ott’s responsibility rests on commanding a killing unit and on his own admissions about the criterion used to select victims. The profile does not automatically attribute every crime of Einsatzgruppe B to him.
postwar_en: The Einsatzgruppen tribunal at Nuremberg sentenced Ott to death. The sentence was commuted to life imprisonment, and the clemency policy of the 1950s ultimately led to his release.
limitations_en: The figure of at least twenty victims is Ott’s own estimate as cited in the judgment, not a complete total for Sonderkommando 7b. The sources do not establish his personal presence at every shooting carried out by the unit.

name: Adolf Theuer
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Auschwitz concentration camp · SS-Totenkopfverbände
role_en: SS medical orderly and member of the Auschwitz disinfection squad; participant in gassing operations
role_pl: sanitariusz SS i członek zespołu dezynfekcyjnego w KL Auschwitz; uczestnik operacji gazowania
role_de: SS-Sanitäter und Angehöriger der Desinfektionsabteilung; Beteiligter an Vergasungen
role_ru: санитар СС и сотрудник дезинфекционной команды; участник газовых убийств
role_fr: infirmier SS et membre de l’équipe de désinfection ; participant aux opérations de gazage
status_en: sentenced to death and executed at Opava on 23 April 1947
interpretation_en: The evidence connects Theuer to the technical execution of killing by gas, not to deportation policy or the selection of every victim. Two independent prisoner accounts reinforce the identification of his role.
postwar_en: Czechoslovak justice sentenced Theuer to death for Nazi crimes. The sentence was carried out at Opava on 23 April 1947.
limitations_en: The sources use the surname variants Teuer and Theuer and differ on his precise SS rank. The profile describes documented participation in gassing procedures without attributing to him decisions over the entire Auschwitz killing programme.

name: Adolf Winkelmann
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Ravensbrück concentration camp · SS
role_en: camp physician at Ravensbrück; participant in selections of women prisoners
role_pl: lekarz obozowy w KL Ravensbrück; uczestnik selekcji więźniarek
role_de: Lagerarzt in Ravensbrück; Beteiligter an Selektionen weiblicher Häftlinge
role_ru: лагерный врач в Равенсбрюке; участник селекций заключённых женщин
role_fr: médecin du camp de Ravensbrück ; participant aux sélections de détenues
status_en: found guilty; died on 1 February 1947 before sentencing
interpretation_en: Winkelmann’s documented responsibility concerns medical selection in the final phase of Ravensbrück. His admission confirms participation, while numerical estimates in witness testimony must remain explicitly attributed.
postwar_en: The first British Ravensbrück trial found Winkelmann guilty. He died in custody on 1 February 1947, so the court did not impose a sentence.
limitations_en: The statement that 4,500 women were selected comes from Gustawa Winkowska’s testimony and is not an adjudicated personal victim total. Other testimony cited in the study gives 1,500–2,000; the profile preserves this discrepancy.

name: Adolf Zutter
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Mauthausen concentration camp · SS-Totenkopfverbände
role_en: adjutant to the Mauthausen commandant; staff link in the processing of execution orders
role_pl: adiutant komendanta KL Mauthausen; ogniwo obiegu rozkazów egzekucyjnych
role_de: Adjutant des Mauthausener Kommandanten; Stabsstelle im Umlauf von Hinrichtungsbefehlen
role_ru: адъютант коменданта Маутхаузена; штабное звено в прохождении приказов о казнях
role_fr: adjudant du commandant de Mauthausen ; maillon administratif du traitement des ordres d’exécution
status_en: sentenced to death on 13 May 1946; executed on 27 May 1947
interpretation_en: Zutter was not the Mauthausen commandant, but as adjutant he was a central link in the circulation of execution orders. The profile rests on his own procedural account and the trial findings.
postwar_en: A US military court at Dachau convicted Zutter in the main Mauthausen trial and sentenced him to death. He was hanged at Landsberg prison on 27 May 1947.
limitations_en: Zutter’s affidavit documents command-office procedure in detail but does not by itself prove his presence at every execution. The profile distinguishes the adjutant’s function from the commandant’s decisions and the acts of other staff.

name: Albert Kesselring
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Wehrmacht · Luftwaffe · Army Group C
role_en: field marshal; Commander-in-Chief South-West and commander of Army Group C in Italy
role_pl: feldmarszałek; naczelny dowódca na południowym zachodzie i dowódca Grupy Armii C we Włoszech
role_de: Generalfeldmarschall; Oberbefehlshaber Südwest und Befehlshaber der Heeresgruppe C in Italien
role_ru: фельдмаршал; главнокомандующий Юго-Западом и командующий группой армий C в Италии
role_fr: maréchal ; commandant en chef Sud-Ouest et chef du groupe d’armées C en Italie
status_en: death sentence in 1947; commuted to life; released in 1952
interpretation_en: Kesselring’s case concerns the responsibility of a senior commander for issuing and maintaining unlawful reprisal orders. It does not mean that he personally selected every victim or carried out the executions.
postwar_en: A British military court at Venice sentenced Kesselring to death for crimes connected with reprisals in Italy. The sentence was commuted to life imprisonment, and he was released in 1952.
limitations_en: The chain of responsibility for the Ardeatine massacre included Hitler, military commanders, Security Police and direct perpetrators. This profile attributes to Kesselring only the orders and command responsibility found by the court.

name: Alexander Piorkowski
organization_en: Dachau concentration camp · SS-Totenkopfverbände
role_en: commandant of Dachau concentration camp from February 1940 to September 1942
role_pl: komendant KL Dachau od lutego 1940 do września 1942
role_de: Kommandant des KZ Dachau von Februar 1940 bis September 1942
role_ru: комендант концлагеря Дахау с февраля 1940 по сентябрь 1942 года
role_fr: commandant du camp de concentration de Dachau de février 1940 à septembre 1942
status_en: sentenced to death and executed on 22 October 1948
interpretation_en: Piorkowski’s responsibility includes both his own command decisions and control of the camp’s machinery of violence. The profile separates those findings from acts of subordinates that were not proved as his personal conduct in every instance.
postwar_en: In a separate trial before a US military court at Dachau, Piorkowski was sentenced to death. The review upheld the sentence, which was carried out on 22 October 1948.
limitations_en: Command responsibility does not mean personally carrying out every punishment or experiment. The profile lists only acts and omissions individualised in the trial record and historical analysis.

name: Alfred Ittner
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Sobibor · Operation Reinhard · SS
role_en: Sobibor staff member; cashier who took victims’ property before the gas chamber
role_pl: członek załogi Sobiboru; kasjer odbierający mienie ofiar przed komorą gazową
role_de: Angehöriger der Sobibór-Besatzung; Kassierer, der den Opfern vor der Gaskammer ihr Eigentum abnahm
role_ru: сотрудник Собибора; кассир, отбиравший имущество жертв перед газовой камерой
role_fr: membre du personnel de Sobibór ; caissier prenant les biens des victimes avant la chambre à gaz
status_en: sentenced in 1966 to four years for aiding mass murder
interpretation_en: Ittner’s role shows that administrative confiscation immediately before the gas chamber formed part of the organised killing process. The judgment classified his responsibility as aiding murder, not as sole perpetration of the entire operation.
postwar_en: In the Sobibor staff trial before the Hagen Regional Court, Ittner received four years’ imprisonment for aiding the murder of at least 68,000 people.
limitations_en: Work at the cashier’s desk immediately preceded entry into the gas chamber, but the sources do not support a claim that Ittner personally operated the gassing equipment. The profile follows the court’s classification of aiding murder.

name: Alfred Trzebinski
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Neuengamme concentration camp · SS-Totenkopfverbände
role_en: SS physician at Neuengamme; participant in the Bullenhuser Damm murders
role_pl: lekarz SS w KL Neuengamme; uczestnik mordu w Bullenhuser Damm
role_de: SS-Arzt in Neuengamme; Beteiligter an den Morden am Bullenhuser Damm
role_ru: врач СС в Нойенгамме; участник убийств в Булленхузер-Дамм
role_fr: médecin SS à Neuengamme ; participant aux meurtres du Bullenhuser Damm
status_en: sentenced to death on 3 May 1946; executed on 8 October 1946
interpretation_en: Trzebinski’s responsibility is individualised through his function as an SS physician and specific acts at Bullenhuser Damm. The profile does not attribute to him every crime committed at the camps where he served.
postwar_en: The first British Neuengamme staff trial at the Curiohaus sentenced Trzebinski to death. He was hanged at Hameln prison on 8 October 1946.
limitations_en: The sources individualise his participation at Bullenhuser Damm, but other defendants also performed parts of the operation. The stated numbers concern this single killing operation, not a personal total for all his acts.

name: Alice Orlowski
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Majdanek · Płaszów · Auschwitz-Birkenau · SS auxiliaries
role_en: SS guard at Majdanek, Płaszów and Auschwitz-Birkenau
role_pl: nadzorczyni SS w Majdanku, Płaszowie i Auschwitz-Birkenau
role_de: SS-Aufseherin in Majdanek, Płaszów und Auschwitz-Birkenau
role_ru: надзирательница СС в Майданеке, Плашуве и Аушвице-Биркенау
role_fr: gardienne SS à Majdanek, Płaszów et Auschwitz-Birkenau
status_en: sentenced to fifteen years on 22 December 1947; released in 1957
interpretation_en: Orlowski’s profile combines witness accounts with the court’s assessment rather than relying on staff membership alone. Her conviction concerned her own conduct and participation in camp violence.
postwar_en: The Supreme National Tribunal sentenced Orlowski to fifteen years in the Kraków Auschwitz trial. She was released in 1957 and later stood trial in the Majdanek proceedings, but died before that trial ended.
limitations_en: Witness accounts describe specific conduct, but not every reference permits an exact date and place. The profile does not automatically link her to every crime committed at the camps where she served.

name: Anneliese Kohlmann
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Neuengamme · Neugraben · Tiefstack · SS auxiliaries
role_en: guard at the Neugraben and Tiefstack subcamps of Neuengamme
role_pl: nadzorczyni w podobozach Neuengamme Neugraben i Tiefstack
role_de: Aufseherin in den Neuengamme-Außenlagern Neugraben und Tiefstack
role_ru: надзирательница в филиалах Нойенгамме Нойграбен и Тифштак
role_fr: gardienne dans les camps annexes de Neuengamme à Neugraben et Tiefstack
status_en: sentenced in 1946 to two years’ imprisonment
interpretation_en: Kohlmann’s responsibility is described through specific guard duties, witness identifications and her own admission to beatings. The short sentence does not erase the established conduct, but it defines the scope of the court’s assessment.
postwar_en: Kohlmann appeared before a British military court at Celle in proceedings concerning Neuengamme subcamp staff. She was sentenced to two years’ imprisonment.
limitations_en: The evidence individualises beatings and escort duties but does not justify attributing every subcamp crime to Kohlmann. The profile distinguishes witness testimony, her admission and the judgment’s scope.

name: Anton Dostler
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Wehrmacht · LXXV Army Corps
role_en: Wehrmacht general and commander of LXXV Army Corps in Italy
role_pl: generał Wehrmachtu; dowódca LXXV Korpusu Armijnego we Włoszech
role_de: Wehrmachtgeneral und Kommandierender General des LXXV. Armeekorps in Italien
role_ru: генерал Вермахта и командир 75-го армейского корпуса в Италии
role_fr: général de la Wehrmacht et commandant du LXXVe corps d’armée en Italie
status_en: convicted of a war crime and executed on 1 December 1945
interpretation_en: The Dostler trial became a precedent that a superior order does not relieve a commander of responsibility for an obviously unlawful execution of prisoners. The profile concerns one specific order affecting fifteen men.
postwar_en: A US military commission convicted Dostler for ordering the unlawful killing of prisoners of war. He was executed by firing squad at Aversa on 1 December 1945.
limitations_en: The case concerns an individualised order to execute fifteen soldiers, not a complete account of LXXV Corps operations. Subordinates participated in the execution chain, but the judgment focused on Dostler’s personal order.

name: Anton Kaindl
organization_en: Sachsenhausen concentration camp · SS-Totenkopfverbände
role_en: commandant of Sachsenhausen concentration camp from 1942 to 1945
role_pl: komendant KL Sachsenhausen w latach 1942–1945
role_de: Kommandant des KZ Sachsenhausen von 1942 bis 1945
role_ru: комендант концлагеря Заксенхаузен в 1942–1945 годах
role_fr: commandant du camp de Sachsenhausen de 1942 à 1945
status_en: sentenced in 1947 to lifelong forced labour; died at Vorkuta in 1948
interpretation_en: Kaindl’s responsibility rests on his position as commandant and the specific order to prepare an evacuation that became a death march. His sworn affidavit also documents his knowledge of the concentration-camp system.
postwar_en: A Soviet military tribunal sentenced Kaindl in 1947 to lifelong forced labour. He was deported to Vorkuta and died there on 31 August 1948.
limitations_en: The figure of more than one thousand deaths concerns the entire death march, not Kaindl’s personal victim total. The profile attributes to him the evacuation order and command responsibility, not every shot fired by guards.

name: Anton Thumann
organization_en: Majdanek · Neuengamme · SS-Totenkopfverbände
role_en: senior prisoner-camp officer at Majdanek and Neuengamme
role_pl: funkcjonariusz kierownictwa więźniarskiego w Majdanku i Neuengamme
role_de: Funktionär der Häftlingslagerführung in Majdanek und Neuengamme
role_ru: руководящий сотрудник лагерного режима в Майданеке и Нойенгамме
role_fr: responsable du régime des détenus à Majdanek et Neuengamme
status_en: sentenced to death on 3 May 1946; executed on 8 October 1946
interpretation_en: Thumann’s responsibility encompasses senior functions in the prisoner regime and participation in two specific executions near the end of Neuengamme. The profile does not rest on rank or assignment alone.
postwar_en: In the first British Neuengamme staff trial at the Curiohaus, Thumann was defendant no. 3 and received a death sentence. He was executed at Hameln on 8 October 1946.
limitations_en: The stated numbers concern two executions on 21 and 23 April 1945, not a complete total for his service at Majdanek and Neuengamme. Other staff also acted in the executions; the profile retains the individualisation in the record.

name: August Becker
organization_en: RSHA · Aktion T4 · SS
role_en: RSHA chemist and technical inspector of T4 gassing installations and Einsatzgruppen gas vans
role_pl: chemik RSHA i inspektor techniczny instalacji gazowych Akcji T4 oraz samochodów gazowych
role_de: Chemiker des RSHA und technischer Inspekteur von T4-Gasanlagen und Gaswagen der Einsatzgruppen
role_ru: химик РСХА и технический инспектор газовых установок T4 и газвагенов айнзацгрупп
role_fr: chimiste du RSHA et inspecteur technique des installations de gazage de T4 et des camions à gaz des Einsatzgruppen
status_en: sentenced to ten years; released before completing the term for health reasons
interpretation_en: His responsibility rests on the documented conversion of chemical expertise into killing procedures and his direct technical supervision of equipment used for mass murder.
postwar_en: He received a ten-year prison sentence but did not serve it in full because of ill health.
limitations_en: Accounts differ over who personally carried out the first Brandenburg gassing. This profile attributes only the tasks supported by the archival record, including his regulation of the second Brandenburg gassing and his work at Grafeneck. The identity record gives an exact death date, while the archive confirms only the year 1967.

name: August Eigruber
organization_en: NSDAP · Reichsgau Oberdonau · SS
role_en: Gauleiter and Reich governor of Reichsgau Oberdonau
role_pl: Gauleiter i namiestnik Rzeszy w Reichsgau Oberdonau
role_de: Gauleiter und Reichsstatthalter des Reichsgaus Oberdonau
role_ru: гауляйтер и рейхсштатгальтер рейхсгау Верхний Дунай
role_fr: Gauleiter et gouverneur du Reich dans le Reichsgau Oberdonau
status_en: sentenced to death in the Mauthausen trial; executed on 28 May 1947
interpretation_en: The profile links his regional authority to a specific documented execution order and does not automatically attribute every crime committed in the Mauthausen complex to him.
postwar_en: The U.S. military tribunal in the main Mauthausen case sentenced him to death; the sentence was carried out at Landsberg.
limitations_en: His political responsibility for the Mauthausen system was broader than one order, but this profile foregrounds the act of 27 April 1945 documented by the Mauthausen Memorial and survivor Richard Dietl.

name: August Frank
tier_label_en: Designers of the machinery of destruction
organization_en: WVHA · SS
role_en: deputy chief of the WVHA and head of Amtsgruppe A
role_pl: zastępca szefa WVHA i kierownik Amtsgruppe A
role_de: Stellvertreter des WVHA-Chefs und Leiter der Amtsgruppe A
role_ru: заместитель начальника ВФХА и руководитель группы управлений A
role_fr: adjoint du chef du WVHA et responsable de l’Amtsgruppe A
region_pl: Berlin · system obozów koncentracyjnych · okupowana Polska
status_en: sentenced to life in the Pohl trial; sentence commuted to fifteen years
interpretation_en: Frank’s responsibility is documented in administrative and financial acts that integrated slave labor and the looting of victims’ property into WVHA operations.
postwar_en: The Pohl tribunal sentenced him to life imprisonment; the sentence was later commuted to fifteen years.
limitations_en: The tribunal expressly found insufficient evidence to hold Frank legally responsible for the murders themselves. This profile separates that finding from his convictions for slave labor and wholesale looting.

name: August Meyszner
organization_en: HSSPF Serbia · Order Police · Security Police and SD · SS
organization_pl: HSSPF Serbien · Ordnungspolizei · Sipo i SD · SS
role_en: Higher SS and Police Leader in occupied Serbia
role_pl: Wyższy Dowódca SS i Policji w okupowanej Serbii
role_de: Höherer SS- und Polizeiführer im besetzten Serbien
role_ru: высший руководитель СС и полиции в оккупированной Сербии
role_fr: chef supérieur de la SS et de la police en Serbie occupée
status_en: sentenced to death in Belgrade; executed on 24 January 1947
interpretation_en: Meyszner’s responsibility rests both on command of the regional SS and police apparatus and on a documented personal order for a mass hostage execution.
postwar_en: After extradition to Yugoslavia, a Belgrade military court sentenced him to death; he was hanged on 24 January 1947.
limitations_en: Meyszner’s role in the gas-van murder of Jewish women and children from Sajmište is disputed because BdS Emanuel Schäfer also operated through an independent RSHA chain. The profile does not attribute personal control of the gas van or every police victim to Meyszner. His Belgrade trial concerned occupation crimes more broadly, not only the Holocaust.

name: August Wilhelm Miete
organization_en: Treblinka II · Operation Reinhard · SS
role_en: Treblinka staff member responsible for the so-called infirmary and supervision of prisoner labor details
role_pl: funkcjonariusz Treblinki odpowiedzialny za tzw. lazaret i nadzór nad więźniami roboczymi
role_de: Angehöriger der Treblinka-Besatzung mit Verantwortung für das sogenannte Lazarett und die Beaufsichtigung von Arbeitskommandos
role_ru: сотрудник Треблинки, отвечавший за так называемый лазарет и надзор за рабочими командами заключённых
role_fr: membre du personnel de Treblinka responsable du prétendu lazaret et de la surveillance des commandos de travail
status_en: sentenced to life imprisonment in the Treblinka trial
interpretation_en: Miete’s guilt rests on direct killings and knowing, active participation in Treblinka’s mass-extermination mechanism, not merely on formal membership in the camp staff.
postwar_en: The Düsseldorf Regional Court sentenced him to life imprisonment on 3 September 1965.
limitations_en: The figure of 300,000 describes legal responsibility as co-perpetrator in the collective mass murder, not the number of people he personally shot. The judgment separately proved eight murder acts against at least nine victims. Further acts disclosed at trial but outside the indictment did not form part of the conviction.

name: Bruno Beger
organization_en: SS-Ahnenerbe · SS
role_en: SS-Ahnenerbe anthropologist involved in the Jewish skeleton-collection project
role_pl: antropolog SS-Ahnenerbe uczestniczący w projekcie kolekcji szkieletów żydowskich ofiar
role_de: Anthropologe des SS-Ahnenerbes im Projekt einer jüdischen Skelettsammlung
role_ru: антрополог СС «Аненербе», участвовавший в проекте коллекции скелетов еврейских жертв
role_fr: anthropologue de l’Ahnenerbe-SS impliqué dans le projet de collection de squelettes juifs
status_en: sentenced to three years for aiding the murder of 86 people
interpretation_en: Beger turned racial anthropology into the selection and documentation of people marked for murder; the Frankfurt judgment precisely defines the scope of his legal guilt.
postwar_en: The Frankfurt Regional Court sentenced him to three years on 6 April 1971, crediting pretrial detention and earlier internment.
limitations_en: The court did not find it proven that Beger already knew the killing plan during the earlier Auschwitz selection or that he co-authored the entire project. The conviction rested on his August 1943 work at Natzweiler, when the court found he knew the victims’ fate. This is a limit of the criminal findings, not a finding that the Auschwitz selection was unrelated to the project.

name: Bruno Kitt
organization_en: Auschwitz-Birkenau · Neuengamme · Waffen-SS
role_en: SS physician at Auschwitz-Birkenau and Neuengamme who participated in prisoner selections
role_pl: lekarz SS w Auschwitz-Birkenau i Neuengamme, uczestnik selekcji więźniów
role_de: SS-Arzt in Auschwitz-Birkenau und Neuengamme, beteiligt an Häftlingsselektionen
role_ru: врач СС в Аушвице-Биркенау и Нойенгамме, участвовавший в селекциях заключённых
role_fr: médecin SS à Auschwitz-Birkenau et Neuengamme, participant aux sélections de détenus
status_en: sentenced to death in the main Neuengamme trial; executed on 8 October 1946
interpretation_en: Kitt used the authority of a camp doctor to select people for death and sustain forced labor through violence and the classification of sick prisoners as fit for work.
postwar_en: The British military court in the first Curio-Haus trial sentenced him to death on 3 May 1946; he was hanged at Hameln on 8 October 1946.
limitations_en: The British conviction concerned participation in crimes at Neuengamme; the profile does not present it as a separate conviction for the Auschwitz selections. Memorial evidence contradicts his 1946 denials, but it does not assign him a named victim total for selections.

name: Curt Rothenberger
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Reich Justice Ministry · Hanseatic Court of Appeal · NSDAP
organization_pl: Ministerstwo Sprawiedliwości Rzeszy · Hanzeatycki Wyższy Sąd Krajowy · NSDAP
role_en: president of the Hanseatic Court of Appeal and state secretary in the Reich Justice Ministry
role_pl: prezes Hanzeatyckiego Wyższego Sądu Krajowego; sekretarz stanu w Ministerstwie Sprawiedliwości Rzeszy
role_de: Präsident des Hanseatischen Oberlandesgerichts und Staatssekretär im Reichsjustizministerium
role_ru: председатель Ганзейского высшего земельного суда и статс-секретарь Министерства юстиции Рейха
role_fr: président de la cour d’appel hanséatique et secrétaire d’État au ministère de la Justice du Reich
status_en: sentenced to seven years in the Justice Case; died by suicide in 1959
interpretation_en: Rothenberger’s responsibility is documented through specific managerial and normative acts and the tribunal’s findings. The profile does not automatically attribute every judgment of subordinate courts or the Justice Ministry’s entire system of repression to him.
postwar_en: The US Military Tribunal found Rothenberger guilty on Counts II and III and sentenced him to seven years in prison. He died by suicide in Hamburg on 1 September 1959; the Hamburg source stresses that his motive is unknown.
limitations_en: The judgment called his Night and Fog role “minor but consenting.” This does not establish personal authorship of the entire program or responsibility for every repressive decision by subordinate institutions. The motive for his suicide is not established.

name: Eberhard Herf
organization_en: Order Police · SS · anti-partisan formations
role_en: Order Police commander in occupied Belarus and staff officer in anti-partisan formations
role_pl: dowódca Ordnungspolizei na okupowanej Białorusi; oficer sztabu formacji zwalczania partyzantki
role_de: Befehlshaber der Ordnungspolizei im besetzten Weißrussland und Stabsoffizier der Bandenkampfverbände
role_ru: командующий полицией порядка в оккупированной Белоруссии и штабной офицер антипартизанских формирований
role_fr: commandant de la police d’ordre en Biélorussie occupée et officier d’état-major des formations antipartisanes
status_en: sentenced to death by a Soviet military tribunal and executed in 1946
interpretation_en: The profile grounds Herf’s responsibility in his command position and the tribunal’s attribution. It does not turn a general account of subordinate formations into proof that Herf personally issued every order or took part in every operation.
postwar_en: Herf was tried in the public Soviet proceeding at Minsk, sentenced to death and executed in 1946. The IfZ analysis stresses both the gravity of the crimes at issue and serious procedural and source-critical problems in the proceeding.
limitations_en: The Minsk record arose within Stalinist demonstrative justice. The IfZ analysis warns against treating every prosecution assertion as independently proved. This profile omits an exact birth day not established by these sources and does not attribute a specific personal killing to Herf.

name: Eberhard von Mackensen
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Wehrmacht · 14th Army
role_en: colonel general and commander of the German 14th Army in Italy
role_pl: generał pułkownik Wehrmachtu; dowódca 14. Armii we Włoszech
role_de: Generaloberst und Oberbefehlshaber der deutschen 14. Armee in Italien
role_ru: генерал-полковник и командующий германской 14-й армией в Италии
role_fr: général d’armée et commandant de la 14e armée allemande en Italie
region_en: Rome and central Italy · occupied Italy
region_pl: Rzym i środkowe Włochy · okupowane Włochy
status_en: death sentence for involvement in the Ardeatine Caves massacre; commuted to life; released in 1952
interpretation_en: Von Mackensen’s responsibility rests on his documented place in the chain of command and the court’s finding. The profile distinguishes his orders and telephone calls from the direct killings carried out by the SD under Herbert Kappler.
postwar_en: The court sentenced von Mackensen to death and the confirming officer commuted the sentence to life imprisonment. He was released on 2 October 1952 and died in Neumünster on 19 May 1969.
limitations_en: The UNWCC report records conflicting evidence about the exact terms of the orders and no evidence that von Mackensen knew the manner in which the shootings were carried out. It also cannot say with certainty whether the court relied on disproportionality, unreasonableness or responsibility for execution. The profile does not claim that he personally shot victims or knew every detail.

name: Eduard Krebsbach
organization_en: Mauthausen concentration camp · SS
role_en: SS chief camp physician at Mauthausen
role_pl: naczelny lekarz obozowy SS w KL Mauthausen
role_de: SS-Standortarzt im Konzentrationslager Mauthausen
role_ru: главный лагерный врач СС в Маутхаузене
role_fr: médecin-chef SS du camp de Mauthausen
status_en: sentenced to death in the Mauthausen Main Case; executed on 28 May 1947
interpretation_en: Krebsbach’s responsibility is individualised by a witness statement, his own sworn statement, USHMM’s institutional finding and the judgment. It concerns medical selections and participation in killing mechanisms, not mere membership of camp medical staff.
postwar_en: Krebsbach was one of the defendants in the Mauthausen Main Case. He was convicted, sentenced to death and executed on 28 May 1947.
limitations_en: The figure of about 200 shootings comes from Krebsbach’s statement and describes participation in a medical capacity, not a proved personal victim total. The number of injection victims is undetermined. Höllriegl’s account is identified as witness testimony rather than presented as an anonymous editorial assertion.

name: Elisabeth Marschall
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Ravensbrück concentration camp · camp infirmary · SS entourage
organization_pl: KL Ravensbrück · obozowa izba chorych · SS-Gefolge
role_en: head nurse in the Ravensbrück camp infirmary
role_pl: naczelna pielęgniarka w izbie chorych KL Ravensbrück
role_de: Oberschwester im Krankenrevier des KZ Ravensbrück
role_ru: старшая медсестра лагерного лазарета Равенсбрюка
role_fr: infirmière-cheffe de l’infirmerie du camp de Ravensbrück
status_en: sentenced to death in the first Ravensbrück trial; executed on 2 May 1947
interpretation_en: Marschall’s responsibility is described through her senior medical role, individualised duties in the archival material, prisoner accounts and the judgment. The profile does not equate selection for labour transports with selection for death and does not claim that she personally performed experiments.
postwar_en: The British military court in the first Ravensbrück trial found Marschall guilty and imposed a death sentence. It was confirmed on 31 March 1947 and carried out at Hameln on 2 May 1947.
limitations_en: The Alvin item is a catalogue summary of preserved testimony, not a full transcript. Schäfer notes that a harsh prosecutorial quotation printed in the press could not be confirmed in the trial material; this profile does not use it. The sources do not establish a personal victim total or that Marschall performed every infirmary act herself.

name: Elisabeth Volkenrath
organization_en: Auschwitz-Birkenau · Bergen-Belsen · concentration-camp system
role_en: head overseer at Auschwitz and Bergen-Belsen
role_pl: Oberaufseherin w Auschwitz i Bergen-Belsen
role_de: Oberaufseherin in Auschwitz und Bergen-Belsen
role_ru: старшая надзирательница в Освенциме и Берген-Бельзене
role_fr: surveillante-chef à Auschwitz et Bergen-Belsen
status_en: sentenced to death; executed at Hameln on 13 December 1945
interpretation_en: Volkenrath’s responsibility is presented through her posts in the camp hierarchy, individualising testimony recorded in the trial report and the judicial outcome. The profile distinguishes allegations and testimony from what the judgment alone establishes.
postwar_en: A British military tribunal convicted Volkenrath in the first Bergen-Belsen staff trial and sentenced her to death by hanging. The sentence was carried out at Hameln on 13 December 1945.
limitations_en: The UNWCC report summarises witness testimony, the defence case and the prosecution’s address. Individual allegations must not be recast as separate judicial findings or used to attribute every crime of both camps to Volkenrath.

name: Emma Zimmer
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Lichtenburg · Ravensbrück · Auschwitz-Birkenau
role_en: camp guard; deputy senior guard
role_pl: nadzorczyni obozowa w Lichtenburgu, Ravensbrück i Auschwitz-Birkenau; zastępczyni starszej nadzorczyni
role_de: KZ-Aufseherin; stellvertretende Oberaufseherin
role_ru: лагерная надзирательница; заместитель старшей надзирательницы
role_fr: surveillante de camp ; adjointe de la surveillante en chef
status_en: sentenced to death; executed in 1948 at Hameln
interpretation_en: Zimmer’s responsibility is described through specific supervisory posts and an individualising account of violence. The profile does not automatically attribute every crime committed at Ravensbrück or Auschwitz to her.
postwar_en: The British military tribunal in the sixth Ravensbrück trial convicted Zimmer of war crimes and sentenced her to death. She was executed in 1948 at Hameln.
limitations_en: The sources use differing shortened titles for Zimmer’s posts; this profile conservatively uses “deputy senior guard”. It does not state a day of execution, and no portrait has been selected because publication rights are unclear.

name: Erhard Milch
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Reich Air Ministry · Luftwaffe
role_en: State Secretary in the Reich Air Ministry; Inspector General and field marshal of the Luftwaffe
role_pl: sekretarz stanu w Ministerstwie Lotnictwa Rzeszy i generalny inspektor Luftwaffe
role_de: Staatssekretär im Reichsluftfahrtministerium; Generalinspekteur und Generalfeldmarschall der Luftwaffe
role_ru: статс-секретарь Имперского министерства авиации; генеральный инспектор и генерал-фельдмаршал люфтваффе
role_fr: secrétaire d’État au ministère de l’Air du Reich ; inspecteur général et maréchal de la Luftwaffe
crime_tags_pl: Praca przymusowa;Jeńcy wojenni;Zbrodnie wojenne;Zbrodnie przeciw ludzkości
status_en: guilty on Counts I and III; not guilty on Count II; life sentence reduced to fifteen years
interpretation_en: Milch’s responsibility is limited to the tribunal’s findings on Counts I and III concerning forced labour. His senior Luftwaffe position is not used here to attribute every action of that organisation to him.
postwar_en: The US Military Tribunal sentenced Milch to life imprisonment. In 1951 the sentence was reduced to fifteen years, and he was released on 28 June 1954.
limitations_en: The judgment separated three counts: the convictions concerned forced labour (I and III), while the medical-experiments count (II) ended in acquittal. The profile does not extend those findings to the Luftwaffe’s collective conduct.

name: Erich Bauer
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Aktion T4 · Sobibor killing centre · SS
organization_pl: Akcja T4 · ośrodek zagłady Sobibór · SS
role_en: Sobibor staff member responsible for the gas-chamber engine
role_pl: funkcjonariusz Sobiboru odpowiedzialny za silnik doprowadzający spaliny do komór gazowych
role_de: Sobibor-Personal; verantwortlich für den Motor der Gaskammern
role_ru: сотрудник Собибора, отвечавший за двигатель газовых камер
role_fr: membre du personnel de Sobibór responsable du moteur des chambres à gaz
status_en: death sentence replaced by life imprisonment; died in prison in 1980
interpretation_en: Bauer’s responsibility rests on a specific technical and operational role in the killing process and on a court judgment. The profile does not automatically attribute every murder at Sobibor to him.
postwar_en: Bauer was recognised in Berlin by Sobibor survivors and brought to trial. The court sentenced him to death; the sentence was replaced by life imprisonment. He died in Tegel prison in 1980.
limitations_en: The profile describes only Bauer’s individually documented function and the outcome of his trial. It gives no date for the replacement of the death sentence by life imprisonment. No portrait was selected: the well-documented available image principally shows him in a group rather than as an unambiguous individual portrait.

name: Erich Priebke
organization_en: Gestapo · Security Police and SD in Rome · SS
organization_pl: Gestapo · Sicherheitspolizei i SD w Rzymie · SS
role_en: Gestapo and SD officer; participant in the Ardeatine Caves massacre
role_pl: oficer Gestapo i SD w Rzymie; uczestnik masakry w Grotach Ardeatyńskich
role_de: Gestapo- und SD-Offizier; Beteiligter am Massaker in den Ardeatinischen Höhlen
role_ru: офицер гестапо и СД; участник массового убийства в Ардеатинских пещерах
role_fr: officier de la Gestapo et du SD ; participant au massacre des Fosses ardéatines
status_en: life imprisonment; sentence served under house arrest until death
interpretation_en: The profile attributes to Priebke only individually documented conduct: an organisational role, maintenance of the victim list and his admitted shooting of two people. It does not automatically transfer Kappler’s decisions or every act of the other perpetrators to him.
postwar_en: Priebke escaped after the war and lived in Argentina for decades. After extradition to Italy he underwent several stages of proceedings; in 1998 he received a final life sentence, served under house arrest on health grounds until his death in 2013.
limitations_en: The number 335 is the total for the massacre, not the number of people personally shot by Priebke. The individualised source records his admission that he shot two men and his maintenance of the list. The profile distinguishes those facts from the group’s wider conduct.

name: Erich Wasicky
organization_en: Mauthausen concentration camp · SS
role_en: SS pharmacist at Mauthausen involved in prisoner selections and in handling agents used for killing
role_pl: aptekarz SS w KL Mauthausen uczestniczący w selekcjach więźniów i obsłudze środków używanych do zabijania
role_de: SS-Apotheker im KZ Mauthausen, beteiligt an Häftlingsselektionen und am Umgang mit Tötungsmitteln
role_ru: аптекарь СС в Маутхаузене, участвовавший в селекциях заключённых и обращении со средствами убийства
role_fr: pharmacien SS à Mauthausen impliqué dans les sélections de détenus et la gestion de moyens de mise à mort
status_en: sentenced to death in 1946; executed on 28 May 1947
interpretation_en: Wasicky’s responsibility rests on an individualised role in selections and in the chain of custody for a killing agent, not merely on employment in the camp pharmacy.
postwar_en: The US military tribunal in the main Mauthausen trial sentenced Wasicky to death. The sentence was carried out at Landsberg on 28 May 1947.
limitations_en: The profile does not attribute every death at Mauthausen or every use of gas to Wasicky personally; it is limited to the acts and functions identified by the sources.

name: Ernst von Weizsäcker
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: German Foreign Office
role_en: State Secretary in the Foreign Office involved in administrative approval of Jewish deportations
role_pl: sekretarz stanu w Auswärtiges Amt uczestniczący w administracyjnym zatwierdzaniu deportacji Żydów
role_de: Staatssekretär im Auswärtigen Amt, beteiligt an der administrativen Genehmigung von Judendeportationen
role_ru: статс-секретарь МИДа, участвовавший в административном согласовании депортаций евреев
role_fr: secrétaire d’État impliqué dans l’approbation administrative de déportations de Juifs
status_en: convicted in 1949; seven years reduced to five; released in 1950
interpretation_en: The profile grounds responsibility in a specific deportation approval and his position as State Secretary; it does not automatically attribute every Foreign Office action to him.
postwar_en: The US tribunal in the Ministries Case sentenced Weizsäcker to seven years in prison. The sentence was reduced to five years, and he was released in 1950.
limitations_en: The tribunal acquitted him of several other allegations, including parts of the aggression case and church persecution. The profile does not extend the judgment beyond the deportation act and the sustained Count Five findings.

name: Erwin Lambert
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: T4 programme · Operation Reinhard · SS
role_en: construction specialist involved in building gas chambers
role_pl: specjalista budowlany akcji „T4” i akcji „Reinhardt” uczestniczący w budowie komór gazowych
role_de: Bauspezialist, beteiligt am Bau von Gaskammern
role_ru: строительный специалист, участвовавший в сооружении газовых камер
role_fr: spécialiste du bâtiment impliqué dans la construction de chambres à gaz
status_en: sentenced to four years’ imprisonment in 1965
interpretation_en: Lambert’s responsibility is technical and operational: the knowing creation of killing infrastructure, without attributing overall command of the camps to him.
postwar_en: In the first Treblinka trial, the Düsseldorf Regional Court convicted Lambert of aiding mass murder and sentenced him to four years in prison.
