limitations_en: The profile does not attribute command of the camps or every death at Sobibor and Treblinka to Lambert; the sources individualise his knowing construction contribution.

name: Erwin Schulz
organization_en: Einsatzkommando 5 · Einsatzgruppe C · SS · Gestapo
role_en: commander of Einsatzkommando 5 within Einsatzgruppe C
role_pl: dowódca Einsatzkommando 5 w Einsatzgruppe C
role_de: Kommandeur des Einsatzkommandos 5 der Einsatzgruppe C
role_ru: командир айнзацкоманды 5 в составе айнзацгруппы C
role_fr: commandant de l’Einsatzkommando 5 au sein de l’Einsatzgruppe C
region_en: Lviv · Zhytomyr · Berdychiv · occupied Soviet Union
status_en: sentenced to twenty years’ imprisonment in 1948
interpretation_en: Schulz’s responsibility rests on direct command of a documented execution and on Einsatzkommando 5’s acts during his command, not on automatically attributing every crime of Einsatzgruppe C to him.
postwar_en: The US tribunal in the Einsatzgruppen trial found Schulz guilty and sentenced him to twenty years’ imprisonment.
limitations_en: The judgment noted his later effort to leave the command but did not treat it as erasing responsibility for the earlier execution. The profile does not transfer all Einsatzgruppe C crimes to him.

name: Ferdinand Schörner
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Wehrmacht · Army High Command
role_en: Wehrmacht field marshal convicted for unlawful killing and attempted killings of subordinate soldiers
role_pl: feldmarszałek Wehrmachtu skazany za bezprawne zabójstwo i usiłowania zabójstwa podległych żołnierzy
role_de: Generalfeldmarschall, wegen rechtswidriger Tötung und versuchter Tötungen unterstellter Soldaten verurteilt
role_ru: фельдмаршал вермахта, осуждённый за незаконное убийство и покушения на убийство подчинённых солдат
role_fr: maréchal de la Wehrmacht condamné pour homicide illégal et tentatives d’homicide sur des subordonnés
status_en: sentenced in 1957 to four years and six months in prison
interpretation_en: The profile rests on individualised acts adjudicated in Munich; his senior military rank is context and does not substitute for proof of conduct.
postwar_en: Munich Regional Court I sentenced Schörner to four years and six months for manslaughter and two attempted killings. He was released before serving the full term on health grounds.
limitations_en: The judgment did not cover every decision Schörner made as a Wehrmacht commander. The profile does not turn rank or reputation into proof of other untried acts.

name: Franz Alfred Six
organization_en: RSHA · Vorkommando Moscow · Einsatzgruppe B · SS and SD
organization_pl: RSHA · Vorkommando Moskau · Einsatzgruppe B · SS/SD
role_en: commander of Vorkommando Moscow in Einsatzgruppe B and senior RSHA official
role_pl: dowódca Vorkommando Moskau w Einsatzgruppe B; kierowniczy funkcjonariusz RSHA
role_de: Führer des Vorkommandos Moskau in der Einsatzgruppe B und leitender RSHA-Funktionär
role_ru: командир передовой команды «Москва» в составе айнзацгруппы B и руководящий сотрудник РСХА
role_fr: commandant du Vorkommando Moscou au sein de l’Einsatzgruppe B et haut responsable du RSHA
status_en: found guilty on Counts I–III in the Einsatzgruppen trial; sentenced to twenty years and released early in 1952
interpretation_en: Six’s responsibility is presented through his command role, his position in the RSHA apparatus and the adjudicated findings. The figure of 144, which belongs to unit reports, is not converted into a number of killings personally committed by Six.
postwar_en: The Einsatzgruppen tribunal found Six guilty on all three counts and sentenced him to twenty years. NARA records that he was released early in 1952 and later appeared in records concerning former Nazi officials in postwar intelligence circles.
limitations_en: The judgment itself left active participation in the murder program unproved to the stated standard; that evidentiary boundary must remain visible. The unit’s reported killings cannot be attributed to Six as personal acts without further evidence. No portrait is included because this review did not verify a specific file together with publication-ready licensing and attribution.

name: Franz Hössler
organization_en: Auschwitz-Birkenau · Auschwitz I · Bergen-Belsen · SS camp staff
organization_pl: KL Auschwitz-Birkenau · KL Auschwitz I · KL Bergen-Belsen · SS
role_en: protective-custody camp leader and supervisor of the women’s camp at Auschwitz-Birkenau
role_pl: Schutzhaftlagerführer i kierownik obozu kobiecego w Auschwitz-Birkenau
role_de: Schutzhaftlagerführer und Leiter des Frauenlagers in Auschwitz-Birkenau
role_ru: начальник лагеря превентивного заключения и руководитель женского лагеря в Аушвице-Биркенау
role_fr: chef du camp de détention préventive et responsable du camp des femmes à Auschwitz-Birkenau
status_en: convicted on the Auschwitz charge and acquitted on the Belsen charge; sentenced to death and executed in 1945
interpretation_en: The profile connects Hössler’s function with individualising testimony and the trial result while keeping witness evidence, defence assertions and judicial findings distinct. The conviction on the Auschwitz charge must be separated from the acquittal on the Belsen charge.
postwar_en: At the 1945 Belsen Trial the British military court convicted Hössler on the Auschwitz charge, acquitted him on the Belsen charge and imposed a death sentence. The confirmed sentence was carried out at Hameln on 13 December 1945.
limitations_en: The law report summarizes contested evidence from both sides; not every witness statement is a separate finding of the tribunal. The profile does not create a named victim total or assign every selection in the camp to Hössler. No portrait is included because a specific file with complete publication-ready licensing and attribution was not verified.

name: Franz Lucas
organization_en: Auschwitz · Mauthausen · SS medical service
organization_pl: KL Auschwitz · KL Mauthausen · służba medyczna SS
role_en: SS camp physician at Auschwitz and Mauthausen implicated in prisoner selections
role_pl: lekarz SS w Auschwitz i Mauthausen, uczestnik selekcji opisanych w źródłach
role_de: SS-Lagerarzt in Auschwitz und Mauthausen, dem Beteiligung an Häftlingsselektionen vorgeworfen wurde
role_ru: лагерный врач СС в Аушвице и Маутхаузене, проходивший по делу об участии в селекциях заключённых
role_fr: médecin SS des camps d’Auschwitz et de Mauthausen mis en cause pour des sélections de détenus
status_en: initially sentenced in 1965; judgment overturned in 1969; finally acquitted on retrial in 1970
interpretation_en: Lucas’s profile must present both the evidence concerning selections and the complete procedural sequence. The 1965 judgment cannot be described as a standing conviction: after reversal, the case ended in a final acquittal in 1970.
postwar_en: The Frankfurt court imposed a three-year-and-three-month sentence in 1965, but the Federal Court of Justice overturned that judgment in 1969. At the retrial Lucas was acquitted on 8 October 1970; he must therefore not be described as finally convicted.
limitations_en: The sources document his assignments and the evidence about selections but do not justify attributing every selection at Auschwitz or Mauthausen to him. The final acquittal must not be omitted or replaced by the first, overturned judgment. No portrait is included because this review did not verify a specific file together with publication-ready licensing and attribution.

name: Franz Romeikat
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Auschwitz concentration camp · Standortverwaltung · SS
role_en: Auschwitz staff member connected with the clothing store and the plunder of victims’ property
role_pl: funkcjonariusz załogi KL Auschwitz związany z magazynem odzieżowym i grabieżą mienia ofiar
role_de: Angehöriger der Auschwitz-Besatzung im Bekleidungslager und bei der Plünderung von Opfervermögen
role_ru: сотрудник персонала Аушвица, связанный с вещевым складом и разграблением имущества жертв
role_fr: membre du personnel d’Auschwitz lié au magasin d’habillement et au pillage des biens des victimes
status_en: sentenced to fifteen years in 1947; released in 1956
interpretation_en: Romeikat’s responsibility rests on specifically established acts of violence and participation in the plunder system, not merely on membership in the Auschwitz staff.
postwar_en: The Supreme National Tribunal sentenced Romeikat to fifteen years’ imprisonment. He was released on 25 June 1956.
limitations_en: The profile does not attribute all plunder at Auschwitz or the acts of other staff members to Romeikat; it follows finding 37 of the judgment and the IPN biography.

name: Franz Xaver Stärfl
organization_en: Kleinbodungen subcamp · SS
organization_pl: SS · podobóz Kleinbodungen (KL Buchenwald, następnie KL Mittelbau)
role_en: SS commander of the Kleinbodungen subcamp and its evacuation column
role_pl: dowódca podobozu Kleinbodungen i kolumny ewakuacyjnej do Bergen-Belsen
role_de: SS-Kommandoführer des Außenlagers Kleinbodungen und des Räumungstransports
role_ru: командир СС лагеря Клайнбодунген и колонны при его эвакуации
role_fr: chef SS du camp annexe de Kleinbodungen et de sa colonne d’évacuation
status_en: convicted on the Bergen-Belsen charge and executed on 13 December 1945
interpretation_en: The documented responsibility concerns command of Kleinbodungen and the evacuation column, the person-specific evidence considered by the court, and its conviction; it does not establish that Stärfl personally shot a prisoner.
postwar_en: The British military court convicted Stofel on the Bergen-Belsen charge and imposed a death sentence, which was carried out in Hameln on 13 December 1945.
limitations_en: The trial report records conflicting witness and defence accounts of shootings on the march. It does not identify Stärfl as the person who fired. The SS-Hauptsturmführer rank is attributed to the Buchenwald Memorial; his birthplace remains unverified.

name: Franz Suchomel
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: SS · Operation Reinhard · Treblinka extermination camp
role_en: Treblinka staff member; head of the Goldjuden unit
role_pl: członek załogi Treblinki; kierownik komanda Goldjuden
role_de: Treblinka-Besatzungsmitglied; Leiter des Goldjuden-Kommandos
role_ru: Сотрудник Треблинки; руководитель команды «золотых евреев»
role_fr: Membre du personnel de Treblinka ; chef du groupe des « Goldjuden »
status_en: Sentenced in Düsseldorf to six years for aiding the joint murder of at least 300,000 people.
interpretation_en: Suchomel’s responsibility rests on the established transport duties, his supervision of prisoners sorting victims’ property and the court judgment. The figure of at least 300,000 defines the scope of his aiding as found by the court, not a personal killing count.
postwar_en: The Düsseldorf court convicted Suchomel of aiding the joint murder of at least 300,000 people and sentenced him to six years’ imprisonment. The sources used here do not reliably establish how much of the sentence he actually served.
limitations_en: The court did not find that Suchomel personally shot the woman taken to the “Lazarett”; this profile does not attribute the shot to him. Sources give different SS ranks (Unterscharführer / Oberscharführer), so no single rank is assigned to his entire service. Portrait rights have not been established; no image is used.

name: Franz Xaver Kraus
organization_en: SS · Auschwitz II-Birkenau · Concentration Camps Inspectorate
organization_pl: SS · KL Auschwitz II-Birkenau · Inspekcja Obozów Koncentracyjnych
role_en: Camp administrator and senior officer in Birkenau’s final phase
role_pl: funkcjonariusz administracji obozowej SS i kierownik w Auschwitz II-Birkenau w końcowej fazie
role_de: Lagerverwaltungsführer und leitender Funktionär in der Endphase Birkenaus
role_ru: Администратор лагерей и руководящий сотрудник Биркенау в конце войны
role_fr: Administrateur SS et cadre de Birkenau pendant la phase finale
status_en: Sentenced to death in the Auschwitz staff trial; executed in 1948.
interpretation_en: The sources connect his senior evacuation role with individualized judicial findings of participation in murders and abuse. That position does not establish a personal victim count.
postwar_en: On 22 December 1947 the Supreme National Tribunal sentenced Kraus to death. Clemency was denied and the sentence was carried out on 24 January 1948.
limitations_en: The IPN describes Kraus’s supervision of the destruction of Crematorium V as probable, not certain. An allegation that he personally shot sick prisoners is not presented as a separate judicial finding; only the court’s finding of participation in murders and abuse is stated. No individual victim number is established. Portrait rights are unverified; no image is used.

name: Friedrich Entress
organization_en: SS · Auschwitz · Mauthausen · Gross-Rosen
organization_pl: SS · KL Auschwitz · KL Mauthausen · KL Gross-Rosen
role_en: SS camp physician
role_pl: lekarz SS w KL Auschwitz i KL Mauthausen
role_de: SS-Lagerarzt
role_ru: Лагерный врач СС
role_fr: Médecin SS des camps
status_en: Sentenced to death in the Mauthausen trial and executed in 1947.
interpretation_en: Two memorial institutions document his involvement in drug testing on prisoners. His death sentence came in the separate Mauthausen staff trial and should not be presented as a judicial ruling on every experiment at Auschwitz.
postwar_en: Entress was a defendant in the main Mauthausen staff trial from March to May 1946. He received a death sentence and was executed at Landsberg Prison on 28 May 1947.
limitations_en: The cited sources do not establish his individual victim count. This profile does not attribute a particular phenol injection to him or equate the Mauthausen judgment with a verdict on Auschwitz experiments. Portrait rights have not been verified; no image is used.

name: Friedrich Hartjenstein
organization_en: SS · Auschwitz II-Birkenau · Natzweiler
organization_pl: SS · KL Auschwitz II-Birkenau · KL Natzweiler
rank: SS-Sturmbannführer podczas służby w Auschwitz II
role_en: Commandant of Auschwitz II-Birkenau and Natzweiler
role_pl: komendant KL Auschwitz II-Birkenau, następnie KL Natzweiler-Struthof
role_de: Kommandant von Auschwitz II-Birkenau und Natzweiler
role_ru: Комендант Освенцима II-Биркенау и Нацвейлера
role_fr: Commandant d’Auschwitz II-Birkenau puis du KL Natzweiler
crime_tags_pl: Auschwitz;Obozy koncentracyjne;Ewakuacje i mordowanie więźniów;Terror obozowy
status_en: Convicted in several trials; died in 1954 before his appeal against the Metz death sentence was heard.
interpretation_en: The documented camp commands, his own evacuation instruction and the trial outcomes establish his responsibility. The British conviction concerned involvement in the killing of four women, but the case report did not establish that he was physically present when they were killed.
postwar_en: Wuppertal: life imprisonment in 1946. Rastatt: death sentence in 1947, commuted in 1952 to twenty years of forced labour. Metz: death sentence on 2 July 1954; he died on 20 October 1954 before the appeal was heard. The French Court of Cassation quashed the Metz judgment after his death.
limitations_en: There was no definite evidence that Hartjenstein was present at the killing of the four women at Natzweiler; this profile does not call him their physical killer. The official Struthof brochure gives conflicting exact days for the Rastatt sentence, so only its year is stated. The Metz judgment was quashed after his death. Portrait rights have not been independently cleared; no image is used.

name: Friedrich Hildebrandt
tier_label_en: Designers of the machinery of destruction
organization_en: NSDAP · Reich administration in Mecklenburg
role_en: Gauleiter and Reich governor of Mecklenburg
role_pl: Gauleiter NSDAP i namiestnik Rzeszy w Meklemburgii
role_de: Gauleiter und Reichsstatthalter von Mecklenburg
role_ru: Гауляйтер и имперский наместник Мекленбурга
role_fr: Gauleiter et gouverneur du Reich au Mecklembourg
status_en: Sentenced to death in an airmen-murder case; executed in 1948; evidence for a specific order is disputed.
interpretation_en: The conviction for involvement in the airmen’s murders is a judicial fact. Evidence for a specific telephone order rested in part on co-defendants’ testimony, which Hildebrandt denied; historians differ in their assessment of its strength.
postwar_en: He was tried by a US military court in the captured-airmen murder case. The court sentenced him to death on 31 March 1947; he was executed at Landsberg on 5 November 1948.
limitations_en: No written order tying him to each killing survives, so such an order is not stated as an uncontested fact. Historians differ over the evidence and trial standards. Separate allegations concerning the killing of patients in Mecklenburg were not the basis of this sentence. Portrait rights are unverified; no image is used.

name: Friedrich Wilhelm Ruppert
organization_en: SS · Dachau concentration camp · Warsaw labour camp
role_en: Dachau protective-custody camp leader
role_pl: funkcjonariusz SS w systemie obozów koncentracyjnych; Schutzhaftlagerführer KL Dachau
role_de: Schutzhaftlagerführer im KZ Dachau
role_ru: Руководитель лагеря заключённых в Дахау
role_fr: Responsable du camp des détenus à Dachau
status_en: Sentenced to death by a US military court and executed in 1946.
interpretation_en: His responsibility is documented by an eyewitness account of his own violence, the case review of his camp activity, and an individual sentence. The more than 90 Soviet POWs mentioned in the review were victims of executions he supervised; that is not a count of people he personally killed.
postwar_en: The military court sentenced him to death on 13 December 1945; the trial register gives 28 May 1946 as the date of his execution at Landsberg.
limitations_en: Rudolf Wolf’s account is witness testimony. This profile does not attribute the personal shooting of four SOE agents to Ruppert or invent an individual victim total without the relevant case records. Portrait rights are unverified; no image is used.

name: Fritz Buntrock
organization_en: SS · Auschwitz-Birkenau concentration camp
role_en: Rapportführer in the Roma camp at Auschwitz-Birkenau
role_pl: Rapportführer w obozie Romów w Auschwitz-Birkenau
role_de: Rapportführer im Roma-Lager von Auschwitz-Birkenau
role_ru: рапортфюрер лагеря ромов в Аушвице-Биркенау
role_fr: Rapportführer dans le camp des Roms à Auschwitz-Birkenau
status_en: sentenced to death in the Auschwitz staff trial and executed on 24 January 1948
interpretation_en: The judgment identifies his own acts, while the museum establishes his role in the liquidation of the Roma camp. The profile does not attribute every killing in that operation to him individually.
postwar_en: The Supreme National Tribunal sentenced Buntrock to death on 22 December 1947. He was hanged at Montelupich prison in Kraków on 24 January 1948.
limitations_en: No individual victim count is established, and oversight of the camp’s liquidation does not itself prove authorship of an extermination order. No portrait is used because reuse rights have not been verified.

name: Fritz Klein
organization_en: SS · Auschwitz · Bergen-Belsen
role_en: SS physician at Auschwitz and Bergen-Belsen
role_pl: lekarz SS w Auschwitz i Bergen-Belsen
role_de: SS-Arzt in Auschwitz und Bergen-Belsen
role_ru: врач СС в Аушвице и Берген-Бельзене
role_fr: médecin SS à Auschwitz et Bergen-Belsen
status_en: sentenced to death in the first Belsen Trial; executed on 13 December 1945
interpretation_en: Ramp and hospital selections directly formed part of the extermination mechanism; these sources do not establish Klein’s individual victim count.
postwar_en: The British military tribunal at Lüneburg sentenced Klein to death in the first Belsen Trial, which ended on 17 November 1945 and also covered Auschwitz crimes. The sentence was carried out at Hamelin prison on 13 December 1945.
limitations_en: In a recorded April 1945 statement Klein gave an age of 58, inconsistent with the birth date he also gave, 24 November 1888. IPN and the Lower Saxony bibliography independently corroborate the date. No portrait is used without checking the precise file’s provenance and license.

name: Fritz Knöchlein
organization_en: Waffen-SS · SS-Totenkopf
role_en: company commander in the 2nd SS-Totenkopf Infantry Regiment
role_pl: dowódca kompanii 2. Pułku Piechoty SS-Totenkopf pod Le Paradis
role_de: Kompaniechef im 2. SS-Totenkopf-Infanterie-Regiment
role_ru: командир роты 2-го пехотного полка СС «Мёртвая голова»
role_fr: commandant de compagnie du 2e régiment d’infanterie SS-Totenkopf
status_en: sentenced to death for the Le Paradis POW massacre; executed on 21 January 1949
interpretation_en: This profile concerns a specific order against prisoners of war and the subsequent court judgment, not every crime committed by the Totenkopf Division.
postwar_en: A British military court tried Knöchlein in Hamburg from 28 August to 25 October 1948 for the murder of surrendered prisoners at Le Paradis. He received a death sentence, carried out at Hamelin prison on 21 January 1949.
limitations_en: The 97 victims are those killed in this massacre, not a lifetime total attributed to Knöchlein. UK National Archives record WO 235/572A identifies the case, but a catalogue entry is not the trial transcript. No portrait is used without confirmed reuse rights.

name: Fritz Suhren
organization_en: SS · Ravensbrück concentration camp
role_en: Ravensbrück camp commandant
role_pl: komendant KL Ravensbrück
role_de: Kommandant des KZ Ravensbrück
role_ru: комендант концлагеря Равенсбрюк
role_fr: commandant du camp de Ravensbrück
status_en: sentenced to death by a French court and executed in 1950; exact day disputed
interpretation_en: His command involved responsibility for the camp system, and the sources also attribute two particular acts to him: participation in Kwiczala’s punishment and ordering the marches. The number marched is not an individual victim count.
postwar_en: After escape and recapture, Suhren appeared before a French court at Rastatt. He was sentenced to death and executed in 1950. Institutional publications disagree on the exact execution date—March, 12 June or 12 July—so only the year is published.
limitations_en: Ravensbrück Memorial gives March 1950, IWM 12 June, and IPN 12 July for the execution. A local archival study reproduces contemporary materials pointing to 12 June, but without resolving the French court records we publish only 1950. No portrait is used without confirmed reuse rights.

name: Georg von Küchler
tier_label_en: Designers of the machinery of destruction
organization_en: Wehrmacht · German Army
role_en: commander of the 18th Army and Army Group North
role_pl: dowódca 18. Armii i Grupy Armii Północ
role_de: Befehlshaber der 18. Armee und der Heeresgruppe Nord
role_ru: командующий 18-й армией и группой армий «Север»
role_fr: commandant de la 18e armée et du groupe d’armées Nord
status_en: sentenced to 20 years in the High Command Trial; released in 1953
interpretation_en: These are court-established findings of command responsibility and transmission of specified orders. Commanding the siege of Leningrad alone does not prove that he personally issued every order concerning starvation or civilian deaths.
postwar_en: The US military tribunal found Küchler guilty on counts II and III, war crimes and crimes against humanity, and sentenced him in October 1948 to 20 years in prison. He was released early from Landsberg in 1953.
limitations_en: The court did not establish a general criminal connection to Einsatzgruppe A exterminations or liability for the Commando Order. The German museum’s description of the legal basis of conviction is unclear or mistaken; this profile follows the judgment itself. No portrait is used without verified reuse rights.

name: Gerhard Schiedlausky
organization_en: Ravensbrück concentration camp · SS
role_en: chief camp physician involved in selections and prisoner selection for experiments
role_pl: lekarz naczelny KL Ravensbrück, uczestnik selekcji i doboru więźniów do eksperymentów
role_de: leitender Lagerarzt, beteiligt an Selektionen und der Auswahl von Häftlingen für Experimente
role_ru: главный лагерный врач, участвовавший в отборах и выборе заключённых для экспериментов
role_fr: médecin-chef du camp, impliqué dans les sélections et le choix de détenus pour les expériences
status_en: sentenced to death; executed on 3 May 1947 in Hameln
interpretation_en: His responsibility is individualised through leadership of camp medical services, selections and identifying prisoners for experiments. The operations are attributed to Gebhardt, not to Schiedlausky.
postwar_en: The British military tribunal sentenced Schiedlausky to death in the first Ravensbrück trial in February 1947. He was executed at Hameln on 3 May 1947.
limitations_en: The figures of thirty selected, six operated on and four deaths derive from Karl Gerber’s account as cited by the memorial; they are not a total victim count for Schiedlausky. No portrait with verified publication rights has been chosen.

name: Gerhard Sommer
organization_en: Waffen-SS · 16th SS Panzergrenadier Division “Reichsführer-SS”
role_en: commander of the 7th Company, SS Panzergrenadier Regiment 35, during the Sant’Anna di Stazzema massacre
role_pl: dowódca 7. kompanii 35. pułku grenadierów pancernych SS podczas masakry w Sant’Anna di Stazzema
role_de: Führer der 7. Kompanie des SS-Panzergrenadier-Regiments 35 beim Massaker von Sant’Anna di Stazzema
role_ru: командир 7-й роты 35-го полка панцергренадеров СС во время резни в Сант-Анна-ди-Стаццема
role_fr: commandant de la 7e compagnie du 35e régiment de panzergrenadiers SS lors du massacre de Sant’Anna di Stazzema
status_en: Italian life sentence in absentia; German proceedings ended without a merits judgment
interpretation_en: Responsibility is tied to command of the company at this massacre and the Italian conviction, not to unproven personal shooting.
postwar_en: An Italian military court sentenced Sommer in absentia to life imprisonment in 2005, affirmed on appeal. German investigations produced no merits judgment; the case was closed in 2015 because he was unfit for trial.
limitations_en: Only the death year 2017 is used: sources differ about the exact day, and a conflicting 2019 year circulates; no civil death record was reviewed. The evidence here does not prove Sommer personally shot civilians. No licensed portrait was selected.

name: Greta Bösel
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Ravensbrück concentration camp · SS auxiliary
role_en: guard assigned to women prisoners’ labour deployment at Ravensbrück
role_pl: nadzorczyni przydziału pracy więźniarek w KL Ravensbrück
role_de: Aufseherin beim Arbeitseinsatz weiblicher Häftlinge im KZ Ravensbrück
role_ru: надзирательница, занимавшаяся распределением заключённых женщин на работы в Равенсбрюке
role_fr: surveillante affectée au travail des détenues à Ravensbrück
status_en: sentenced to death; executed on 2 May 1947 at Hameln
interpretation_en: Individual responsibility is grounded in her labour-deployment role and the testimony and admission of violence, not the camp’s entire crime record.
postwar_en: A British military court sentenced Bösel to death in the first Ravensbrück trial on 3 February 1947; the sentence was carried out at Hameln on 2 May 1947.
limitations_en: The British judgment lacks written reasons attributing findings to each particular allegation. The records vary between Greta/Grete and Bösel/Boesel; her own signatures support Greta. No portrait with established publication rights was chosen.

name: Günther Herrmann
organization_en: Sonderkommando 4b · Einsatzgruppe C · Security Police/SD
role_en: commander of Sonderkommando 4b, Einsatzgruppe C, during mass killings in Ukraine
role_pl: dowódca Sonderkommando 4b Einsatzgruppe C podczas masowych mordów w Ukrainie
role_de: Führer des Sonderkommandos 4b der Einsatzgruppe C bei Massenmorden in der Ukraine
role_ru: командир зондеркоманды 4b айнзацгруппы C во время массовых убийств на Украине
role_fr: commandant du Sonderkommando 4b de l’Einsatzgruppe C lors des massacres en Ukraine
status_en: sentenced to seven years’ imprisonment in Düsseldorf (1973)
interpretation_en: Responsibility is grounded in his documented command and the specific Vinnytsia order, without attributing all of Einsatzgruppe C’s actions to him.
postwar_en: The Düsseldorf Regional Court sentenced Herrmann to seven years’ imprisonment in 1973. The available sources do not justify describing every individual act adjudicated in the case.
limitations_en: Institutional sources establish only the birth and death years 1908–2004; exact days were not independently verified here. No victim count is assigned to the Vinnytsia order. The full Düsseldorf judgment should be read before giving a more precise legal classification. No licensed portrait was selected.

name: Gustav Adolf Steengracht von Moyland
organization_en: German Foreign Office
role_en: State Secretary at the Nazi Foreign Office from 1943 to 1945
role_pl: sekretarz stanu w nazistowskim Ministerstwie Spraw Zagranicznych w latach 1943–1945
role_de: Staatssekretär im Auswärtigen Amt von 1943 bis 1945
role_ru: статс-секретарь нацистского Министерства иностранных дел в 1943–1945 годах
role_fr: secrétaire d’État au ministère nazi des Affaires étrangères de 1943 à 1945
status_en: convicted in the Ministries Trial; final sentence after review: five years
interpretation_en: The profile distinguishes his political-administrative responsibility from personally carrying out deportations and from count III, which was set aside on review.
postwar_en: At the Ministries Trial Steengracht initially received seven years. On review on 12 December 1949, count III was set aside, count V remained and the sentence was reduced to five years; he was released on 28 January 1950.
limitations_en: The overturned count III must not be presented as a final conviction. Retained count V does not prove that he personally issued every deportation order. No portrait with verified licence was selected.

name: Gustav Krupp von Bohlen und Halbach
name_ru: Густав Крупп фон Болен унд Хальбах
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Fried. Krupp AG · Reich Association of German Industry · Adolf Hitler Fund
organization_pl: Fried. Krupp AG · Reichsverband der Deutschen Industrie · Adolf-Hitler-Spende
role_en: Industrialist and chairman of the Krupp supervisory board
role_pl: przemysłowiec; przewodniczący rady nadzorczej Fried. Krupp AG i zarządu Adolf-Hitler-Spende
role_de: Industrieller und Vorsitzender des Krupp-Aufsichtsrats
role_ru: Промышленник и председатель наблюдательного совета Круппа
role_fr: Industriel et président du conseil de surveillance de Krupp
status_en: Charged for the IMT but medically unfit to stand trial; no conviction.
interpretation_en: His leadership roles and deliberate organization of financial support for the regime are individually documented. The forced-labour total belongs to the company; it does not establish that Gustav personally ordered any particular use of forced labour or caused every counted harm.
postwar_en: He was charged for the IMT in 1945, but a unanimous medical commission found him unable to stand trial. He was not tried or convicted and died in 1950.
limitations_en: The 1933 letter proves financing activity, not a judicial finding of guilt. The at-least-100,000 figure is company-wide and extends beyond his chairmanship; no personal forced-labour order or his son Alfried’s later conviction is attributed to him. Portrait rights are unverified; no image is used.

name: Gustav Adolf Nosske
organization_en: Einsatzkommando 12 · Einsatzgruppe D · Security Police/SD
role_en: commander of Einsatzkommando 12, Einsatzgruppe D, in 1941–1942
role_pl: dowódca Einsatzkommando 12 Einsatzgruppe D w latach 1941–1942
role_de: Führer des Einsatzkommandos 12 der Einsatzgruppe D 1941–1942
role_ru: командир айнзацкоманды 12 айнзацгруппы D в 1941–1942 годах
role_fr: commandant de l’Einsatzkommando 12 de l’Einsatzgruppe D en 1941–1942
status_en: sentenced to life, later reduced to ten years; released in 1951
interpretation_en: Responsibility follows the tribunal’s individualized reasoning, not the total crimes of the parent unit.
postwar_en: The Nuremberg Military Tribunal found Nosske guilty on Counts I–III and imposed life imprisonment. The sentence was later reduced to ten years and he was released in 1951.
limitations_en: Only birth and death years are used; exact dates in Harvard metadata have not been independently checked against civil records. The tribunal expressly did not charge him with the parent unit’s full aggregate death toll. He opposed a separate Düsseldorf shooting order in 1944, which did not cancel his conviction for earlier conduct. No portrait with confirmed rights was selected.

name: Gustav Hermann Sorge
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Sachsenhausen concentration camp · SS
role_en: Sachsenhausen Rapportführer involved in violence and killings of prisoners
role_pl: Rapportführer KL Sachsenhausen, sprawca przemocy i zabójstw więźniów
role_de: Rapportführer im KZ Sachsenhausen, an Gewalt und Tötungen von Häftlingen beteiligt
role_ru: рапортфюрер Заксенхаузена, причастный к насилию и убийствам заключённых
role_fr: Rapportführer à Sachsenhausen, impliqué dans les violences et meurtres de détenus
status_en: convicted in the Soviet Sachsenhausen trial and again at Bonn; life plus 15 years
interpretation_en: The profile rests on an individualized court finding about a prisoner killing and the distinct outcomes of two trials, without assigning him every Sachsenhausen death.
postwar_en: A Soviet tribunal sentenced Sorge to 25 years of forced labour in 1947. Transferred to West Germany in 1956, he stood trial at Bonn and in 1959 received life imprisonment plus an additional 15 years.
limitations_en: Exact birth and death dates are not independently documented; only 1911–1978 is used. An archive finding aid incorrectly places the 1959 verdict at Wiesbaden; the court-case index and trial reporting identify Bonn. Detailed murder counts and legal findings require reading the full case 473 judgment. No licensed portrait was selected.

name: Hanns Elard Ludin
organization_en: German Foreign Office · SA
role_en: German envoy in Bratislava
role_pl: poseł Rzeszy w Bratysławie
role_de: Deutscher Gesandter in Bratislava
role_ru: германский посланник в Братиславе
role_fr: envoyé allemand à Bratislava
status_en: sentenced to death by the Bratislava National Court; executed on 9 December 1947
interpretation_en: His own diplomatic acts in deportation policy and personal delivery of repressive demands are documented. This does not establish that he personally ordered every transport from Slovakia or support an individual victim count.
postwar_en: After extradition to Czechoslovakia, Ludin stood trial before the Bratislava National Court. He was sentenced to death on 3 December 1947 and executed on 9 December 1947.
limitations_en: The reported admission concerning political prisoners comes from defence counsel’s later recollection, not a full judgment transcript. The study also reports a remark by the presiding judge suggesting prejudgment; the profile does not treat every 1945 allegation as a separate court finding. Portrait reuse rights are unverified.

name: Hans Aumeier
organization_en: SS; Auschwitz concentration camp
role_en: protective-custody camp leader at Auschwitz
role_pl: Lagerführer KL Auschwitz
role_de: Schutzhaftlagerführer in Auschwitz
role_ru: руководитель лагеря заключённых в Аушвице
role_fr: chef du camp de détention à Auschwitz
status_en: Sentenced to death in the first Auschwitz trial and executed on 24 January 1948.
interpretation_en: His responsibility rests both on his command function and on source-confirmed direct conduct, not merely on membership in the camp staff.
postwar_en: In the first Auschwitz trial the Supreme National Tribunal found him guilty, sentenced him to death and had the sentence carried out in Kraków.
limitations_en: No separate victim total or every act committed by subordinate personnel is attributed to him. No portrait was selected because the precise reuse rights of a specific file were not verified.

name: Hans Eisele
organization_en: SS; Dachau and Buchenwald concentration camps
role_en: SS camp physician
role_pl: lekarz obozowy SS
role_de: SS-Lagerarzt
role_ru: лагерный врач СС
role_fr: médecin SS de camp
status_en: Twice sentenced to death by US military courts; the sentences were commuted, he was released in 1952 and later fled to Egypt.
interpretation_en: The court sources establish conviction for participation in the criminal camp system, but the common-design doctrine does not automatically attribute every crime committed at Dachau to him.
postwar_en: The 2 death sentences were set aside or commuted to imprisonment. After release he returned to medicine; in 1958 he fled to Egypt, whose authorities refused extradition.
limitations_en: Sources differ over his birth year, giving 1912 or 1913; we retain 1913 in line with the candidate identifier and most biographical data. No death covered by the common-design theory is attributed to him without an individual finding. No portrait was selected because rights to a specific file were not verified.

name: Hans Karl Möser
organization_en: SS; Mittelbau-Dora concentration camp
role_en: protective-custody camp leader at Mittelbau-Dora
role_pl: Schutzhaftlagerführer w Mittelbau-Dora

role_ru: руководитель лагеря заключённых в Миттельбау-Дора
role_fr: chef du camp de détention à Mittelbau-Dora
status_en: Sentenced to death in the Mittelbau-Dora staff trial and executed on 26 November 1948.
interpretation_en: Responsibility is documented through his leadership role in the camp and his conviction in the Dora-Nordhausen case; not every death in the complex is automatically attributed to him.
postwar_en: In the US trial of the Mittelbau-Dora staff he was found guilty, sentenced to death and executed at Landsberg.
limitations_en: The charge and common-design theory describe the criminal operation of the complex but do not individualize every victim to Möser. No portrait was selected because reuse rights for a particular photograph were not confirmed.

name: Hans Koch
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: SS; Auschwitz concentration camp
role_en: disinfection-unit member who introduced Zyklon B

interpretation_en: Responsibility concerns a specific technical act within the killing mechanism; his postwar denial quoted by the museum is the defendant’s position, not a court finding.
crime_profile_pl: obsługa Cyklonu B + udział w gazowaniu
postwar_en: In the first Auschwitz trial he received life imprisonment. He died while serving the sentence at Gdańsk prison.
limitations_en: No number of people killed in operations in which he participated is stated because the cited sources provide no source-safe individual total. The quotation from his postwar deposition is presented only as his defense. No portrait was selected because file rights were not verified.

name: Hans Merbach
organization_en: SS; Buchenwald concentration camp
role_en: protective-custody camp leader and evacuation-transport commander
role_pl: Schutzhaftlagerführer w KL Buchenwald

role_fr: chef du camp de détention et responsable d’un convoi d’évacuation
crime_tags_pl: Obozy koncentracyjne;Terror obozowy;Ewakuacje i mordowanie więźniów
status_en: Sentenced to death in the Buchenwald main trial and executed on 14 January 1949.
interpretation_en: His responsibility covers leadership service in the camp and command of a specific evacuation transport. Not every death along the entire route is transferred to him without an additional finding.
crime_profile_pl: kierownictwo obozu + ewakuacja więźniów + transport śmierci
postwar_en: In the Buchenwald main trial before a US military court he was sentenced to death. The sentence was carried out at Landsberg prison.
limitations_en: The court material also discusses disagreement over the extent of his sole responsibility for the transport catastrophe. No single victim count is presented as individually attributable to Merbach. No portrait was selected because rights to a particular file were not verified.

name: Hans Reiter
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Reich Health Office; Nazi Party
role_en: president of the Reich Health Office
role_pl: prezes Urzędu Zdrowia Rzeszy
role_de: Präsident des Reichsgesundheitsamtes
role_ru: президент Имперского ведомства здравоохранения
role_fr: président de l’Office de santé du Reich
status_en: Interned and questioned after the war, but neither charged nor convicted.
interpretation_en: The evidence points to administrative and planning responsibility, not personal performance of experiments. Reiter was not a defendant in the Medical Case, so these findings are not presented as a criminal judgment.
crime_profile_pl: administracja zdrowia + polityka rasowa + planowanie eksperymentów
postwar_en: After the war he was interned and questioned but was not indicted. He was released in 1947 and was never convicted for the conduct described here.
limitations_en: The absence of a judgment requires a clear distinction between historical and interrogation evidence and a judicial finding of guilt. Reiter is not said to have personally performed experiments or every act of the office under him. No portrait was selected because rights to a particular file were not verified.

name: Hans Stark
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: SS; Political Department of Auschwitz concentration camp
role_en: block leader and Political Department officer at Auschwitz
role_pl: funkcjonariusz Wydziału Politycznego KL Auschwitz
role_de: Blockführer und Angehöriger der Politischen Abteilung in Auschwitz
role_ru: блоковый и сотрудник Политического отдела Аушвица
role_fr: chef de block et membre du service politique à Auschwitz
status_en: Convicted in Frankfurt as a co-perpetrator of murder and sentenced under juvenile law to 10 years’ imprisonment.
interpretation_en: The profile rests on individualized findings in the judgment, not only on his Auschwitz service. The use of juvenile law followed from his age at the time and did not amount to acquittal.
crime_profile_pl: rozstrzeliwania + udział w gazowaniu + policja obozowa
postwar_en: The Frankfurt Regional Court found him a co-perpetrator of murder and sentenced him under juvenile law to 10 years’ imprisonment.
limitations_en: No aggregate number of all victims of the Political Department and not every alleged act is attributed to Stark; the findings stated in the reasons are used. Age affected the sentencing basis. No portrait was selected because rights to a specific file were not verified.

name: Hans Theodor Schmidt
organization_en: SS · Buchenwald concentration camp
role_en: adjutant to the commandant of Buchenwald concentration camp
role_pl: adiutant komendanta KL Buchenwald
role_de: Adjutant des Kommandanten des KZ Buchenwald
role_ru: адъютант коменданта концлагеря Бухенвальд
role_fr: adjoint du commandant du camp de concentration de Buchenwald
status_en: sentenced to death in 1947 and executed on 7 June 1951
interpretation_en: Schmidt’s responsibility rests on his command-staff function and individual judgment, not on automatic attribution of every act committed by the camp staff.
postwar_en: The US military tribunal sentenced Schmidt to death in the main Buchenwald trial. He was executed at Landsberg on 7 June 1951.
limitations_en: The sources establish his position, trial and outcome. They do not by themselves attribute every execution at Buchenwald to Schmidt.

name: Hans von Salmuth
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Wehrmacht · German Army

status_en: sentenced to 20 years in 1948; sentence reduced and released in 1953
interpretation_en: Responsibility is tied to documented orders, command practices and the tribunal’s individual findings.
postwar_en: The tribunal convicted Salmuth on Counts II and III and sentenced him to 20 years. The sentence was later reduced and he was released in 1953.
limitations_en: The tribunal did not find that the Commissar Order was carried out within his command; such executions are not attributed to him here.

name: Heinrich Matthes
organization_en: SS · Operation Reinhard · Treblinka
role_en: head of the Treblinka II extermination area

interpretation_en: Matthes’s responsibility rests on his command of the extermination area and the acts established in judicial proceedings.
postwar_en: The Düsseldorf court sentenced Matthes to life imprisonment on 3 September 1965. He died in Bochum prison in 1978.
limitations_en: The judicial scale of complicity is not a count of persons whom he personally killed.

name: Heinrich Schwarz
organization_en: SS · Auschwitz III-Monowitz · Natzweiler

role_fr: commandant d’Auschwitz III-Monowitz et du système concentrationnaire de Natzweiler
status_en: sentenced to death for Natzweiler crimes and executed on 20 March 1947
interpretation_en: Schwarz’s responsibility is tied to command of two camp complexes and to the scope established by the French proceedings.
postwar_en: A French military tribunal sentenced Schwarz to death for crimes connected with the Natzweiler system. He was executed on 20 March 1947.
limitations_en: The Natzweiler judgment was not a separate adjudication of every act committed at Monowitz.

name: Heinz Baumkötter
organization_en: SS · Sachsenhausen concentration camp

status_en: convicted in 1947; sentenced to 8 years in West Germany on 19 February 1962
interpretation_en: Baumkötter’s responsibility rests on his senior medical function and specific conduct established in the proceedings.
postwar_en: Baumkötter was convicted in the Soviet Sachsenhausen trial in 1947. The Münster court sentenced him to 8 years on 19 February 1962; the Federal Court ruled in 1963.
limitations_en: The Soviet and West German trials had different scopes; their findings are not merged into an unlimited list of acts.

name: Heinz Lammerding
organization_en: Waffen-SS · 2nd SS Panzer Division Das Reich

role_fr: commandant de la 2e division blindée SS Das Reich
status_en: sentenced to death in absentia in 1953; not extradited and died in 1971
interpretation_en: Lammerding’s responsibility is individualized by the Tulle order and the French judgment.
postwar_en: A French military tribunal sentenced Lammerding to death in absentia in 1953 for Tulle. West Germany did not extradite him; he died in 1971.
limitations_en: The profile does not attribute a personal order for the Oradour-sur-Glane massacre, which the cited sources do not establish.

name: Helmut Knochen
organization_en: Sipo and SD · BdS France · RSHA

interpretation_en: Knochen’s responsibility covers management of the regional Sipo and SD apparatus and documented decisions and orders.
postwar_en: A French court sentenced Knochen to death in 1954. The sentence was later commuted, and he was released and transferred to West Germany in 1962.
limitations_en: Command authority does not mean personal execution of every deportation or killing carried out by subordinate units.

name: Helmut Poppendick
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: SS · RuSHA · Reich Physician SS and Police

region_en: Nazi Germany · SS medical and racial apparatus
region_pl: III Rzesza · aparat medyczny i rasowy SS
status_en: sentenced to ten years solely for membership in the criminal SS
interpretation_en: The profile separates his offices in the SS apparatus from acts for which the tribunal did not convict him. It does not present him as convicted for experiments.
postwar_en: The US tribunal acquitted him of the experiment-related war-crime and humanity charges but imposed ten years for membership in the criminal SS.
limitations_en: The judgment distinguishes suspicion and knowledge from proof of criminal responsibility for experiments; this profile preserves that boundary.

name: Helmut Vetter
organization_en: SS · Auschwitz concentration camp · Gusen concentration camp
role_en: SS physician at Auschwitz and Gusen
role_pl: lekarz SS w Auschwitz i Gusen

role_ru: врач СС в Аушвице и Гузене
role_fr: médecin SS à Auschwitz et Gusen
status_en: sentenced to death by a US military court
interpretation_en: The museum documents individual medical conduct and the archive documents the legal outcome; no unsupported personal victim total is assigned.
postwar_en: A US military court imposed a death sentence in proceedings concerning Gusen personnel.
limitations_en: The sources establish experiments and sentence but do not support a reliable personal victim estimate.

name: Helmuth von Pannwitz
organization_en: Wehrmacht · Waffen-SS · Cossack collaborationist formations
rank: Generalleutnant; Gruppenführer und Generalleutnant der Waffen-SS
role_en: commander of the First Cossack Cavalry Division and the Fifteenth Cossack Cavalry Corps

role_ru: командир Первой казачьей кавалерийской дивизии и Пятнадцатого казачьего кавалерийского корпуса
role_fr: commandant de la Première division de cavalerie cosaque et du Quinzième corps de cavalerie cosaque
status_en: sentenced to death by a Soviet court and executed
interpretation_en: Responsibility is stated at command level and through the persistent pattern of unit crimes, without attributing personal execution of every act.
postwar_en: A Soviet court sentenced Pannwitz to death and the sentence was carried out in Moscow.
limitations_en: The sources document crimes by units under his command and ineffective disciplinary action, but do not prove that he personally carried out each offence.

name: Herbert Hagen
organization_en: SS · Security Police and Security Service · Reich Security Main Office
role_en: security official responsible for organizing deportations of Jews from France
role_pl: funkcjonariusz Sipo i SD odpowiedzialny za organizację deportacji Żydów z Francji

role_fr: responsable de la sécurité chargé d’organiser les déportations de Juifs depuis la France
status_en: sentenced in Cologne to twelve years for aiding the murder of seventy-three thousand deported Jews
interpretation_en: The figure of seventy-three thousand comes from the court finding on assistance in deportation and murder; it is not presented as a number personally killed by Hagen.
postwar_en: After an earlier French judgment in absentia, Hagen faced trial in Cologne and received twelve years for aiding the murder of seventy-three thousand deportees.
limitations_en: The profile attributes organizational and administrative assistance established by the court, not personal execution of every killing.

name: Hermann Höfle
organization_en: SS · Waffen-SS · German occupation forces in Slovakia
organization_pl: SS · Waffen-SS · niemieckie wojska okupacyjne na Słowacji
rank: SS-Obergruppenführer und General der Waffen-SS und Polizei
role_en: commander of German forces in Slovakia during suppression of the uprising
role_pl: dowódca wojsk niemieckich na Słowacji podczas tłumienia powstania
role_de: Befehlshaber deutscher Truppen in der Slowakei während der Niederschlagung des Aufstands
role_ru: командующий немецкими войсками в Словакии во время подавления восстания
role_fr: commandant des forces allemandes en Slovaquie pendant la répression du soulèvement
status_en: sentenced to death by the National Court in Bratislava and executed
interpretation_en: This profile concerns the older commander and his command responsibility in Slovakia; he must not be confused with the namesake linked to Aktion Reinhardt.
postwar_en: After extradition to Czechoslovakia he faced the National Court in Bratislava, received a death sentence and was executed.
limitations_en: Sources differ on secondary details of the execution date and method; the profile does not choose a method and clearly distinguishes the younger namesake.

name: Hermann Hoth
tier_label_en: Designers of the machinery of destruction
organization_en: Wehrmacht · Army High Command
role_en: armoured-force commander on the eastern front
role_pl: dowódca wojsk pancernych na froncie wschodnim
role_de: Panzertruppenbefehlshaber an der Ostfront
role_ru: командующий танковыми войсками на восточном фронте
role_fr: commandant de forces blindées sur le front oriental
status_en: sentenced to fifteen years in the High Command Case
interpretation_en: Responsibility rests on specific court findings about transmission of the order and conduct of subordinate units, not on rank alone.
postwar_en: The US tribunal found Hoth guilty on the war-crime and crimes-against-humanity counts and imposed fifteen years in prison.
limitations_en: The judgment concerns specified orders and command practices; the profile does not automatically attribute every offence by every unit to him.

name: Hermann Pister
organization_en: SS; Hinzert and Buchenwald concentration camps
role_en: commandant of Buchenwald concentration camp
role_pl: Komendant KL Buchenwald
role_de: Kommandant des Konzentrationslagers Buchenwald
role_ru: комендант концлагеря Бухенвальд
role_fr: commandant du camp de concentration de Buchenwald
status_en: Sentenced to death in 1947; died in prison on 28 September 1948 before execution.
interpretation_en: Pister is presented as responsible in his capacity as camp commandant. Without a separate finding, the profile does not attribute to him every act by subordinate personnel or every death at Buchenwald.
crime_profile_pl: komendantura obozu + system więźniarski + odpowiedzialność kierownicza
postwar_en: Arrested in June 1945, he was tried in the Buchenwald main trial. The death sentence was not carried out because he died in US custody on 28 September 1948.
limitations_en: The sources safely establish his office, conviction and death in custody. No individual victim total or specific killing order is attributed without separate evidence. No portrait was selected because rights to a particular file were not verified.

name: Hildegard Lächert
organization_en: SS camp staff; Majdanek and Auschwitz concentration camps
organization_pl: SS camp staff; KL Majdanek; KL Auschwitz
role_en: SS overseer at Majdanek and Auschwitz
role_pl: Nadzorczyni SS w Majdanku i Auschwitz

role_ru: надзирательница СС в Майданеке и Аушвице
role_fr: surveillante SS à Majdanek et Auschwitz
status_en: Sentenced to 15 years in 1947; sentenced again to 12 years in 1981.
interpretation_en: The profile rests responsibility on an individualized description of violence and two judgments, not on camp-staff membership alone.
crime_profile_pl: nadzór nad więźniami + przemoc obozowa + reżim więźniarski
postwar_en: After the 15-year sentence she was released under the 1956 amnesty. Arrested again in 1975, she received 12 years in the Majdanek trial that ended in 1981.
limitations_en: No victim count is attributed exclusively to Lächert. Her place of death was not independently confirmed and remains blank. No portrait was selected because rights to a particular file were not verified.

name: Horst Paul Silvester Fischer
organization_en: SS; Auschwitz-Monowitz concentration camp
role_en: camp doctor and deputy garrison physician at Auschwitz-Monowitz
role_pl: Lekarz obozowy i zastępca lekarza garnizonowego Auschwitz-Monowitz

role_fr: médecin du camp et adjoint au médecin de garnison à Auschwitz-Monowitz
status_en: Sentenced to death on 25 March 1966; executed on 8 July 1966.
interpretation_en: Responsibility rests on his individualized role in selections and on preserved documentation of operations. The indictment’s numerical allegation is not reproduced as a separately established victim total.
crime_profile_pl: medycyna obozowa + selekcje + medycznie zbędne operacje
postwar_en: Arrested in 1965, he was convicted of crimes against humanity and sentenced to death on 25 March 1966. The sentence was carried out on 8 July 1966.
limitations_en: Bundesarchiv sources discuss the political instrumentalization of Nazi-crime prosecutions in the GDR. That context does not erase the documented role and judgment, but it requires separating findings from the trial’s propaganda setting. No portrait was selected because rights to a particular file were not verified.

name: Joachim Mrugowsky
organization_en: SS; Waffen-SS; Waffen-SS Hygiene Institute
role_en: head of the Waffen-SS Hygiene Institute and chief hygienist of the Waffen-SS

role_de: Leiter des Hygiene-Instituts und oberster Hygieniker der Waffen-SS
role_ru: руководитель Института гигиены и главный гигиенист войск СС
role_fr: chef de l’Institut d’hygiène et hygiéniste en chef de la Waffen-SS
region_en: German Reich and the concentration-camp system
region_pl: Rzesza Niemiecka i system obozów koncentracyjnych
status_en: Sentenced to death in the Doctors Trial and executed on 2 June 1948.
interpretation_en: His responsibility rests on his leadership role in the Waffen-SS medical apparatus and on tribunal findings concerning specific experiment programs.
postwar_en: United States Military Tribunal I convicted him on counts two, three and four, sentenced him to death, and the sentence was carried out on 2 June 1948.
limitations_en: No separate victim total is attributed to him, nor is every experiment conducted by SS medical personnel. No portrait was selected without verified reuse rights.

name: Johann Altfuldisch
organization_en: SS; Mauthausen concentration camp
role_en: protective-custody camp leader at Mauthausen
role_pl: Schutzhaftlagerführer KL Mauthausen

role_fr: chef du camp des détenus à Mauthausen
region_en: Mauthausen in Austria annexed to the Reich
status_en: Sentenced to death in the Mauthausen main trial and executed on 28 May 1947.
interpretation_en: His responsibility joins a camp leadership function with the judicial finding of participation in the common design; the profile does not automatically attribute every staff act to him.
postwar_en: A United States military tribunal at Dachau sentenced him to death in the Mauthausen main trial; the sentence was carried out on 28 May 1947.
limitations_en: No killing or beating committed by Mauthausen staff is attributed to him without a separate source, and no distinct victim total is assigned. No portrait was selected without verified rights.

name: Johann Paul Kremer
organization_en: SS; Auschwitz concentration camp
role_en: Auschwitz camp physician and professor of anatomy

role_fr: médecin du camp d’Auschwitz et professeur d’anatomie
status_en: Sentenced to death on 22 December 1947; the sentence was commuted to life imprisonment, and he was convicted again after release.
interpretation_en: His responsibility rests on his own conduct as a camp physician, not merely on SS membership or presence at Auschwitz.
postwar_en: The death sentence was commuted to life imprisonment. After his release in 1958, a Münster court imposed ten years in prison and credited his prior confinement.
limitations_en: No separate victim total or acts of other Auschwitz physicians are attributed to him. No portrait was selected without precisely verified reuse rights.

name: Johann Pauls
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: SS; Stutthof concentration camp
role_en: SS non-commissioned officer and commander of a prisoner labor detail
role_pl: dowódca kolumny roboczej więźniów KL Stutthof
role_de: SS-Unterführer und Führer eines Häftlingsarbeitskommandos
role_ru: унтер-офицер СС и начальник рабочей команды заключённых
role_fr: sous-officier SS et chef d’un kommando de travail de détenus
status_en: Sentenced to death in the first Stutthof trial and executed on 4 July 1946.
interpretation_en: His responsibility rests both on his supervisory function and on judicial findings about his own acts of violence and killing.
postwar_en: The Special Criminal Court in Gdańsk sentenced him to death; the sentence was carried out publicly on 4 July 1946.
limitations_en: No separate victim total or acts of other Stutthof staff members are attributed to him. No portrait was selected without verified reuse rights.

name: Johann-Georg Richert
organization_en: Wehrmacht; 286th Security Division; 35th Infantry Division
role_en: commander of the 286th Security Division and 35th Infantry Division
role_pl: dowódca 286. Dywizji Bezpieczeństwa i 35. Dywizji Piechoty
role_de: Kommandeur der 286. Sicherungs-Division und der 35. Infanterie-Division
role_ru: командир 286-й охранной и 35-й пехотной дивизий
role_fr: commandant de la 286e division de sécurité et de la 35e division d’infanterie
status_en: Sentenced to death at the Minsk trial on 29 January 1946 and executed the next day.
interpretation_en: Richert’s responsibility rests on both his own documented statement and his command role in the Ozarichi operation; the sources do not support attributing every killing to his personal execution.
postwar_en: A Soviet military tribunal in Minsk sentenced him to death. The proceeding had serious procedural limitations and a propagandistic character, so the conduct account is also supported by independent archival scholarship on Ozarichi.
limitations_en: Not every death in his divisions’ operational area, nor any separate victim total, is attributed solely to Richert. No portrait was selected because rights to a specific file were not verified.

name: Johanna Bormann
organization_en: SS entourage; Auschwitz concentration camp; Bergen-Belsen
role_en: overseer at Auschwitz-Birkenau and Bergen-Belsen
role_pl: nadzorczyni w Auschwitz-Birkenau i Bergen-Belsen
role_de: Aufseherin in Auschwitz-Birkenau und Bergen-Belsen
role_ru: надзирательница в Аушвице-Биркенау и Берген-Бельзене
role_fr: surveillante à Auschwitz-Birkenau et Bergen-Belsen
status_en: Convicted on the Auschwitz charge, acquitted on the Bergen-Belsen charge, and executed on 13 December 1945.
interpretation_en: The profile distinguishes witness testimony, which Bormann denied, from the scope of the verdict: guilt concerned the Auschwitz charge, while the Bergen-Belsen charge ended in acquittal.
postwar_en: The British military court at Lüneburg convicted her on the Auschwitz charge, acquitted her on the Bergen-Belsen charge and sentenced her to death by hanging.
limitations_en: Not every witness allegation is presented as a separate final finding, and no victim total is attributed to Bormann. No portrait was selected without verified rights to a specific file.

name: Josef Altstötter
tier_label_fr: Rouages de la guerre et de l’occupation
organization_en: Reich Justice Ministry; SS
role_en: chief of the Civil Law and Procedure Division
role_pl: dyrektor Wydziału Prawa Cywilnego w Ministerstwie Sprawiedliwości Rzeszy
role_de: Leiter der Abteilung Zivilrecht und Zivilprozess
role_ru: начальник отдела гражданского права и процесса
role_fr: chef de la division du droit civil et de la procédure civile
status_en: Acquitted of war crimes and crimes against humanity; sentenced to five years for knowing membership in the SS.
interpretation_en: Responsibility must remain within the judgment: Altstötter was convicted for knowing SS membership, not for war crimes, crimes against humanity, Night and Fog, or particular racial judgments.
crime_profile_pl: nazistowski wymiar sprawiedliwości + świadome członkostwo w SS
postwar_en: US Military Tribunal III acquitted him on Counts II and III, convicted him on Count IV and imposed five years’ imprisonment with credit for pretrial confinement.
limitations_en: No conduct covered by the acquitted counts or crimes of other SS members is attributed to him. No portrait was selected without verified rights to a specific file.

name: Josef Dietrich
organization_en: SS; Waffen-SS; Leibstandarte SS Adolf Hitler
organization_pl: SS; Waffen-SS; Leibstandarte SS Adolf Hitler
role_en: commander of the Leibstandarte SS, I SS Panzer Corps and 6th SS Panzer Army
role_pl: dowódca Leibstandarte SS i 6. Armii Pancernej SS
role_de: Kommandeur der Leibstandarte SS, des I. SS-Panzerkorps und der 6. SS-Panzerarmee
role_ru: командир «Лейбштандарта СС», I танкового корпуса СС и 6-й танковой армии СС
role_fr: commandant de la Leibstandarte SS, du Ier corps blindé SS et de la 6e armée blindée SS
status_en: Sentenced to life at the Malmedy trial, later commuted; separately sentenced to eighteen months by a West German court.
interpretation_en: The profile presents the trial findings as ordering and command responsibility; it does not claim that Dietrich personally shot the victims at Malmedy.
crime_profile_pl: bezprawny rozkaz + egzekucje jeńców + odpowiedzialność dowódcza
postwar_en: The Malmedy life sentence was commuted to twenty-five years and Dietrich was released in 1955. In 1957 a West German court imposed eighteen months for aiding killings committed in 1934; he was released in 1958.
limitations_en: The account rests on an individualized court document but does not equate command responsibility with personally carrying out every killing. No portrait was selected without verified rights.

name: Josef Erber
organization_en: SS; Political Department of Auschwitz concentration camp
role_en: camp Gestapo official and admissions chief at Birkenau
role_pl: funkcjonariusz Politische Abteilung i kierownik przyjęć w Auschwitz-Birkenau
role_de: Angehöriger der Lager-Gestapo und Leiter der Aufnahme in Birkenau
role_ru: сотрудник лагерного гестапо и начальник приёма в Биркенау
role_fr: membre de la Gestapo du camp et chef de l’admission à Birkenau
status_en: Sentenced to life at the second Frankfurt Auschwitz trial; released on 9 August 1986.
